# Agent Fleet, clean style (Pro)

Several agents side by side – each card sums up its sub-agents, and a click opens its tree to the right while the last one folds back into its card

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-fleet
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-fleet-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-fleet-clean`

### When to use

- Several agents working at the same time – a launch, the support queue, a release – each with sub-agents of its own
- Seeing at a glance which agent needs you, which one failed and what the whole fleet costs – without every tree open at once
- A fleet overview on a dashboard: one tree open, the others folded to a single card

### When not to use

- One run with one orchestrator – use Agent Tree
- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- Handing tasks to agents yourself – use Delegate Board

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentFleet, type FleetAgent } from "@/components/ui/agent-fleet-clean";

const fleet: FleetAgent[] = [
  {
    id: "launch", name: "Launch lead", model: "Opus 5.5", task: "Launch the new pricing page",
    status: "running", cost: 0.42, started: Date.now() - 840_000,
    children: [
      { id: "research", name: "Researcher", task: "Compare five competitors", status: "done", cost: 0.31, started: Date.now() - 780_000, ended: Date.now() - 360_000 },
      { id: "copy", name: "Writer", task: "Write the plan copy", status: "waiting", cost: 0.18, started: Date.now() - 720_000 },
    ],
  },
  { id: "support", name: "Support lead", task: "Answer the open tickets", status: "running", cost: 0.12, started: Date.now() - 1_560_000 },
];

export function Fleet() {
  return <AgentFleet agents={fleet} onSelect={(agent) => openLog(agent.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `FleetAgent[]` |  | { id, name, task, model?, avatar?, tools?, status, steps?, cost?, started?, ended?, children? } – the main agents, each with its sub-agents; pass them again whenever something changes; tools are small marks shown as overlapping tiles before the task |
| steps | `FleetStep[]` |  | Per sub-agent, { title, status?, tool?, took? } – the tasks it worked through; a click on its card opens them in a small window |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "stopped"` |  | Per agent – "waiting" reads "Needs you"; queued and stopped sub-agents and their connectors are muted |
| cost | `number` |  | Per agent, its own cost – a main agent shows its whole branch, the bar the whole fleet |
| open / defaultOpen | `string \| null` | `the first agent` | Id of the main agent whose tree is open, controlled or uncontrolled – null folds them all |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | An agent was opened – or folded with a second click |
| ask / error | `string` |  | Per sub-agent – what a waiting one needs you to decide, and what went wrong for a failed one; shown at the top of its window above Approve and Reject, or Retry and Dismiss |
| onResolve | `(agent, action: "approve" \| "reject" \| "retry" \| "dismiss") => void` |  | An answer for a sub-agent that needs you or failed – update its status in your data; without it, those cards get no Answer or Resolve button |
| onSelect | `(agent: FleetAgent) => void` |  | A click on a sub-agent – makes the sub-agent cards clickable; one with steps opens its tasks window as well |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for running times – without it the cards tick every second while an agent runs |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Moves between the main agents
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or the last main agent
- Enter / Space: On a main agent: opens its tree, or folds it when it's open – on a sub-agent: opens or closes its tasks window
- Tab: Moves on into the open tree's cards – those with steps, an answer to give or onSelect; in an answer window, Approve or Retry has focus and Tab reaches the other
- Esc: Closes the tasks window and puts focus back on its card

### Accessibility

- Every main agent is a button with aria-expanded, pointing at the open tree with aria-controls
- The open tree is a tree labelled "Sub-agents of …"; every sub-agent is a treeitem labelled with its name and status
- The totals in the bar – agents, running, needs you, cost – are announced politely when they change
- Status is never color alone: every card spells it out, and the phrase under each main agent says what the ring shows
- The small Answer or Resolve button on a card is a pointer shortcut – keyboard users open the same window from the card itself
- A sub-agent with steps, or one that needs you or failed, has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; its tasks window is a dialog labelled "Tasks of …", closed by Esc or a click elsewhere

### Motion

- The agent you open stays as it is while the others fade back to half – hover brings one forward again
- The open tree leaves first – bottom card first, while its connectors pull back into the card – then the new connectors draw themselves out and the cards rise in one after another
- The tree stands centered on its agent, as far as the column reaches; when it grows while open, it glides to its new place
- Costs that still climb carry a light shimmer
- A sub-agent's tasks window drops down from its card, the tasks fading in one after another
- With prefers-reduced-motion the trees switch at once

# Agent Graph, clean style (Pro)

Agents and the tools they call as a living network – a pulse along the link for every call and its answer, busy links growing thicker, agents that breathe while they work and turn amber when they need you

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-graph
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-graph-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-graph-clean`

### When to use

- A live overview of a multi-agent system: which agents run, which tools and data sources they call, and how busy each link is
- Spotting at a glance who waits for you, which call failed and where the traffic (and the cost) goes
- A hero or status view next to a log or a chat – click a node to see what it does and its latest calls

### When not to use

- Who started whom, with status and cost per sub-agent – use Agent Tree
- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's single tool call in detail – use Tool Call Card
- Graphs with dozens of agents – the orbits are made for a handful of agents and up to a dozen tools

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentGraph, type GraphNode, type GraphCall } from "@/components/ui/agent-graph-clean";

const nodes: GraphNode[] = [
  { id: "lead", kind: "agent", name: "Orchestrator", detail: "Opus 5.5", status: "working", lead: true },
  { id: "research", kind: "agent", name: "Researcher", detail: "Sonnet 5.5", status: "working", cost: 0.12 },
  { id: "web", kind: "tool", name: "Web search", short: "Search" },
  { id: "notion", kind: "tool", name: "Notion", icon: <NotionLogo /> },
  { id: "you", kind: "user", name: "You" },
];

// Newest last – every new id sends a pulse; when "pending" turns "ok" or "error" the answer travels back
const calls: GraphCall[] = [
  { id: "c1", from: "lead", to: "research", at: Date.now() - 4000, status: "pending", label: "Compare pricing" },
  { id: "c2", from: "research", to: "web", at: Date.now() - 900, status: "ok", ms: 820, label: "pricing linear.app" },
];

export function Live() {
  return <AgentGraph nodes={nodes} calls={calls} edges={[["you", "lead"], ["research", "notion"]]} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| nodes | `GraphNode[]` |  | { id, name, kind, short?, icon?, detail?, status?, doing?, cost?, lead? } – every agent, tool and user; pass the whole list each time, ids keep nodes in place and new ids grow in |
| kind | `"agent" \| "tool" \| "user"` |  | Per node – agents sit on the inner orbit (the lead in the middle), tools and you on the outer one, each turned towards the agents it talks to |
| status | `"idle" \| "working" \| "waiting" \| "error" \| "done"` |  | Per node – working agents breathe, waiting ("Needs you") and error look alike in amber and red – a light fill with a shine sweeping across and a thin stroke running around the edge; waiting and error also show a chip in the bar |
| short | `string` |  | Per node – a shorter label for narrow containers, e.g. "Search" |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Per node – a logo or mark; defaults to the initials (a person for the user) |
| detail / doing | `string` |  | Per node – the model or what a tool is (under the agent's name and in its card), and what it is doing right now (in its card) |
| cost | `number` |  | Per node – what it has cost so far; the bar sums all nodes |
| lead | `boolean` | `first agent` | Per node – the agent in the middle |
| calls | `GraphCall[]` | `[]` | { id, from, to, at, status?, label?, ms? } – recent calls, newest last. A new id sends a pulse from → to; when its status turns "ok" the answer travels back in green, "error" comes back red and flashes the link. Calls also create the links they need |
| edges | `[string, string][]` | `[]` | Links that are always there, even before their first call |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for calls per minute and link heat – without it the graph ticks every second |
| heatWindow | `number` | `20000` | How far back (ms) calls count towards a link's activity – kept for parity with the classic style; here every link is the same light gray 1.5px line |
| onSelect | `(node: GraphNode \| null) => void` |  | A node was clicked (its card opens) – null when the card closes |
| height | `number` | `fits the width` | Fixed height of the graph in px – by default 0.6 × the width (360–520px) when wide, 1.2 × when narrow |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agent graph"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the nodes (and the "needs you" / "failed" chips); a focused node lights up its neighbourhood
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the focused node's card
- Esc: Closes the card and returns focus to its node

### Accessibility

- Every node is a button labelled with its name, kind, status, what it does and its calls in the last minute; aria-expanded tells whether its card is open
- The card is a dialog; its close button takes focus, Esc closes it
- A visually hidden list gives the same picture as text: every node, its status, whom it called how often in the last minute and its cost
- "needs you" and "failed" chips sit in a polite live region, so a waiting or failed agent is announced
- Status is never color alone: waiting and failed agents get a badge (clock, exclamation mark) and a text line under the name

### Motion

- On the first draw the lead pops in, then the agents, then the tools around the orbit – each link draws itself towards the node it reaches
- Every call sends a short line along its link that fades out behind, with a light glow – blue for a call, green for the answer, amber for you, red for an error; the node it lands on ripples once
- Links are one even 1.5px line each in a light gray, with one rounded right-angled turn, busy or not – only the moving lines carry color
- Working agents breathe with a soft ring, waiting ones a little quicker in amber
- When nodes come or go every node glides to its new place on a spring – a new tool slides out of the first agent it is linked to; a leaving one shrinks away while its link pulls back
- One requestAnimationFrame loop drives gliding and pulses; it pauses when the graph is off screen or the tab is hidden
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing glides or travels: a link simply lights up for each call

### Responsive

- The width is measured with a ResizeObserver and the whole layout is computed from it – orbits, node sizes and label room
- Below 520px the graph turns taller than wide, nodes get smaller, labels use their short names, the model line is left out and the card docks to the bottom of the graph
- Labels and the outer orbit always stay inside the panel – nothing is cut off and nothing scrolls sideways, down to 320px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole nodes and calls arrays every time something changes; a call's id must stay the same while its status goes from pending to ok/error
- Calls older than four seconds when they first appear don't send a pulse – they only count towards heat and calls per minute
- Brand logos are not part of the component – pass them as icon; the UI icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT), keep the credit comment
- The link color is --ui-aggc-link (a light gray); calls use --ui-aggc-pulse, answers --ui-aggc-ok
- Keep it to a handful of agents and about a dozen outer nodes – more get crowded on the outer orbit

### Requirements

- React 19

- Status is never color alone: waiting and failed agents get a badge (clock, exclamation mark) and a text line under the name

### Motion

- On the first draw the lead pops in, then the agents, then the tools around the orbit – each link draws itself towards the node it reaches
- Every call sends a solid dot with a short tail along its link; the answer comes back as a hollow dot, amber for you, red for an error – the node it lands on ripples once
- Links thicken with use (stroke-width eases over 0.7s) and fade back after six quiet seconds; a link lights up while a pulse runs along it
- Working agents breathe with a soft ring, waiting ones a little quicker in amber
- When nodes come or go every node glides to its new place on a spring – a new tool slides out of the first agent it is linked to; a leaving one shrinks away while its link pulls back
- One requestAnimationFrame loop drives gliding and pulses; it pauses when the graph is off screen or the tab is hidden
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing glides or travels: a link simply lights up for each call

### Responsive

- The width is measured with a ResizeObserver and the whole layout is computed from it – orbits, node sizes and label room
- Below 520px the graph turns taller than wide, nodes get smaller, labels use their short names, the model line is left out and the card docks to the bottom of the graph
- Labels and the outer orbit always stay inside the panel – nothing is cut off and nothing scrolls sideways, down to 320px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole nodes and calls arrays every time something changes; a call's id must stay the same while its status goes from pending to ok/error
- Calls older than four seconds when they first appear don't send a pulse – they only count towards heat and calls per minute
- Brand logos are not part of the component – pass them as icon; the UI icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT), keep the credit comment
- The link color is --ui-agg-link (#82bcff), the soft blue of Agent Tree; pulses use --ui-agg-pulse
- Keep it to a handful of agents and about a dozen outer nodes – more get crowded on the outer orbit

import { AgentHandoff, type HandoffAgent, type Handoff } from "@/components/ui/agent-handoff-clean";

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `HandoffAgent[]` |  | In relay order: { id, name, model?, avatar?, description? } – each card shows what it's for and the task it's on, taken from tasks |
| handoffs | `Handoff[]` |  | What was handed over: { id, from, to, task, items } – each lands as a card in the column between from and to, latest on top; a new id sends light along its lines |
| items | `HandoffItem[]` |  | Per handoff: { id, label, kind?: "file" | "source" | "fact" | "decision" | "note", lost?, why? } – lost ones are struck through, why shows on hover |

# Agent Ledger, clean style (Pro)

Everything an agent changed in your systems, each change with an undo – before and after per row, and pointing at Undo shows what builds on it: what would be undone too, and what can't be taken back

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-ledger
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-ledger-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-ledger-clean`

### When to use

- An agent works in real systems – code, payments, CRM, docs, chat – and people need to see what it changed and take it back
- An audit trail next to a run, with before and after for every change
- Anywhere undo needs to be honest about consequences: what goes with it, and what can't be undone

### When not to use

- Approving a change before it happens – use Approval Card or Review Center
- Where the time of one run goes – use Trace Waterfall
- A single decision the agent can't take alone – use Decision Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentLedger, type LedgerEntry } from "@/components/ui/agent-ledger-clean";

const entries: LedgerEntry[] = [
  { id: "price", action: "Changed price", target: "Pro plan", system: "Stripe", at: Date.now() - 120000,
    change: ["$29 / month", "$34 / month"] },
  { id: "deals", action: "Updated 212 deals", target: "Renewals in Q4", system: "HubSpot", at: Date.now() - 60000,
    change: ["$29 per seat", "$34 per seat"], dependsOn: ["price"] },
  { id: "email", action: "Sent email", target: "3,812 customers", system: "HubSpot", at: Date.now(),
    detail: "New price and the code LAUNCH20", dependsOn: ["price"], reversible: false },
];

export function Changes() {
  return <AgentLedger entries={entries} agent="Launch agent" onUndo={(ids) => revert(ids)} onRedo={(ids) => reapply(ids)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entries | `LedgerEntry[]` |  | { id, action, target?, system, icon?, at, change?, detail?, reversible?, dependsOn? } – every change, any order; newest shows first |
| change | `[before, after]` |  | Per entry – shown as before (struck) → after; or pass detail for a single line |
| dependsOn | `string[]` |  | Per entry – the changes it builds on; undoing one of those undoes this one too, if it can be |
| reversible | `boolean` | `true` | Per entry – false for things that can't be taken back (a sent email, a payout): no Undo, and "Can't undo" when something it builds on is undone |
| agent | `string` |  | Who made the changes, next to the title |
| now | `number` |  | The clock for "2m ago" (epoch ms) – defaults to now, kept fresh |
| undone / defaultUndone | `string[]` |  | Ids of undone changes, controlled or not |
| onUndo / onRedo | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | The change and its reversible dependents – revert or reapply them |
| pointAt | `string \| null` |  | Lights up a change and what builds on it, as if its Undo were pointed at – for a walkthrough |
| title | `string` | `"Ledger"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the Undo and Redo buttons; focusing Undo shows what goes with it
- Enter / Space: Undoes or redoes the focused change

### Accessibility

- The ledger is an ordered list labelled with its title, newest first
- Undo is labelled with the change and how many changes build on it; Redo with the change
- Before → after is plain text; the arrow is read as "to"

### Motion

- New changes open their row at the top – the panel grows smoothly – and then fade in
- Pointing at Undo lights up the change and everything built on it – "Also undone" in blue, "Can't undo" in amber
- Undo draws a line across each row, down the chain a beat after each other; the rows go quiet and their logos gray
- Rows never change height – the time, Undo, Redo and the flags all share one slot
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: under 480px the numbers move to a line of their own, the time drops the system's name and Undo / Redo shrink to round icon buttons
- On touch screens Undo and Redo show on every row, in place of the time
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every change every time – ids keep rows in place, new ids slide in
- at is epoch ms; pass now to drive "2m ago" yourself
- Undo calls onUndo with the ids to revert – actually reverting them in Stripe, GitHub etc. is up to you
- Mark irreversible changes with reversible: false – honesty about what can't be undone is the point
- Colors are variables on .ui-ldgc, e.g. --ui-ldgc-also-bg / --ui-ldgc-kept-bg
- The undo, redo and lock icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

- React 19

# Agent / Memory (Pro)

What your agent knows about you and your work – grouped by where it applies, each with where it came from and where it was used; a memory it recalls lights up while it works, and what it picks up on its own waits for your OK

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-memory
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-memory.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-memory`

### When to use

- Showing what an agent remembers about a person and their work – and letting them correct it, move it to a project or forget it
- Making memory visible while the agent works: which memory it just used, how often, and for what
- Asking for consent before the agent keeps something it picked up on its own

### When not to use

- Instructions that apply to every chat (a system prompt) – use Settings / Preferences
- Files and sources the agent can read – use Folders
- What waits on a decision – use Agent / Inbox

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentMemoryScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-memory";

export default function Page() {
  const [memories, setMemories] = useState(initialMemories);
  return (
    <AgentMemoryScreen
      memories={memories} // a newer usedAt plays the recall sheen on that row
      projects={["Northwind", "Platform", "Evalkit"]}
      onChange={(m) => api.updateMemory(m)}
      onForget={(id) => api.forget(id)}
      onRestore={(m, at) => api.restore(m)}
      onKeep={(id) => api.keep(id)}
      onCreate={(m) => api.remember(m.text, m.project)}
      onOpenSource={(m) => router.push(sourceUrl(m))}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| memories | `{ id; text; project?; source: { kind: "thread" \| "decision" \| "told" \| "file"; at; quote?; question?; file? }; uses?; usedAt?; usedIn?: { task; how; at }[]; review? }[]` |  | Every memory. Without a project it lists under About you and applies everywhere; source is where it came from – your words go in quote, a decision's question in question, a file's name in file; usedIn is where it was used, newest first; review lists it under To review until Keep. Pass a stable array (state): the screen follows it, and when a memory's usedAt moves on, its row lights up |
| projects | `string[]` | `in the order they appear` | The projects, in the order their groups show – and the choices for Applies to |
| defaultTab | `"saved" \| "review"` | `"saved"` | The list the screen opens with |
| defaultSelected | `string \| null` | `"friday"` | The memory open on the right when the screen starts |
| inboxCount | `number` | `5` | The Inbox count in the sidebar |
| onSelect | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when a memory is opened |
| onCreate | `(memory: AgentMemory) => void` |  | Called with a memory you added with Remember – source told, at the top of its group |
| onChange | `(memory: AgentMemory) => void` |  | Called with the whole memory when you edit its words or where it applies – and when Undo takes a Keep back (review: true) |
| onForget | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called once a forgotten (or not kept) memory's row has folded away |
| onRestore | `(memory: AgentMemory, index: number) => void` |  | Called when Undo brings it back – index is where it was in the list |
| onKeep | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with Keep on a memory under To review |
| onOpenSource | `(memory: AgentMemory) => void` |  | Called with Open next to where it came from – without it the screen calls onNavigate("Thread") or onNavigate("Agent Inbox") for a decision |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Fieldwork"` | The workspace in the sidebar |
| labels | `{ memory?; saved?; review?; reviewShort?; aboutYou?; everywhere?; remember?; keep?; dontKeep?; forget?; undo?; … }` |  | Labels, e.g. for a translation |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While your memories load: gray rows under gray group heads in the list and gray lines in the Memory panel, in the shape of the real ones (the shared Skeleton) |
| empty | `boolean` |  | No memories at all: Saved shows Nothing remembered yet with a sentence on where memories come from and a Remember button, To review shows Nothing to review, and the Memory panel shows nothing open |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- J / K: Next and previous row – anywhere in the screen, as long as you're not typing
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In the list: move through the group heads and rows (one Tab stop)
- Enter / Space: On a row: open the memory on the right. On a group's head: fold or unfold it
- ← / →: On a group's head: fold, unfold (→ on an open one steps into it). On a row, ← goes to its group's head
- Delete / Backspace: On a row: forget it – or, under To review, don't keep it; Undo brings it back for five seconds
- /: Search – Esc clears it, ↓ steps into the results
- N: Remember something new – Enter saves it and clears the line for the next one, Esc closes it
- Enter / Esc: In the panel's text: Enter saves your edit, Esc puts the old words back

### Accessibility

- The list is a role="tree": group heads are level-1 items with aria-expanded and their count, rows level-2 items; one Tab stop, the arrow keys move it
- Every row is named in full – what it knows, where it came from, how often and when it was last used – while the faint columns stay hidden from screen readers
- Keep and Don't keep on a row are a pointer's shortcuts; the keyboard reaches the same through Enter, then the panel's buttons, or Delete
- A polite live region says what happened: "Forgotten: …", "Kept – it uses this from now on"
- Text fields never get a ring – the caret and a firmer edge say it; rings show for the keyboard only and sit inset in the list and the panel
- Applies to is the App Shell's menu – every item with an icon, the chosen one checked
- Long text ends in '…' with the full text in a tooltip; right-to-left text reads in its own direction and still starts at the row's glyph

### Motion

- One moment: when the agent recalls a memory, a soft sheen with a glowing leading edge runs through its row, its glyph warms for a beat, the count ticks up and the time says now
- A new memory glides in at the top of its group; a forgotten one folds away to the side

- ↑ / ↓: On the focused step list: scroll through the finished steps
- Enter: Waiting, with the card focused: Allow
- Escape: Waiting, with the card focused: Decline – with an info card open, it closes the info card and puts the focus back on its row

- The card is a labelled region naming the agent, its state and its current step; the folded bar is a button with the same name
- The time strip is one image whose label lists each step with its time; the rows are a list, and the logos are decoration

### Motion

- A new step rolls into the well from below; the state tag rolls the same way
- A finished step drops into the top of the list and pushes the others down; past three rows the list scrolls, with a soft fade at the edge that has more

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component only draws – update state, steps, since, pausedFor and cost from your agent's events
- Fill tool, detail and output on each step – a click on it should answer what it did, with what, and how long it took

# Agent / Orchestration (Pro)

A live multi-agent run as a tree on a canvas – watch work flow to the running agents, follow every call in the trace below and open an agent for its tasks, context and cost

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-orchestration
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-orchestration.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-orchestration`

### When to use

- Watching a multi-agent run live – who started whom, what runs, what waits for you and what it costs so far
- Debugging a finished run: which agent took the time, which burned the tokens, where it failed and what retried

### When not to use

- One agent with a few tool calls – use Trace Waterfall or Agent Run
- Building the flow by hand – use Workflow Builder

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentOrchestrationScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-orchestration";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <AgentOrchestrationScreen
      project="Market research"
      runId={run.id}
      agents={run.agents}
      events={run.events}
      elapsed={run.elapsed}
      onResolve={(agent, answer) => api.answer(run.id, agent.id, answer)}
      onRunControl={(action) => api.control(run.id, action)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Northwind"` | The workspace in the sidebar |
| project | `string` | `"Market research"` | Project in the path |
| runId | `string` | `"run_8f3a2c"` | The run in the path – its menu lists earlier runs, Compare, Copy run ID and Download trace |
| agents | `{ id; parent?; name; role; task; model; maker?; mark?; tools?; status; start?; end?; tokensIn?; tokensOut?; tokensCached?; cost?; rate?; ask?; error?; retryOf?; tasks?; context? }[]` |  | Every agent – the one without a parent is the orchestrator on top. status is queued, running, waiting, done, failed or stopped; start and end in ms from the start of the run; cost is its own, the branch is summed up; rate { tokens, cost } per second keeps a running agent ticking; ask is what a waiting agent asks you, error what failed, retryOf the agent it retries; tasks are the items of its task list |
| tools | `{ id; label; icon }[]` |  | The tools agents call – the icons are the tiles on the cards and the rows in the panel |
| spans | `{ id; agent; name; kind: "agent" \| "llm" \| "tool"; start; end?; status; detail? }[]` |  | The trace's bars – made up from each agent's tasks when left out (an LLM call, then the tool call, per task) |
| events | `{ id; at; agent; type: "start" \| "handoff" \| "tool" \| "approval" \| "error" \| "retry" \| "done"; text }[]` |  | What happened – each one shows under Events once the run's clock reaches its at |
| elapsed | `number` | `94000` | How far the run is when the screen opens, in ms – the figures in agents describe this moment |
| live | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the clock runs on – running agents keep adding time, tokens and cost; false opens it paused |
| defaultTab | `"Trace" \| "Tokens & cost" \| "Events"` | `"Trace"` | The run panel's tab when the screen opens |
| onSelect | `(agent: AoAgent \| null) => void` |  | Called when an agent's panel opens, and with null when it closes |
| onResolve | `(agent: AoAgent, answer: "approve" \| "reject") => void` |  | An answer to an agent that waits for you – Approve lets it go on, Reject stops its branch |
| onRunControl | `(action: "start" \| "pause" \| "resume" \| "stop" \| "restart") => void` |  | Start run (in the empty state), Pause run, Resume, Stop and Run again on the top right |
| labels | `{ start?; pause?; resume?; stop?; restart? }` |  | Labels, e.g. for a translation |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While the run loads: gray cards on the canvas in the tree's shape – the same sizes, places and gray lines – gray rows in the run panel's open tab and no figures in its head (the shared Skeleton); the clock waits and nothing flows, then the run starts from elapsed |
| empty | `boolean` |  | A run that hasn't started: an empty canvas with one centered “Start the run” and a Start run button (also on the top right, in place of Pause and Stop), the run panel's own empty states and a clock that waits at zero |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Sidebar → path bar → run controls → canvas (one stop) → toolbar → run panel (resize edge, tabs, fold, the open tab's rows – one stop) → the agent's panel when open (close, tabs, the tab's content)
- ↑ / ↓: Canvas: ↑ the agent that started it, ↓ the first one it started – on a leaf, the nearest card below; with the panel open it follows
- ← / →: Canvas: the agents beside it with the same parent – past the last one, the nearest card that way. Toolbar: the next or previous button
- Alt ← / Alt → / Alt ↑ / Alt ↓: Canvas: pan the view without a pointer (Alt Shift: further)
- Home / End: Canvas: the orchestrator, the last agent. Toolbar: its first and last button. Trace, Tokens & cost and Events: the first and last row
- Enter / Space: Open the focused agent's panel (focus moves into it); on a row in the run panel, open that row's agent – the focus stays on the row, on a phone it moves into the sheet
- → / ←: Trace: → shows an agent's LLM and tool calls, then steps onto the first; ← folds them, then goes to the agent that started it; ← on a call goes back to its agent
- Enter / Space / ↓: Path bar: open the project or run menu – the arrows and Home / End move in it, Esc closes it with the focus back on its button
- + / - / ⇧1: Zoom in, zoom out, fit to view
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: On the run panel's top edge: resize it (Shift: bigger steps), Home / End for the smallest / largest
- Esc: Close the agent's panel – focus goes back where it came from: the card, or the trace, cost or event row it was opened from

### Accessibility

- The canvas is a tree and one Tab stop (a roving tabindex): the focused agent – or the orchestrator – takes Tab, the arrows follow the tree, so 40 agents are never 40 stops
- Every card is a labelled tree item that says its name, role, status and who started it, its place among the agents with the same parent and whether it started any; the opened one is selected
- The run panel's tabs and the agent panel's tabs are one stop each with arrows; Trace is a tree, Tokens & cost a table with row headers, Events an ordered list – each list one Tab stop, every row named in full (time, agent, kind, text)
- The agent panel's content is a Tab stop of its own, so a long task list scrolls from the keyboard
- Status always comes with words – Running, Needs you, Done, Failed, Queued, Stopped – the colour only repeats it; the error count on Events is read as 'Events, 1 error'
- The focus is never dropped: Stop and Run again swap their buttons and the focus moves to the one that takes the place; an answered approval moves it to the panel's open tab while the toast says what happened; the clock's ticks and new events leave it where it is
- Every control shows the accent focus ring for the keyboard only (:focus-visible) – inset where a scroller would cut it, and a focused row never hides under the trace's axis or the table's head; toolbar buttons have labels and a tooltip with their shortcut
- On phones the agent's panel is a sheet that takes the focus however it opens and keeps it inside until it closes
- Long names, roles and translated control labels end in '…' with the full text in a tooltip; names in right-to-left scripts read in their own direction; tokens and durations roll up (84.2K, 1m 34s, 1d 3h); a figure that was left out shows '–', never 0

### Motion

- Toward every running agent a gradient keeps flowing along its connector, from the parent to the child – the one motion on the canvas
- In the trace, running bars grow with the clock, a sheen sweeps along them and their leading edge glows; the now line moves with them; new bars grow in from their start
- The dot grid pans and zooms with the canvas – its spacing follows the zoom, the dots keep their size
- Opening an agent fades the others and glides the view so its card stays clear of the panel – never zooms; the panel slides in from the right
- New events rise in at the top of Events; figures change in place, in fixed widths, so nothing jumps
- Pause freezes the clock, the flows and the sheens where they are
- With prefers-reduced-motion there is no flow along the connectors, no sheen and nothing slides

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- The tree opens at 80% or more and starts at the top when it's taller than the canvas; Fit to view never zooms past 100%
- Pan by dragging, with a plain wheel or two fingers; zoom with the toolbar, ⌘/Ctrl + wheel or a pinch. A plain wheel pans right away when the canvas fills a page that doesn't scroll; in a longer page, once you've clicked into it
- The run panel stays open under the canvas – drag its top edge, or fold it to a slim bar; the canvas keeps its zoom and place either way
- Below 640px the agent's panel becomes a sheet from the bottom, the run controls and tabs turn into icons, the trace and the cost table keep the columns that matter; touch targets grow to 36px
- Beside the open panel, when the top bar runs short, the run controls turn into icons too, so the path keeps its words
- The trace's axis grows with the run – seconds, minutes, then hours and days – and keeps as many ticks as it has room for
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19

# Agent / Permissions (Pro)

What your agent may do without asking – one choice on top (Careful, Balanced, Hands-off) said in plain words, the apps it works in, the red lines that always ask, and each app with its actions grouped Reads, Changes, Needs care

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-permissions
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-permissions.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-permissions`

### When to use

- Letting people decide what an agent may do on its own – one choice for everything first, then app by app and action by action
- Showing in plain words how autonomous an agent is: what it does on its own, what it asks about, what it never does
- Red lines that must always ask, whatever the choice above

### When not to use

- Answering one request in the moment – use Permission Request or Approval Gates
- What the agent knows about you – use Agent / Memory
- Connecting apps – use Integrations

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentPermissionsScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-permissions";

export default function Page() {
  const [rules, setRules] = useState(initialRules);
  return (
    <AgentPermissionsScreen
      apps={connectedApps}
      rules={rules}
      onChange={(rule) => {
        setRules((l) => l.map((r) => (r.id === rule.id ? rule : r)));
        api.savePermission(rule.id, rule.level, rule.limit);
      }}
      onPreset={(preset) => analytics.track("preset", { preset })}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| apps | `{ id; name; account?; icon? }[]` | `seven sample apps` | The connected apps, in the order their groups show – icon is a Hugeicons icon, shown in the app's color |

# Agent Plan, clean style (Pro)

An agent's step-by-step plan to review before it runs – rename, drag to reorder, remove or add steps, then watch each one run with live timers and retry from a failed step

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-plan
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-plan-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-plan-clean`

### When to use

- An agent is about to do several things in a row and people should agree to the plan first
- Long or expensive runs (tool calls, emails, writes) where a wrong order or an extra step costs real time
- Showing the same plan as it executes – which step is running, how long each took, where it failed

### When not to use

- A single action that needs a yes or no – use Approval Card
- Model reasoning without editable steps – use Thinking State
- A user's own onboarding checklist – use Progress Tracker

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AgentPlan, type PlanStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-plan-clean";

export function PlanReview({ plan }: { plan: PlanStep[] }) {
  const [steps, setSteps] = useState(plan);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"draft" | "running" | "done">("draft");

  return (
    <AgentPlan
      title="Prepare the Q3 board update"
      estimate="~2 min"
      steps={steps}
      status={status}
      onChange={setSteps}
      onRun={(final) => {
        setStatus("running");
        agent.run(final); // stream step updates back into setSteps
      }}
      onCancel={() => agent.discard()}
      onRetry={(id) => agent.retryFrom(id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `PlanStep[]` |  | Controlled steps: { id, title, detail?, tool?, status?, duration?, error? }. Pair with onChange |
| defaultSteps | `PlanStep[]` | `[]` | Initial steps when uncontrolled – edits are kept inside the component |
| status | `"draft" \| "running" \| "done"` | `"draft"` | Review and edit, executing, or finished. Editing is only possible in draft |
| onChange | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | Every edit during review: rename, remove, reorder, add |
| onRun | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | "Run plan" pressed – gets the steps in their final order. Set status to "running" here. Also shows "Run again" in the card's last row once done |
| onCancel | `() => void` |  | Shows a Cancel button next to Run plan |
| onRetry | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | Shows "Retry from here" under failed steps |
| title | `string` |  | The goal of the plan, shown as the heading and used as the list's label |
| estimate | `string` |  | Estimated run time shown in review, e.g. "~2 min" |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between steps, their remove buttons, the Add step field and the actions
- ↑ / ↓: Moves focus to the previous or next step
- Alt / ↑ / ↓: Moves the focused step up or down
- Enter: Renames the focused step; Enter again saves. In Add step: adds the step at the end and keeps the field ready for the next one
- Esc: Cancels a rename
- Delete: Removes the focused step

### Accessibility

- The steps are an ordered list labelled with the plan's title; each step is focusable in review and describes its shortcuts
- Moves, renames, removals and additions are announced in a polite live region ("Moved 'Draft the board memo' to position 3 of 5")
- While running, each step carries its status as text, the active one has aria-current="step", and finished or failed steps are announced
- The drag grip is pointer-only; Alt+arrow keys do the same from the keyboard
- Icon buttons are labelled, focus rings show on keyboard focus only, and the folded-away Add step is inert while running

### Motion

- Reordering is live: the dragged step follows the pointer, the others slide aside, and everything settles with a FLIP glide – also for keyboard moves and order changes from props
- Removed steps collapse and the list closes the gap; added steps fade up into place
- Numbers in a hairline ring turn into a ray spinner, then into a white check on a blue fill that draws itself; the progress line fills blue segment by segment
- Add step folds away when the plan starts, and the card's last row swaps its actions for the run's status – a shimmering "Running · 2 of 5" with the elapsed time, then "Done in 14s"
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the spinner stands still

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 440px; titles and details wrap, tool chips stay on one line
- Below 400px the footer hint drops away, below 340px gutters tighten – works down to 320px
- On touch screens the grip and remove button are always visible
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step a stable id – reorder animations, timers and announcements follow the id, not the index
- Leave duration out to have it measured from when a step turned active; pass it when your agent reports its own timing
- On retry, reset the failed step and everything after it to "pending" and keep status "running"
- Run the steps onRun hands you, not the original proposal – the user may have renamed, removed or reordered them

### Requirements

- React 19

# Agent Queue, clean style (Pro)

The work waiting for your agents, and how fast it moves – jobs drop into a live queue, glide into free worker slots as growing bars and land in Done or Failed, while a depth chart shows the backlog build up when a rate limit pauses the workers and drain when they resume

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-queue
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-queue-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-queue-clean`

### When to use

- A job queue in an agent product – how many tasks wait, which worker runs what, and how fast the backlog moves
- Watching backpressure live: a provider rate-limits, the workers pause, the queue builds up and drains again
- An ops view next to your agents where people can pause the queue, add or remove workers, or move a job to the front

### When not to use

- Several agents side by side over time – use Agent Lanes
- Handing work to a specific agent by hand – use Delegate Board
- A list of background tasks with their results – use Agent Inbox
- Where the time and money of one run go – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentQueue, type QueueJob, type QueueWorker } from "@/components/ui/agent-queue-clean";

const workers: QueueWorker[] = [
  { id: "w1", name: "Sonnet 5.5" },
  { id: "w2", name: "GPT-6 Sol" },
];

const jobs: QueueJob[] = [
  { id: "j1", name: "Summarize ticket #4821", kind: "llm", status: "running", worker: "w1",
    enqueuedAt: t0, startedAt: t0 + 1200, progress: 0.4 },
  { id: "j2", name: "Embed 240 docs", kind: "tool", status: "queued", enqueuedAt: t0 + 800 },
  { id: "j3", name: "Draft reply – Acme", kind: "llm", status: "queued", priority: "high", enqueuedAt: t0 + 2100 },
];

export function Jobs() {
  // Times are on one clock (epoch ms here) – without now, the component ticks Date.now while there is work
  return <AgentQueue jobs={jobs} workers={workers} backpressure={20} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| jobs | `QueueJob[]` |  | { id, name, kind, status, enqueuedAt, priority?, startedAt?, endedAt?, worker?, progress?, estimate?, attempt?, maxAttempts?, detail?, icon?, error? } – waiting, running and recently finished jobs |
| kind | `"llm" \| "tool" \| "agent" \| "human"` |  | Per job – picks its tint: LLM calls violet, tool calls teal, sub-agents slate, human review blue |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per job – a job that goes from running back to queued with a higher attempt shows as a retry |
| priority | `"high" \| "normal" \| "low"` | `"normal"` | Per job – a high one glides past the others to the front |
| progress / estimate | `number` |  | Per job – 0–1 while it runs, or the expected run time in ms to estimate it |
| workers | `QueueWorker[]` |  | { id, name, detail?, icon? } – the slots; their number is the concurrency |
| now | `number` |  | The clock, on the same scale as the job times – without it, the component keeps its own (Date.now) |
| rateLimits | `{ from, until, label? }[]` |  | Stretches when the provider rate-limits – while one is active the running jobs pause in amber with a countdown |
| paused / onPausedChange | `boolean / (paused) => void` |  | The queue is paused; the handler shows a Pause/Resume button |
| onConcurrencyChange | `(workers: number) => void` |  | Shows a – N + stepper for the number of workers |
| minConcurrency / maxConcurrency | `number` | `1 / 8` | The stepper's range |
| backpressure | `number` |  | A depth that means trouble – a dashed line on the chart; above it Waiting turns amber |
| window | `number` | `120000` | How far back the depth chart looks, in ms |
| totals | `{ done?, failed? }` |  | Counts since the start, when jobs only holds the recent ones |
| openId / defaultOpenId | `string \| null` | `null` | The job whose card is pinned, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null, job?: QueueJob) => void` |  | A job's card was pinned or closed |
| onPromote / onCancel | `(job: QueueJob) => void` |  | Show "Move to front" and "Cancel" in a pinned card |
| title / name | `string` | `"Queue"` | Heading, and the queue's name muted next to it |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the jobs (one job is in the tab order), then to the card's buttons
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: Walks through the running jobs, slot by slot, then the queue from the front; Home and End jump to the ends
- Enter / Space: Pins or closes the focused job's card
- Esc: Closes the card

### Accessibility

- Every job is a real button, labelled with its name, kind, how long it waited or ran, its place in line, priority and attempt
- Roving focus – only one job is in the tab order, so the flow is a single stop
- The pinned card is a dialog with a close button; Esc closes it and returns focus to the job
- Rate limits, their end, failures, retries and crossing the backpressure line are announced in a polite live region
- The chart is an image with a text summary: how many wait now, the peak, the average and the rate-limited stretches
- Pause is a toggle button with aria-pressed; the stepper's buttons say what they do and the count is announced

### Motion

- New jobs drop in at the back of the queue; a high-priority job lands at the back first, then glides past the others
- The front job moves into a free worker and becomes a bar that grows with its progress, with a sheen and a glowing front edge
- A finished job turns green for a beat and flies into Done; a failed one shakes red and goes to Failed – or slides back into the queue with a retry badge
- During a rate limit the bars stop and turn amber, a countdown runs out; the chart line climbs, then falls as the queue drains
- The numbers ease to their new value and the chart's scale glides when it changes – one frame loop that sleeps when nothing moves or the queue is off-screen
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears in place

### Responsive

- Built on a container query and the measured width: wide, the flow runs left to right – queue, workers, Done and Failed
- Under 600px the flow stacks: queue on top, the workers below (just their marks, the rail gets the room), Done and Failed side by side
- The four numbers wrap to two columns; under 440px Pause and the stepper get a row of their own
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole list every time something changes – ids keep jobs in place and every change glides
- All times are on one clock – epoch ms, or your own (then pass now)
- A retry is the same id going back to "queued" with attempt + 1, a new enqueuedAt and no startedAt or worker
- The chart is computed from the jobs: keep finished jobs for as long as window, or pass totals and accept a shorter history
- Pass progress while a job runs for honest bars; otherwise give an estimate
- Colors are variables on .ui-agqc, e.g. --ui-agqc-llm-bg / --ui-agqc-llm-edge for LLM calls
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

import { AgentRecap, type RecapEvent } from "@/components/ui/agent-recap-clean";

  { id: "sync", kind: "failed", at: "2026-10-30T03:02", title: "Contact sync to the CRM",
    detail: "Token expired after 1,284 of 3,900 contacts" },
  { id: "tickets", kind: "done", at: "2026-10-29T19:05", title: "Answered support tickets", count: 38 },
];

export function Morning() {

}

| since / until | `Date \| string \| number` |  | When the person left, and now – the chart runs between them; until defaults to the time it renders |
| onAction | `(event, action: "primary" \| "review") => void \| Promise` |  | The main action (Approve, Retry …) or Review. Return a promise and the row shows it working until it settles – a rejected one puts the row back |

| title | `string` | `"While you were away"` | Heading |

| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

- Tab: Moves through the actions card by card – Review, then the main action (or Undo / Redo)

- A section named by its heading; each lane has a heading with its count – of everything in it, also beyond the limit

# Agent Router, clean style (Pro)

A router agent sorting incoming requests to the agents that handle them – the request coming in on top, the router under it and the agents side by side at the bottom, each with its task queue below, all as Agent Crew's cards on its soft blue connectors – people sit off to the right, a fading line with a Human tag. A light runs into the router, which reads the request and settles on an agent with a confidence; the light runs on, the agent's card lights up in its color and the request drops into its queue. Unsure, it hands the request to a person. A click opens why it went where it went, with every agent's score and a way to send it elsewhere

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-router
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-router-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-router-clean`

### When to use

- A support inbox, a help desk or any queue where an agent decides which agent – or person – takes each request
- Showing that routing happens and why: the confidence, every agent's score and the reason, one click away
- Live: requests come in, the router reads them and hands them on while you watch

### When not to use

- A lead splitting one task among sub-agents – use Agent Crew or Agent Tree
- One run, message by message – use Agent Sequence
- The requests themselves, to read and answer – use Agent Inbox
- A task passed on from agent to agent – use Agent Handoff

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentRouter, type RouterAgent, type RouterRequest } from "@/components/ui/agent-router-clean";

const router: RouterAgent = { id: "router", name: "Router", model: "Claude Haiku", status: "active", activity: "Reading “Refund for order #4821”" };

const agents: RouterAgent[] = [
  { id: "billing", name: "Billing", model: "Claude Sonnet", status: "active", activity: "Refunding order #4821", load: 0.45, queue: 2 },
  { id: "tech", name: "Tech support", model: "Claude Sonnet", status: "idle", load: 0.3, queue: 1 },
  { id: "human", name: "Support lead", model: "Human", human: true },
];

const requests: RouterRequest[] = [
  { id: "r1", title: "Refund for order #4821", from: "maria@northwind.io", channel: "email", preview: "I was charged twice…", status: "routed", to: "billing", confidence: 0.94, scores: { billing: 0.94, tech: 0.12 }, reason: "A double charge – billing." },
];

export function Inbox() {
  return <AgentRouter title="Support inbox" router={router} agents={agents} requests={requests} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| router | `RouterAgent` |  | The router itself, in the middle – { id, name, model?, status?, activity? }; its bar shows how sure it is about the request it reads or last sent on |
| agents | `RouterAgent[]` |  | Who it sends requests to – { id, name, model?, status?, activity?, load?, queue?, human?, color?, logo? }. Agents get their pixel mark in a color of the palette, a person (human: true) the full square in ink and an orange glow when a request reaches them |
| requests | `RouterRequest[]` |  | Newest first – { id, title, from?, channel?, icon?, preview?, status, to?, confidence?, scores?, reason?, tags? } |
| tags | `(string \| { label, color? })[]` |  | Per request – up to three small tags on its card in a task queue, gray or tinted with their own color |
| status | `"new" \| "routing" \| "routed" \| "escalated" \| "done"` |  | Per request – routing runs the light into the router and shimmers its line; routed or escalated with to runs it on to that agent, whose card lights up in its color |
| channel / icon | `"email" \| "chat" \| "ticket" \| "call" \| "slack" \| ReactNode` |  | Where the request came in – its icon in the card's tile; icon puts your own there |
| confidence / scores / reason | `number / Record<string, number> / string` |  | How sure the router is (0–1), every agent's score and why – shown on the card and when it is open |
| layout | `"lanes" \| "columns"` |  | lanes (default): the request coming in on top, the router under it, the agents side by side at the bottom, each with its task queue below as in Agent Handoff – a request drops into the queue when the light reaches its agent. People (human: true) get no card: a line out of the router's right side fades out, with a Human tag on it that counts what waits for them. columns: requests, router and agents side by side |
| modelLogo | `ReactNode` |  | Per agent and on the router – the model maker's logo, before the model's name (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini …) |
| max | `number` |  | How many requests show on the left in columns – 4 by default |
| onReroute | `(request, agentId) => void` |  | With it, an open request lists every agent as a button to send it there – update the request's to and the light runs to the new agent |
| onSelect | `(request) => void` |  | A request was opened |
| title | `string` |  | The header's name, with how many are routing, need you and are routed |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Keyboard

- Tab: One stop for the whole map
- ← / → / ↑ / ↓: Walk the cards – the request on top, the router, each agent and its task queue
- Home / End: First or last card
- Enter / Space: On a request: opens why it went where it went. On an agent: keeps its requests clear and fades the rest
- Esc: Closes the open request, or clears the agent you look at

### Accessibility

- Every card reads what it is and where it stands – "Refund for order #4821, from maria@northwind.io: Routed, to Billing, 94% sure"
- The open request is a dialog; with onReroute its agents are buttons that say which one it went to
- A polite live region says where each request went
- The connectors and the light are decoration – everything they show is in the cards' labels
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only (:focus-visible), in light and dark

### Motion

- Agent Crew's light runs along a request's connector into the router, then on to the agent it goes to – clear in the middle, fading at both ends; in lanes the request then drops into that agent's task queue
- The card it reaches lights up with the Gradient Floor in that agent's color, rising from the edge the light came in by
- The router's pixel mark twinkles and its line shimmers while it reads; the confidence bar fills as it decides
- Cards rise in and the connectors draw themselves; with prefers-reduced-motion everything changes at once and the light stays off

### Responsive

- Lanes (wide): the request on top, the router, every agent side by side with its task queue – the queues fade out at the bottom and keep one height
- Columns (wide): requests, router and agents side by side, joined by connectors with rounded bends
- Narrow: one column – the requests indented above the router, the agents hanging below it as in Agent Crew; the light runs the same way
- Every card keeps its rows – a long subject, sender or line ends in … with the full text on hover
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give requests and agents stable ids – the light and the open request track them by it
- Move a request through new → routing → routed (or escalated) – each step runs the light once
- Keep titles short – a subject; put the first line of the message in preview
- Route unsure requests to an agent with human: true and status escalated

- React 19

# Agent Sequence, clean style (Pro)

One agent run as a sequence diagram – a column for you, every agent and every tool, and each message an arrow from one lifeline to the next: calls solid, replies dashed, every label a tag in its line's color, a bar on the lifeline while a participant works, parallel and retried messages in labelled frames; new messages draw themselves across with a light at the tip, and a click on a participant or a message opens its card

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-sequence
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-sequence-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-sequence-clean`

### When to use

- Showing who talked to whom in one agent run – you, the agents and the tools they called, message by message
- Debugging a multi-agent run: which call waited on which reply, what ran in parallel, where a retry happened and what failed
- A live view of a run as it happens – every new message draws itself in

### When not to use

- How long each step took on a time axis – use Trace Waterfall
- Many agents over a long stretch of time, lane by lane – use Agent Lanes
- The structure of a crew rather than its messages – use Agent Crew or Agent Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentSequence, type SeqMessage, type SeqParticipant } from "@/components/ui/agent-sequence-clean";

const participants: SeqParticipant[] = [
  { id: "you", name: "You", kind: "person" },
  { id: "lead", name: "Lead", kind: "agent", model: "Claude Opus" },
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", kind: "agent", model: "Claude Sonnet" },
  { id: "github", name: "GitHub", kind: "tool", logo: <GitHubLogo /> },
];

const messages: SeqMessage[] = [
  { id: "m1", from: "you", to: "lead", label: "Fix the checkout crash", at: 0 },
  { id: "m2", from: "lead", to: "lead", label: "Plan: find, patch, preview", at: 2_000 },
  { id: "m3", from: "lead", to: "research", label: "Find the cause", at: 3_000 },
  { id: "m4", from: "research", to: "github", label: 'search_code("emptyCart")', at: 5_000 },
  { id: "m5", from: "github", to: "research", label: "3 matches", kind: "reply", replyTo: "m4", at: 6_000 },
  { id: "m6", from: "research", to: "lead", label: "Null total in cart.ts:42", kind: "reply", replyTo: "m3", at: 11_000 },
];

export function Run() {
  return <AgentSequence title="Fix the checkout crash" participants={participants} messages={messages} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| participants | `SeqParticipant[]` |  | A column each, left to right, with a dashed lifeline – a chip on top opens its card |
| SeqParticipant.kind | `"person" \| "agent" \| "tool"` | `"agent"` | A person gets the full pixel mark in the ink color, an agent its own pixel mark – twinkling while it works – a tool its logo |
| SeqParticipant.logo / color | `ReactNode / string` |  | A logo instead of the pixel mark; the agent's color – by default the first agent is blue and the others take the palette in order |
| SeqParticipant.model / description | `string / string` |  | In its card: the model as a tag, and a line on what it does |
| messages | `SeqMessage[]` |  | In order, top to bottom – each new id draws itself across with a light at its tip and lands with a small ripple |
| SeqMessage.kind / replyTo | `"call" \| "reply" / string` | `"call"` | A call is a solid line and the receiver works – a bar on its lifeline – until a reply with its id as replyTo comes back as a dashed line. From and to the same: a loop back to its own lifeline |
| SeqMessage.status | `"failed" \| "waiting"` |  | failed is red with a small cross where it lands; waiting – it needs a person – is amber |
| SeqMessage.at | `number` |  | When it was sent, ms since the run started – shown in the gutter on the left, and used for the timing in the cards |
| SeqMessage.frame | `string` |  | Messages next to each other with the same frame sit in one white box with it as a tag – "par", "retry", "loop ×3" |
| SeqMessage.detail | `string` |  | In its card: what exactly went along – the arguments of a call, a result, an error |
| title | `string` |  | The header's name, with how many work or failed, how many messages and the run's time |
| running | `boolean` | `true` | false once the run is over – open bars stop shimmering and marks stop twinkling |
| times | `boolean` |  | The time gutter – by default there while no message has come in yet and whenever one has a time, so the first one doesn't push the diagram over; false hides it |
| onSelect | `(message \| null) => void` |  | A click or Enter on a message – its card opens; null when it closes |
| formatTime | `(ms) => string` | `m:ss` | Formats the gutter and the cards' times |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the participants, then into the messages – one stop for all of them
- ↑ / ↓: Walks the messages
- Home / End: The first, the last message
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes a message's card – a participant's opens with Enter or Space on its chip
- Esc: Closes the card – focus goes back to what opened it

### Accessibility

- The messages are an ordered list; each is named with sender, receiver, text, status and time – "Researcher to GitHub: search_code(\"emptyCart\"), 0:05" – and says it opens a dialog
- Participants are buttons; their cards and the messages' cards are dialogs named after them, with a close button reachable by Tab
- A polite live region reads each new message
- Colors never carry meaning alone: replies are dashed, failures say "Failed" and carry a cross, frames say what they are
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only, in light and dark – outside on the chips, inside on the message rows

### Motion

- A new message draws itself across from the sender with a soft light at its tip and lands with a small ripple; its tag rises in
- Each line fades from faint where it leaves to full where it lands, so it reads which way it goes; a loop fades the same way as it turns back
- The receiver's bar grows down its lifeline; a light sweeps down bars that are still open and working agents' marks twinkle
- Cards pop in under a participant, or beside a message's tag
- Reduced motion turns it all off – messages simply appear

### Responsive

- Columns share the width evenly; below about 100px a column (84px on phones) the diagram scrolls sideways instead of squeezing, with a soft edge on the side there's more
- Phones get a narrower time gutter and smaller times; touch screens a bigger target around each participant and the close button
- Rows are fixed, so a new message never moves the ones above it – the diagram only grows down
- Labels are solid tags in their line's color that read over every line and bar they cross; a long one ends in … with the full text on hover and in its card
- Cards float in the top layer and stay inside the diagram – a message's opens on the left when there's no room on the right, or below it on a phone; they follow their anchor on scroll and close once it's scrolled out of the diagram
- An agent talking to itself on the last column gets its text on the left of its lifeline
- Broken data holds: messages to or from someone who isn't a participant are left out, a time that isn't a number shows none, a negative one reads 0:00, runs past an hour widen the gutter for 1:02:05, an empty label draws just the line, and a reply to a call that doesn't exist is still drawn
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every participant and message a stable id – messages draw in once per id
- Pass messages in the order they happened; set replyTo on replies so the receiver's bar ends and the cards can say how long it took
- Keep labels short – a tool call with its main argument, a result in a few words – and put the rest in detail
- Four to six participants fit 760px comfortably; more scroll sideways
- Colors are --ui-asqc-* variables on the root; the first agent is --ui-asqc-blue

### Requirements

- React 19

# Agent Sequence (Pro)

One agent run as a sequence diagram – a column for you, every agent and every tool, and each message an arrow from one lifeline to the next: calls solid, replies dashed, every label a tag in its line's color, a bar on the lifeline while a participant works, parallel and retried messages in labelled frames; new messages draw themselves across with a light at the tip, and a click on a participant or a message opens its card

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-sequence
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install, classic style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-sequence.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Install, clean style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-sequence-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key) – lands as `agent-sequence-clean.tsx`, import from `@/components/ui/agent-sequence-clean` – its docs: `agent-sequence-clean.md`
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-sequence`

### When to use

- Showing who talked to whom in one agent run – you, the agents and the tools they called, message by message
- Debugging a multi-agent run: which call waited on which reply, what ran in parallel, where a retry happened and what failed
- A live view of a run as it happens – every new message draws itself in

### When not to use

- How long each step took on a time axis – use Trace Waterfall
- Many agents over a long stretch of time, lane by lane – use Agent Lanes
- The structure of a crew rather than its messages – use Agent Crew or Agent Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentSequence, type SeqMessage, type SeqParticipant } from "@/components/ui/agent-sequence";

const participants: SeqParticipant[] = [
  { id: "you", name: "You", kind: "person" },
  { id: "lead", name: "Lead", kind: "agent", model: "Claude Opus" },
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", kind: "agent", model: "Claude Sonnet" },
  { id: "github", name: "GitHub", kind: "tool", logo: <GitHubLogo /> },
];

const messages: SeqMessage[] = [
  { id: "m1", from: "you", to: "lead", label: "Fix the checkout crash", at: 0 },
  { id: "m2", from: "lead", to: "lead", label: "Plan: find, patch, preview", at: 2_000 },
  { id: "m3", from: "lead", to: "research", label: "Find the cause", at: 3_000 },
  { id: "m4", from: "research", to: "github", label: 'search_code("emptyCart")', at: 5_000 },
  { id: "m5", from: "github", to: "research", label: "3 matches", kind: "reply", replyTo: "m4", at: 6_000 },
  { id: "m6", from: "research", to: "lead", label: "Null total in cart.ts:42", kind: "reply", replyTo: "m3", at: 11_000 },
];

export function Run() {
  return <AgentSequence title="Fix the checkout crash" participants={participants} messages={messages} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| participants | `SeqParticipant[]` |  | A column each, left to right, with a dashed lifeline – a chip on top opens its card |
| SeqParticipant.kind | `"person" \| "agent" \| "tool"` | `"agent"` | A person gets the full pixel mark in the ink color, an agent its own pixel mark – twinkling while it works – a tool its logo |
| SeqParticipant.logo / color | `ReactNode / string` |  | A logo instead of the pixel mark; the agent's color – by default the first agent is blue and the others take the palette in order |
| SeqParticipant.model / description | `string / string` |  | In its card: the model as a tag, and a line on what it does |
| messages | `SeqMessage[]` |  | In order, top to bottom – each new id draws itself across with a light at its tip and lands with a small ripple |
| SeqMessage.kind / replyTo | `"call" \| "reply" / string` | `"call"` | A call is a solid line and the receiver works – a bar on its lifeline – until a reply with its id as replyTo comes back as a dashed line. From and to the same: a loop back to its own lifeline |
| SeqMessage.status | `"failed" \| "waiting"` |  | failed is red with a small cross where it lands; waiting – it needs a person – is amber |
| SeqMessage.at | `number` |  | When it was sent, ms since the run started – shown in the gutter on the left, and used for the timing in the cards |
| SeqMessage.frame | `string` |  | Messages next to each other with the same frame sit in one white box with it as a tag – "par", "retry", "loop ×3" |
| SeqMessage.detail | `string` |  | In its card: what exactly went along – the arguments of a call, a result, an error |
| title | `string` |  | The header's name, with how many work or failed, how many messages and the run's time |
| running | `boolean` | `true` | false once the run is over – open bars stop shimmering and marks stop twinkling |
| times | `boolean` |  | The time gutter – by default there while no message has come in yet and whenever one has a time, so the first one doesn't push the diagram over; false hides it |
| onSelect | `(message \| null) => void` |  | A click or Enter on a message – its card opens; null when it closes |
| formatTime | `(ms) => string` | `m:ss` | Formats the gutter and the cards' times |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the participants, then into the messages – one stop for all of them
- ↑ / ↓: Walks the messages
- Home / End: The first, the last message
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes a message's card – a participant's opens with Enter or Space on its chip
- Esc: Closes the card – focus goes back to what opened it

### Accessibility

- The messages are an ordered list; each is named with sender, receiver, text, status and time – "Researcher to GitHub: search_code(\"emptyCart\"), 0:05" – and says it opens a dialog
- Participants are buttons; their cards and the messages' cards are dialogs named after them, with a close button reachable by Tab
- A polite live region reads each new message
- Colors never carry meaning alone: replies are dashed, failures say "Failed" and carry a cross, frames say what they are
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only, in light and dark – outside on the chips, inside on the message rows

### Motion

- A new message draws itself across from the sender with a soft light at its tip and lands with a small ripple; its tag rises in
- Each line fades from faint where it leaves to full where it lands, so it reads which way it goes; a loop fades the same way as it turns back
- The receiver's bar grows down its lifeline; a light sweeps down bars that are still open and working agents' marks twinkle
- Cards pop in under a participant, or beside a message's tag
- Reduced motion turns it all off – messages simply appear

### Responsive

- Columns share the width evenly; below about 100px a column (84px on phones) the diagram scrolls sideways instead of squeezing, with a soft edge on the side there's more
- Phones get a narrower time gutter and smaller times; touch screens a bigger target around each participant and the close button
- Rows are fixed, so a new message never moves the ones above it – the diagram only grows down
- Labels are solid tags in their line's color that read over every line and bar they cross; a long one ends in … with the full text on hover and in its card
- Cards float in the top layer and stay inside the diagram – a message's opens on the left when there's no room on the right, or below it on a phone; they follow their anchor on scroll and close once it's scrolled out of the diagram
- An agent talking to itself on the last column gets its text on the left of its lifeline
- Broken data holds: messages to or from someone who isn't a participant are left out, a time that isn't a number shows none, a negative one reads 0:00, runs past an hour widen the gutter for 1:02:05, an empty label draws just the line, and a reply to a call that doesn't exist is still drawn
- Participants are white pills and labels pill-shaped tags, like the rest of the library; frames and cards have soft hairline borders
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every participant and message a stable id – messages draw in once per id
- Pass messages in the order they happened; set replyTo on replies so the receiver's bar ends and the cards can say how long it took
- Keep labels short – a tool call with its main argument, a result in a few words – and put the rest in detail
- Four to six participants fit 760px comfortably; more scroll sideways
- Colors are --ui-asq-* variables on the root; the first agent is --ui-asq-blue

### Requirements

- React 19
