# Agent Steering, clean style (Pro)

Steer an agent while it works – queue a note for the next step and watch it glide into the plan when the agent picks it up, or interrupt right away

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-steering
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-steering-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-steering-clean`

### When to use

- An agent runs for a while and people notice something it should do differently – without stopping it
- Long runs where a correction is cheaper at the next step than a restart from scratch
- Showing which instruction changed which step, so the run stays easy to follow later

### When not to use

- Reviewing a plan before the run starts – use Agent Plan
- Many background runs at a glance – use Agent Inbox
- A single yes or no before the agent acts – use Approval Card

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AgentSteering, type SteerNote, type SteerStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-steering-clean";

export function Run({ run }: { run: AgentRun }) {
  const [steps, setSteps] = useState<SteerStep[]>(run.steps);
  const [queue, setQueue] = useState<SteerNote[]>([]);

  // Your agent takes the queue in at the start of each step: move the notes into that step – the glide is automatic
  run.on("step", (index) => {
    setSteps((list) => list.map((s, i) => (i === index ? { ...s, status: "active", notes: queue.map((n) => ({ ...n, picked: "next" })) } : s)));
    setQueue([]);
  });

  return (
    <AgentSteering
      title="Migrate users table"
      agent="Opus 5.5"
      steps={steps}
      queue={queue}
      startedAt={run.startedAt}
      onQueue={(text) => setQueue((q) => [...q, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), text }])}
      onInterrupt={(text, id) => run.interrupt(text, id)}
      onRemove={(id) => setQueue((q) => q.filter((n) => n.id !== id))}
      onPause={() => run.pause()}
      onResume={() => run.resume()}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | What the agent is working on, shown as the heading |
| agent | `string` |  | Name of the agent or model, shown under the title |
| steps | `SteerStep[]` |  | The plan: { id, title, status?, duration?, startedAt?, notes? }. status is "done", "active" or "pending" |
| queue | `SteerNote[]` |  | Notes waiting for the next step: { id, text }. Move one into a step's notes (same id, picked set) and it glides over |
| status | `"running" \| "paused" \| "done"` | `"running"` | The run. Clocks tick while running; when done the field closes |
| startedAt | `number \| Date` |  | When the run started – the header clock ticks from here |
| onQueue | `(text: string) => void` |  | ↵ in the field: add the note to your queue |
| onInterrupt | `(text: string, queuedId?: string) => void` |  | ⌘↵ (Ctrl ↵) in the field, or "Now" on a queued note. Shows the shortcut hint and the Now buttons |
| onRemove | `(id: string) => void` |  | ✕ on a queued note |
| onPause / onResume | `() => void` |  | Shows Pause while running and Resume while paused |
| draft / onDraftChange | `string / (text: string) => void` |  | Controlled field text, e.g. to prefill a suggestion |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Steer the agent…"` | Text in the empty field |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↵: Queues the note for the next step
- ⌘ / ↵: Applies the note to the active step right away (Ctrl ↵ on Windows)
- Shift / ↵: New line in the note
- Esc: Clears the field
- Tab: Moves to Pause, the queued notes' Now and ✕ buttons and the send button

### Accessibility

- The plan is an ordered list labelled "Plan"; the active step has aria-current="step"
- Queuing, interrupting and every note the agent picks up are announced in a polite live region
- The field is labelled "Steer the agent" and described by the shortcut hint below it
- Icon buttons have labels: Pause, Resume, Remove “…”, Queue for the next step

### Motion

- A note the agent takes in glides from the queue into its step (620 ms) and lights up softly once it lands
- The card's height follows its content, so the queue opening and closing never jumps
- The active step spins and shimmers; done steps pop their check in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the shimmer stops

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px
- Below 380px the padding gets tighter
- Touch screens get larger buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component never runs anything itself: it shows steps and queue as passed and reports onQueue / onInterrupt / onRemove
- To show that the agent took a note in, remove it from queue and add it (same id, picked: "next" or "now") to the step's notes in one update
- Give each step a startedAt when it becomes active, so its clock is right after re-renders

### Requirements

- React 19

# Agent / Tasks (Pro)

Your work as tasks, not agents – a calm list grouped by project, each row a ring, where it is in words and a small Needs you, and a click opens what happened so far and what it made

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-tasks

### When to use

- You talk to one orchestrator in one thread and want to see the work as tasks and projects – however many agents run behind them
- Understanding a task at a glance: where it is, what it made, what happened so far and whether it needs you

### When not to use

- Watching agents, calls and traces – use Agent / Orchestration
- Answering what waits on you – use Agent / Inbox

```tsx
import { AgentTasksScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-tasks";

export default function Page() {
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState(initialTasks);
  return (
    <AgentTasksScreen
      tasks={tasks}
      projects={["Northwind", "Platform", "Evalkit"]}
      artifacts={files}
      onCreate={(task) => api.startTask(task.title, task.project)}
      onOpenInbox={(taskId, itemId) => router.push("/inbox?item=" + itemId)} // Decide, and a row's Needs you
      onSelect={(id) => api.markSeen(id)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} // "Inbox", "Agent Orchestration", the sidebar's items
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

### Keyboard

- J / K: Next and previous row – anywhere in the screen, as long as you're not typing
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In the list: move through the group heads and rows (one Tab stop)
- Enter / Space: On a row: open the task on the right – on one that needs you, its Decide is the next Tab stop. On a group's head: fold or unfold it

- C / N: New task – type what you want, Enter creates it and clears the line for the next one, Esc closes it
- ← →: Active / Done: switch between the two lists
- ← → / Home / End / Delete: Task panel tabs: move between them; Delete closes the focused tab – closing the last one folds the panel
- Shift F10 / Context menu key: In an artifact's tab: the App Shell's context menus – the sheet, document and folder keep their own shortcuts

### Accessibility

- The list is a role="tree": group heads are level-1 items with aria-expanded and their count, rows level-2 items with their position in the group; one Tab stop, the arrow keys move it
- Every row is named in full – title, where it is, Needs you, steps, artifacts and when it last moved – while the faint columns stay hidden from screen readers
- A polite live region says what happened: "Task created in Northwind"
- The Needs you badge on a row is a pointer's shortcut to the Inbox; the keyboard reaches the same through Enter on the row, then the panel's Decide (named with its question)

- One moment: a new task glides in at the top of its project, its row growing from nothing

# Agent / Thread (Pro)

One conversation with your orchestrator – it answers in plain text with small task and decision cards, folds its parallel tools into one line, and keeps working through a dropped connection, a slow upload or a long time away

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-thread
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-thread.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-thread`

### When to use

- You work through one orchestrator in one thread – it launches the sub-agents in the background and you only see the conversation, the tasks it mentions and the decisions it needs
- A chat that has to hold up in real life: parallel tool calls, reading back while it streams, a dropped connection, slow uploads, dictation on a bad network, coming back after an hour

### When not to use

- Picking a model per message – the orchestrator chooses its models itself; pass `models` for a picker, or use AI Chat / Start
- Watching every agent and trace of a run – use Agent / Orchestration or AI Chat / Run

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentThreadScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-thread";

export default function Page() {
  const { messages, send, stop, retry } = useOrchestrator(); // your stream – append to the last message as tokens arrive
  return (
    <AgentThreadScreen
      messages={messages}
      onSend={(text, attachments) => send(text, attachments)}
      onStop={stop}
      onRetry={retry}
      lastSeen={user.lastSeenAt}
      running={{ running: tasks.running, needs: inbox.open }}
      decisions={inbox.open}
      onDecide={(id, answer) => api.answer(id, answer)}
      onLater={(id) => api.snooze(id)}
      tasks={taskDetails}
      onShowTask={(id) => router.push(`/tasks?task=${id}`)}
      onOpenInbox={(item) => router.push(item ? `/inbox?item=${item}` : "/inbox")}
      upload={(file, progress, signal) => uploadWithProgress(file, progress, signal)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send – offline it queues and goes out once you're back
- Shift Enter: A new line – the field grows up to about ten lines, then scrolls
- Esc: In the field: stop the answer while it streams; while dictating, discard the clip
- End: Jump to the latest and follow it again – anywhere in the screen, as long as you're not typing
- /: Focus the field
- 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5: Answer the docked decision with that row; the number after the last option goes to "Something else…"
- ↑ ↓ / ← → / Home / End / Enter: In the dock: move through the rows (← → on tiles), Enter answers the focused one; a click answers at once, like Claude
- Esc: In the dock: Later – it folds to one line above the field
- Tab: Through the tool groups (Enter opens or folds one), every card's Open or Decide, the artifact chips, Retry and the composer's buttons

### Accessibility

- The conversation is role="log" with aria-live="polite" and aria-busy while an answer streams – a screen reader reads the finished answer, not every word
- The connection banner is role="status"; "Waiting to send", "Back online", "Stopped" and upload failures are announced in a polite live region
- The Jump pill is named with its count – "Jump to latest, 12 new lines, still writing" – and lists End as its shortcut
- Each tool group is a button with aria-expanded; folded rows are inert, so Tab skips them; each row says whether it runs, failed or is done
- Task cards are reached by their own Open, named with the task and its status
- The dock is a role="group" labelled by its question; its rows are a listbox with a roving tabindex and aria-keyshortcuts 1–5; "Answered: Kafka" is announced politely and, answered from the keyboard, the focus moves to the composer
- Where it asked, a button says "Asked: … · waiting" or "· answered below" – it brings the dock up (the focus lands on its option) or scrolls to your answer
- Every control shows the 2px accent focus ring for the keyboard only (:focus-visible); the text field never shows one – only its edge firms up while you type
- Shortcuts never fire while you type, apart from Enter, Shift Enter and Esc in the field

### Motion

- One signature: parallel tools finish at their own moments – each check pops in – then, a beat after the last, the rows fold together into "Ran 3 tools · 4.2s"
- The answer types in word by word behind a soft, breathing caret; running tool names carry a slow sheen
- Messages and cards rise in by 8px; the banner drops in, the Jump pill rises in
- The dock folds away smoothly once the last decision is answered; the next one fades in; brought up from elsewhere it pulses gray once
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing slides, folds or breathes – states simply change; spinners slow down

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- One width, --th-col (680px): the orchestrator's text, every block – task cards, tool groups, the away card, error lines – the dock and the composer share the same edges; your bubbles stay right-aligned at most 80%
- The decision is its own card, 8px above the composer and as wide – not an overlay: the thread above shrinks with it, so the latest message and the Jump pill stay above it. The composer always starts a new prompt; your own answer goes in the card's last row

- There is deliberately no model picker, effort selector or agent list – the orchestrator decides; keep it that way
- Stream by updating the last agent message: append to its last text part, set tools' status as they finish, then streaming: false
- The sample story and the simulate presets live in the component for previews; the demo page's state switcher is demo-only chrome
- Decisions are answered in the thread, never by switching pages: put them in `decisions`, answer them in onDecide; the inline decision part is only the "Asked" line

# Agent Timing, clean style (Pro)

An agent run as a timing diagram – time runs left to right, you and every agent a row with its own signal line. Idle it rests on the baseline, thinking it steps up a little, calling a tool all the way up with the tool's name under the line, waiting on you a dashed amber step – one line per row, rounded where it steps and gliding to each new level, a soft fill under it fading down, so steps that touch flow into each other. The step still running ends in a softly pulsing dot on the now line, and beside every name stands what it does right now. Hand-offs are dashed lines straight to the other row, drawn in as they happen, with a small white dot where they land. Point at a step or a hand-off for what it was, when and how long

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-timing
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-timing-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-timing-clean`

### When to use

- An agent run where it matters when each agent worked, how long, and where it waited
- Finding where a run loses time – long tool calls, agents sitting idle, the run waiting on you
- A live view of a multi-agent run next to its chat or log

### When not to use

- Who said what to whom, in order – use Agent Sequence
- Spans of one trace with their nesting – use Trace Waterfall
- Agents working side by side on separate tasks – use Agent Lanes

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTiming, type TimingParticipant, type TimingSegment, type TimingHandoff } from "@/components/ui/agent-timing-clean";

const participants: TimingParticipant[] = [
  { id: "you", name: "You", kind: "person" },
  { id: "lead", name: "Lead" },
  { id: "coder", name: "Coder" },
];

const segments: TimingSegment[] = [
  { who: "lead", state: "thinking", start: 0.5, end: 4, label: "Planning the fix" },
  { who: "lead", state: "tool", start: 4, end: 8, label: "search_code" },
  { who: "coder", state: "tool", start: 9, label: "edit_file" }, // no end – still running
];

const handoffs: TimingHandoff[] = [
  { from: "you", to: "lead", at: 0.2, label: "Fix the cart total bug" },
  { from: "lead", to: "coder", at: 8.6, label: "Fix rounding in cart.ts" },
];

export function Run({ now }: { now: number }) {
  return <AgentTiming title="Fix the cart total" participants={participants} segments={segments} handoffs={handoffs} now={now} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| participants | `TimingParticipant[]` |  | The rows – { id, name, kind?, color? }. person is the full pixel mark in ink; agents their own mark, the first blue, the others the palette |
| segments | `TimingSegment[]` |  | What each one did – { who, state, start, end?, label?, id? } in seconds from the start. thinking is a low step, tool a high one with its name, waiting a dashed amber step. No end: it still runs and reaches to now |
| handoffs | `TimingHandoff[]` |  | Hand-offs – { from, to, at, label?, id? }. A thin arrow from one row to the other, drawn in as now passes it |
| now | `number` |  | Seconds since the run started – the now line; steps without an end grow to it. Leave it out for a finished run |
| duration | `number` |  | Seconds the axis shows – by default the run's length with a little room |
| title | `string` |  | The run's name in the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it, e.g. --ui-atgc-gutter |

### Keyboard

- Tab: One stop for the diagram
- ← / →: The step before or after in the same row – each shows its card
- ↑ / ↓: The nearest step in the row above or below
- Home / End: The row's first or last step
- Esc: Hides the card

### Accessibility

- Steps and hand-offs are a list; each reads who, what, when and how long – "Coder, tool call, edit_file, from 0:17 for 5.5s"
- Waiting on you shows as words in the bar, not only as amber
- Every step names itself inside when there is room – the tool, what it thinks about, "Waiting on you"
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only (:focus-visible)

### Motion

- A new step glides up or down to its level, and back to the baseline when it ends; a running step grows to the now line and ends in a softly pulsing dot
- A hand-off – a dashed line straight to the other row – draws itself as now passes it, then a small white dot appears where it lands
- Every part is worked out from now, so it stays right however often it renders
- With prefers-reduced-motion the pulse and the twinkle stop; the steps still follow now

### Responsive

# Agent Timing (Pro)

An agent run as a timing diagram – time runs left to right, you and every agent a row with its own signal line. Idle it rests on the baseline, thinking it steps up a little, calling a tool all the way up with the tool's name under the line, waiting on you a dashed amber step – one line per row, rounded where it steps and gliding to each new level, a soft fill under it fading down, so steps that touch flow into each other. The step still running ends in a softly pulsing dot on the now line, and beside every name stands what it does right now. Hand-offs are dashed lines straight to the other row, drawn in as they happen, with a small white dot where they land. Point at a step or a hand-off for what it was, when and how long

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-timing
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install, classic style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-timing.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Install, clean style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-timing-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key) – lands as `agent-timing-clean.tsx`, import from `@/components/ui/agent-timing-clean` – its docs: `agent-timing-clean.md`
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-timing`

### When to use

- An agent run where it matters when each agent worked, how long, and where it waited
- Finding where a run loses time – long tool calls, agents sitting idle, the run waiting on you
- A live view of a multi-agent run next to its chat or log

### When not to use

- Who said what to whom, in order – use Agent Sequence
- Spans of one trace with their nesting – use Trace Waterfall
- Agents working side by side on separate tasks – use Agent Lanes

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTiming, type TimingParticipant, type TimingSegment, type TimingHandoff } from "@/components/ui/agent-timing";

const participants: TimingParticipant[] = [
  { id: "you", name: "You", kind: "person" },
  { id: "lead", name: "Lead" },
  { id: "coder", name: "Coder" },
];

const segments: TimingSegment[] = [
  { who: "lead", state: "thinking", start: 0.5, end: 4, label: "Planning the fix" },
  { who: "lead", state: "tool", start: 4, end: 8, label: "search_code" },
  { who: "coder", state: "tool", start: 9, label: "edit_file" }, // no end – still running
];

const handoffs: TimingHandoff[] = [
  { from: "you", to: "lead", at: 0.2, label: "Fix the cart total bug" },
  { from: "lead", to: "coder", at: 8.6, label: "Fix rounding in cart.ts" },
];

export function Run({ now }: { now: number }) {
  return <AgentTiming title="Fix the cart total" participants={participants} segments={segments} handoffs={handoffs} now={now} />;
}
```

The steps an agent works through, as one quiet trail – a header with the task and "3/5", done ones with a check and their time, the one it is on says what it is doing and branches into its sub-steps with a live timer, a step that needs approval waits with a dashed ring; a short fading light runs down the trail into the sub-step it is on

```tsx
import { AgentTrail, type TrailStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-trail-clean";

const steps: TrailStep[] = [
  { id: "read", title: "Read the bug report", state: "done", duration: 8000 },
  { id: "repro", title: "Reproduce the crash", state: "done", duration: 34000 },
  {
    id: "patch",
    title: "Patch the checkout form",
    state: "running",
    status: "Testing",
    startedAt: Date.now(),
    substeps: [
      { title: "Found the empty-cart case", detail: "cart.ts:142" },
      { title: "Added a guard and 2 tests", detail: "+18 −3" },
      { title: "Running the test suite", detail: "182/214", state: "running" },
    ],
  },
  { id: "notes", title: "Write the release note", state: "pending" },
  { id: "pr", title: "Open a pull request", state: "pending", gate: true },
];

export function Progress() {
  return <AgentTrail title="Fix the checkout crash" steps={steps} />;
}
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `TrailStep[]` |  | { id, title, state, duration?, status?, startedAt?, gate?, substeps? } – in the order the agent walks them |
| title | `string` |  | The task, in a header over the trail with how many steps are done – "3/5". Leave it out for no header |
| agent | `{ name: string; logo?: ReactNode }` |  | Who works on it – the agent or model's logo and name in the header, before the count |
| state | `"done" \| "running" \| "pending" \| "waiting" \| "failed" \| "declined"` |  | Per step – done shows a tinted check and its time, running a spinning ring with its status, waiting an orange disc with a pause and Needs you, failed a red mark, declined (you said no at Needs you) a quiet gray dash with its title struck through |
| duration | `number \| string` |  | How long a done step took – ms as a number (12s, 1m 4s, 1h 2m, 3d 4h), or your own text |
| status / startedAt | `string / number` |  | What a running step does right now, shimmering – "Testing" – and when it started (Date.now()) for a live timer next to it |
| gate | `boolean` |  | Needs approval before it runs – a dashed orange ring and "Approval" until it is reached, then "Needs you" while state is waiting |
| tool | `{ logo: ReactNode; name: string }` |  | Per step – the tool or system it works in (GitHub, Linear, Notion …); its 14px logo sits before the title, faded while the step is still to come |
| substeps | `{ id?, title, state?, detail? }[]` |  | What the agent does inside a step – state done (default), running or pending, and a short fact on the right (long ones keep their end: "src/…Wrapper.tsx:1284"). The light runs to the running one; more than six fold to five around it with "+N earlier" and "+N more" |
| expanded / onExpandedChange | `string[] / (ids) => void` |  | Which steps show their sub-steps. By default the running one opens, the rest open with a click |
| onApprove | `(step: TrailStep) => void` |  | A waiting step was approved – with this (or onDecline) "Needs you" becomes a button that opens Approve and Decline under the row |
| onDecline | `(step: TrailStep) => void` |  | A waiting step was declined – update its state in your data to declined |
| ask | `string` |  | Per step – what a waiting step asks you to approve, shown above Approve and Decline: "Open PR #482 against main – 3 files, 214 tests passing" |
| labels | `Partial<AgentTrailLabels>` |  | Every word: title (the list's name without a header), running, approval, waiting, failed, declined, done, pending, empty (no steps – "No steps yet"), untitled (a step without a title), earlier / more / fewer (the rows that fold long sub-step lists), approve / decline (the two answers to Needs you) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves to each step that has sub-steps
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes its sub-steps
- Tab / Enter: On "+N earlier" or "+N more": shows every sub-step; "Show fewer" folds them again – focus stays on the row
- Enter: On "Needs you": opens Approve and Decline – focus lands on Approve
- Esc: Closes the answer panel and returns to "Needs you"

### Accessibility

- An ordered list named after the task; the running step and sub-step carry aria-current="step"
- The header count reads "3 of 5 steps done"
- Each step reads its title, state and time – "Read the bug report – Done, 8s"; a step with sub-steps is a button with aria-expanded
- Closed sub-steps are inert, so the keyboard and screen readers skip them
- A step that loses its sub-steps while focused keeps the focus; times, badges and status read in their own direction, so "<1s" stays "<1s" in right-to-left pages
- A polite live region says when a step finishes, fails or waits for you
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only (:focus-visible), in light and dark

### Motion

- A short light – full at the front, fading to nothing at the back – runs from the running step down its branch into the sub-step it is on, and that dot rings once as it arrives
- The running marker's arc goes round, its status shimmers and the timer counts up
- A finished step's check pops in and draws itself; the line to the next step fills
- Sub-steps fold open and closed, the branch line follows
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything changes at once and the light stays off

### Responsive

- Rows are fixed – 32px for a step, 24px for a sub-step, 40px and 28px on touch screens – so a changing status, timer or detail never moves another row
- Long sub-step lists fold to five rows around where the agent is, so the card and the light stay short
- No steps: the header stays and a quiet "No steps yet" takes the list's place; a missing title reads "Untitled step"
- Long titles end in … with the full text on hover; the right side never takes more than 40% of the row, so the title keeps its room
- Right-to-left: the trail moves to the right edge and the branch bends the other way
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step a stable id – opening, closing and the live region track steps by it
- Keep status to one word in the present – "Testing", "Writing"
- Sub-step titles say what happened – "Found the empty-cart case" – and detail a short fact: a file, a diff, a count
- Only one step should be running; the light goes to its running sub-step
- Colors are variables on .ui-atrc – --ui-atrc-accent and --ui-atrc-wash set the trail, --ui-atrc-loop the light's speed

- React 19

- A step that loses its sub-steps while focused keeps the focus; times, badges and status read in their own direction, so "<1s" stays "<1s" in right-to-left pages
- A polite live region says when a step finishes, fails or waits for you
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only (:focus-visible), in light and dark

### Motion

- A short light – full at the front, fading to nothing at the back – runs from the running step down its branch into the sub-step it is on, and that dot rings once as it arrives
- The running marker's arc goes round, its status shimmers and the timer counts up
- A finished step's check pops in and draws itself; the line to the next step fills
- Sub-steps fold open and closed, the branch line follows
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything changes at once and the light stays off

### Responsive

- Rows are fixed – 32px for a step, 24px for a sub-step, 40px and 28px on touch screens – so a changing status, timer or detail never moves another row
- Long sub-step lists fold to five rows around where the agent is, so the card and the light stay short
- No steps: the header stays and a quiet "No steps yet" takes the list's place; a missing title reads "Untitled step"
- Long titles end in … with the full text on hover; the right side never takes more than 40% of the row, so the title keeps its room
- Right-to-left: the trail moves to the right edge and the branch bends the other way
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step a stable id – opening, closing and the live region track steps by it
- Keep status to one word in the present – "Testing", "Writing"
- Sub-step titles say what happened – "Found the empty-cart case" – and detail a short fact: a file, a diff, a count
- Only one step should be running; the light goes to its running sub-step
- Colors are variables on .ui-atr – --ui-atr-accent and --ui-atr-wash set the trail, --ui-atr-loop the light's speed

- React 19

### When to use

- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's steps – use Agent Plan or Agent Steering

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTree, type TreeAgent } from "@/components/ui/agent-tree-clean";

const run: TreeAgent = {
  id: "lead", name: "Orchestrator", model: "Opus 5.5", task: "Launch the new pricing page",
  status: "running", cost: 0.42, started: Date.now() - 80_000,
  children: [
    { id: "research", name: "Researcher", task: "Compare five competitors", status: "done", cost: 0.29, started: Date.now() - 70_000, ended: Date.now() - 25_000 },
    { id: "build", name: "Coder", task: "Build the page", status: "running", cost: 0.18, started: Date.now() - 60_000 },
  ],
};

export function Run() {
  return <AgentTree root={run} onSelect={(agent) => openLog(agent.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| root | `TreeAgent` |  | { id, name, task, model?, avatar?, tools?, status, ask?, error?, cost?, started?, ended?, children? } – the whole tree, rebuilt as the run goes on; tools are small marks shown as overlapping tiles before the task |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "stopped"` |  | Per agent – "waiting" reads "Needs you"; queued and stopped agents and their connectors are muted |
| cost | `number` |  | Per agent, its own cost – a card with children shows the whole branch |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of folded branches, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: string[]) => void` |  | A branch was folded or opened |
| ask / error | `string` |  | Per agent – what a waiting agent needs you to decide, and what went wrong for a failed one; shown in the window behind "needs you" and "failed" |
| onResolve | `(agent, action: "approve" \| "reject" \| "retry" \| "dismiss") => void` |  | An answer from that window – update the agent's status in your data |
| onSelect | `(agent: TreeAgent) => void` |  | A click on a card – makes the cards clickable |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for running times – without it the tree ticks every second while an agent runs |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the fold buttons – and the cards, when onSelect is set
- Enter: On a card: selects it (onSelect)
- Enter / Space: Folds or opens the focused branch

### Accessibility

- The tree is a tree with groups; every agent is a treeitem labelled with its name and status, aria-expanded on branches
- Fold buttons name what they do, e.g. "Show 2 sub-agents of Researcher"
- "needs you" and "failed" are buttons with aria-expanded; their window is a dialog, the first answer is focused and Esc closes it
- The totals in the bar – agents, running, needs you, failed, cost – are announced politely when they change

### Motion

- A new agent's connector draws itself from the parent's dot, then the card rises in; several new agents rise one after another
- When the tree changes, every card glides to its new place and the connectors follow frame by frame
- Agents that leave – a folded branch, removed data – fade out a beat apart, bottom first, while their connectors pull back into the parent
- Status glyphs: a spinning loader while running, a check when done, a warning triangle when failed, a clock when it needs you
- Costs that still climb – a running agent, a branch with one, the total – carry a light shimmer that runs over the amount
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- From 560px the first level sits side by side under the root, deeper levels hang below their parent – every card has the same width
- Narrower, every level is indented under its parent and the connectors run down the left; the cards shrink together so the deepest level still fits
- The connectors are measured from the cards, so any width or zoom works
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole tree every time something changes – ids keep the cards in place, new ids grow in with a drawn connector
- cost is the agent's own spend; the component adds the children up, so don't pre-sum it
- A failed agent that gets retried is a new child with its own id – keep the failed one, it tells the story
- The connector color is --ui-agtc-link (#82bcff), the soft blue of the Project Flow illustration
- The chevron is Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

- React 19

# Agent / Usage (Pro)

What your agent costs – the month added up day by day against the budget, where it lands at this pace in one plain line, money ticking up as runs finish, where it went by project or model, and what's worth a look

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-usage
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-usage.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-usage`

### When to use

- Showing what an agent costs this month – against a budget, and where it lands at this pace
- Answering where the money went – by project or by model – and what stands out
- Making spend feel live: the sum moves as runs finish

### When not to use

- One run's cost, call by call – use Agent / Orchestration or the Cost Waterfall
- Plans and invoices – use Settings / Billing
- Product analytics – use Analytics

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentUsageScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-usage";

export default function Page() {
  const { days, projects, models, notes, latestRun } = useUsage("2026-11");
  return (
    <AgentUsageScreen
      days={days}              // what it cost each day so far – the last is today
      daysInMonth={30}
      budget={500}
      currency="EUR"
      projects={projects}
      models={models}
      notes={notes}
      latest={latestRun}       // a new id plays "+€0.42 · Ingest pipeline"
      onOpenNote={(note) => router.push("/runs/" + note.id)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| days | `number[]` | `19 sample days` | What it cost each day of the month so far – the last one is today. The curve adds them up; the pace of these days makes the dashed forecast |
| daysInMonth | `number` | `30` | How many days the month has |
| budget | `number \| null` | `500` | The month's budget – the curve draws it as a line and the sentence says on which day it would be passed; null for none |
| currency | `string` | `"EUR"` | ISO 4217 code – every amount is formatted with it |
| projects / models | `{ id; name; amount; last?; tone?; days?; tasks?: { title; runs; cost }[] }[]` |  | Where it went – amount this month, last for the change on last month, tone a palette name or any color, days for the panel's bars, tasks for what cost the most |
| notes | `{ id; kind: "spike" \| "jump" \| "budget"; text; detail?; badge? }[]` |  | What's worth a look – Open calls onOpenNote (or onNavigate("Runs")) |
| stats | `{ tasks?; runs?; tokens? }` |  | The month's numbers under the curve – with tasks it also shows the cost per task |
| latest | `{ id; task; cost } \| null` |  | The run that just finished – a new id plays its moment: the sum ticks up and "+€0.42 · task" shows beside it |
| defaultView | `"projects" \| "models"` | `"projects"` | What Where it went shows first |
| defaultSelected | `string \| null` | `"northwind"` | The project or model open on the right |
| onOpenNote | `(note: UsageNote) => void` |  | Called with Open on a note |
| onSelect | `(view, id) => void` |  | Called when a project or a model is opened |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| labels | `{ usage?; month?; monthShort?; spent?; onTrack?; over?; whereItWent?; worthALook?; … }` |  | Labels, e.g. for a translation – onTrack and over take {amount}, {budget} and {date} |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While your data loads: gray spend card, curve, rows, notes and panel in the shape of the real ones; the header, labels and the Projects | Models switch stay |
| empty | `boolean` |  | Nothing spent yet: the page shows Nothing spent yet with a sentence on when spend shows up and a Start a task button (calls onNavigate with "Tasks"); the breakdown and notes hide and the Details panel shows nothing open |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: On the curve: day by day – what it cost that day and the sum so far
- Home / End: On the curve: the first day, today
- Esc: On the curve: hide the day
- ← / →: Projects / Models: switch what Where it went shows
- Tab / Enter: Every project, model and note is a button – Enter opens it

### Accessibility

- The curve is one image whose name says it all – the sum so far, the budget and where it lands; ← → read it day by day through a live line
- Each project or model is a button named with its amount, its share and its change on last month
- The run that just finished is said once through a status line: "+€0.42 · Ingest pipeline"
- Color is never the only sign: the change has its arrow, a warning its icon and words
- Rings show for the keyboard only

### Motion

- One moment: as a run finishes the sum's digits roll into place like an odometer – only the ones that change, up from below, fading at the edges – today's point rises on the curve and "+€0.42 · task" shows for a moment
- Every number that changes rolls the same way – the forecast in the sentence, the share, runs and tokens, a project's amount; going down they roll the other way
- On load the curve draws itself in and its fill fades up; today's point breathes; the bars grow from the left
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing draws, breathes or grows

- Fills its container; the page keeps a readable 720px column and the curve takes its full width
- Below 620px the numbers stack two by two, the bars make room for name, amount and change, and a note's badge and Open move under its text
- Amounts keep their column at any size – €1.28M in a row with the whole amount in its tooltip and the panel; a change of thousands of percent reads as a factor (↑12×); every currency gets its own decimals (€270.40, ¥43,264)
- Touch targets grow to 36px on touch screens
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

# Agent Workbench, clean style (Pro)

One agent at work: the person who asked on the left with their message, the agent in the middle with a work area showing what it does right now, the files it was given on the right under a macOS folder, and its tools below as cards with what each may do and what it did last – joined by soft rounded connectors, with a light running along the one in use

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-workbench
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-workbench-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-workbench-clean`

### When to use

- Showing one agent at work on one request: who asked, what it reads, which tools it calls and what it does right now
- An assistant that works across a person's apps – mail, calendar, files – where people should see what it touches
- A live view next to a chat, or a still picture of how an agent is wired up

### When not to use

- Many agents handing work to each other – use Agent Crew or Agent Tree
- What an agent remembers and every tool it can reach – use Memory Graph
- Each tool call with its input and output – use Agent Tool Calls

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentWorkbench, type WorkbenchStep, type WorkbenchTool } from "@/components/ui/agent-workbench-clean";

const tools: WorkbenchTool[] = [
  { id: "gmail", name: "Gmail", logo: <GmailLogo />, scope: "Read & send · ryan@lumen.co", last: "Sent the weekly digest", when: "2h ago" },
  { id: "calendar", name: "Google Calendar", logo: <CalendarLogo />, scope: "Read & book · Work" },
];

const steps: WorkbenchStep[] = [
  { id: "s1", text: "Reading Ryan's request", at: "user" },
  { id: "s2", text: "Checking Marc's calendar next week", at: "calendar", running: true },
];

export function Workbench() {
  return (
    <AgentWorkbench
      user={{ name: "Ryan Brooks", photo: "/ryan.jpg", message: "Find 30 minutes with Marc next week." }}
      agent={{ id: "assistant", name: "Assistant", subtitle: "Works in your Google account" }}
      tools={tools}
      files={[{ id: "budget", name: "budget-q4.xlsx", logo: <ExcelLogo />, meta: "48 KB" }]}
      steps={steps}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user | `{ name, message, photo?, avatar? }` |  | Who asked, on the left – their photo URL shown round beside the name (avatar takes your own node instead), and their message; without a photo, or if it doesn't load, the person's full mark |
| agent | `{ id, name, subtitle?, details? }` |  | The agent in the middle – its pixel mark from its id, twinkling while it works; click it and its info card opens below with details, what it does now, its steps and the tools it used |
| tools | `WorkbenchTool[]` |  | Its tools below as cards – logo, name, what each may do and where, and what it did last; up to four, with more the last spot sums up the rest ("+3 more tools") |
| WorkbenchTool.scope / last / when | `string / string / string` |  | "Read & send · ryan@lumen.co", its last action and when – while it's called, what it does now shows instead |
| WorkbenchTool.details / WorkbenchFile.details | `{ label, value }[]` |  | Lines in the info card that opens below a tool or a file when it's clicked – a tool's card also lists what it did for this request |
| files | `WorkbenchFile[]` |  | What it was given, on the right under a macOS folder – name, logo and a short meta like "48 KB"; up to four, then "+N more"; a file without a logo gets a plain page |
| steps | `WorkbenchStep[]` |  | What it did and does, oldest first – the last three show in its work area, newest on top |
| WorkbenchStep.at / running | `string / boolean` |  | Where it reaches – a tool id, "files" or "user" – and whether it still runs; the running step's line carries the light |
| reading | `string` |  | The id of the file it reads right now – lit up in the list |
| done | `boolean` |  | Finished – the status says Done and nothing runs |
| title | `string` |  | The section's accessible name |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Accessibility

- The work area is a list with a polite live region – each new step is read as it comes in
- Every card is plain text and logos marked decorative; the connectors and their dots are hidden from screen readers
- Status is said in words – Working, Done, Calling, Used, Ready – never by color alone
- The agent, every tool and every file is a button with its name and "details" – Enter or Space opens its info card, aria-expanded says it's open
- One info card at a time; clicking it again, clicking outside or Esc closes it, and Esc puts focus back on the button
- A focus ring shows only for the keyboard

### Motion

- A light runs along the line in use – in from the person who asked, out to the files or the tool – full at its front and fading to nothing behind
- Each new step comes in from above at the top of the work area and shimmers while it runs; the agent's mark twinkles and Working turns
- The tool it calls shows what it does now, shimmering; the file it reads lights up
- An info card fades and rises in from the card it opens from in 180ms, and drops out faster when it closes
- Reduced motion turns it all off – steps and info cards simply appear

### Responsive

- Fills its container's width – the person, the agent and the files in a row, the tools in a row below, joined by soft rounded connectors with a hollow dot at each end
- Below 720px everything stacks – the person, the agent, the files, then the tools – and the connectors step aside
- Long names, scopes, file names and steps end in … with the full text on hover; the message keeps to four lines
- Broken data holds: a photo that doesn't load shows the person's mark, a step without text says Working… or Done, a tool without a last action says Nothing yet, no steps at all reads Waiting for a request
- One or two tools stay card-sized in the middle instead of stretching across
- The work area keeps three rows of the same height, so the card never jumps as steps come in
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step and tool a stable id; set at to a tool id, "files" or "user"
- Keep step texts short and in the present while they run – "Checking Marc's calendar" – one step at a time running
- Update a tool's last and when once it's done its part
- Pass the files the person attached; set reading while the agent reads one
- Give the agent, tools and files a few details – short labels, short values – for their info cards

- React 19

```tsx
const tools: WorkbenchTool[] = [
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| agent | `{ id, name, subtitle?, details? }` |  | The agent in the middle – its pixel mark from its id, twinkling while it works; click it and its info card opens below with details, what it does now, its steps and the tools it used |
| tools | `WorkbenchTool[]` |  | Its tools below as cards – logo, name, what each may do and where, and what it did last; up to four, with more the last spot sums up the rest ("+3 more tools") |

| files | `WorkbenchFile[]` |  | What it was given, on the right under a macOS folder – name, logo and a short meta like "48 KB"; up to four, then "+N more"; a file without a logo gets a plain page |

### Accessibility

- The work area is a list with a polite live region – each new step is read as it comes in
- Every card is plain text and logos marked decorative; the connectors and their dots are hidden from screen readers
- Status is said in words – Working, Done, Calling, Used, Ready – never by color alone
- The agent, every tool and every file is a button with its name and "details" – Enter or Space opens its info card, aria-expanded says it's open
- One info card at a time; clicking it again, clicking outside or Esc closes it, and Esc puts focus back on the button
- A focus ring shows only for the keyboard

### Motion

- A light runs along the line in use – in from the person who asked, out to the files or the tool – full at its front and fading to nothing behind
- Each new step comes in from above at the top of the work area and shimmers while it runs; the agent's mark twinkles and Working turns
- The tool it calls shows what it does now, shimmering; the file it reads lights up
- An info card fades and rises in from the card it opens from in 180ms, and drops out faster when it closes
- Reduced motion turns it all off – steps and info cards simply appear

### Responsive

- Fills its container's width – the person, the agent and the files in a row, the tools in a row below, joined by soft rounded connectors with a hollow dot at each end
- Below 720px everything stacks – the person, the agent, the files, then the tools – and the connectors step aside
- Long names, scopes, file names and steps end in … with the full text on hover; the message keeps to four lines
- Broken data holds: a photo that doesn't load shows the person's mark, a step without text says Working… or Done, a tool without a last action says Nothing yet, no steps at all reads Waiting for a request
- One or two tools stay card-sized in the middle instead of stretching across
- The classic style has rounder cards, pill tags and status and firmer type – the same behavior as the clean one
- The work area keeps three rows of the same height, so the card never jumps as steps come in
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step and tool a stable id; set at to a tool id, "files" or "user"
- Keep step texts short and in the present while they run – "Checking Marc's calendar" – one step at a time running
- Update a tool's last and when once it's done its part
- Pass the files the person attached; set reading while the agent reads one
- Give the agent, tools and files a few details – short labels, short values – for their info cards

- React 19

### When to use

- Research, support or knowledge-base products where people need to check the source before they act

### When not to use

- Casual chat without sources – a plain message bubble is lighter
- Long documents or code – the answer is made for a few paragraphs and lists

### Usage

```tsx
import { AIAnswer, type AnswerSource } from "@/components/ui/ai-answer-clean";

const sources: AnswerSource[] = [
  { name: "Notion", title: "Offsite plan – shortlist and budget", href: "https://notion.so/…", snippet: "Budget €4,500 for three nights…" },
  { name: "Slack", title: "#team-offsite – who can make which dates", href: "https://slack.com/…" },
];

export function Answer({ text, done }: { text: string; done: boolean }) {
  return (
    <AIAnswer
      question="Where should we hold the team offsite?"
      sources={sources}
      // Blank lines: paragraphs · "- ": list · **bold** · [1] or [1,2]: citations (1-based)
      answer={text}
      streaming={!done}
      onRegenerate={() => regenerate()}
      onFeedback={(value, reason) => track("answer_feedback", { value, reason })}
      // No surface of its own – add framed when it stands alone on the page
      framed
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| question | `string` |  | Shown as the title above the sources |
| sources | `AnswerSource[]` |  | Each { title, name, href?, icon?, snippet? }; name is the short label on the citation chip |
| answer | `string` |  | Blank lines make paragraphs, lines starting with "- " a list, **bold**, [1] or [1,3] cite sources (1-based). It may grow while streaming; a different text starts over |
| streaming | `boolean` | `false` | More text is still coming from your model – keeps the cursor going once it has caught up |
| animate | `boolean` | `true` | Stream the text in; false shows it at once |
| speed | `number` | `38` | Words per second while streaming in |
| followUps | `string[]` |  | Related questions shown below the finished answer |
| onFollowUp | `(question: string) => void` |  | A follow-up was clicked |
| onRegenerate | `() => void` |  | Regenerate was clicked – the answer streams in again; pass a new answer to replace it |
| onStop | `() => void` |  | Stop was clicked while writing – cancel your request here |
| onFeedback | `(value: "up" \| "down", reason?: string) => void` |  | Thumbs up, or thumbs down with the reason that was picked |
| feedbackReasons | `string[]` | `["Not accurate", "Wrong source", "Too long", "Out of date"]` | Reasons offered after a thumbs down |
| onCopy | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called with the copied text: the answer without markup plus a numbered source list |
| framed | `boolean` | `false` | Puts the answer on its own white card with hairline shadows. Off, it has no background, shadow or padding and takes on the thread, panel or sheet it sits in |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through source cards, citation chips, follow-ups and actions
- Esc: Closes the source preview of the focused chip

### Accessibility

- Citation chips are buttons named after their sources; the preview is a tooltip linked to the chip
- The answer is marked busy while it streams, so screen readers read it once it's complete
- Copy, feedback and status changes are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- Hovering a chip lights up its source card (or the "+N" tile), hovering a card or the tile lights up its chips

- Asking about exactly the part they mean – drag across weeks on a line, or click a provider's bar

### When not to use

- Spend over time without a conversation – use Agent / Usage
- A rate limit plan per agent – use Rate Limit Planner
- Revenue rather than cost – use AI Chat / Revenue Analyst

### Usage

```tsx
import { SpendChatScreen, type ChartFocus } from "@/components/ui/ai-chat-spend";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <SpendChatScreen
      onAsk={async (question: string, focus?: ChartFocus) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/spend", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ question, focus }) });
        return res.json(); // { role: "assistant", text, kpis?, chart?, caption?, sources?, next? }
      }}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onAsk | `(question, focus?) => Answer \| Promise<Answer>` |  | How the screen answers – an answer is { role: "assistant", text, kpis?: { label; value; change?; since?; goodWhenDown? }[], chart?, caption?, sources?, next? }. focus is set when the question is about part of a chart: { chart, from, to, label, detail }. Without it the screen answers the questions it offers from its sample |
| chart | `{ kind: "split" \| "trend" \| "forecast" \| "plan"; … }` |  | "split": { title, previous?, since?, groups: { name, logo?, color?, parts: { name, value }[] }[] } – one bar per provider or team, a segment per model, drawn with Model Usage (values in dollars). "trend": { labels, current, previous, mark? } and "forecast": { labels, actual, forecast, target? } – drawn with Trend Chart (values in thousands). "plan": { now, months, growth, levers } – the totals, the levers and the forecast that follows them |
| levers | `{ id; label; detail; kind: "range" \| "switch"; base; save; max?; value }[]` |  | The changes a plan offers. base is what it touches a month in dollars, save the share of that it saves at full; a slider goes from 0 to max %, a switch is on (1) or off (0). What each saves, the totals and the six-month forecast follow as they move. Turn into rules asks the next question with the plan quoted above it |
| turns | `ChatTurn[]` |  | The conversation so far – { role: "user", text, quote? } and answers as above |
| chats | `ShellChat[]` |  | The chats in the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | Gray lines, cards and chart in place of the conversation |
| empty | `boolean` |  | A new chat – a short note and questions to start with |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the levers, the charts and the buttons
- ← / →: On a slider: 5% at a time – on a line chart: from point to point
- Space: On the batch switch: on or off
- Enter: On a line chart: start a pick, stretch it with the arrows, Enter again to ask – on a bar: pick it
- Esc: Close the field over a pick – back to the chart

### Accessibility

- Each slider is named by its lever and says what it saves; the batch switch is a role="switch"
- Every chart is focusable and named by its caption; stepping through it shows each point's numbers in a tooltip screen readers hear
- The answer is marked busy while its words arrive; a polite live region says when it is working and when something was copied
- Rings show for the keyboard only – never on the text fields

### Motion

- While it works the pixel mark twinkles beside "Reading your usage…"; the words arrive one by one, then the cards and the chart rise in
- Moving a lever rolls the totals and lets the forecast glide to its new line – Trend Chart and Model Usage bring their own motion and tooltips
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything is simply there

### Responsive

- The sidebar starts folded to its icons so the chat has the room; the column stays at 760px in the middle, cards and charts as wide as the composer
- On phones the mark steps back, cards sit two by two, sliders take the whole width and grow to touch size
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Assistant Home, Chat Composer, Trend Chart and Model Usage (installed with it)

- ⌘ / Enter: Approve while focus is anywhere in the card (Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux)
- Escape: Deny while focus is in the card
- Tab: Moves through the checkbox, Edit, Deny and Approve

### Accessibility

- role="group" named by the title and described by the description and the countdown
- Real buttons with aria-keyshortcuts; the kbd hints are aria-hidden
- The decision is announced through a polite live region ("Approved: Send campaign email")
- The countdown has a full text description ("Expires in 24 seconds unless approved…") linked via aria-describedby; the visible clock is aria-hidden so it isn't read every second, and it pauses while the card is hovered or focused

- After a decision focus moves to the resolved row (tabIndex -1) if it was inside the card

### Motion

- On a decision the card and its tray footer fade and blur out, the height glides down to a compact row inside the tray and the check or cross draws itself in
- The countdown text ticks down once per second without animation and turns amber in the last 10 seconds
- Buttons press in slightly; the checkbox tick scales in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and only the spinner keeps turning slowly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; below 400px card width the buttons share a full-width row and the shortcut hints hide
- Below 340px the risk badge drops the word "risk" and the resolved row drops its time
- Titles, descriptions and detail values truncate instead of wrapping; works down to 320px
- Shortcut hints are hidden on touch screens
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Render one card per pending tool call that needs consent; resolve the tool call with the onApprove / onDeny result
- Return the real execution promise from onApprove so the card stays locked until the action has actually started
- Persist { always: true } per tool name and skip the card next time
- Set risk from the action, not the model's confidence: anything external, paid or irreversible is at least medium
- Keep title an imperative verb phrase and put the concrete values (recipients, amount, target) in details

# Approval Gates, clean style (Pro)

The approval requests of an agent run as a stack of cards – the one to decide now on top with who asks, what exactly and why, the diff or arguments on it; approve, reject or change it first, and it drops into the decided list while the next rises – open ones hold the steps behind them

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/approval-gates
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/approval-gates-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/approval-gates-clean`

### When to use

- Human-in-the-loop for agent runs: every tool call, file change, sub-agent or message that needs a person before it goes out
- A run that pauses on approvals – who asks, what exactly and why, with the diff or the arguments right on the card
- Reviewing several requests one after another, and seeing afterwards what was approved, changed or rejected

### When not to use

- Setting how much an agent may do on its own – use Autonomy Dial
- Steering a run while it works, without stopping it – use Agent Steering
- Every message and request of many agents in one place – use Agent Inbox

### Usage

```tsx
import { ApprovalGates, type ApprovalGate } from "@/components/ui/approval-gates-clean";

const gates: ApprovalGate[] = [
  {
    id: "migrate",
    agent: "Coder",
    kind: "tool",
    action: "Run the database migration",
    reason: "Changes the production schema",
    status: "approved",
    at: "6m ago",
  },
  {
    id: "prices",
    agent: "Coder",
    kind: "file",
    action: "Change prices in pricing.ts",
    reason: "Changes what customers pay from Monday",
    status: "open",
    at: "1m ago",
    diff: [{ file: "src/billing/pricing.ts", lines: [{ type: "del", text: "pro: { seat: 8 }," }, { type: "add", text: "pro: { seat: 10 }," }] }],
    holds: ["Deploy to production", "Post to #launch"],
  },
];

export function RunApprovals() {
  return <ApprovalGates gates={gates} task="Launch the new pricing page" live onDecide={(id, decision, value) => agent.decide(id, decision, value)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gates | `ApprovalGate[]` |  | Every gate of the run, in the order they came up – open ones form the stack, the rest the Decided list |
| task | `string` |  | What the run is about – shown muted next to the title |
| live | `boolean` | `false` | The run is still going: with nothing open it reads Running, and new requests slide in behind the stack |
| onDecide | `(id, decision: "approved" \| "edited" \| "rejected", value?: string) => void` |  | A gate was decided – with edited, value is the changed input, or for a file change what should change |
| title | `string` | `"Approvals"` | Heading of the block on top |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| ApprovalGate | `{ id, agent, avatar?, kind, action, reason, status, at?, input?, diff?, files?, context?, holds?, note? }` |  | kind: "tool" | "file" | "agent" | "message"; status: "open" | "approved" | "edited" | "rejected"; input – the arguments, prompt or message; diff – lines per file; context – the steps before it; holds – the steps that wait for it; note – what the person changed or said |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: In the stack: the previous and next open request – the focus moves to its Approve
- Tab: Through the card on top – its data scrolls with the arrow keys – to Edit, Reject and Approve
- ⌘ / Enter: While editing: approve with your changes
- Esc: While editing: back without changes – the focus returns to Edit
- Enter / Space: On a decided row: open or close it

### Accessibility

- The stack is a group that says how many requests wait and which one is on top; after a decision, focus moves on to the next card's Approve
- Every decision is announced politely – what was decided and how many requests are left
- Diff lines say Added and Removed for screen readers; status is never color alone – Blocking, Approved and Stopped the run are words

### Motion

- The open requests lie like a stack of toasts – a decided card drops out towards the list, the next one rises; a rejected one shakes once first
- A request that comes in while you decide slides in behind the stack
- The stack keeps the height of its tallest card, so Holds and Decided below never move
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears

### Responsive

- No layer of its own around it – the block, the cards and the list share one width (--ui-gatec-w, 560px) and sit straight in your panel
- Narrow, the numbers wrap onto two rows and the decided rows drop the agent's name
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Add a gate as open the moment the agent asks, with holds for the steps that wait on it – then move it to approved, edited or rejected
- Never remove a decided gate; a rejected one stays as the point where the run stopped
- Keep action to what exactly happens ("Email 1,284 trial users") and reason to why it needs a person, in one line
- How far the cards behind peek out is --ui-gatec-peek, how much smaller each is --ui-gatec-shrink

### Requirements

- React 19

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AutonomyDial, type AgentAction, type AutonomyLevel } from "@/components/ui/autonomy-dial-clean";

const actions: AgentAction[] = [
  { id: "read", label: "Read files and docs", detail: "Drive · Notion", risk: "safe" },
  { id: "draft", label: "Draft emails", risk: "safe" },
  { id: "send", label: "Send emails", detail: "To customers", risk: "risky" },
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete files", risk: "destructive" },
  { id: "spend", label: "Spend money", detail: "Up to $500", risk: "destructive" },
];

export function AgentPermissions() {
  const [level, setLevel] = useState<AutonomyLevel>(1);
  const [pinned, setPinned] = useState(["spend"]);
  return (
    <AutonomyDial
      title="Sales agent"
      actions={actions}
      level={level}
      onLevelChange={setLevel}
      pinned={pinned}
      onPinnedChange={setPinned}
    />
  );
}
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| level | `0 \| 1 \| 2` |  | Controlled level: 0 Always ask, 1 If risky (safe actions run), 2 Full auto |
| defaultLevel | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | `1` | Starting level when uncontrolled |
| onLevelChange | `(level: AutonomyLevel) => void` |  | Another level was picked |
| pinned | `string[]` |  | Controlled ids of actions that always ask, whatever the level |

- Every change is announced politely: the level and how many actions run on their own or ask first

- Actions glide to their new group when the level or a lock changes, a beat after each other

# Avatar, clean style (Free)

A person's picture or initials on a soft color of their own – rounded squares for workspaces, an agent's pixel mark that twinkles while it works, a status dot and a group that overlaps and ends in +N

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/avatar
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/avatar-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/avatar-clean`

### When to use

- A person next to their name: comments, members, assignees, the account menu
- A workspace, team or org – shape="square" with its initial or logo
- An AI agent – kind="agent" draws its own pixel mark in its color, twinkling while it works
- Who is on something, in little space – AvatarGroup overlaps them and ends in +N

### When not to use

- A status on its own, without a person – use the Badge
- A tool or app logo inside text – use an inline icon, like Tool Call Card does
- Picking people – use the Tag Input or a Combobox, with an avatar in each option

### Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@/components/ui/avatar-clean";

type Member = { id: string; name: string; picture?: string; online?: boolean };

export function Reviewers({ members }: { members: Member[] }) {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup size={24} max={4} aria-label={`${members.length} reviewers`}>
      {members.map((m) => (
        <Avatar key={m.id} seed={m.id} name={m.name} src={m.picture} status={m.online ? "online" : undefined} />
      ))}
      <Avatar kind="agent" seed="triage" name="Triage agent" />
    </AvatarGroup>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` |  | Who it is – the initials (first and last word), the accessible name and the color come from it. Left out: a person outline on gray |
| src | `string` |  | The picture. The initials show while it loads and stay when it fails to load |
| size | `20 \| 24 \| 32 \| 40` | `32` | Width and height in pixels; the initials, the status dot and an agent's mark scale with it |
| shape | `"circle" \| "square"` | `"circle" (agents: "square")` | circle for people · square, a rounded square, for workspaces, teams and agents |
| status | `"online" \| "away" \| "busy"` |  | A green, amber or red dot on the corner – added to the accessible name, e.g. "Mara Lindqvist, online" |
| kind | `"person" \| "agent"` | `"person"` | agent: the agent's own 3×3 pixel mark on a white tile instead of initials – never a monogram. A src still shows its logo |
| seed | `string` | `name` | What the color and an agent's pattern are made from – pass a stable id so a rename keeps them |
| color | `string` | `blue` | agent: the mark's color – use the same color the agent has elsewhere |
| working | `boolean` |  | agent: the squares twinkle in a diagonal wave while it works |
| ...span props | `ComponentProps<"span">` |  | className, style, title, aria-label, aria-hidden, ref and the rest go to the outer <span> |
| AvatarGroup max | `number` | `4` | How many show before the rest becomes +N (99+ above 99) |
| AvatarGroup size | `20 \| 24 \| 32 \| 40` | `32` | Sets the size of every Avatar in it and of the +N |
| AvatarGroup total | `number` |  | How many there are in all, when you pass only the first few – +N counts from it |

### Accessibility

- With a name it is an image named after the person (role="img"), plus the status – "Jonas Weber, away"
- Next to the written name, pass aria-hidden so screen readers don't say the name twice; without a name it is hidden on its own
- The picture itself has an empty alt – the name is on the avatar, never read twice
- AvatarGroup is a group: give it an aria-label like "9 reviewers"; +N reads "5 more"
- The status color is never the only signal – it is part of the accessible name

### Motion

- A picture fades in once it has loaded, over the initials – no empty circle while it loads
- working: the agent's squares fade down and back in a diagonal wave, 1.2s
- With prefers-reduced-motion the picture appears at once and the mark stays still

### Responsive

- Initials are whole characters (Intl.Segmenter): accents, emoji with skin tones and flags never split; a name that starts with an emoji shows just that emoji
- "III", "Jr." and the like don't make an initial, nor do brackets or quotes in front of a word – "Christopher Montgomery III" is CM
- Right-to-left: the status dot and the overlap mirror to the other side
- The group's ring and the status ring use --ui-avtc-ring – set it to the background the avatars sit on (white by default)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Agents never get initials, sparkles or a bot glyph – always kind="agent" with the agent's id as seed
- Pass a stable id as seed, so a person's color doesn't change when they edit their name

### Requirements

- React 19

# Away Summary, clean style (Pro)

The “While you were away” card for a chat thread – right where you left off: how long you were gone, what needs you, what failed and what's done as a short list with one action per row; Got it folds it into a one-line divider

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/away-summary
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/away-summary-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/away-summary-clean`

### When to use

- Coming back to a chat with an agent that kept working – the card sits in the thread right where you left off
- A short catch-up: what needs you first, then what failed, then what's done, each with one action
- A thread that should stay a thread – Got it folds the card into a one-line divider

### When not to use

- A full overnight recap with a chart and a board of what needs you – use Agent Recap
- Every message and request of many agents in one place – use Agent Inbox
- Approving one step of a run in detail – use Approval Gates

### Usage

```tsx
import { AwaySummary, type AwayItem } from "@/components/ui/away-summary-clean";

const items: AwayItem[] = [
  { id: "ingest", title: "Ingest pipeline", kind: "needs-you", detail: "Waiting on: Which queue – Kafka or SQS?" },
  { id: "billing", title: "Billing sync", kind: "failed", detail: "Failed: rate limit on Stripe" },
  { id: "auth", title: "Auth refactor", kind: "done", detail: "Opened PR #482" },
];

export function Thread() {
  return (
    <>
      {messagesBefore}
      <AwaySummary since={lastSeenAt} items={items} onAction={(id) => openTask(id)} onDismiss={() => markSeen()} />
      {messagesAfter}
    </>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| since | `Date \| number \| string` |  | When the person left – the head reads how long ago (2h 14m), or since 9:40 with timeStyle="clock" |
| items | `AwayItem[]` |  | { id, title, kind, detail?, action? } – what happened, any order; what needs you comes first |
| kind | `"needs-you" \| "failed" \| "done"` |  | Per item – sets the mark, the order and the default action (Decide, Retry, Open) |
| action | `string \| false` |  | Per item – the button's label; false leaves the row without one |
| onAction | `(id, item) => void \| Promise` |  | A row's action was pressed. Return a promise and the button shows it working until it settles |
| onDismiss | `() => void` |  | Got it was pressed – store that the person has seen it |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `boolean` | `false` | Folded into the divider – controlled, or where it starts |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed) => void` |  | Folded or opened from the card or the divider |
| limit | `number` | `5` | Rows before Show N more |
| timeStyle | `"duration" \| "clock"` | `"duration"` | 2h 14m, or since 9:40 |
| now | `Date \| number` |  | Now – defaults to the clock, updated every half minute |
| labels | `Partial<AwaySummaryLabels>` |  | Every word on it – title, counts, actions, Show more, Got it, the divider |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the row actions in list order, then Show more and Got it
- Enter / Space: Runs the focused action; on Got it the card folds and focus moves to the divider; on the divider it opens again
- Esc: Inside the card: fold it – focus lands on the divider, and opening again brings it back to the action you left from (else the first action)
- Enter: On Show more: the rows grow open and focus moves to the first new row's action, so Tab reads on from there; Show less keeps focus on the button

### Accessibility

- A region named "While you were away" with a heading that says how long; the rows are a list
- Every action says which task – "Decide: Ingest pipeline" – and each row says its state in words, never color alone
- Got it and the divider are buttons with aria-expanded; the folded part is inert, so Tab never lands in it
- When an item changes, a polite live region says so – "Ingest pipeline: done. 1 needs you"
- Focus never drops to the page: a working button stays focusable (aria-disabled, not disabled), and when a row loses its button or the card folds from outside, focus moves to the next action or the divider

### Motion

```tsx
import { AwaySummary, type AwayItem } from "@/components/ui/away-summary";
```

# Breadcrumb, clean style (Free)

Where a page sits and the way back up – links with quiet separators, the current page last, a long middle folded into a … menu, long names shortened with the full one on hover

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/breadcrumb
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/breadcrumb-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/breadcrumb-clean`

### When to use

- Where a page sits in a hierarchy: workspace, agent, runs, the run
- Going back up several levels in one press – files and folders, a settings section, an issue in a project
- Deep trails: the middle folds into a … menu past maxItems, and on its own when the row gets narrow

### When not to use

- Moving between pages of one list – use the Pagination
- Switching between views on the same level – use the Segmented Control or tabs
- Steps of a flow the user goes through in order – use the Stepper Form
- Picking another workspace or project from the trail – put a Dropdown Menu on that crumb yourself

### Usage

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "@/components/ui/breadcrumb-clean";

export function RunHeader({ agent, run }: { agent: { id: string; name: string }; run: { title: string } }) {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb
      items={[
        { label: "Agents", href: "/agents" },
        { label: agent.name, href: `/agents/${agent.id}` },
        { label: "Runs", href: `/agents/${agent.id}/runs` },
        { label: run.title },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `BreadcrumbItem[]` |  | From the top down; the last one is the page you are on – shown in ink, not a link, marked aria-current="page" |
| items[].label | `string` |  | The name. Long ones shorten with … at 200px and show in full on hover |
| items[].href | `string` |  | Makes the crumb a link |
| items[].onClick | `(event) => void` |  | Without href the crumb is a button; with href it runs first (call preventDefault to navigate with a router) |

```tsx
import { BreakdownChart } from "@/components/ui/breakdown-chart-clean";

const dimensions = [

  { key: "priority", label: "Priority", values: ["High", "Medium", "Low"], colors: { High: "#e5484d", Medium: "#3c85e9" } },
];
const measures = [
  { key: "count", label: "Task count", unit: "tasks" },
  { key: "points", label: "Story points", unit: "points", field: "points" },
];

export function Sprint({ tasks }) {
  return <BreakdownChart title="Sprint 24" records={tasks} dimensions={dimensions} measures={measures} />;
}
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

- React 19

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button-clean";
```

- When label or icon change, the width glides to the new size and the new content fades in from a soft blur
- With prefers-reduced-motion the sweep stops and changes are instant

### Responsive

- On touch screens (pointer: coarse) every size grows to a comfortable tap height; the look stays the same
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19
