# Card, clean style (Free)

The card every screen is built from – header with title, quiet line and an action, content and a footer, the whole card a click target and a gray fill when selected

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/card
- Section: Components · Cards
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/card-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/card-clean`

### When to use

- A self-contained thing on a page: an agent, a project, an integration, a plan – with its name, a line about it and an action
- A settings group: its title and note on top, the fields inside, Save in the footer
- A grid or list of things to open – interactive, with a link as the title
- A small set of choices shown as cards – interactive and selected, with aria-pressed on the title's button

### When not to use

- A floating panel on top of the page – use the Popover or the Dialog
- Rows of a long list – plain rows with hairlines between them read faster than a stack of cards
- Only a line between groups – use the Separator
- One of the purpose-built cards: Approval Card, Decision Card, Project Card – they come with their behavior

### Usage

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardFooter, CardHeader } from "@/components/ui/card-clean";

export function AgentCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader
        title="Support triage"
        description="Sorts new tickets and drafts the first reply"
        action={<button aria-label="More">⋯</button>}
      />
      <CardContent>142 tickets this week · 96% resolved</CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        Running · started 2 min ago
        <button style={{ marginInlineStart: "auto" }}>Open</button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Card · as | `"div" \| "section" \| "article" \| "li"` | `"div"` | The element it renders as – li inside a <ul> of cards, section or article when it stands for a part of the page |
| Card · interactive | `boolean` |  | The whole card is a click target: it lifts on hover and a link or button in the title stretches over the card. Other buttons and links inside stay clickable on their own |
| Card · selected | `boolean` |  | Shown as picked: a gray fill and a firmer edge, no colored ring. Say it to screen readers too – aria-pressed or aria-current on the title's button or link |
| CardHeader · title | `ReactNode` |  | The title, in an h3 by default. A link or button here makes an interactive card clickable |
| CardHeader · description | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line or two under the title |
| CardHeader · icon | `ReactNode` |  | Something small at the start – an icon, a logo, an agent's mark or a tile with one |
| CardHeader · action | `ReactNode` |  | At the end of the title line, centred on it: an icon button, a menu, a badge |
| CardHeader · titleAs | `"h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "p"` | `"h3"` | The title's element – pick the level that fits your page, or p for cards in a list of choices |
| CardHeader · children | `ReactNode` |  | Anything more under the title and description, e.g. a row of badges |
| CardContent | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | The card's body – any content |
| CardFooter | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | A row at the bottom of the card in quiet 12px text. Status or meta on the start; give the first button marginInlineStart: auto to push the buttons to the end. Last inside Card |
| ...props | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | className, style, id, ref, onClick and the rest go to each part's element |

### Keyboard

- Tab: An interactive card is reached through the link or button in its title – the ring goes around the whole card – then through the other buttons inside
- Enter: Opens the title's link or presses its button
- Space: Presses the title's button

### Accessibility

- The title is a real heading (h3 by default), so screen-reader users can jump from card to card
- Interactive cards keep one click target – a link or button in the title – instead of a clickable <div>, so it's announced with its name and works from the keyboard
- Buttons inside an interactive card stay separate targets above the stretched title; don't nest a second link that does the same thing
- Selected is shown with a gray fill and edge, not color – say it with aria-pressed or aria-current as well
- In Windows high-contrast mode the card keeps a visible edge, and a selected card a highlighted one

### Motion

- An interactive card's shadow deepens on hover over 160ms
- With prefers-reduced-motion it changes without the transition

### Responsive

- Fills its container's width – set width on a grid or the card's style
- Long titles and unbreakable words wrap inside the card instead of pushing it wider; the footer wraps its buttons onto a new line when narrow
- No hover lift on touch screens, so it doesn't stick after a tap
- Logical properties – right-to-left text mirrors the header and the footer
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Keep a card to one thing: a title, a line about it, at most one primary action
- In a grid of cards, give every card the same parts so they line up – an empty description still takes no room
- For choices, mark only the picked card selected; keep the others as they are rather than graying them out

- React 19

### Keyboard

- Tab: An interactive card is reached through the link or button in its title – the ring goes around the whole card – then through the other buttons inside
- Enter: Opens the title's link or presses its button
- Space: Presses the title's button

### Accessibility

- The title is a real heading (h3 by default), so screen-reader users can jump from card to card
- Interactive cards keep one click target – a link or button in the title – instead of a clickable <div>, so it's announced with its name and works from the keyboard
- Buttons inside an interactive card stay separate targets above the stretched title; don't nest a second link that does the same thing
- Selected is shown with a gray fill and edge, not color – say it with aria-pressed or aria-current as well
- In Windows high-contrast mode the card keeps a visible edge, and a selected card a highlighted one

### Motion

- An interactive card's shadow deepens on hover over 160ms
- With prefers-reduced-motion it changes without the transition

### Responsive

- Fills its container's width – set width on a grid or the card's style
- Long titles and unbreakable words wrap inside the card instead of pushing it wider; the footer wraps its buttons onto a new line when narrow
- No hover lift on touch screens, so it doesn't stick after a tap
- Logical properties – right-to-left text mirrors the header and the footer
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Keep a card to one thing: a title, a line about it, at most one primary action
- In a grid of cards, give every card the same parts so they line up – an empty description still takes no room
- For choices, mark only the picked card selected; keep the others as they are rather than graying them out

# Checkbox, clean style (Free)

A real checkbox with a label and a second line, a some-of-them state for Select all, an error and a card row – the check draws itself

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/checkbox
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/checkbox-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/checkbox-clean`

### When to use

- Yes or no choices that are saved with a form: agreeing to terms, picking several items of a list, opting in
- Select all over a list – the some-of-them state shows a dash while only part of it is picked

### When not to use

- A setting that applies the moment you flip it – use the Switch
- One choice out of several – use radio buttons, the Segmented Control or the Select

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/ui/checkbox-clean";

export function Topics() {
  const all = ["mentions", "approvals", "summary"];
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState<string[]>([]);

  return (
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Email me about</legend>
      <Checkbox
        label="Everything"
        checked={picked.length === all.length}
        indeterminate={picked.length > 0 && picked.length < all.length}
        onChange={() => setPicked(picked.length === all.length ? [] : all)}
      />
      {all.map((id) => (
        <Checkbox
          key={id}
          label={id}
          checked={picked.includes(id)}
          onChange={(e) => setPicked((p) => (e.target.checked ? [...p, id] : p.filter((x) => x !== id)))}
        />
      ))}
    </fieldset>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown next to the box; clicking it toggles |
| description | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet second line under the label, linked with aria-describedby |
| indeterminate | `boolean` | `false` | Some of them – a dash instead of the check; set it on a Select all whose list is partly picked |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks it invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message under it |
| variant | `"plain" \| "card"` | `"plain"` | card: a bordered row that is clickable as a whole; checked, its edge turns dark |
| ...input props | `ComponentProps<"input">` |  | checked, defaultChecked, onChange, name, value, required, disabled, ref – everything goes to the real checkbox |

### Keyboard

- Space: Toggles it
- Tab: Moves to the next checkbox – each one is its own stop, as with native checkboxes

### Accessibility

- A real <input type="checkbox"> inside its <label>: forms, screen readers and the some-of-them state (mixed) work as with any checkbox
- The description and the error are linked with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid and is announced politely
- Group related ones in a <fieldset> with a <legend>, so the question is read with each choice
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click

### Motion

- The box fills and the check draws itself; the dash grows from the middle
- A press nudges the box a little smaller
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Long labels wrap; the box stays on the first line
- Touch screens get a 20px box, 15px text and a hit area larger than the box
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19

### When to use

### Usage

```tsx
import { CitedAnswer, type CitedSegment, type CitedSource } from "@/components/ui/cited-answer-clean";

const sources: CitedSource[] = [
  {
    id: "caching",
    site: "Tokenwise",
    title: "Prompt caching, explained",
    url: "https://tokenwise.dev/blog/prompt-caching",
    date: "Sep 18, 2026",
    quote: "A cached prefix is read instead of recomputed …",
    highlight: ["read instead of recomputed"],
  },
];

const segments: CitedSegment[] = [
  { text: "Prompt caching reuses the processed start of your prompt.", cite: ["caching"] },
  { text: " Streaming makes the rest feel faster." },
];

export function Answer() {
  return <CitedAnswer segments={segments} sources={sources} pagesRead={12} />;
}
```

| sources | `CitedSource[]` |  | { id, title, site, url?, date?, quote?, highlight?, icon? } – numbered in this order, one chip each |

# Code Block, clean style (Free)

Code to read and copy – a header with the file name or language and a copy button, line numbers, highlighted lines, long lines that scroll inside and a small built-in colorizer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/code-block
- Section: Components · Text
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/code-block-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/code-block-clean`

### When to use

- Showing code someone will copy: an install command, a config file, an API example, a snippet an agent wrote
- Tool inputs and outputs, logs or JSON payloads that need to keep their exact spacing
- Pointing at a few lines – highlightLines marks them, showLineNumbers lets people refer to them

### When not to use

- A single name or value inside a sentence – use an inline <code> or a Kbd chip for shortcuts
- A secret someone copies once, like an API key – a read-only Text Field with a copy button fits better
- Comparing two versions of code – use the Inline Diff
- A whole tool call with its arguments and result – use the Tool Call Card

### Usage

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@/components/ui/code-block-clean";

export function ReviewerConfig() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock
      language="ts"
      filename="agents/reviewer.ts"
      showLineNumbers
      highlightLines={[8, 9]}
      code={`import { defineAgent } from "@acme/agents";

export const reviewer = defineAgent({
  name: "Code reviewer",
  model: "claude-opus",
  tools: ["github", "linear"],
  // Ask before anything leaves the repo
  approval: { required: true, timeout: "2h" },
  maxSteps: 24,
});`}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code | `string` |  | Required. The code – copied exactly as given; one trailing newline isn't shown as an empty line |
| language | `string` |  | ts, tsx, js, jsx, json, bash, sh, python … – TypeScript / JavaScript, JSON, Bash and Python are colored, anything else is plain text. Named in the header when there is no filename |
| filename | `string` |  | Shown in the header instead of the language; long names end in … with the full name as a tooltip |
| showLineNumbers | `boolean` | `false` | Numbers in front of every line – they stay in place while long lines scroll sideways and are left out when code is selected |
| highlightLines | `number[]` |  | Lines to mark, counted from 1 – a light tint with a thin edge on the left |
| wrap | `boolean` | `false` | Long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways |
| maxHeight | `number \| string` |  | After this height the code scrolls inside, e.g. 320 or "40vh" |
| copyable | `boolean` | `true` | The copy button; without it and without a filename or language there is no header |
| onCopy | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called after the code was copied, e.g. to show a toast |
| className / style | `string / CSSProperties` |  | On the root <figure> |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves to the copy button, then into the code when it scrolls
- Enter / Space: Copies the code (on the copy button)
- ← / → / ↑ / ↓: Scroll the code when it's focused

### Accessibility

- A <figure> with the header as its <figcaption>, the code in <pre><code>
- The copy button is named Copy code, then Copied; a polite status also announces Copied
- When the code scrolls it becomes a focusable region, so keyboard users can scroll it; when it fits it's not a tab stop
- Line numbers are hidden from screen readers and can't be selected, so copying by hand gives clean code
- Code always runs left to right, also in right-to-left pages; the file name follows its own direction
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click

### Motion

- On copy the copy glyph blurs away into a check, which turns back after 1.4s
- With prefers-reduced-motion it swaps instantly

### Responsive

- Never wider than its container: long lines scroll inside the card (or wrap with wrap) instead of stretching the page
- Touch screens get a bigger hit area around the copy button
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Collaboration Stream, clean style (Pro)

What agents actually say to each other – a quiet chat where every message shows who it is from and who it is for, handoffs and questions for you tagged, files as chips that open a preview, a card with details under every message, and a composer to name agents with @ or answer a question

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/collaboration-stream
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/collaboration-stream-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/collaboration-stream-clean`

### When to use

- Showing what the agents of a run say to each other – not just who started whom, but the actual messages, handoffs and questions
- Multi-agent runs where you step in: a question for you is tagged, and you answer it or name an agent with @ right from the composer
- Live runs, where messages come in while the agents work and the stream follows the newest one

### When not to use

- Who started whom, at a glance – use Agent Tree
- What every agent did over time, side by side – use Agent Lanes
- A chat between one person and one assistant – use Chat Composer with your own message list
- Requests that wait for a person across many runs – use Agent Inbox

### Usage

```tsx
import { CollaborationStream, type StreamAgent, type StreamMessage } from "@/components/ui/collaboration-stream-clean";

const agents: StreamAgent[] = [
  { id: "orch", name: "Orchestrator", model: "Opus 5.5" },
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", model: "Gemini 3.8 Flash" },
];

const messages: StreamMessage[] = [
  { id: "m1", from: "you", to: "orch", kind: "ask", text: "Launch the new pricing page by Friday.", at: "14:02" },
  { id: "m2", from: "orch", to: "research", kind: "spawn", text: "Find out what the others charge per seat." },
  { id: "m3", from: "research", to: "orch", kind: "share", text: "Linear $10, Notion $12, Figma $15 per seat.", at: "14:04",
    replyTo: "m2", attachments: [{ label: "pricing-table.csv" }] },
];

export function RunChat() {
  return <CollaborationStream agents={agents} messages={messages} task="Launch the new pricing page" live />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `StreamAgent[]` |  | { id, name, model?, avatar? } – every agent gets its own pixel mark and color in this order; avatar swaps the mark for a logo |
| messages | `StreamMessage[]` |  | { id, from, to, kind, text, at?, replyTo?, typing?, attachments?, details? } – in the order they were sent; from and to are agent ids, "you" or (to) "all" |
| kind | `"ask" \| "reply" \| "handoff" \| "share" \| "question" \| "spawn"` |  | Per message – a handoff is tagged, a question to you says Needs you, a spawn is a quiet line "X started Y" |
| replyTo | `string` |  | Per message – the id it answers; it shows as a quote unless that message is right above, and a click on the quote jumps there |
| typing | `boolean` |  | Per message – still being written: Writing… shimmers and the sender's mark twinkles |
| attachments | `StreamAttachment[]` |  | Per message – { label, kind?, preview?, meta? } as gray chips; a click opens the preview window. kind is told from the label when left out: "…/" a folder, .csv a table |
| details | `StreamDetails` |  | Per message – { facts?, items? } shown in a card under the message when it's clicked |
| task | `string` |  | What the run is about – part of the stream's label |
| live | `boolean` | `false` | The run is still going – a Live dot, and the stream follows new messages unless you scrolled up |
| selected | `string \| null` |  | Controlled id of the picked message – its details open, the rest fades |
| onSelectedChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | A message was picked or let go |
| focusAgent | `string \| null` |  | Controlled id of the agent whose messages stay – the tabs on top |

# Color Picker, clean style (Free)

A swatch button that opens a color card – saturation and brightness, hue and optional opacity by drag or arrows, a hex field that also reads rgb(), named presets, a hex string as the value

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/color-picker
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/color-picker-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/color-picker-clean`

### When to use

- Picking a color that belongs to something: an agent, a project, a label, a calendar
- Brand or theme settings where any color is allowed, with a few presets to start from
- ColorPickerPanel: the same card right in a form or a settings page, without the button

### When not to use

- Only a handful of fixed colors – a row of swatches as a radio group (the presets alone) or the Toggle Group is quicker
- A color that is really a status or a kind – use the Select or the Segmented Control with named options
- Anything that isn't a color – the Popover is the base for other small floating forms

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { ColorPicker } from "@/components/ui/color-picker-clean";

const PRESETS = [
  { value: "#0190fe", label: "Blue" },
  { value: "#13b3a0", label: "Teal" },
  { value: "#e8b000", label: "Amber" },
  { value: "#a651f0", label: "Purple" },
];

export function AgentColor({ onSave }: { onSave: (hex: string) => void }) {
  const [color, setColor] = useState("#0190fe");

  return (
    <ColorPicker
      label="Agent color"
      value={color}
      onValueChange={setColor}
      onOpenChange={(open) => !open && onSave(color)}
      presets={PRESETS}
      align="end"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string` |  | The color as lowercase hex – "#0190fe", or "#0190fecc" when alpha is on and opacity is below 100%. From outside it also takes #rgb and rgb() |
| defaultValue | `string` | `"#0190fe"` | The starting color when value isn't controlled |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called on every change, while dragging too |
| alpha | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the opacity slider and its percentage; without it, opacity in a value is dropped |
| presets | `(string \| { value: string; label: string })[]` |  | Round swatches under the sliders; a label is read out and shown as the tooltip (a plain string reads as its hex) |
| open | `boolean` |  | ColorPicker only – whether the card is open; leave it out to let the picker handle it |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | ColorPicker only – open from the first render, without taking the focus |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | ColorPicker only – called when the button, a press outside, Escape or tabbing away opens or closes it |
| label | `string` | `"Color"` | ColorPicker only – what the color is for; names the button ("Agent color: #0190FE") and the card |
| showValue | `boolean` | `true` | ColorPicker only – the hex next to the swatch; off: a square swatch button |
| size | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | ColorPicker only – a 24 or 28px high button; bigger on touch screens |
| side | `"bottom" \| "top"` | `"bottom"` | ColorPicker only – where the card opens; it flips when there is more room on the other side |
| align | `"start" \| "end"` | `"start"` | ColorPicker only – which edges line up; switches when it would stick out |
| name | `string` |  | ColorPicker only – sends the hex with a form (a hidden input) |
| ...button / div props | `ComponentProps<"button"> \| ComponentProps<"div">` |  | ColorPicker: disabled, aria-label, id, ref … go to the button. ColorPickerPanel: className, style, aria-label … go to its box |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the button: opens the card, the focus lands on the area
- ← / →: Area: less or more saturation · sliders: down or up by 1
- ↑ / ↓: Area: brighter or darker · sliders: up or down by 1
- Shift / Arrows: Steps of 10
- Page Up / Page Down: Area: brightness by 10 · sliders: by 10
- Home / End: Area: no or full saturation · sliders: the start or the end
- Enter: In the hex field: takes what you typed (#rgb waits for this; six digits and rgb() apply as you type)
- Arrows: In the presets: moves to the next swatch and picks it – one tab stop for all of them
- Esc: Closes the card – the focus goes back to the button

### Accessibility

- The area and every slider are role="slider" with a name and a spoken value: "Saturation 64%, brightness 99%", "210°, blue", "80%"
- The button says what the color is for and which one it is ("Agent color: #A651F0"), with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded
- The card is a non-modal dialog named by label; it takes the focus only when it is opened, never from the first render
- The presets are a radio group with names – "Blue" instead of a hex – so the chosen one is announced
- The hex field has no ring, only a firmer edge; a value it can't read gets a red edge and aria-invalid on Enter, and is dropped when you leave
- Rings show only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click or a drag

### Motion

- The card fades and scales in from the corner it is attached to
- Swatches grow a little on hover
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears and changes at once

### Responsive

- Dragging captures the pointer, so you can drag past the card's edge and the thumb stays at the end
- The hex is set in a fixed-width face, so the button doesn't change size while you drag
- The card lives in the top layer, follows its button on scroll and resize, and stays fully on screen; 256px wide, it fits a 320px phone
- The sliders always run left to right, also in right-to-left pages – a color scale isn't text
- Touch screens get a taller area, bigger thumbs and swatches, and 16px in the hex field so iOS doesn't zoom in
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/combobox
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/combobox-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/combobox-clean`

### When to use

- Assigning people, labels, tags or projects – anything picked from a list that's too long to scan
- Filters where several values can apply at once, like owners or statuses
- Tag fields that should also accept new values (creatable)

### When not to use

- Up to five fixed choices – checkboxes or a segmented control show them all at once
- Free text with no list behind it – use a plain input
- Running actions rather than picking values – use the command menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { Combobox, type ComboboxOption } from "@/components/ui/combobox-clean";

const people: ComboboxOption[] = [
  { value: "maya", label: "Maya Chen", hint: "Product Designer", avatar: true, group: "Design" },
  { value: "sara", label: "Sara Okafor", hint: "Staff Engineer", avatar: "/avatars/sara.jpg", group: "Engineering" },
  { value: "elif", label: "Elif Yilmaz", hint: "Head of Product", avatar: true, group: "Product" },
];

export function Reviewers() {
  const [reviewers, setReviewers] = useState<string[]>(["maya"]);
  return (
    <Combobox
      label="Reviewers"
      options={people}
      value={reviewers}
      onChange={setReviewers}
      placeholder="Add reviewers…"
      maxVisibleTags={4}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options | `{ value, label, hint?, avatar?, color?, icon?, group?, keywords? }[]` |  | The list. avatar is an image URL or true for initials; options with the same group are listed under one title |
| multiple | `boolean` | `true` | Pick many (chips) or one – one closes the list after picking |
| value | `string[]` |  | Controlled values (also for single choice, with at most one entry) |
| defaultValue | `string[]` | `[]` | Starting values when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value: string[], options: ComboboxOption[]) => void` |  | Called on every pick, removal or creation |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Search…"` | Shown while nothing is picked |
| creatable | `boolean` | `false` | Offer a create row when no option matches the typed text exactly |
| onCreate | `(text: string) => ComboboxOption \| void` |  | Builds the new option – defaults to { value: text, label: text } |
| createLabel | `(text: string) => string` | `Create “…”` | Text of the create row, e.g. Invite “…” |
| maxVisibleTags | `number` |  | An upper limit for the chips. The field always stays one line – chips that don't fit go into a "+3" chip on their own |
| label | `string` |  | Visible label above the field (also names the list) |

| emptyText | `string` | `"No results"` | Shown when nothing matches |

# Commit Trail, clean style (Pro)

One line per commit with a tinted check on a blue trail, the message, a colored tag for the kind of change and how long ago; open a commit for who wrote it (agents with their pixel mark), the hash and what changed. A merge folds the commits it brought in, which bend off the trail as small dots. While an agent commits its marker turns and "Committing" shimmers, and when it lands the check draws itself

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/commit-trail
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/commit-trail-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/commit-trail-clean`

### When to use

- A branch's history where people and agents both commit – who wrote what, at a glance
- A side panel or a PR page that shows recent commits, with merged branches folded away until you want them
- Live: an agent that commits while you watch – its marker turns at the top until the commit lands

### When not to use

- The change itself, line by line – use Inline Diff or Diff Timeline
- The steps an agent works through, not what it committed – use Agent Trail
- A full branch graph with many parallel lines and cross merges – this shows one branch and the branches merged into it

### Usage

```tsx
import { CommitTrail, type TrailCommit } from "@/components/ui/commit-trail-clean";

const claude = { name: "Claude", agent: true };

const commits: TrailCommit[] = [
  { id: "a41c7e2b", message: "Release 3.1", author: { name: "Mara Lind" }, time: Date.now() - 26 * 60_000, tag: "v3.1" },
  {
    id: "9be20f11",
    message: "Merge `invoice-pdf` into `main`",
    author: { name: "Tomás Reyes" },
    time: "2026-11-13T09:10:00Z",
    commits: [
      { id: "d7a90c4e", message: "Render line items as a PDF table", author: claude, added: 286, removed: 22 },
      { id: "53f1b8a0", message: "Embed fonts in invoice exports", author: { name: "Tomás Reyes" }, coAuthor: claude },
    ],
  },
  { id: "e02c6d97", message: "Fix rounding on prorated plans", author: { name: "Kai Brandt" }, kind: "fix", files: 2, added: 18, removed: 9 },
];

export function History() {
  return <CommitTrail commits={commits} branches={["main", "invoice-pdf"]} hasMore />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| commits | `TrailCommit[]` |  | Newest first – { id, message, author, coAuthor?, time?, tag?, files?, added?, removed?, body?, commits?, pending? } |
| author / coAuthor | `{ name; agent?; color?; avatar? }` |  | Who wrote it – shown when the commit is open, "Ines Okoro with Claude": an agent with its pixel mark before its name (in its color, blue when there is one), a person with avatar – your own icon or symbol – when you give one. The rows themselves stay quiet; screen readers hear the names on every row |
| time | `number \| Date \| string` |  | When – ms, a Date or ISO text, shown on the right as "now", 4m, 2h, 3d, 1w, 5mo, 2y and in full when open; other text shows as it is |
| commit.commits | `TrailCommit[]` |  | On a merge: the commits of the branch it brought in – the row folds them, with a chevron on hover; open, they bend off the trail as small dots with their kind and when on the right |
| message | `string` |  | One line – put branch and file names in backticks ("Merge `invoice-pdf` into `main`") and they show as light chips: a file (it has an extension) with the file icon, anything else with the branch icon |
| refs | `Record<string, string>` |  | More about the names in messages – rest the pointer on one for 0.4s and a compact dark tooltip shows above it: its icon, its name and this text (File or Branch without one) ("src/webhooks/queue.ts", "3 commits, merged by Tomás Reyes") |
| kind | `string` |  | What kind of change – a colored tag on the right, before the time: feat (Feature, green), fix (orange), refactor (violet), perf (teal), docs (blue), test (Tests, amber), chore (gray), release (pink), merge (indigo), or a kind of your own |
| kinds | `Record<string, { label?; color? }>` |  | Rename a kind or add your own with its color – { feat: { label: "New" }, ui: { label: "UI", color: "#ee3e9e" } }; a kind without a color is gray |

# Compact Breakdown, clean style (Pro)

A total split into its parts in one small card – numbers roll, the bar glides and the ranked rows trade places when the period changes

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/compact-breakdown
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/compact-breakdown-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/compact-breakdown-clean`

### When to use

- One number and what it is made of – revenue by channel, usage by feature, tokens by model, tickets by category
- Dashboards where the card sits next to others and a full chart would be too much
- Whenever people switch between periods and should see what moved

### When not to use

- Trends over time – a line chart shows those; this card compares the parts of one total
- More than about seven parts – group the small ones into "Other" first
- Several measures and slicing options – use Breakdown Chart

### Usage

```tsx
import { CompactBreakdown } from "@/components/ui/compact-breakdown-clean";

export function RevenueByChannel() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = useState("30d");
  const { items, delta } = useRevenue(period); // [{ label: "Direct", value: 16900 }, …]
  return (
    <CompactBreakdown
      title="Revenue by channel"
      periods={[
        { id: "7d", label: "7d" },
        { id: "30d", label: "30d" },
        { id: "90d", label: "90d" },
      ]}
      period={period}
      onPeriodChange={setPeriod}
      items={items}
      delta={delta}
      format={(n) => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString("en-US")}`}
      totalLabel="Total revenue"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `BreakdownItem[]` |  | { id?, label, value, color? } – the parts of the shown period; the list ranks them by value. Give an id when labels can change |
| title | `string` | `"Breakdown"` | Heading of the card |
| periods | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the period switch – no switch when left out |
| period | `string` |  | Controlled period id |
| defaultPeriod | `string` | `first period` | Starting period when uncontrolled |
| onPeriodChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new period – pass the matching items and delta back in |
| delta | `number` |  | Change against the previous period in percent (12.4 or -3) – a small green or red tag next to the total |
| format | `(value: number) => string` | `whole numbers with separators` | Formats every value – the total, the rows and the hovered part |
| totalLabel | `string` | `"Total"` | Line under the big number while nothing is hovered |
| footer | `ReactNode \| null` | `"Largest: <part>"` | Replaces the last row of the card (under a hairline); null hides it |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves to the period switch, then through the rows – a focused row is highlighted like a hovered one
- ← / →: In the period switch: previous or next period (wraps around)
- Home / End: In the period switch: first or last period

### Accessibility

- A group named by its title; the period switch is a radiogroup with one tab stop
- The rolling numbers are aria-hidden – screen readers get the final total and the change in one sentence, and every row with its value and share
- Rows can be focused, so the highlight and the part's value are reachable without a mouse
- The bar is decorative: everything it shows is in the list

### Motion

- On a new period every number rolls to its value in one shared tween, so the total, the rows and the bar move in step
- The bar keeps each part's place and color and only glides to the new widths
- Rows slide to their new rank when the order changes; a part that is not in the new period folds away
- Hovering a part dims the others, lifts its segment and rolls the big number to that part's value – leaving rolls it back to the total
- The light fill of the period switch slides to the chosen option in a short, crisp move; the change tag pops in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 360px; below 250px the share column goes and the values stay
- Touch screens: taller rows and period options
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Keep the same id (or label) for a part across periods – that is what lets rows and bar segments animate instead of being replaced
- Pass raw numbers and do the formatting in format, so the rolling values stay smooth

### Requirements

- React 19

# Conflict Radar, clean style (Pro)

Agents working on their own branches at once, and where they get in each other's way – a row per file and a column per agent, a line between the agents that changed the same lines, each agent's way in one sentence to pick from, and Merge once all are settled

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/conflict-radar
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/conflict-radar-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/conflict-radar-clean`

### When to use

- Several coding agents work on their own branches of the same repo at once, and people need to see where they overlap before anything is merged
- Agents came up with different ways to solve the same thing and someone has to pick one

### When not to use

- When the agents try the same task and the best one simply wins – use Parallel Attempts
- When the timeline matters – use Agent Lanes
- For a single agent's changes – use Agent Ledger

### Usage

```tsx
import { ConflictRadar, type RadarAgent, type RadarFile } from "@/components/ui/conflict-radar-clean";

export function Branches({ agents, files }: { agents: RadarAgent[]; files: RadarFile[] }) {
  const [resolved, setResolved] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  return (
    <ConflictRadar
      agents={agents} // { id, name, model?, avatar?, status?: "running" | "done" }
      files={files} // { path, edits: [{ agentId, lines: [from, to], summary?, active? }] }
      resolved={resolved}
      onResolve={(path, agentId) => setResolved((r) => ({ ...r, [path]: agentId }))}
      onMerge={() => mergeBranches(resolved)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `RadarAgent[]` |  | One column each: name, model or branch, a mark, and whether it's still working |
| files | `RadarFile[]` |  | One row each, with every agent's edit – the lines it changes, whether it's still writing, and for conflicts its way in one sentence |
| title | `string` | `"Parallel work"` | Heading in the bar |
| resolved | `Record<string, string>` |  | The agent picked per conflicting file – leave it out and the component keeps the picks itself |
| onResolve | `(path: string, agentId: string) => void` |  | A way was picked for a conflict |
| onMerge | `() => void` |  | Merge was clicked – it's only enabled once every conflict is settled and every agent is done |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through Merge, the conflicting files and the ways to settle the one in focus
- Enter / Space: On a conflicting file: shows its ways below; on a way: keeps it

### Accessibility

- The grid is a table with the agents as column headers; every cell says who changed the file and whether it was kept
- Conflicts and settled files are named in text, not only by color
- The ways to settle a conflict are a radio group
- The comparison is a polite live region, so the next conflict is announced when it comes into focus

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/conflict-radar
- Section: Components · Agents

- Import: `@/components/ui/conflict-radar`

### When to use

- Several coding agents work on their own branches of the same repo at once, and people need to see where they overlap before anything is merged
- Agents came up with different ways to solve the same thing and someone has to pick one

### When not to use

- When the agents try the same task and the best one simply wins – use Parallel Attempts
- When the timeline matters – use Agent Lanes
- For a single agent's changes – use Agent Ledger

### Usage

```tsx
import { ConflictRadar, type RadarAgent, type RadarFile } from "@/components/ui/conflict-radar";

export function Branches({ agents, files }: { agents: RadarAgent[]; files: RadarFile[] }) {
  const [resolved, setResolved] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  return (
    <ConflictRadar
      agents={agents} // { id, name, model?, avatar?, status?: "running" | "done" }
      files={files} // { path, edits: [{ agentId, lines: [from, to], summary?, active? }] }
      resolved={resolved}
      onResolve={(path, agentId) => setResolved((r) => ({ ...r, [path]: agentId }))}
      onMerge={() => mergeBranches(resolved)}

  );
}
```

# Context Map, clean style (Pro)

What fills an agent's context window, as a living treemap – system prompt, tools, memory, every file, the chat and tool results as tiles that glide as it grows, the free space dashed, and compaction squeezing old turns into a summary

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/context-map
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/context-map-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/context-map-clean`

### When to use

- Showing what fills an agent's context window – and why it's running out
- Debugging long sessions: which files, turns or tool results take the room
- Making compaction visible – old turns squeezing into a summary

### When not to use

- Just a fill level – use Context Window or Usage Meter
- Where the time and money of a run go – use Trace Waterfall
- What the agent remembers across sessions – use Memory Panel

### Usage

```tsx
import { ContextMap, type ContextBlock } from "@/components/ui/context-map-clean";

const blocks: ContextBlock[] = [
  { id: "system", label: "System prompt", kind: "system", tokens: 6200 },
  { id: "tools", label: "Tool definitions", kind: "tools", tokens: 14800 },
  { id: "spec", label: "checkout.spec.ts", kind: "file", tokens: 8200, detail: "Read at 0:09" },
  { id: "chat", label: "Chat", kind: "chat", tokens: 41000 },
  { id: "run", label: "Test run · 20×", kind: "result", tokens: 22400 },
];

export function Context() {
  return <ContextMap blocks={blocks} limit={200000} model="Opus 5.5" modelIcon={<ClaudeLogo />} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocks | `ContextBlock[]` |  | { id, label, kind, tokens, detail?, icon?, items? } – every part of the context, in the order the tiles should sit; items (label + icon) are listed on hover |
| kind | `"system" \| "tools" \| "memory" \| "file" \| "chat" \| "result" \| "summary"` |  | Per block – picks its tint |
| limit | `number` |  | The context window's size in tokens – what's left shows as dashed free space |
| model / modelIcon | `string / ReactNode` |  | The model and its maker's logo, next to the title – the window's size follows as a small tag |
| agents / agent / onAgentChange | `ContextAgent[] / string / (id) => void` |  | Agents to switch between – the bar shows the current one as a menu, its limit replaces limit |
| compaction | `ContextCompaction \| null` |  | { before, summarized?, dropped?, summary? } – the blocks just before the last compaction and which of them were summarized or dropped (the rest were kept); adds Before | After to the bar and a line under the map. null shows that line as "not compacted yet", so the height stays put |
| view / onViewChange | `"before" \| "after" / (view) => void` |  | Controlled: which side of the compaction shows – leave it out and the switch keeps its own |
| status | `string` |  | A short status in the bar – e.g. "Compacting" |
| onSelect | `(block \| null) => void` |  | A tile was clicked – null for the free space |
| title | `string` | `"Context"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- The map is a list labelled with its title; every tile is an item with its name, kind and tokens
- The fill level is text in the bar – its color is extra, not the only signal

### Motion

- A tile's card shows while you point at it; a click pins it – a second click, Escape or the block leaving the map lets it go
- Text that changes after a compaction rolls: the old line slides up and out, the new one comes in from below
- Before | After glides between the two maps: kept blocks stay, summarized and dropped ones grow back in while the summary shrinks away – and back
- Tiles keep their order and glide to their new place and size when anything changes
- New parts fade in where the layout puts them; parts that leave shrink to nothing
- A shine sweeps over the used token count all the time
- With prefers-reduced-motion tiles jump to their place

### Responsive

- The area keeps its height; tiles too small for a label show only their color – point at them for the details
- Under 480px the area is shorter and the numbers move to a line of their own
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every part every time something changes – ids keep tiles in place and let them glide
- Order matters: the layout keeps it, so put stable parts (system, tools) first and growing ones later
- To show compaction, shrink the squeezed parts to 0 over a moment while a summary block grows
- Colors are variables on .ui-cmpc, e.g. --ui-cmpc-file-bg / --ui-cmpc-file-edge

### Requirements

- React 19

# Context Window, clean style (Pro)

What fills the model's context, as a field of cells – hover a part to light it up, remove files, and compact the conversation while its cells shimmer and clear

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/context-window
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/context-window-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/context-window-clean`

### When to use

- Chat and agent products where people should see what the model currently has in mind – and why answers get slow, expensive or forgetful
- Next to a composer or in a session panel, to clean up before the window is full: drop files, compact the conversation
- Debug and admin views that explain a request: how much went to the system prompt, tools, files and history

### When not to use

- Billing and plan usage over a month – use Usage Meter
- A plain "72% used" – a single progress bar says that with less
- More than about six parts – group the small ones, the cells need colors people can tell apart

### Usage

```tsx
import { ContextWindow } from "@/components/ui/context-window-clean";

export function SessionContext() {
  return (
    <ContextWindow
      limit={200_000}
      model="claude-sonnet-5-5"
      parts={[
        { id: "system", label: "System prompt", tokens: 4200, locked: true },
        { id: "tools", label: "Tools", tokens: 12800 },
        {
          id: "files",
          label: "Files",
          items: [
            { id: "schema", label: "schema.prisma", tokens: 9400 },
            { id: "billing", label: "billing.ts", tokens: 21300 },
          ],
        },
        { id: "chat", label: "Conversation", tokens: 108600, compact: true },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| parts | `ContextPart[]` |  | { id, label, tokens?, items?, locked?, compact?, color? } – they fill the field in this order |
| limit | `number` |  | Size of the context window in tokens |
| title | `string` | `"Context window"` | Heading of the card |
| model | `string` |  | Small tag in the head, e.g. the model name |
| modelIcon | `ReactNode` |  | Logo in front of the model name, shown at 12px |
| onRemoveItem | `(partId: string, itemId: string) => void` |  | Called when an item is removed. With it the card shows exactly what you pass; without it the removal lives inside the card |
| onCompact | `(partId: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called when Compact is pressed; the cells shimmer until the promise settles. Without it the part shrinks on its own to its compact share |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A secondary button in the card's last row, e.g. New chat |
| warnAt | `number` | `0.8` | Share of the limit from which the percentage tag turns amber and the last row says how much is left; from 0.95 the window counts as full |
| cells | `number` | `216` | Number of cells in the field |
| columns | `number` | `36` | Cells per row |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the parts that can be opened, the Compact button, the items' remove buttons and the action
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes a part with items, presses Compact or removes an item

### Accessibility

- A group named by its title; the rolling number is aria-hidden and screen readers get the final "used of limit" in one sentence
- The field of cells is decorative – every number it shows is in the list below
- Parts with items are buttons with aria-expanded; closed lists are inert, remove buttons are named after their item
- The caption in the last row is announced politely: compacting, how much was saved, and how much is left once the window fills up

### Motion

- Any change sweeps through the field cell by cell, so removing a file empties its cells from left to right and everything behind it moves up
- Compacting makes the part's cells shimmer in a lighter wave while the caption shimmers "Compacting…"; then most of them clear, the numbers roll down and the button morphs into a green check on a light green fill with "Compacted" for a moment and then fades away – it only comes back once the part has grown again
- Hovering a part (row or cells) fades the other cells and rolls the big number to that part
- Items unfold in place; a removed item folds away before it goes
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 360px. Below 310px the field puts fewer cells in a row so they stay readable, the model tag shortens and Compact keeps only its icon
- Touch screens: taller rows and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- A part with items takes its tokens from the items' sum – leave tokens out there
- One cell stands for limit / cells tokens; any part with tokens gets at least one cell so it never disappears
- The card does not count tokens – pass the numbers your provider or tokenizer returns

### Requirements

- React 19

# Cost Waterfall, clean style (Pro)

Where the money and tokens of an agent run go – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a step in a waterfall, with model, tokens, cost and time, the most expensive step on top and a switch between cost and tokens

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/cost-waterfall
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/cost-waterfall-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/cost-waterfall-clean`

### When to use

- Showing what an agent run cost, and which steps spent it – next to a chat, in a run log or on a billing page
- Finding the expensive step: the bars step across to the total, so the long ones are where the money went
- Live runs, where new steps appear and the totals climb while the agent works

### When not to use

- When each step ran and how long it took – use Trace Waterfall
- Who started whom, at a glance – use Agent Tree
- A budget or quota over days and weeks – use Usage Meter

### Usage

```tsx
import { CostWaterfall, type CostStep } from "@/components/ui/cost-waterfall-clean";

const steps: CostStep[] = [
  { id: "plan", name: "Plan the report", kind: "llm", status: "done", model: "Opus 5.5",
    tokensIn: 4120, tokensOut: 960, cost: 0.044, duration: 3000,
    input: "Write a report on LLM API prices…", output: "1. Research  2. Write  3. Review" },
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", kind: "agent", status: "running", model: "Gemini 3.8 Flash", duration: 8500,
    children: [
      { id: "s1", name: "web_search", kind: "tool", status: "done", detail: "API prices 2026", cost: 0.01, duration: 1300,
        input: '{ "query": "LLM API pricing 2026" }', output: "10 results" },
    ] },
];

export function RunCost() {
  return <CostWaterfall steps={steps} task="Report on LLM API prices in 2026" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `CostStep[]` |  | { id, name, kind, status, model?, detail?, icon?, tokensIn?, tokensOut?, cost?, duration?, input?, output?, error?, children? } – the run's steps in order, sub-agents hold theirs as children |
| kind | `"agent" \| "llm" \| "tool"` |  | Per step – picks the bar's tint and what its details are called: Task/Result, Prompt/Response, Input/Output |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per step – running steps shimmer, failed ones turn red with their error in the details |
| cost / tokensIn / tokensOut | `number` |  | Per step, its own – sub-agents add up their children, so don't pre-sum. A negative cost is a credit and steps the waterfall back |
| duration | `number` |  | Per step, in ms – how long it took or runs so far |
| input / output / error | `string` |  | Per step – the prompt and response, or the tool's input and output, shown when the row opens |
| task | `string` |  | What the run is about – muted next to the title |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Overrides the run's state in the bar – by default Live while a step runs |
| mode / defaultMode | `"cost" \| "tokens"` | `"cost"` | What the bars measure, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onModeChange | `(mode) => void` |  | The switch was used |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of folded sub-agents, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: string[]) => void` |  | A sub-agent was folded or opened |
| openId / defaultOpenId | `string \| null` | `null` | The step whose details are open, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null, step?: CostStep) => void` |  | Details opened (with the step) or closed |
| maxHeight | `number` |  | Long runs: the rows scroll past this height in px |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.042"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Run cost"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the switch, the most expensive step and into the rows – the rows are one stop
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Moves between the rows; Home and End jump to the first and the last
- ArrowRight: Opens a folded sub-agent, or moves to its first step
- ArrowLeft: Folds an open sub-agent, or moves to its parent
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the details of the focused step
- Esc: Closes the details and returns to the row – also from inside them

### Accessibility

- The rows are a tree: every step is a treeitem with its level, labelled with name, kind, status, cost, tokens and time; aria-expanded on sub-agents
- Roving focus – only one row is in the tab order, so the waterfall is a single stop
- The switch is two toggle buttons with aria-pressed in a labelled group
- "Most expensive" unfolds the step's sub-agents, opens it and moves focus to its row
- Long prompts and outputs scroll in their box and are then a tab stop, so the keyboard can scroll them
- The run's state (Live, Done, Failed) is announced politely when it changes; ticks and grid lines are hidden from assistive tech

### Motion

- New steps slide in as rows and their bars grow from where the step before ended
- A running step's bar has a sheen and a soft glow at its leading edge; numbers that still climb shimmer
- When the total outgrows the axis, it glides to the next round value and every bar follows
- Switching between cost and tokens glides every bar to its new place and length
- Details open under their row and close the same way; folding closes the sub-agent's rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: wide, the steps sit on the left, the waterfall in the middle, the numbers on the right
- Under 720px the In and Out columns step aside – in the tokens view the step's tokens take the cost's place
- Under 520px each row stacks: name, cost and time on one line, the bar across the whole width under it
- Touch screens get larger targets for the switch and the chevrons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole list every time something changes – ids keep rows in place, new ids slide in
- cost and tokens are the step's own; sub-agents add their children up
- NaN, Infinity and missing numbers show as – and count as zero; a negative cost is a credit
- For a live run update tokensOut, cost and duration of the running step as they come in
- Colors are variables on .ui-cwfc, e.g. --ui-cwfc-llm-bg / --ui-cwfc-llm-edge for LLM calls
- The chevron and warning icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

```tsx
];
```

- Shift / Arrow keys: Grow the selected range
- ⌘ / Ctrl / Arrow keys: Jump to the first or last row or column

# Date Picker, clean style (Free)

Pick one day in the Text Field's look – a month in a small card, today marked, days outside min and max or ruled out stay visible, full keyboard control and the locale's own week

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/date-picker
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/date-picker-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/date-picker-clean`

### When to use

- One day in a form: the first run of a schedule, a due date, a launch day, when an export expires
- Settings rows next to Text Fields and Selects – same height, edge, label, hint and error, so the form reads as one

### When not to use

- A period with a start and an end, or comparing two periods – use the Date Range Picker
- A time of day – use the Time Picker (put both side by side for a date and a time)
- A birthday or a date far away that people know by heart – a plain Text Field is quicker to type

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { DatePicker } from "@/components/ui/date-picker-clean";

const weekend = (d: Date) => d.getDay() === 0 || d.getDay() === 6;

export function FirstRun() {
  const [day, setDay] = useState<Date | null>(null);
  return (
    <DatePicker
      label="First run"
      value={day}
      onChange={setDay}
      min={new Date()}
      isDateDisabled={weekend}
      hint="Research Agent only runs on weekdays."
      name="firstRun"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `Date \| null` |  | The chosen day – makes it controlled; null shows the placeholder |
| defaultValue | `Date \| null` | `null` | Starting day when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(date: Date) => void` |  | Called with the picked day, at local midnight |
| min | `Date` |  | Days before it can't be picked; the month arrow stops there |
| max | `Date` |  | Days after it can't be picked; ignored when it lies before min |
| isDateDisabled | `(date: Date) => boolean` |  | Rules out single days, e.g. weekends or holidays – they stay visible but can't be picked |
| locale | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for month names, weekdays, digits and the shown value – the browser's by default |
| weekStartsOn | `0 – 6` |  | 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday – by default the locale's first day of the week |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Pick a date"` | Shown in gray while nothing is chosen |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown above the field and read out with the value |
| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – the error takes its place while there is one |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks the field invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message where the hint was |
| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 28 · 32 · 36px high, like the Text Field; taller on touch screens |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the field and ignores input |
| name | `string` |  | Sends the day as YYYY-MM-DD with a form, through a hidden input |
| required | `boolean` |  | Sets aria-required – check it on submit like any other field |
| today | `Date` |  | Where the today marker sits – the real today by default |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Opens the calendar on mount without taking the focus – for previews |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper, e.g. a fixed width in a settings row |
| ref | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  | The field's button – focus it after a validation error |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space / ↓: On the field: open the calendar, with the focus on the chosen day (or today)
- ← / →: Previous or next day (mirrored in right-to-left layouts)
- ↑ / ↓: Same weekday a week earlier or later
- PageUp / PageDown: Same day a month earlier or later; with Shift a year
- Home / End: First or last day of the week
- Enter / Space: Pick the focused day and close
- Esc: Close without changing anything; the focus goes back to the field
- Tab: Between the month arrows and the days; tabbing out closes the calendar

### Accessibility

- The date picker dialog pattern: the field is a button with aria-haspopup="dialog"; the calendar is a non-modal dialog named by its month, the days a grid with one tab stop that moves with the arrow keys
- Every day is read out in full ("Thursday, November 12, 2026"); today carries aria-current="date", the chosen day aria-selected
- Days that can't be picked keep the focus (aria-disabled) so the arrow keys can walk past them, but Enter and clicks do nothing
- The month name is a polite live region, so paging through months is announced; weekday heads carry their full names
- The label names the field together with its value; hint and error are linked with aria-describedby, an error sets aria-invalid
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click – inside the day it sits on

### Motion

- The calendar fades in out of a small lift from the field's edge – downward, or upward when it opens above
- Months slide in from the side you went to; the chosen day pops in as a dark chip
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; the calendar stays inside the window and opens above the field near the bottom of the screen
- Always six weeks high, so the card never changes height between months
- It lives in the top layer (popover), so a card's overflow or z-index never cuts it
- Touch screens get 40px days and 16px text; dark mode built in via .dark or data-theme="dark" on an ancestor

### Requirements

- React 19

# Decision Card, clean style (Pro)

An agent's question, asked the way Claude asks one – its own card just above the chat composer: numbered options with one Recommended, Approve / Decline for an approval, preview tiles for a pick, and a last row for your own words; a click or 1–5 answers, Later folds it to one line

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/decision-card
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/decision-card-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/decision-card-clean`

### When to use

- An agent in a chat needs one answer from you before it goes on – which option, approve or not, which variant
- Several tasks wait on you at once: one card with a pager, right where you type
- You want answers by keyboard – 1–5, arrows, Enter – without leaving the chat

### When not to use

- Many open decisions across agents, worked through as a list – use Decision Inbox
- Approving tool calls, file changes or messages with their diff or arguments – use Approval Gates
- Steering a run while it works – use Agent Steering

### Usage

```tsx
import { DecisionCard, type Decision } from "@/components/ui/decision-card-clean";

const decisions: Decision[] = [
  {
    id: "queue",
    task: "Ingest pipeline",
    question: "Which queue should the ingest service use?",
    options: [
      { id: "kafka", title: "Kafka", summary: "A durable log – a day of events to replay", recommended: true },
      { id: "sqs", title: "SQS", summary: "Managed, nothing to run – but no replay" },
      { id: "pg", title: "Postgres queue", summary: "The database you already have" },
    ],
  },
];

export function Chat() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(decisions);
  return (
    <>
      <DecisionCard
        decisions={open}
        onDecide={(id, answer) => {
          agent.answer(id, answer);
          setOpen((l) => l.filter((d) => d.id !== id));
        }}
      />
      <Composer />
    </>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decisions | `Decision[]` |  | The open decisions, oldest first – an answered one leaves the card at once; drop it from the array in onDecide |
| onDecide | `(id: string, answer: DecisionAnswer) => void` |  | An answer: { option } for a row or tile, { text } for your own words, "approve" or "decline" |
| onLater | `(id: string) => void` |  | Later or Esc folded the card to one line |
| defaultFolded | `boolean` | `false` | Start folded to "2 decisions waiting · Show" |
| reveal | `number` |  | Change it to bring the card up – it unfolds, pulses gray once and focuses the selected row |
| labels | `Partial<DecisionCardLabels>` |  | Every text, e.g. needsYou, later, show, recommended, approve, decline, own, waiting(n), of(i, n) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| Decision | `{ id, question, task?, kind?, options?, facts? }` |  | kind: "decision" (default) | "pick" | "approval"; options: three to five { id, title, summary?, recommended?, preview?, blocks? }; facts: two or three { label, value } for an approval |

### Keyboard

- 1 / – / 5: Answer with that row at once; the next number goes into the field
- Home / End: First or last row
- ↑ / ↓: Move between the rows (← → on tiles); ↓ from the last row goes into the field, ↑ from an empty field back
- Enter / Space: Answer with the row in focus; in the field, Enter sends your own words
- Esc: Later – folds the card to one line

### Accessibility

- The card is a group labelled by the question; the rows are a listbox with one tab stop that moves with the arrows
- Every row says its number key (aria-keyshortcuts); Later says Escape
- Answers and Later are announced politely – what you picked and how many still wait
- Focus rings show only for the keyboard (:focus-visible); the field for your own words gets no ring, only a firmer edge
- After an answer the focus moves to the next decision, the pager arrows keep it while you page, Later moves it to Show and Show back to the row – it never falls back to the page, even when your array drops the decision in focus
- After the last answer the card folds away and can't know your composer: move the focus there yourself in onDecide, e.g. if (open.length === 1) composerRef.current?.focus()

### Motion

- The next decision fades in; after the last answer the card folds away – its height to zero, then gone
- Brought up with reveal, the card pulses gray once
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears

### Responsive

- One white card with a hairline edge and a soft lift, no gray layer around it – it takes the width of your composer
- Long titles and fact values wrap to a second line, then end in …; summaries and the task stay on one line – nothing leaves the card on phones
- One or two tiles keep the size of three; below 420px the tiles turn into rows
- On touch screens rows are 44px tall and buttons 32px to see, 40px to hit
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Put it right above the chat composer, in the same column – the composer stays for new prompts, the card has its own field
- Keep options to three to five with a one-line summary each; mark at most one recommended
- Remove a decision from the array in onDecide – after the last one the card folds away by itself; then focus the composer

### Requirements

- React 19

# Decision Tree, clean style (Pro)

An agent stuck on a decision lays out its options as a tree – the consequences of each branch, the risky ones marked, its own pick highlighted – and you choose a path or write your own

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/decision-tree
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/decision-tree-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/decision-tree-clean`

### When to use

- An agent hits a fork it shouldn't take alone – it asks how to proceed and shows what each way would change
- Backend calls without much to look at: data cleanups, refunds, rollouts, escalations – the consequences are the content
- When the agent has a preference but a person decides – its pick is marked, the other ways stay one click away

### When not to use

- Reviewing finished work – a diff, an email, a refund – one item after another: use Review Center
- One action that only needs a yes or no, with a countdown – use Approval Card
- A few quick questions with two answers each – use Decision Inbox
- An agent asking for access to a tool or scope – use Permission Request

### Usage

```tsx
import { DecisionTree, type Decision } from "@/components/ui/decision-tree-clean";

const decisions: Decision[] = [
  {
    id: "dupes",
    question: "3 customers have two active subscriptions – how should I proceed?",
    context: "All three signed up twice during the checkout outage.",
    agent: "Billing agent", model: "Sonnet 5.5", risk: "high",
    options: [
      { label: "Cancel the newer ones", pick: true, effects: ["Cancels 3 subscriptions · reversible", "Sends 3 emails"] },
      // A flagged part: marked in the leaf, its note shows on hover or with F
      { label: "Refund the newer ones", effects: [["Refunds ", { text: "$147 · not reversible", note: "One charge is two cycles old." }]] },
      { label: "Ask the customers", effects: ["Sends 3 emails · waits for answers"] },
    ],
  },
];

export function Decisions() {
  return (
    <DecisionTree
      decisions={decisions}
      onChoose={async (decision, choice) => {
        if ("other" in choice) return await agent.instruct(decision.id, choice.other); // its answer shows under your branch
        await agent.resume(decision.id, choice.option.label);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decisions | `Decision[]` |  | { id, question, context?, agent, model?, icon?, risk?, options } – everything waiting for a call; decided ones leave, new ids join at the end |
| options | `DecisionOption[]` |  | Per decision, two to four – { label, icon?, effects?, apps?, pick?, next? }; effects are what the branch leads to, one line each; pick marks the agent's own preference; icon is the logo of the tool it runs with, apps the logos of the systems it touches |
| next | `{ question, options }` |  | Per option – a follow-up question this branch leads to, with its own two to four options (one level deep). The whole tree shows at once; after the branch is picked, its follow-up wakes up and is picked the same way |
| effects | `DecisionText[]` |  | Per option – a string, or an array of strings and { text, note, source? } flags; flags are marked and explain themselves on hover, focus or F |
| risk | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` |  | Per decision – high and medium show as a small tag next to the agent |
| onChoose | `(decision, choice) => string \| void \| Promise<string \| void>` |  | A path was picked ({ index, option, then? } – then is the follow-up's pick) or an instruction written ({ other }) – for an instruction, return the agent's short answer |
| allowOther | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the "Other…" branch for your own instruction |
| ref | `Ref<DecisionTreeHandle>` |  | hover, choose, setOther, send, next, previous, peek |
| title | `string` | `"Decisions"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: Picks a branch; the number after the last option opens "Other…"
- Enter: In "Other…": sends your instruction – Shift+Enter starts a new line
- ArrowRight / ArrowLeft: Next and previous decision (J and K too)
- F: Shows the agent's note on the next flagged consequence
- Esc: Closes "Other…" or a note

### Accessibility

- Every branch is a real button labelled with its option and, where it applies, "the agent's pick"; shortcuts are set with aria-keyshortcuts
- Flagged consequences are focusable and point to their note with aria-describedby (role tooltip)
- The "Other…" field is a labelled textarea; it has no focus ring of its own – its outline darkens instead, so focus stays visible
- Picks, instructions and the agent's answers are announced in a polite live region
- The lines are decoration and hidden from assistive tech

### Motion

- A new decision grows in: the question first, then its branches and their consequences, each line drawing itself out a beat after the other
- Pointing at a branch lights its path and lets the others step back

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/decision-tree
- Section: Components · Agents

- Import: `@/components/ui/decision-tree`

### When to use

- An agent hits a fork it shouldn't take alone – it asks how to proceed and shows what each way would change
- Backend calls without much to look at: data cleanups, refunds, rollouts, escalations – the consequences are the content
- When the agent has a preference but a person decides – its pick is marked, the other ways stay one click away

### When not to use

- Reviewing finished work – a diff, an email, a refund – one item after another: use Review Center
- One action that only needs a yes or no, with a countdown – use Approval Card
- A few quick questions with two answers each – use Decision Inbox
- An agent asking for access to a tool or scope – use Permission Request

### Usage

```tsx
import { DecisionTree, type Decision } from "@/components/ui/decision-tree";

const decisions: Decision[] = [
  {
    id: "dupes",
    question: "3 customers have two active subscriptions – how should I proceed?",
    context: "All three signed up twice during the checkout outage.",
    agent: "Billing agent", model: "Sonnet 5.5", risk: "high",
    options: [
      { label: "Cancel the newer ones", pick: true, effects: ["Cancels 3 subscriptions · reversible", "Sends 3 emails"] },
      // A flagged part: marked in the leaf, its note shows on hover or with F
      { label: "Refund the newer ones", effects: [["Refunds ", { text: "$147 · not reversible", note: "One charge is two cycles old." }]] },
      { label: "Ask the customers", effects: ["Sends 3 emails · waits for answers"] },
    ],
  },
];

export function Decisions() {
  return (
    <DecisionTree
      decisions={decisions}
      onChoose={async (decision, choice) => {
        if ("other" in choice) return await agent.instruct(decision.id, choice.other); // its answer shows under your branch
        await agent.resume(decision.id, choice.option.label);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```
