# Delegate Board, clean style (Pro)

Hand work to your agents by dragging it onto them – each agent previews its new “busy until” time, or switch to Auto and every new task goes to whoever is free first

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/delegate-board
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/delegate-board-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/delegate-board-clean`

### When to use

- People hand tasks to a team of agents and want to see who is free and how long each one is busy
- Re-balancing work between agents: move a queued task to someone with more room
- Showing an automatic routing suggestion before it happens (suggestion prop)
- Weighing time against money: a fast, pricey model or a slower, cheaper one (rate on each agent)

### When not to use

- Watching what agents are doing right now over time – use Agent Lanes
- Approving single results – use Approval Card or Agent Inbox
- Assigning people in a project tool – this one is about agents, their models and queues

### Usage

```tsx
import { DelegateBoard, type DelegateAgent, type DelegateTask } from "@/components/ui/delegate-board-clean";

export function Dispatch({ agents, tasks }: { agents: DelegateAgent[]; tasks: DelegateTask[] }) {
  return (
    <DelegateBoard
      agents={agents} // { id, name, model?, avatar?, current? }
      tasks={tasks} // { id, title, estimate, tools?, agentId? } – no agentId: unassigned
      onAssign={(taskId, agentId) => api.assign(taskId, agentId)} // agentId null: back to unassigned
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `DelegateAgent[]` |  | { id, name, model?, avatar?, current?, rate? } – current: minutes left on the task it runs now, for the Busy until time; rate: cost per minute of work, shown after the model, as the price of a hand-off and as the total in the queues |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.60"` | Formats every cost – swap in your currency or credits |
| tasks | `DelegateTask[]` |  | { id, title, estimate (minutes), tools?, agentId? }. In each queue the first task is the running one; past three, a +N chip lists the rest in a tooltip on hover or focus |
| onAssign | `(taskId: string, agentId: string \| null) => void` |  | A drop, a keyboard pick or Auto. null means back to Unassigned. Without it the board moves tasks itself |
| mode / defaultMode | `"auto" \| "manual"` | `"manual"` | Auto hands every unassigned task to the least busy agent, about one a second; Manual waits for a drag. The Auto switch sits in the bar |
| onModeChange | `(mode: DelegateMode) => void` |  | The Auto switch was turned on or off |
| suggestion | `{ taskId, agentId } \| null` |  | A proposed hand-off: the agent lights up and previews its new time, the task is marked |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for the Busy until times |
| title | `string` | `"Delegate"` | Heading in the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Picks up the focused task; Enter again hands it to the highlighted agent
- ↑ / ↓: Chooses the agent while a task is picked up
- 1–9: Hands the focused task to that agent at once (the numbers show next to the names)
- Esc: Puts a picked-up task back

### Accessibility

- Unassigned and Agents are labelled sections; every queue is a list named after its agent
- Tasks are buttons described by how to move them; every hand-off is announced politely ("Write release notes → Writer")
- Dragging is never the only way: keyboard pick-up, number keys and Auto do the same; Auto is a switch (role switch) labelled by its word

### Motion

- The dragged card lifts, tilts a little and follows the pointer; the agent under it lights up with its new time
- On drop the card glides and shrinks into the agent's queue; queued chips glide when they move between agents
- In Auto the next task goes out about every second, so each hand-off can be followed
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything moves at once, without glides

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 720px; below 560px the pile sits above the agents
- Works with touch: cards and chips can be dragged with a finger
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- estimate is in minutes; Busy until adds the agent's current (or its first task's estimate) and every queued task's estimate to now
- To route automatically, set suggestion first so people see it, then call your own assign

- React 19

# Dialog, clean style (Free)

A modal window on a dimmed backdrop – title and quiet line, content that scrolls under a fixed header and footer, Escape and backdrop close, the focus kept inside and handed back, a sheet on phones, and an AlertDialog to confirm with a red button

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/dialog
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/dialog-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/dialog-clean`

### When to use

- A task that needs the whole attention before going on: create a task, edit an agent, invite people, connect an app
- A confirmation before something that can't be undone – delete an agent, cancel a subscription, revoke a key (use AlertDialog)
- Content that should open over the page and come back to the same place when it closes

### When not to use

- A short form or a few settings next to the button that asks for them – use the Popover, which doesn't block the page
- A list of actions or choices – use the Dropdown Menu
- Searching and running commands – use the Command Menu
- A short status after an action, like "Saved" or "Deleted · Undo" – use the Toaster; an undo is often kinder than a confirm
- Nothing to show yet – use the Empty State

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Dialog } from "@/components/ui/dialog-clean";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button-clean";

export function EditAgent({ agent, onSave }: { agent: { name: string }; onSave: (name: string) => void }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [name, setName] = useState(agent.name);

  return (
    <Dialog
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Edit</Button>}
      title="Edit agent"
      description="Changes apply from its next run."
      footer={
        <>
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            onClick={() => {
              onSave(name);
              setOpen(false);
            }}
          >
            Save
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      <input aria-label="Name" value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | `boolean` |  | Shows it – pass it with onOpenChange to control it, or leave both out and use trigger |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Open from the start when it isn't controlled |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with false on Escape, a backdrop press, the × (and AlertDialog's buttons), with true from the trigger |
| trigger | `ReactElement` |  | A button that opens it – it keeps its own onClick, gets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded, and the focus comes back to it on close |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Required. The heading – also the dialog's accessible name (aria-labelledby) |
| description | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the title, read out with it (aria-describedby) |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The content – it scrolls when it is taller than the window, a hairline shows at the edge that has more |
| footer | `ReactNode` |  | The actions, aligned to the end – they stay in view while the content scrolls and wrap rather than squeeze |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md" (AlertDialog "sm")` | 400, 480 or 720px wide – never wider than the window |
| width | `number \| string` |  | Any width instead of a size, e.g. 560 or "40rem" |
| closeOnBackdrop | `boolean` | `true` | A press on the backdrop closes it. Off, the card gives a small nudge instead. AlertDialog never closes this way |
| closeButton | `boolean` | `true` | The × in the corner. AlertDialog has none – its Cancel is the way out |
| closeLabel | `string` | `"Close"` | The ×'s accessible name and tooltip – for other languages |
| initialFocus | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` |  | The control that gets the focus on open. By default: an element with data-autofocus, else the first control in the content, then in the footer |
| contained | `boolean` | `false` | Stays inside its nearest positioned parent – an app frame, a preview – instead of covering the window; Tab still goes round inside |
| ...dialog props | `ComponentProps<"dialog">` |  | className, style, id, aria-* … go to the <dialog> layer |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the controls inside and goes round – the page behind can't be reached
- Esc: Closes it (AlertDialog: cancels) – a menu or popover opened inside closes first
- Enter: Clicks the focused button – in AlertDialog that is the safe one first

### Accessibility

- A native <dialog> opened with showModal(): the top layer, everything behind it inert, the focus kept inside by the browser
- Named by its title and described by its description; AlertDialog has role="alertdialog"
- On open the focus moves to the first control (or initialFocus); on close it goes back to the trigger, or to whatever had it before
- AlertDialog puts the focus on the safe button, never closes on a backdrop press, and its busy confirm sets aria-busy
- contained keeps aria-modal and loops Tab itself, since the page around it isn't inert

### Motion

- The backdrop fades in, the card rises and scales from 97% – the way out is quicker and shrinks it slightly
- As a sheet on phones it slides up from the bottom and back down
- With prefers-reduced-motion it appears and goes at once

### Responsive

- On phones (or in a frame narrower than 520px) it becomes a sheet from the bottom: full width, the actions within the thumb's reach and above the home bar, AlertDialog's two buttons sharing the row
- Long content scrolls inside while the title and the actions stay put; long titles and unbroken words wrap
- The page under it stops scrolling while it is open, without shifting sideways
- Touch screens get bigger buttons and a bigger ×
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Actions and choices behind any trigger – icons, shortcuts, checks, red items and submenus, a gliding highlight, type-ahead and the full menu keyboard

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/dropdown-menu
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/dropdown-menu-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/dropdown-menu-clean`

### When to use

- Actions on one thing behind a ⋯ button: rerun, duplicate, copy link, move, delete

- Searching across many commands or pages – use the Command Menu

- Filters with several groups and counts – use the Filter Menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { Copy01Icon, Delete02Icon, Folder01Icon, MoreHorizontalIcon, RepeatIcon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons";
import { HugeiconsIcon } from "@hugeicons/react";
import { DropdownMenu } from "@/components/ui/dropdown-menu-clean";

export function RunActions({ run }: { run: { id: string; name: string } }) {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu
      align="end"
      items={[
        { label: "Rerun", icon: RepeatIcon, shortcut: "⌘R", onSelect: () => rerun(run.id) },
        { label: "Duplicate", icon: Copy01Icon, onSelect: () => duplicate(run.id) },
        {
          label: "Move to",
          icon: Folder01Icon,
          divider: true,
          submenu: folders.map((f) => ({ label: f.name, icon: f.icon, checked: f.id === run.folder, onSelect: () => move(run.id, f.id) })),
        },
        { label: "Delete run", icon: Delete02Icon, danger: true, divider: true, onSelect: () => remove(run.id) },
      ]}
      trigger={({ triggerProps }) => (
        <button type="button" aria-label={`Actions for ${run.name}`} {...triggerProps}>
          <HugeiconsIcon icon={MoreHorizontalIcon} size={16} />
        </button>
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | `({ open, toggle, triggerProps }) => ReactNode` |  | Draws the trigger. Spread triggerProps on it (id, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, onClick) – or call toggle yourself |
| items | `DropdownMenuItem[]` |  | { label, description?, icon?, logo?, checked?, type?, danger?, shortcut?, divider?, disabled?, keepOpen?, submenu?, onSelect? } |
| item.icon | `ReactNode \| HugeIcon` |  | A 16px glyph before the label – an inline SVG, or a Hugeicons icon object passed as it is |
| item.logo | `ReactNode` |  | A brand mark in its own colors in place of the icon (Gmail, Slack, a flag) |
| item.checked | `boolean` |  | Makes the item a choice with a check on the right; leave it out for a plain action |
| item.type | `"radio" \| "checkbox"` | `"radio"` | radio: one of a set (menuitemradio) · checkbox: on or off on its own (menuitemcheckbox) |
| item.danger | `boolean` |  | Red label and icon, a red-tinted highlight – for Delete and the like |
| item.shortcut | `string` |  | Shown on the right, e.g. "⌘R" – only shown, wire the keys up yourself |
| item.divider | `boolean` |  | A hairline above the item, to start a group |
| item.disabled | `boolean` |  | Shown faint; can't be picked and the arrow keys skip it |
| item.keepOpen | `boolean` |  | The menu stays open after the pick – for checkboxes you tick several of |
| item.submenu | `DropdownMenuItem[]` |  | Opens beside the item on hover, →, Enter or Space; ← or Esc steps back |
| align | `"start" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Which edges of menu and trigger line up; switches when the menu would stick out |
| side | `"bottom" \| "top"` | `"bottom"` | Where it opens; flips when the other side has more room |
| title | `string` |  | A small gray heading above the items – also the menu's accessible name |
| header | `ReactNode` |  | Anything above the items, e.g. the signed-in user |

| className | `string` |  | On the inline wrapper around the trigger |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Names the menu when there is no title (otherwise the trigger names it) |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space / ↓: On the trigger: open with the checked or first item focused
- ↑: On the trigger: open with the last item focused
- ↓ / ↑: Next or previous item, wrapping around; disabled ones are skipped
- Home / End: First or last item
- A–Z: Jump to the next item that starts with what you type
- Enter / Space: Pick the item, or open its submenu
- → / ←: Into a submenu, and back out of it
- Esc: Close the submenu, or the menu – the focus goes back to the trigger
- Tab: Close the menu and move on from the trigger

### Accessibility

- The menu button pattern: the trigger has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls; the list is role="menu" named by the title or the trigger
- Items are menuitem, menuitemradio or menuitemcheckbox with aria-checked; an item with a submenu has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; dividers are separators

- Opened with the pointer, the focus waits on the menu itself – no item looks picked until you hover or press a key
- However it closes, the focus goes back to the trigger – unless the pick moved it on purpose (e.g. into a rename field)
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), inside the row

### Motion

- The menu fades and scales in from the corner it is attached to; submenus fade in beside their item
- One soft highlight glides between the rows as the pointer or the arrow keys move – red-tinted on a danger item
- The check on a choice draws itself
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- It lives in the top layer (popover), so a card's overflow or z-index never cuts it; it follows its trigger on scroll
- Opens where there is room – under or above the trigger, the edges line up the other way near the screen's side; a long menu scrolls
- A submenu opens to the right, to the left when there is no room, and under its item on a narrow phone
- Long labels end in … with the full text on hover; touch screens get 40px rows
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- Optional: @hugeicons/core-free-icons – its icon objects can be passed straight to icon

# Dropzone, clean style (Pro)

Drag files in and watch them upload – fanning documents, colored type badges, progress with time left, errors with retry

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/dropzone
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/dropzone-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/dropzone-clean`

### When to use

- Uploading documents, images or media – attachments, imports, asset libraries, onboarding
- Several files at once, where people want to see what's done, what's still running and what failed

### When not to use

- A single avatar or logo – a simple picker with a preview is lighter
- Huge uploads that run in the background for minutes – show them in a separate transfer panel

### Usage

```tsx
import { Dropzone } from "@/components/ui/dropzone-clean";

export function Attachments() {
  return (
    <Dropzone
      accept={[".pdf", ".png", ".jpg", ".xlsx"]}
      maxSize={25 * 1024 * 1024}
      onUpload={(file, onProgress) =>
        new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
          xhr.upload.onprogress = (e) => onProgress(e.loaded / e.total);
          xhr.onload = () => (xhr.status < 300 ? resolve() : reject(new Error("Upload failed")));
          xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error("Upload failed – connection lost"));
          xhr.open("POST", "/api/upload");
          xhr.send(file);
        })
      }
      onChange={(items) => setAttachments(items.filter((i) => i.status === "done"))}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

- Import: `@/components/ui/empty-state-clean`

### When to use

- A list, table or board that has nothing in it yet – say what will show up and offer the first step

- A side panel or page with nothing picked – bare, without a frame

### When not to use

- While the data is still loading – show skeletons or the Thinking Loader, then the empty state only if it stays empty
- Errors or a failed load – say what went wrong in a Toaster or inline, with a retry
- A first-run checklist with several steps – use the Setup Guide

### Usage

```tsx
import { Calendar03Icon, PlusSignIcon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons";
import { HugeiconsIcon } from "@hugeicons/react";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button-clean";
import { EmptyState } from "@/components/ui/empty-state-clean";

export function Schedules({ schedules, onNew }: { schedules: { id: string }[]; onNew: () => void }) {
  if (!schedules.length) {
    return (
      <EmptyState
        icon={Calendar03Icon}
        title="No schedules yet"
        text="Runs you ask an agent to repeat show up here, with their next time."
        action={
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" icon={<HugeiconsIcon icon={PlusSignIcon} size={15} />} onClick={onNew}>
            New schedule
          </Button>
        }
      />
    );
  }
  return null; // …the list
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Required. What's empty, e.g. "No schedules yet" |
| text | `ReactNode` |  | One line on what will show up here, or how to get there – balanced over two lines when it wraps |
| action | `ReactNode` |  | The first step, usually a small secondary Button; several sit in a row and wrap |
| icon | `ReactNode \| HugeIcon` | `a file` | The glyph on the soft tile – an inline SVG or a Hugeicons icon object, drawn 18px at a 1.9 stroke; null leaves the tile out |
| bare | `boolean` | `false` | Without the frame – for a panel or page where it is the only content |
| tall | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its parent's height and centres itself in it – for a list or table area that keeps its size |
| ...div props | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | className, style, id, role, ref and the rest go to the outer <div> |

### Accessibility

- Plain text and the button you pass – nothing is hidden from screen readers except the decorative icon
- When it replaces a list after a search or filter, announce the change: give a wrapper role="status" or aria-live="polite"
- The action keeps its own focus ring; the empty state itself takes no focus

### Responsive

- Centered and as wide as its parent; the text stops at 430px and wraps in balance
- Long titles and unbroken words wrap instead of running out
- Below 560px the frame tightens to 36px top and 18px at the sides
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- Optional: @hugeicons/core-free-icons – its icon objects can be passed straight to icon

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/experiment-card-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/experiment-card-clean`

### When to use

- A/B tests, prompt or model comparisons, pricing experiments – anything with a few variants measured the same way
- Lists of running experiments where the result should be one hover away
- When people should not only read the result but act on it: pick the winner and ship it

### When not to use

- More than about five variants – the head chart and the rows get crowded; use a table
- Results over time – a line chart shows when a variant pulled ahead; this card shows where things stand
- A single number without variants – use KPI Chart or Compact Breakdown

### Usage

```tsx
import { ExperimentCard } from "@/components/ui/experiment-card-clean";

export function SignupCopyTest() {
  return (
    <ExperimentCard
      title="Signup button copy"
      status={{ label: "Running", tone: "green" }}
      note="Day 9 of 14"
      metrics={[
        { id: "conversion", label: "Conversion", format: (n) => `${n.toFixed(1)}%` },
        { id: "revenue", label: "Revenue", format: (n) => `$${n.toFixed(2)}` },
      ]}
      variants={[
        { id: "a", key: "A", name: "Start free trial", control: true, visitors: 4790, values: { conversion: 4.2, revenue: 18.4 } },
        { id: "b", key: "B", name: "Try it free", visitors: 4812, values: { conversion: 4.7, revenue: 19.1 }, confidence: { conversion: 96, revenue: 81 } },
      ]}
      action={{ label: (v) => `Ship ${v.key}`, onClick: (v) => ship(v.id) }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Name of the experiment |
| variants | `ExperimentVariant[]` |  | { id, key, name, values, control?, visitors?, confidence?, color? } – values and confidence hold one number per metric id; key is the short letter in the badge |
| metrics | `ExperimentMetric[]` |  | { id, label, format?, lowerIsBetter? } – the switch above the rows; no switch with a single metric |
| metric | `string` |  | Controlled metric id |
| defaultMetric | `string` | `first metric` | Starting metric when uncontrolled |
| onMetricChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new metric |
| winner | `string \| null` |  | Controlled id of the picked variant |
| defaultWinner | `string \| null` | `null` | Picked variant when uncontrolled |
| onWinnerChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | Called when a variant is picked, or null when the pick is taken back |
| status | `{ label: string; tone?: ExperimentTone }` |  | The tag under the title – tone is red, amber, green, blue, violet or gray |
| note | `string` |  | Short text next to the status, e.g. "Day 9 of 14" |
| action | `{ label: string \| (variant) => string; onClick: (variant) => void }` |  | The button that appears in the last row of the card once a winner is picked |
| hint | `ReactNode` | `"Pick a winner"` | The line in the last row of the card while nothing is hovered or picked |
| trigger | `"hover" \| "click"` | `"hover"` | Hover opens under the mouse; taps and the keyboard always toggle |
| open | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Starts open when uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the card opens or closes |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the card: opens or closes it
- ← / →: In the metric switch: previous or next metric (wraps around)
- Tab: Through the metric switch, the variants and the action
- Space: On a variant: picks it as the winner, or takes the pick back
- Esc: Closes the card and returns focus to it

### Accessibility

- The head is one button with aria-expanded; its name carries the status and who is ahead
- The metric switch and the variants are radio groups; every variant's name includes its value and its change against the baseline
- The small chart in the head is decorative – everything it shows is in the rows
- While the card is closed, everything inside is inert; the line in the last row is announced politely

### Motion

- Nothing travels: the head stays where it is and the comparison unfolds below it while it fades in
- Switching the metric rolls every number in one shared tween while bars and columns glide to their new size; the soft fill of the switch moves along in a short, crisp step
- Hovering a variant widens its column in the head and fades the others – and the other way round
- Picking a winner turns its badge into a check and pops the dark action button into the last row
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 340px; below 300px the note next to the status goes and the chips tighten
- Touch screens: a tap opens, a tap outside closes, rows and the metric switch are taller
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Changes are measured against the control (the variant with control: true, else the first). With lowerIsBetter a drop is shown as it is (−7.5%) but colored green and counted as the lead
- Pass raw numbers and do the formatting in the metric's format, so the rolling values stay smooth
- The card does not compute confidence – pass what your stats engine gives you

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: project-card, compact-breakdown, kpi-chart

# Fallback Chain, clean style (Pro)

One request finding a model that answers, as a small flow diagram – the request branches out to each model in its fallback order, a light runs to the one being tried, failed branches break red, and the one that answers runs on to the response

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/fallback-chain
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/fallback-chain-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/fallback-chain-clean`

### When to use

- A request can go to several models, providers or regions and people should see which one answered – and why the others didn't
- Model routers, LLM gateways, retries across providers, uptime and incident views

### When not to use

- When several models answer the same prompt at once and you compare them – use Parallel Attempts
- When the full timeline of one run matters – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { FallbackChain, type FallbackAttempt } from "@/components/ui/fallback-chain-clean";

export function Route({ attempts }: { attempts: FallbackAttempt[] }) {
  return (
    <FallbackChain
      title="Summarize support ticket"
      route="openrouter/auto"
      attempts={attempts} // { id, model, provider?, providerLogo?, region?, logo?, status, startedAt?, duration?, timeout?, cost? (USD), reason?, note?, details? }
      request={{ name: "HubSpot · Ticket #4821", logo: <HubSpotLogo />, text: prompt }}
      response={{ name: "Slack · #support", logo: <SlackLogo />, text: answer }}
      onRetry={() => resend()}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attempts | `FallbackAttempt[]` |  | The models in the order they're tried, each with its status: waiting, trying, failed, answered or skipped |
| title | `string` | `"Request"` | What was asked, above the diagram next to the attempt and the running time and cost |
| route | `string` |  | The route on the request node, e.g. "openrouter/auto" |
| request | `ChainEnd` |  | Where the request came from – { name, logo, text, details } for its hover card: the source, a preview of the prompt and extra lines |
| response | `ChainEnd` |  | Where the answer goes – { name, logo, text, details } for its hover card; the preview shows once a model answered |
| now | `number` |  | A clock you control for the live timer – without it it follows real time |
| onRetry | `() => void` |  | Shows a Retry button once every model failed |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the request, each model and the response – each opens its hover card while focused; then the Retry button once every model failed

### Accessibility

- The summary on top is a status region – “Attempt 2 of 4”, “Answered in 8.5s” and failures are announced
- The branches are decoration – the models are an ordered list with each one's provider, status and time
- Hover cards are tooltips tied to their element (aria-describedby), so they're read on focus too
- Every state is written out (“Rate limited · 429”, “Not needed”), not only shown by color
- The running light and the drawing branches stop with reduced motion

### Responsive

- Below 680px the provider moves into the model's hover card; below 520px the diagram turns into a tree – the request on top, the models branching off one line, the result stays in the line above
- Dark mode built in; colors are CSS variables on .ui-fbkc

### Requirements

- React 19

# Fan-out Grid, clean style (Pro)

One agent hands a big job to many workers – every task a cell on a live grid that fills in as they get through it, with retries, failures, cost and the time left, and the details of any task on hover

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/fan-out-grid
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/fan-out-grid-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/fan-out-grid-clean`

### When to use

- An agent fans one job out to many workers – enriching leads, translating pages, labelling tickets, running evals – and you want to watch it fill in
- Batch runs with hundreds of tasks, where retries and failures matter more than any single step
- A live overview next to a run's log: how far it is, what it costs, how long is left

### When not to use

- A handful of agents and who started whom – use Agent Tree
- Where the time of one run goes, step by step – use Trace Waterfall
- Several agents side by side over time – use Agent Lanes

### Usage

```tsx
import { FanoutGrid, type FanoutTask } from "@/components/ui/fan-out-grid-clean";

const tasks: FanoutTask[] = leads.map((lead) => ({
  id: lead.id,
  label: lead.domain,
  status: lead.status, // "queued" | "running" | "retrying" | "done" | "failed"
  worker: lead.worker,
  start: lead.startedMs, end: lead.endedMs,
  cost: lead.cost, attempts: lead.attempts,
  result: lead.summary, error: lead.error,
}));

export function Enrichment({ elapsed }: { elapsed: number }) {
  return <FanoutGrid tasks={tasks} job="Enrich 240 leads" workers={16} now={elapsed} onRetry={(ids) => retry(ids)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `FanoutTask[]` |  | { id, label, status, worker?, start?, end?, cost?, attempts?, result?, error? } – one per task, in the order the cells should show |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "retrying" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per task – picks the cell's tint: gray, blue with a shine, amber, green, red |
| start / end | `number` |  | Per task, in ms from the start of the job – used for its duration and the time left |
| attempts | `number` |  | Per task – 2 and more show in its details |
| job | `string` |  | What the whole job does, next to the title – e.g. "Enrich 240 leads" |
| workers | `number` |  | How many workers run at once – the time left is worked out from it (defaults to the tasks running now) |
| now | `number` | `0` | The clock, in ms from the start of the job |
| onRetry | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | Shows "Retry failed" while tasks have failed, and gets their ids |
| onSelect | `(task \| null) => void` |  | A task was picked (click or Enter) – null when it's let go |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Fan-out"` | Heading of the bar |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | A small mark before the title, e.g. the agent's logo |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the grid (one stop) and on to the counts under it and Retry
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight / ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Walks the cells and shows each one's details; Home and End jump to the first and the last
- Enter / Space: Keeps the details open, or lets them go
- Esc: Lets go of the details

### Accessibility

- The grid is a single tab stop; the details of the cell you're on are its description
- The counts under the grid are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) that show only one state
- The run's progress is announced politely in steps of ten percent, and once more when it's finished

### Motion

- Cells appear in a quick wave; running ones carry a shine that sweeps across, each a little out of step
- Retrying cells breathe in amber; done and failed cells pop once when they land
- The details window opens with a soft scale and fade from its cell
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: the grid fills whatever width it gets, the cells wrap into rows
- Under 520px the cells get smaller and the numbers move to a line of their own
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every task every time something changes – ids keep cells in place, and a cell animates when its status changes
- start and end are ms from the job's start, not timestamps
- The time left needs at least three finished tasks; pass workers for an honest estimate
- A retried task keeps its id – raise attempts and set status back to running
- Colors are variables on .ui-fogc, e.g. --ui-fogc-done-bg / --ui-fogc-done-edge
- The retry icon is Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-tree, trace-waterfall, agent-lanes, agent-queue

# Flow Builder, clean style (Pro)

An automation drawn as a top-down flow you build in place – a + on every line adds a step, If / else forks into named paths, steps move and come back with Undo, and a test run sends a light down the line into the step that's working

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/flow-builder
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/flow-builder-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/flow-builder-clean`

### When to use

- Automation and agent products where people put together what happens after a trigger – onboarding, routing, follow-ups
- A flow that branches on a condition, built and tested in place, inside a settings page, a side panel or a dialog

### When not to use

- A free-form graph where anything connects to anything – this is a top-down flow with forks; use a canvas library
- Reviewing an agent's own plan before it runs – Agent Plan is made for that
- Watching runs that already happened – Trace Waterfall and Run Replay show those

### Usage

```tsx
import { FlowBuilder } from "@/components/ui/flow-builder-clean";

export function Automation({ flow, run }) {
  return (
    <FlowBuilder
      name="Onboard new signups"
      steps={flow.steps}              // the first step is the trigger
      onStepsChange={flow.save}       // every add, move and remove
      status={run.status}             // { research: "done", welcome: "running", enterprise: "skipped" }
      onRun={run.start}
      onStop={run.stop}
      onSelect={(id) => openInspector(id)}
    />
  );
}

// A step
{ id: "welcome", kind: "action", icon: "mail", title: "Send welcome email", detail: "Gmail · from Flo",
  note: "A personal welcome, written from the research" }

// An If / else – each path has its own steps
{ id: "size", kind: "branch", title: "Company size", detail: "employees > 200",
  paths: [
    { id: "enterprise", label: "Enterprise", steps: [...] },
    { id: "self", label: "Self-serve", steps: [...] },
  ] }
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | `"Untitled workflow"` | The workflow's name, in the header |
| steps / defaultSteps / onStepsChange | `FlowStep[]` |  | The flow, controlled or not – the first step is the trigger. A step is { id, kind, title, detail?, note?, icon?, paths? } – note is the line that shimmers while it runs |
| kind | `"trigger" \| "action" \| "agent" \| "branch" \| "wait"` |  | An agent step shows its pixel mark; a branch draws its paths side by side |
| icon | `"webhook" \| "schedule" \| "form" \| "mail" \| "message" \| "slack" \| "database" \| "http" \| "wait" \| "branch" \| "user" \| "task" \| "flash"` |  | The glyph in the step's tile |
| templates | `{ kind; title; detail?; icon?; paths? }[]` |  | What the + menu offers – paths names the paths of a new If / else |
| triggers | `FlowTemplate[]` |  | What Add a trigger offers while the flow is empty |
| status | `Record<string, "idle" \| "running" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "skipped">` |  | The test run, by step id; a path id set to skipped fades the whole path |
| selected / defaultSelected / onSelect | `string \| null` |  | The selected step – open your own inspector from onSelect |
| onRun / onStop | `() => void` |  | Run test, and Stop while it runs; Run test needs onRun and at least two steps |
| height | `number` | `420` | Height of the canvas in px – it scrolls and pans inside |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the steps and the + on each line
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: From step to step, in reading order – into the paths too
- Enter / Space: Select a step, or open the + menu
- ⌥ / ↑ / ↓: Move the step up or down in its path
- ⌫: Remove the step – the one before it gets the focus; an If / else hands its first path's steps back up
- ⌘ / Z: Undo the last change
- Esc: Close the menu, then clear the selection

### Accessibility

- Each step is a toggle button (aria-pressed) whose status – Running, Passed, Failed, Skipped – is read with it
- Every + is named for where it adds: “Add a step after Research the company”, “Add a step at the start of Self-serve”
- The menu is a real menu: it opens with the focus on its first item, arrows move, Esc returns to the +
- Run results, removals and Undo are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- The steps rise in one after another while their lines draw themselves down, dots and + popping in behind
- A step that starts gets a soft blue floor of light rising from where its line comes in; a light runs down the line into it, its line shimmers, its bar sweeps and its time counts up – an agent step's mark twinkles
- Tags swap with a small pop – Running, Passed, Failed; a skipped path fades and its name is struck through
- Reduced motion turns all of it off

### Responsive

- No background of its own – it sits on your page; the canvas keeps its height, scrolls both ways with soft edges, pans by dragging and opens centred on the flow
- Every step has one size, so nothing jumps while the test runs; each step's time is measured from the status you feed; long names end in an ellipsis with the full name on hover
- Below 480px the steps get narrower, so two paths still sit side by side
- The + menu opens below its line, or above it when there's no room, and stays inside the card
- On touch screens the key hints go and each + gets a bigger target
- Right-to-left: the layout mirrors
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

The frame around any control – label with a required mark or Optional, a hint, an error in its place and a count, all wired up with ids and aria

### When to use

- Any control that needs a label, a hint and an error but doesn't draw them itself: a plain <input> or <select>, a Number Input without its own label, a slider, a radio group, your own picker
- Forms that mix controls – every label, hint and error sits at the same distance and looks the same, whatever is inside

### When not to use

- Around a Text Field, Text Area or Select that already has its label, hint and error – pass those props to them instead
- A single checkbox or switch – their own label and description sit next to them (Checkbox, Switch)
- Grouping several fields under one heading – use a <fieldset> with a <legend>

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { FormField } from "@/components/ui/form-field-clean";

export function AgentForm() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const [budget, setBudget] = useState("40");
  const over = Number(budget) > 100;

  return (
    <form className="grid gap-4">
      <FormField label="Agent name" required counter={`${name.length}/40`}>
        <input value={name} maxLength={40} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
```

### When to use

- Hero sections for AI assistants, chat or writing tools – the prompt types itself and invites people to try
- Landing pages that want an interactive scene instead of a video

### When not to use

- As your real chat input – it is a showcase; use Chat Composer for a working input
- Small cards on mobile – the keyboard legends get tiny below ~360px width

### Usage

```tsx
import { GlowKeyboard } from "@/components/ui/glow-keyboard";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <GlowKeyboard />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompts | `string[]` | `three hiking prompts` | Prompts the demo types one after another; each one is sent with Enter |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask AI anything..."` | Placeholder of the chat input |

### Keyboard

- Click: Anywhere on the scene puts the cursor into the input and stops the demo
- Any key: Types and lights up the same key on the drawn keyboard
- Enter: Sends the prompt and clears the input

### Accessibility

- The input is a real text field with a label; the drawn keyboard and the floor are hidden from screen readers
- The demo stops as soon as the input gets focus, so it never types over the user

### Motion

- The demo types each prompt with an uneven, human rhythm, holds Shift for capitals and corrects one typo
- Every key press: the key sinks in, a wave rises out of the gradient below it and the input glow flashes at the same spot
- The floor's two layers – colour and white plus-lighter – drift and morph slowly
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the scene stays still and the demo does not type, typing yourself still works

### Responsive

- Keeps an 11 : 6 frame and scales to the width of its container – every detail is sized in container units
- Set the background with --ui-gk-bg (default #fafafa, #111113 in dark mode)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19

# Agent / Inbox (Pro)

What your orchestrator needs from you, one question at a time – pick an option, a variant or approve, send it in a keystroke and the next one glides in

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/inbox
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/inbox.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/inbox`

### When to use

- You work with one orchestrator in one thread, and it hands you the decisions it can't make alone – a choice between options, a variant to pick, an action to approve or a question to answer
- Clearing what waits on you quickly, from the keyboard, without reading traces or agent trees

### When not to use

- Watching how a run unfolds – use Agent / Orchestration or AI Chat / Run
- A few decisions inside another page – use Decision Inbox or Approval Card

### Usage

```tsx
import { InboxScreen } from "@/components/ui/inbox";

export default function Page() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(initialItems);
  return (
    <InboxScreen
      items={items}
      running={tasks.filter((t) => t.running).length}
      onDecide={(id, answer) => api.answer(id, answer)}
      onLater={(id) => api.snooze(id)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item – and with "Tasks" from the empty state |
| workspace | `string` | `"Fieldwork"` | The workspace in the sidebar |
| items | `{ id; kind: "decision" \| "pick" \| "approval" \| "question"; question; context?; task; at; unread?; options?; facts?; suggestions?; done? }[]` |  | Everything the orchestrator asked. at is a timestamp in ms; options { id, title, summary?, recommended?, pros?, cons?, wireframe?, preview? } for decision and pick – the recommended one is chosen when it opens; facts { label, value } for approval; suggestions for question; done { answer, at, label? } lists it under Done. Pass a stable array (state) – the screen follows it when it changes |
| running | `number` | `3` | How many tasks keep running – the line under "You're all caught up" |
| defaultTab | `"open" \| "done"` | `"open"` | The list the screen opens with |
| defaultSelected | `string` |  | The item open when the screen starts, by id – for a deep link, e.g. a task's Decide on the Tasks screen (?item=queue); it opens in its own list, and on phones full-width |
| onDecide | `(id: string, answer: { option?: string; text?: string } \| "approve" \| "decline") => void` |  | Called when you send – with the chosen option, what you wrote in the reply field, or both; approve / decline for an approval |
| onLater | `(id: string) => void` |  | Later – the item moves to the end of the open list |
| onReopen | `(id: string) => void` |  | Reopen on a done item – it moves back to the top of the open list |
| onSelect | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | Called when another item shows, and with null when none is left |
| tasks | `Record<string, { goal?; project?; status?; started?; steps?; artifacts? }>` |  | About each task, by its name – shown in the Task panel on the right |
| artifacts | `Record<string, { updated?; doc?; table?; sheet?; code?; image?; files?; preview? }>` |  | What each artifact shows in its tab, by file name. doc { title, paragraphs?, bullets?, html? } opens as a page you write in – bullets that start with "[ ] " / "[x] " make a checklist, html is what you wrote; table is rows of strings (a cell starting with = is a formula) with sheet { widths?, styles? } for column widths and cell styles by "row:col" ({ bold?, format?: "general" | "number" | "percent" | "currency" }); files is a folder – names, or { name, size?, modified?, kind?, files? } with size in bytes and modified as an ISO date or timestamp; a name without an extension is a subfolder |
| defaultOpenArtifacts | `{ task: string; name: string }[]` |  | Artifacts already open as tabs in the Task panel when the screen starts – once every tab was closed, the panel comes back with the task alone |
| suggested | `WorkspaceSource[]` | `a few of the artifacts` | Suggested in a New tab of the Task panel (the + after its tabs) – one with an artifact opens it in that tab |
| onOpenArtifact | `(task: string, name: string) => void` |  | Called when an artifact opens – from the Task panel, a done item or a folder |
| onArtifactChange | `(name: string, artifact: ShellArtifact) => void` |  | Called with the whole artifact whenever you change it in its tab – a cell, a column width, a style, the document's text, a folder's entries. The screen keeps every change itself while it lives (switch tabs, close and reopen); save it here |
| labels | `{ inbox?; open?; done?; send?; later?; approve?; decline?; reopen?; recommended?; reply?; answer?; sent?; caughtUp?; tasks?; running?: (n) => string; … }` |  | Labels, e.g. for a translation |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While your items load: gray rows in the list, a gray question in the reading column and gray lines in the Task panel, in the shape of the real ones (the shared Skeleton) |
| empty | `boolean` |  | No items at all: the list's head and Open / Done stay, the reading column shows “Nothing in your inbox yet” with a short line and a Go to Thread button, the Task panel says no task is open and the Inbox count hides; loading wins when both are on |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- J / K: Next and previous item – anywhere in the screen, as long as you're not typing
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In the list: move through the items (one Tab stop, the selected row takes it); the item shows on the right as you go
- 1 / 2 / 3: Pick that option or variant; in the options themselves ↑ ↓ ← → move between them
- Enter: Send – from anywhere, from the reply field too; on an option, picks it and sends. An approval is approved (or your words are sent instead)
- L: Later – the item moves to the end of the list and the next one shows
- R / /: Focus the reply field (on a question: the answer field)
- Shift Enter: A new line in a question's answer
- Esc: Leave the reply field – on phones, go back from the item to the list
- ← →: Open / Done: switch between the two lists
- ← → / Home / End: Task panel tabs: move between them; Delete closes the focused tab – the task too; closing the last one folds the panel and the focus moves to its open button
- ↑ ↓ ← → / Shift + arrows / ⌘ + arrows: Sheet: move the active cell, extend the selection, jump to the edge of the data
- Tab / Shift Tab / Enter / Shift Enter: Sheet: move right / left / down / up like Excel; Tab at the last column (Shift Tab at A) leaves the sheet
- Type / F2 / Enter / Esc: Sheet: typing replaces the cell (arrows then write it and move on), F2 or a double-click edits in place, Enter or Tab writes, Esc cancels; = starts a formula and a click on a cell adds its name
- ⌘A / ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V / ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z / ⌘B / Delete: Sheet: select all, copy / cut / paste as tab-separated text, undo, redo, bold, clear the selection
- ⌘B / ⌘I / ⌘U / ⇧⌘X / ⌘E / ⌘K: Document: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, link
- ⇧⌘7 / ⇧⌘8 / ⇧⌘9 / ⌘Enter / Tab: Document: numbered, bulleted and checklist; ⌘Enter ticks a checklist item; Tab / Shift Tab nest a list item. Typing "# ", "## ", "- ", "1. ", "[ ] " or "> " at the start of a line formats it
- ↑ ↓ / Shift ↑ ↓ / ⌘A / Enter / Space: Folder: move, extend, select all, open (a file in its own tab, a folder in place), Quick Look; type a name's start to jump to it
- ⌘[ / ⌘] / ⌘↑ / F2 / ⌘D / ⌘⌫ / ⇧⌘N / ⌘1 / ⌘2 / ⌘F: Folder: back, forward, up, rename, duplicate, move to trash, new folder, list / icons, search
- Shift F10 / Context menu key: Opens the context menu on the active cell, the caret or the selected item; ↑ ↓ move, → opens a submenu, ← and Esc go back

### Accessibility

- The list is a listbox with a roving tabindex – one Tab stop; every row is named in full: its kind, the question, the task, when it came in and whether it's unread
- Options and variants are radio groups – the chosen one is checked, its pros and cons are read with it and hidden from the others
- After you send, the focus stays on the item's heading while it confirms, then moves to the next item's heading – or to "You're all caught up"; Later and Reopen move it the same way, so it's never dropped
- A polite live region says what happened: "Sent. 4 left.", "Later. Next: …", "Reopened. 5 open."
- Shortcuts are listed on their buttons (aria-keyshortcuts) and never fire while you type, apart from Enter and Esc
- Every control shows the accent focus ring for the keyboard only (:focus-visible) – inside rows and option cards it sits inset, so a scroller never cuts it
- Long questions, tasks and options end in '…' with the full text in a tooltip; right-to-left text reads in its own direction
- The artifact toolbars are role="toolbar" with one Tab stop – ← → Home End move between the 28px tools; every tool has a name and a tip with its shortcut, toggles are aria-pressed
- The sheet is a role="grid" with aria-activedescendant on the active cell and aria-selected on every selected one; the active cell's ring turns accent while the sheet has the focus; changes, sorts and formula results are announced in a polite live region
- The document is a multi-line textbox; the folder a multi-select listbox with the keyboard's place shown as an inset accent ring; Quick Look is a dialog that leaves the focus in the list
- Menus, the link field and Quick Look close with Esc and hand the focus back; context menus are role="menu" with menuitem / menuitemcheckbox items, disabled ones marked aria-disabled
- The Task panel is the App Shell's work area: a tablist whose every tab – the task included – has a labelled ×; + opens a New tab with Suggested artifacts; the viewers, toolbars and menus are the App Shell's
- No shortcut fires while you type in a field, and the work area never scrolls sideways – only the sheet does, inside itself

### Motion

- One moment: sending turns the answer into a check that draws itself and "Sent – it'll take it from here", then the row folds out of the list and the next item glides in
- The chosen option opens to its pros and cons; the unread dot fades once you've seen the item
- Menus, tips and Quick Look fade in quickly; the sheet's selection moves without animation, like Excel's
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing slides, folds or draws – the confirmation simply shows

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Rows have one fixed height; the reading column stays at most 560px wide and centered
- Below 640px the list fills the screen; a row opens its item full-width with a back button, and Esc goes back
- On phones the reply field takes its own line above the buttons, the variants keep three to a row, shortcut hints hide; touch targets grow to 36px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell (installed with it)

# Inline Diff, clean style (Pro)

AI edits to prose shown inline – struck and added words you accept or reject one by one, with keys, a popover and undo

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/inline-diff
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/inline-diff-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/inline-diff-clean`

### When to use

- An AI rewrote a piece of prose – an email, a paragraph, a product description – and people should approve each edit
- "Make it shorter", "fix the tone", "fix grammar" actions where most edits are small and scattered through the text
- Review steps in an agent flow where the result should only change with an explicit yes

### When not to use

- Code or line-based text – use a line diff with gutters instead
- Full rewrites where almost every word changes – show the new version next to the old one
- Live typing suggestions inside an editor – this reviews a finished suggestion, it isn't a text field

### Usage

```tsx
import { InlineDiff } from "@/components/ui/inline-diff-clean";

export function ReviewRewrite({ draft, rewrite }: { draft: string; rewrite: string }) {
  return (
    <InlineDiff
      label="Suggested by AI · Make it shorter"
      original={draft}
      suggested={rewrite}
      onChange={(text) => saveDraft(text)}
      onDone={(text) => setFinal(text)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| original | `string` | `""` | The text as it is now |
| suggested | `string` | `""` | The text the AI suggests – diffed word by word against original |
| changes | `DiffSegment[]` |  | Pre-computed segments ({ type: "equal", text } or { type: "change", remove, insert }) instead of original and suggested |
| onChange | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called on every decision and undo with the text so far – pending changes keep the original words |
| onDone | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called when the last pending change is decided, with the final text |
| label | `string` |  | Small line at the top of the card, e.g. "Suggested by AI · Make it shorter" |
| ref | `Ref<InlineDiffHandle>` |  | highlight(index | null), accept(index), reject(index), acceptAll(), rejectAll(), undo(), reset() |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab / Shift+Tab: Move between pending changes
- ‹ / ›: Toolbar arrows: highlight the previous / next pending change (wrapping around) and open its popover
- Y / Enter: Accept the focused change and move to the next one
- N / Backspace: Reject the focused change and move to the next one
- Esc: Leave the change or clear the arrow highlight

### Accessibility

- Every pending change is a focusable button labelled like "Suggestion 2 of 4: replace “available” with “live”. Press Y to accept, N to reject"
- Removed words are a <del>, new words an <ins>; the side that was dropped is hidden from screen readers once decided
- Each decision, Accept all, Reject all and Undo are announced in a polite live region with the number left
- After the last decision focus moves to Undo, so the keyboard is never stranded; the hidden toolbar is inert
- Popover buttons are labelled and keep focus on the change; visible focus rings throughout
- The prev/next arrows never steal focus: a focused change hands focus to the next one, otherwise the change is highlighted while focus stays on the arrow
- Deleted words sit on a red tint and are struck, added words on a green one – color is never the only cue (strike-through, <del> and <ins>)

### Motion

- Accepting shrinks the struck words to nothing while the green tint fades and the new words settle into the text
- Rejecting does the opposite – the new words shrink away, the strike-through and red tint fade
- The popover fades up above a change and steps quickly from one change to the next
- The arrows only scroll the page when the next change is out of view (smoothly, or instantly with reduced motion)
- The toolbar cross-fades into "All changes reviewed" and the check draws itself
- With prefers-reduced-motion every change happens instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; the paragraph wraps freely and changes wrap across lines with their tints
- The popover stays inside the card horizontally, down to 320px wide
- In cards narrower than 360px the prev/next arrows step aside; on touch screens the popover buttons grow and drop the key hints
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the user's text as original and the model's rewrite as suggested – diffWords groups adjacent removals and insertions into one change
- Ask the model for a rewrite that keeps unchanged sentences verbatim; the fewer stray edits, the easier the review
- Write the result back with onDone (or onChange for drafts); undecided changes keep the original words
- diffWords is exported, so you can count edits or build the same segments on the server

### Requirements

- React 19

# Inline Diff (Pro)

AI edits to prose shown inline – struck and added words you accept or reject one by one, with keys, a popover and undo

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/inline-diff
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install, classic style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/inline-diff.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Install, clean style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/inline-diff-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key) – lands as `inline-diff-clean.tsx`, import from `@/components/ui/inline-diff-clean` – its docs: `inline-diff-clean.md`
- Import: `@/components/ui/inline-diff`

### When to use

- An AI rewrote a piece of prose – an email, a paragraph, a product description – and people should approve each edit
- "Make it shorter", "fix the tone", "fix grammar" actions where most edits are small and scattered through the text
- Review steps in an agent flow where the result should only change with an explicit yes

### When not to use

- Code or line-based text – use a line diff with gutters instead
- Full rewrites where almost every word changes – show the new version next to the old one
- Live typing suggestions inside an editor – this reviews a finished suggestion, it isn't a text field

### Usage

```tsx
import { InlineDiff } from "@/components/ui/inline-diff";

export function ReviewRewrite({ draft, rewrite }: { draft: string; rewrite: string }) {
  return (
    <InlineDiff
      label="Suggested by AI · Make it shorter"
      original={draft}
      suggested={rewrite}
      onChange={(text) => saveDraft(text)}
      onDone={(text) => setFinal(text)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| original | `string` | `""` | The text as it is now |
| suggested | `string` | `""` | The text the AI suggests – diffed word by word against original |
| changes | `DiffSegment[]` |  | Pre-computed segments ({ type: "equal", text } or { type: "change", remove, insert }) instead of original and suggested |
| onChange | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called on every decision and undo with the text so far – pending changes keep the original words |
| onDone | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called when the last pending change is decided, with the final text |
| label | `string` |  | Small line on the gray tray above the card, e.g. "Suggested by AI · Make it shorter" |
| ref | `Ref<InlineDiffHandle>` |  | highlight(index | null), accept(index), reject(index), acceptAll(), rejectAll(), undo(), reset() |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab / Shift+Tab: Move between pending changes
- ‹ / ›: Toolbar arrows: highlight the previous / next pending change (wrapping around) and open its popover
- Y / Enter: Accept the focused change and move to the next one
- N / Backspace: Reject the focused change and move to the next one
- Esc: Leave the change or clear the arrow highlight

### Accessibility

- Every pending change is a focusable button labelled like "Suggestion 2 of 4: replace “available” with “live”. Press Y to accept, N to reject"
- Removed words are a <del>, new words an <ins>; the side that was dropped is hidden from screen readers once decided
- Each decision, Accept all, Reject all and Undo are announced in a polite live region with the number left
- After the last decision focus moves to Undo, so the keyboard is never stranded; the hidden toolbar is inert
- Popover buttons are labelled and keep focus on the change; visible focus rings throughout
- The prev/next arrows never steal focus: a focused change hands focus to the next one, otherwise the change is highlighted while focus stays on the arrow
- Deleted words are red and struck, added words green – color is never the only cue (strike-through, <del> and <ins>)

### Motion

- Accepting shrinks the struck words to nothing while the green tint fades and the new words settle into the text
- Rejecting does the opposite – the new words shrink away, the strike-through and red tint fade
- The popover fades up above a change and glides from one change to the next
- The arrows only scroll the page when the next change is out of view (smoothly, or instantly with reduced motion)
- The toolbar cross-fades into "All changes reviewed" and the check draws itself
- With prefers-reduced-motion every change happens instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; the paragraph wraps freely and changes wrap across lines with their tints
- The popover stays inside the card horizontally, down to 320px wide
- Below 400px the prev/next arrows step aside; on touch screens the popover buttons grow and drop the key hints
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the user's text as original and the model's rewrite as suggested – diffWords groups adjacent removals and insertions into one change
- Ask the model for a rewrite that keeps unchanged sentences verbatim; the fewer stray edits, the easier the review
- Write the result back with onDone (or onChange for drafts); undecided changes keep the original words
- diffWords is exported, so you can count edits or build the same segments on the server

### Requirements

- React 19

# Integration Beam (Free)

Your product between the tools it connects – light pulses flow along curved beams, hover to focus a tool, click to pause it

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-beam
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-beam.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-beam`

### When to use

- A hero or integrations section that shows your product sitting between the tools a team already uses
- Landing pages where a calm, self-playing data flow explains “we connect to X and Y” faster than a logo wall

### When not to use

- A real integration settings page – pausing a tool here is only part of the scene, nothing is saved
- More than four tools per side – the beams get crowded; use Integration Grid or Logo Cluster for long lists

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationBeam } from "@/components/ui/integration-beam";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationBeam />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| left | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `Slack, Notion, Gmail` | Tools that send data in – on the left, or above the hub on narrow widths. The logo fills a 28 × 28 box |
| right | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `HubSpot, Linear, Google Drive` | Tools that receive data – on the right, or below the hub on narrow widths |
| center | `{ name: string; logo?: ReactNode }` | `{ name: "Acme" }` | Your product. The logo is drawn white into a 36 × 36 box on the dark tile (currentColor); a neutral flower mark when left out |
| label | `string` | `"Acme connected to Slack, Notion, …"` | Accessible name of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the tool tiles; the focused tool's beam comes forward and its name shows
- Enter / Space: Pauses or reconnects the focused tool

### Accessibility

- The scene is a labelled group; every tool is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a name like “Slack, connected”
- Pausing or reconnecting is announced in a polite live region, with the new count (“5 of 6 connected”)
- The beams, pulses and logos are decorative and hidden from screen readers
- Visible focus ring on the tiles; the tooltip also shows on keyboard focus

### Motion

- Sync cycles: pulses leave the left tools 280 ms apart, travel 1.5 s along their beam and, as they land, the hub glows and the next wave leaves for the right tools
- Each pulse is a short gradient – clear tail, accent body, pale tip – with a soft blurred glow; one accent color only
- The status chip under the hub slides between “Syncing…” and “6 connected”, and its width glides with the text
- When the layout switches between side by side and stacked, the tiles glide to their new spots and the curves morph with them (460 ms)
- The loop only runs while the scene is on screen (IntersectionObserver)
- With prefers-reduced-motion the beams are drawn as static lines – no pulses, no glides; hover, focus and pausing still work

### Responsive

- The beams are measured from the real tile positions (ResizeObserver), so the scene reflows with its container
- Below 460px of container width the senders stack above the hub and the receivers below, with vertical beams; fits 320px screens
- On touch screens a tap pauses a tool and shows its name for a moment instead of a hover tooltip
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

### When to use

- A hero or feature section that shows your product pulling data in from the tools teams already use

### When not to use

- A real list of connected integrations – the pills are decorative, not interactive
- Very small spaces below ~320px wide, where the pill text gets hard to read
- Brands that clash with the warm coral background

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationFlow } from "@/components/ui/integration-flow";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationFlow />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `{ name: string; icon: ReactNode; title?: string; mono?: boolean }[]` | `Okta, Snowflake, Slack, ClickUp, Zendesk` | Integrations that rotate through the pills (5 or more look best). The icon fills a 64 × 64 box; mono logos turn black in the centre |
| label | `string` | `"Integrations like Slack, Okta and Snowflake…"` | Accessible description of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- The scene is exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the pills and cards inside are hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The pills travel along the dashed arc one slot at a time (0.9 s); the one landing in the centre turns light and shows its logo in color
- The centre pill charges up, a beam sweeps over to the Data Analysis hub (1.1 s) and the hub lights up as it arrives
- The coral background blobs drift and breathe slowly on a 16 s loop
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything stands still in the centre state, with the beam drawn in

### Responsive

- Drawn on a 2400 × 1490 stage and scaled to the width of its container, so the layout never reflows
- Keeps its 2400 : 1490 aspect ratio; set a width or max-width via className
- Set --ui-if-bg and --ui-if-fade to change the stage background and the color the bottom fades into
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Invoice & Credit Note, clean style (Pro)

An invoice and its credit note stacked like paper – switch between them, pick lines to credit, adjust amounts and issue

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/invoice-credit
- Section: Blocks · Billing
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/invoice-credit-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/invoice-credit-clean`

### When to use

- Billing portals and admin tools that show an invoice and let a team credit it
- Product pages for invoicing software – a document that looks real and can be tried

### When not to use

- Printing or PDF generation – render a dedicated print layout instead
- Invoices with dozens of lines – the credit list is built for a handful

### Usage

```tsx
import { InvoiceCredit } from "@/components/ui/invoice-credit-clean";

export function Billing() {
  return (
    <InvoiceCredit
      invoiceNo="INV-2041"
      creditNo="CN-0117"
      lines={[
        { id: "plan", name: "Growth plan", qty: 1, rate: 1250, tax: 0.2 },
        { id: "api", name: "API calls (per 1k)", qty: 18420, rate: 0.42, tax: 0.2, group: "Metered usage" },
      ]}
      onIssue={(credits, total) => api.issueCreditNote(credits, total)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seller / buyer | `{ name, lines: string[] }` |  | From and To blocks on the invoice |
| invoiceNo / creditNo | `string` |  | Document numbers shown under Terms |
| invoiceDate / dueDate / period | `string` |  | Dates shown on both documents; an empty one leaves its line out |
| lines | `InvoiceLine[]` |  | Each { id, name, qty, rate, tax, group? } – lines with a group are listed under a heading. A negative rate is a discount; a rate that is not a number shows — and counts as 0 |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | A symbol shown in front of amounts ("$", "£"), or an ISO code ("EUR", "JPY") formatted with Intl – the code is also shown after the applied total |
| onIssue | `(credits, total) => void` |  | Called when the credit note is issued, with the credited amount per line and the total incl. tax |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the switch (one stop), the actions, every line and amount
- ← / →: On the switch: moves between Invoice and Credit note
- Home / End: On the switch: jumps to Invoice or Credit note
- Space: Picks or drops a line to credit
- Enter: Confirms an amount
- Esc: In an amount: throws the typed amount away

### Accessibility

- The switch is a tablist with one tab stop and its sheets are tabpanels; buttons that send you to the other sheet move focus to its tab, and Issue and Edit hand focus to each other; the sheet in the back is hidden from screen readers and can't be focused
- Credit lines are checkboxes with labels; amounts are labelled per line and stay within the line total

### Motion

- Switching slides the sheets: the chosen one comes forward, the other tucks behind it with only its top edge showing
- Checkmarks draw in; the white chip glides between Invoice and Credit note
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 560px the parties stack, the rate and tax columns hide and the credit list drops the total column
- Clean look: single white sheets with hairline shadows and no tray, tiny uppercase labels, spacing instead of rules, one dark Issue button
- Touch screens get 36px buttons and fields and larger checkboxes
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
