# Judge Bracket, clean style (Pro)

How an LLM judge picks the best of several attempts, as a tournament – two answers at a time, the one it prefers moves on, the other fades back; the winner's way through the bracket lights up, and every match opens both answers side by side with the scores and why

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/judge-bracket
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/judge-bracket-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/judge-bracket-clean`

### When to use

- LLM-as-a-judge: several models, prompts or temperatures answer the same task and a judge picks the best, two at a time
- Showing why a generated answer won – every match with both answers side by side, the scores and the judge's reason
- Best-of-n for coding agents: several fixes for the same bug, judged on whether they solve the cause, pass the tests and stay small

### When not to use

- Several attempts running at once, without a judge comparing them – use Parallel Attempts
- Trying models one after another until one works – use Fallback Chain
- Comparing many cells of work at a glance – use Fan-out Grid

### Usage

```tsx
import { JudgeBracket, type Contender } from "@/components/ui/judge-bracket-clean";

const contenders: Contender[] = [
  { id: "a", name: "Sonnet · warm", meta: "142 words", output: "Subject: Your 14 days start now…" },
  { id: "b", name: "GPT-5 · formal", meta: "168 words", output: "Subject: Welcome to your trial…" },
  { id: "c", name: "Gemini · bullets", meta: "104 words", output: "Subject: 3 steps to your first project…" },
  { id: "d", name: "Sonnet · short", meta: "96 words", output: "Subject: Start your first project…" },
];

export function BestEmail() {
  return (
    <JudgeBracket
      contenders={contenders}
      verdicts={{ "0:0": { winner: "a", scores: [8.1, 7.4], reason: "Warmer, and it names the trial length." } }}
      judging="0:1"
      judge="Claude Opus"
      task="Welcome email for new trial users"
      onPick={(winner) => send(winner.output)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| contenders | `Contender[]` |  | Every attempt, in seed order – 2, 4, 8 or 16; neighbours meet in the first round |
| Contender | `{ id, name, icon?, meta?, output? }` |  | name – what makes this attempt different; icon – e.g. the model maker's logo; meta – a quiet line like "118 words · 2.1s"; output – what it produced |
| verdicts | `Record<string, { winner, reason?, scores? }>` |  | What the judge decided, by match "round:match" from 0 – e.g. "0:2" is the third match of the first round; scores are for the upper and the lower contender |
| judging | `string` |  | The match the judge works on right now, same key – both names shimmer |
| judge | `string` |  | Who judges – e.g. "Claude Opus" |
| task | `string` |  | What the attempts are for – shown muted next to the title |
| onPick | `(winner: Contender) => void` |  | Use the winner – without it, the final has no button |
| title | `string` | `"Judge"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Into the bracket, match by match, then to the answers and Use
- ← / →: To the match this one feeds, and back to the first one feeding it
- ↑ / ↓: The match above and below in the same round
- Enter / Space: Shows that match's answers; again goes back
- Esc: Back to what the judge works on

### Accessibility

- Every match is a button that says its round, both contenders and who won – or that it's being judged
- The match below the bracket is announced politely when it changes, and the bar says who's ahead
- Winning is never color alone: the winner keeps its full color and a check or its score, the other fades and its line is dashed

### Motion

- The match being judged shimmers; the one it prefers slides into the next round, the other fades back flat but stays
- When the final is decided, the winner's way through the bracket draws itself in blue, round after round, and a cup appears in the final
- The answers below ease to their new height when you open another match
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears

### Responsive

- Every slot has a fixed height, so nothing moves while the judge works; the rounds share the width
- When the rounds don't fit side by side it becomes a list per round, two contenders a row, and the answers stack
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Seed the contenders in the order they should meet – neighbours play each other first
- Only add a verdict for a match whose two contenders are both known; winner must be one of them
- Keep name to what makes the attempt different (model · prompt), and reason to one sentence
- The blue of the winner's way is --ui-jbc-path; how far what you didn't pick fades is --ui-jbc-dim

### Requirements

- React 19

# KPI Board, clean style (Pro)

The top of a dashboard – three trend cards, an overview chart that compares this period with the last, and a focus card; hover shows any day's value and every number rolls when the range changes

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/kpi-board
- Section: Blocks · Analytics
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/kpi-board-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/kpi-board-clean`

### When to use

- The top of a dashboard: a few headline numbers with their trend, one chart that compares this period with the last, and one product or plan in focus
- Sales, growth and usage overviews of a SaaS or AI product, above a table or a list
- When the charts belong together – same range, same filter – and should react as one

### When not to use

- One metric in depth – use KPI Chart or Breakdown Chart
- Parts of a whole (shares, funnels, rankings) – the board only draws trends over time
- Reports that are printed or exported – this is built for pointing and switching

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiBoard, type KpiBoardData } from "@/components/ui/kpi-board-clean";

const ranges = [
  { id: "7d", label: "Last 7 days" },
  { id: "30d", label: "Last 30 days" },
];

export function Overview({ data }: { data: Record<string, KpiBoardData> }) {
  // data["30d"] = { stats, overview, focus }
  return <KpiBoard data={data} ranges={ranges} defaultRange="30d" compareLabel="vs. last month" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | `Record<string, KpiBoardData>` |  | One data set per range id: { stats, overview, focus } |
| ranges | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the date range picker |
| range | `string` |  | Controlled range id |
| defaultRange | `string` | `first range` | Starting range when uncontrolled |
| onRangeChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new range |
| segments | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | A filter inside the overview card, e.g. All items / Pro / Team – it only switches that card's lines; no filter when left out |
| segment | `string` |  | Controlled segment id |
| defaultSegment | `string` | `first segment` | Starting segment when uncontrolled |
| onSegmentChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new segment |
| compareLabel | `string` | `"vs. last period"` | Words after every change |
| currentLabel | `string` | `"This period"` | Name of the main line in the tooltip and the focus card |
| previousLabel | `string` | `"Last period"` | Name of the comparison line |
| formatMoney | `(value: number) => string` | `$1,234.00` | Formats money values |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Icon in the focus card |
| title | `string` |  | Heading on the left of the bar above the cards |
| setup | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The small button at the top right of the focus card, e.g. Set up |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The button at the bottom of the focus card |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the pickers, the charts and the action
- Enter / Space / ↓: On a picker: opens its menu
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In an open menu: moves through the choices
- Enter: Picks the highlighted choice
- Esc: Closes the menu without changing anything
- ← / → / Home / End: On a chart: steps through the days and shows that day's value; Esc lets go

### Accessibility

- Every card has its numbers as text; each chart is a focusable group whose value at the chosen day is announced (the focus card reads its day out through a status line)
- The pickers are comboboxes with a listbox: the open state, the highlighted and the chosen option are announced
- Changes are small tinted badges with an arrow, so they don't rely on color alone; the color follows whether the change is good news (lowerIsBetter)

### Motion

- On first view the cards rise in one after another and every line draws itself in from the left
- Switching the range rolls every number while every line glides from the old data to the new
- The filter inside the overview does the same for that card only – the other cards stay still
- Hovering a small card marks the day under the pointer with a dot and its value and date in a small tag
- Hovering the overview shows a tooltip that compares this period with the last at that day
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- The date range sits above the cards on the right. Three small cards over a wide overview and the focus card; below 820px of container width the two lower cards take a full row each, below 600px everything stacks
- It follows its container, not the window
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Series may have different numbers of points per range (7 days, 30 days, 13 weeks) – the lines glide between them
- A stat's value is the sum of its series; `previous` is the total of the period before and drives the change in percent under the number
- Points that are not a number count as 0 in the totals and leave a gap in the line; a previous total of 0 leaves the change out instead of showing +0%
- focus.unitOne is the word after a count of exactly 1 – without it the unit loses its plural s ("1 license"), so only irregular words like person need it; long labels end in an ellipsis with the full text in a tooltip, numbers are never cut
- The date range sits in the bar above the cards because it changes all of them; the picker inside the overview is the segment and only switches the overview's own lines (overview.segments)

### Requirements

- React 19

# KPI Chart, clean style (Pro)

Metric card with a multi-line chart and a tooltip that follows the pointer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/kpi-chart
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/kpi-chart-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/kpi-chart-clean`

### When to use

- Dashboards that show one headline number and how its parts moved over a short period
- Comparing a handful of channels, pages or plans day by day

### When not to use

- More than about six lines – the chart and the tooltip get hard to read
- Long time ranges with hundreds of points – use a chart library with zoom and sampling

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiChart } from "@/components/ui/kpi-chart-clean";

export function Revenue() {
  return (
    <KpiChart
      title="Revenue"
      value="$96.4k"
      delta={7900}
      format={(n) => `$${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`}
      labels={["Mar 3", "Mar 4", "Mar 5"]}
      series={[
        { label: "Organic", color: "#2f6bff", values: [4600, 4900, 5200] },
        { label: "Paid ads", color: "#ec4899", values: [3100, 3400, 3200] },
      ]}
      footer="Top channels"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Label above the number |
| value | `string` |  | Headline value, already formatted |
| delta | `number` |  | Change against the previous period – green when positive, red when negative |
| labels | `string[]` |  | One label per point; first, middle and last are shown on the axis |
| tooltipLabels | `string[]` |  | Longer labels for the tooltip header, falls back to labels |
| series | `KpiSeries[]` |  | Lines with a label, a color and one value per label |
| format | `(n: number) => string` | `compact, e.g. 1.2k` | Formats axis, tooltip and delta values |
| footer | `string` |  | Line under the chart |
| defaultIndex | `number` |  | Point that stays highlighted while nobody hovers |
| emptyText | `string` | `"No data yet"` | Quiet text in the plot when there are no values, or only zeros (0% on a percent axis still draws) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focus the chart
- ← / →: Move to the previous or next point
- Esc: Close the tooltip

### Accessibility

- The chart is focusable and readable with the arrow keys
- The tooltip is a polite live region, so screen readers announce the values of the current point

### Motion

- Lines draw in from the left on mount
- Guide, dots and tooltip move between points in a short, crisp step; reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- The white card fills its container up to 460px; the plot scales, line widths stay crisp
- Touch works too – tap or drag across the chart
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Layer Stack (Free)

Isometric stack of five layers with a list beside it – the chosen entry lifts its layer out in color

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/layer-stack
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/layer-stack.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/layer-stack`

### When to use

- Explaining a layered product or platform – each entry is one layer of the stack
- Feature sections that walk through capabilities one by one, with a visual that follows along

### When not to use

- More than five layers – the stack and the list are sized for up to five
- Navigation that changes page content – this is an illustration with its own small state

### Usage

```tsx
import { LayerStack } from "@/components/ui/layer-stack";

export function PlatformSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <LayerStack
        items={[
          { title: "Triggered by events", hint: "Webhooks", icon: "bolt" },
          { title: "Grounded in your data", hint: "Context", icon: "database" },
          { title: "Connected to your apps", hint: "APIs", icon: "plug" },
          { title: "Works with any model", hint: "Routing", icon: "spark" },
          { title: "Traced at every step", hint: "Logs", icon: "pulse" },
        ]}
      />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `LayerStackItem[]` | `five sample layers` | Up to five entries, top layer first – { title, hint?, icon? } with icon one of bolt, database, plug, spark, pulse |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `0` | Entry to start on |
| interval | `number` | `2600` | Time per entry while it plays on its own, in ms |
| onChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called when the user picks an entry |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves focus to the chosen entry
- ↑ / ↓: Picks the previous or next entry

### Accessibility

- The list is a vertical tablist with real buttons; the chosen entry has aria-selected
- The stack itself is decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The chosen layer and the ones above it glide up to open a gap; its face, edge and icon turn blue and a soft glow fades in beneath it
- A white card glides behind the chosen entry in the list
- Steps through the entries on its own and pauses while hovered or focused; after a click or key press it stays put
- With prefers-reduced-motion it doesn't play on its own and changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – text and layers are sized in container units
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Live Session, clean style (Pro)

Work with a team of agents while they work – their conversation in the middle, the team's plan ticking off beside it, and the shared context under it; picking an agent points at its steps

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/live-session
- Section: Blocks · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/live-session-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/live-session-clean`

### When to use

- The working view of a multi-agent product: you talk to the team, watch the plan move and see how full the context gets – on one screen
- Human-in-the-loop work where agents ask you things mid-run and you answer in the same place
- Showing who is on which step: pick an agent and its part of the plan stands out

### When not to use

- A finished run to look back on – Run Inspector shows one run in depth
- One agent and one user – Agent Chat or Chat Composer alone is simpler

### Usage

```tsx
import { LiveSession, type SessionStep } from "@/components/ui/live-session-clean";

const steps: SessionStep[] = [
  { id: "prices", title: "Compare per-seat prices", agent: "research", status: "done", duration: 84_000 },
  { id: "copy", title: "Draft the copy for the three plans", agent: "writer", status: "active", startedAt: Date.now() - 60_000 },
  { id: "price", title: "Pick the Team price", agent: "you" },
];

export function Session() {
  return (
    <LiveSession
      agents={[{ id: "research", name: "Researcher" }, { id: "writer", name: "Writer" }]}
      messages={messages}
      task="Launch the new pricing page"
      steps={steps}
      context={{ limit: 200_000, model: "Opus 5.5", parts: [{ id: "talk", label: "Conversation", tokens: 42_000 }] }}
      live
      onSend={({ text, to }) => send(text, to)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `StreamAgent[]` |  | The agents in the session – { id, name, model?, avatar? }; "you" is there on its own |
| messages | `StreamMessage[]` |  | The conversation, as in Collaboration Stream – { id, from, to, kind, text, at?, replyTo?, typing?, attachments?, details? } |
| task | `string` |  | What the team works on – the label of the whole session |
| steps | `SessionStep[]` |  | The team's plan – Agent Steering steps plus agent, the id of whoever works on it ("you" for a step that's yours) |
| status | `"running" \| "paused" \| "done"` | `"running"` | How the plan stands |
| startedAt | `number \| Date` |  | When the session started – the plan counts its running time from here |
| context | `{ parts, limit, model?, modelIcon? }` |  | The shared context as Context Window parts – leave it out to show the plan alone |
| live | `boolean` |  | Agents are still at work – the stream follows new messages and says so |
| logos | `Record<string, ReactNode>` |  | Names that get their logo when a message mentions them, e.g. { Stripe: <StripeLogo /> } |
| focusAgent | `string \| null` |  | Controlled agent the session is narrowed to – the stream fades the rest, the plan keeps that agent's steps |
| onFocusAgentChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | Called when an agent is picked or let go |
| onSend | `(message: { text, to, replyTo? }) => void` |  | A message from you – to everyone, to the agents you named with @, or as a reply |
| onPause / onResume | `() => void` |  | The plan's pause button |
| maxHeight | `number` | `560` | The stream's height when the plan goes under it on narrow screens; side by side it matches the plan and the context |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the agent tabs, the messages, the composer and the context – each shows an accent focus ring; clicking into the composer shows none
- ← / →: In the agent tabs, moves between agents – Home and End jump to the ends
- ↑ / ↓: Moves between messages; Enter opens a message's details
- Esc: Lets go of the picked message or agent – the plan shows every step again
- @: In the composer, opens the agents to name – ↑ ↓ and Enter pick one
- Enter: Sends; Shift + Enter makes a new line

### Accessibility

- The session is a labelled region named after its task
- The plan is an ordered list – the running step is marked as the current one and its time is announced
- Messages carry who wrote them, to whom and when in their label

### Motion

- Picking an agent fades the other messages and the other steps – one pick, both sides
- Steps tick off as they finish; the context's cells fill as the conversation grows
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything changes in one step

### Responsive

- Side by side, the stream is exactly as tall as the plan and the context – its messages scroll, the composer stays at the bottom
- Follows its own width: below 860px the plan and the context go under the stream, which takes maxHeight
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: collaboration-stream, agent-steering, context-window, mission-control

# Memory Graph, clean style (Pro)

An agent in the middle with what it remembers and the tools it can reach in a ring around it – every memory a card with the file, chat or email it came from and that app's logo, every tool with what it may do and where, joined by Agent Tree's rounded connectors; a light runs out to each tool it uses and in from a tool through the agent to what it learns, lighting the card up with a Gradient Floor; switch anything off, forget a memory, or click the agent to drop in a file or connect a tool

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/memory-graph
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/memory-graph-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/memory-graph-clean`

### When to use

- Showing what an assistant or agent knows about the user and their work, and where each piece came from – the file, the chat, the email
- Showing which tools an agent can reach, what it may do with them, and which one it uses right now
- Letting people manage that: switch a memory or a tool off, forget a memory, drop in a file or connect a tool

### When not to use

- A flat, editable list of memories with categories and undo – use Memory Panel
- What fills one run's context window – use Context Map
- Every tool an agent touched in one run, with its calls – use Tool Access Map

### Usage

```tsx
import { MemoryGraph, type Memory, type MemoryTool } from "@/components/ui/memory-graph-clean";

const memories: Memory[] = [
  { id: "m1", text: "Prefers short answers", source: "You asked for it twice", artifact: { name: "Feedback", kind: "chat" } },
  { id: "m2", text: "Q4 design budget €48k", source: "From the budget sheet", artifact: { name: "budget-q4.xlsx" } },
  { id: "m3", text: "Redesign ships Dec 11", source: "Lea moved it in today's standup", artifact: { name: "standup-nov-14.md" }, via: "notion" },
];

const tools: MemoryTool[] = [
  { id: "notion", name: "Notion", logo: <NotionLogo />, access: "Read", scope: "Design wiki", note: "Read the standup notes" },
  { id: "github", name: "GitHub", logo: <GitHubLogo />, access: "Read & write", scope: "lumen/web" },
```

# Memory Panel, clean style (Pro)

What the assistant remembers about you, grouped and editable – a master switch, category filters, and on every memory edit in place, pause or forget with Undo on the tray

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/memory-panel
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/memory-panel-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/memory-panel-clean`

### When to use

- Assistants and agents that remember things across chats – the place where people see, correct and remove what was kept
- Settings or a side panel next to the chat, so a wrong memory can be fixed the moment it shows up in an answer
- Products that need a clear off switch for personalization without losing what was saved

### When not to use

- What the model has in mind right now, inside one conversation – use Context Window
- Hundreds of entries with sorting and bulk actions – a Data Table handles that better
- Account settings that are not about what the assistant learned – a plain settings list says that with less

### Usage

```tsx
import { MemoryPanel } from "@/components/ui/memory-panel-clean";

export function AssistantMemory() {
  return (
    <MemoryPanel
      memories={[
        { id: "ts", text: "Prefers TypeScript examples over plain JavaScript", category: "Preferences", source: "From chat", date: "Oct 12" },
        { id: "role", text: "Product designer and front-end developer", category: "Work", source: "From chat", date: "Sep 28" },
        { id: "fintech", text: "Redesigning a fintech onboarding flow, due Oct 24", category: "Projects", source: "From chat", date: "Oct 11" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| memories | `Memory[]` |  | { id, text, category, source?, date?, paused? } – source and date are shown as given, e.g. "From chat" and "Oct 12" |
| onChange | `(memories: Memory[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list after any change. With it the panel shows exactly the memories you pass; without it the changes live inside the panel |
| onAdd | `(memory: Memory) => void` |  | A memory was added with New memory |
| onEdit | `(id: string, text: string) => void` |  | The text of a memory was edited and saved |
| onPause | `(id: string, paused: boolean) => void` |  | A memory was paused or resumed |
| onForget | `(id: string) => void` |  | A memory was forgotten – it can still come back with Undo |
| onRestore | `(memory: Memory) => void` |  | A forgotten memory was brought back with Undo, at its old place |
| enabled | `boolean` |  | The Use memory switch, controlled |
| defaultEnabled | `boolean` | `true` | Start state of the switch when it is not controlled |
| onEnabledChange | `(enabled: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the switch is flipped |
| categories | `string[]` |  | Order of the groups and the choices for new memories – defaults to the categories in the order they appear |
| title | `string` | `"Memory"` | Heading of the panel |
| maxHeight | `number` | `360` | Height of the list in px before it scrolls |
| undoFor | `number` | `5000` | How long Undo stays in the last row after forgetting, in ms |
| addedSource | `string` | `"You added"` | Source given to memories added in the panel; their date is today |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button in the last row of the card – Undo takes its place for a moment after forgetting |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Switch, the selected category chip, search, then each memory's Edit, Pause and Forget, New memory and the last-row button
- ← / →: Move between category chips (and between categories of a new memory)
- Enter: Saves an edited or new memory (Shift + Enter for a line break)
- Esc: Cancels editing, closes New memory or the search field

### Accessibility

- A group named by its title; Use memory is a switch with aria-checked and controls the note that unfolds
- Category chips are a radiogroup with arrow keys and one tab stop; each group of memories is a labelled section
- Every action button is named after its memory, e.g. "Forget “Prefers TypeScript…”"; actions also show on keyboard focus
- Rows that are filtered out or folding away are inert, so the keyboard never lands on something hidden
- The status line in the last row is announced politely: counts, the forgotten memory with Undo, and editing hints

### Motion

- Filtering folds the rows that don't match closed and fades them – nothing slides across the list
- Forgetting folds the row away with a soft blur; Undo unfolds it at its old place and scrolls it into view
- Pausing greys the text and a Paused tag fades in; the pause icon swaps to play
- Counts on the head and in the last row roll to their new value; changing status text crossfades
- Turning memory off dims the list and unfolds a short note; New memory unfolds into the editor in place of the button
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 400px; works from 300px wide. Below 360px the chips drop their counts, below 320px the switch keeps only its track
- Category chips scroll sideways when they don't fit, with a soft fade at the edge while more hide past it
- Touch screens: the actions are always visible and every button gets a taller hit area
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass source and date already formatted – the panel shows them as they are
- Forgetting calls onForget right after the row folds away; keep the item around (soft delete) until undoFor has passed if your backend can't restore it
- Paused memories stay in the list and count in the total; filter them out yourself before sending memories to the model
- Without onChange the panel copies memories once on mount – give it a new key to reset it

### Requirements

- React 19

# Metering Chart, clean style (Pro)

Usage per day as soft gradient bars drifting from blue to lilac, with a live bar for today that keeps growing, a Real-time badge and rolling totals

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/metering-chart
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/metering-chart-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/metering-chart-clean`

### When to use

- Usage-based billing and metering – API calls, tokens, events, minutes per day
- A usage card where today is still counting and should look alive
- A calm daily bar chart that reads as a whole, with totals above it

### When not to use

- Comparing series or periods – use Trend Chart
- Hundreds of days – the bars get too thin; group them into weeks first

### Usage

```tsx
import { MeteringChart } from "@/components/ui/metering-chart-clean";

export function ApiCalls() {
  return (
    <MeteringChart
      title="API calls"
      live
      period="Sep 1 – Sep 21"
      data={[
        { label: "Sep 1", value: 1870 },
        { label: "Sep 2", value: 2290 },
        { label: "Sep 3", value: 2860 },
      ]}
      totals={[
        { label: "Total volume", value: 50390, format: (n) => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString()}` },
        { label: "Total events", value: 36000 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Heading of the card |
| data | `MeteringDay[]` |  | { label, value } per day, oldest first; a missing or broken value leaves an empty slot |
| totals | `MeteringTotal[]` |  | { label, value, format? } – figures under the title that roll to their new values |
| period | `string` |  | The span on the right, e.g. "Sep 1 – Sep 21" |
| live | `boolean` | `false` | The last bar is today and still counting: accent color, a running sheen, a turning spinner in the pink badge |
| badge | `string` | `"Real-time" when live` | Text next to the title; empty for none |
| format | `(n: number) => string` | `1,284` | Formats the tag and the totals |
| axisFormat | `(n: number) => string` |  | Shorter numbers for the value axis, e.g. 4.5k |
| colors | `string[]` | `light blue → lilac → mauve` | Colors the bars drift through from left to right |
| accent | `string` | `"#5e5cff"` | Color of the live bar |
| height | `number` | `120` | Height of the plot in px |
| emptyText | `string` | `"No usage yet"` | Quiet text when there is nothing to draw |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focus the chart
- ← / →: Move to the previous or next day
- Home / End: Jump to the first day or today
- Esc: Close the tag

### Accessibility

- The chart is one focusable stop, readable with the arrow keys; the tag is a polite live region
- Totals are read out with their final value, never a number on its way

### Motion

- Bars rise from the left in a wave on first view; heights and the axis ease when values change
- The live bar carries a slow sheen and the badge's spinner turns; reduced motion turns all of it off

### Responsive

- Fills its container; bars stay 11px wide and thin out on narrow cards, the period moves under the title
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: trend-chart, stat-card, usage-meter

# Metrics Dashboard, clean style (Pro)

Sales overview – KPI cards pick the metric, one Trend Chart switches between area and bars, with top products and channels – built from Stat Card and Trend Chart

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/metrics-dashboard
- Section: Blocks · Analytics
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/metrics-dashboard-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard-clean`

### When to use

- A compact sales or business overview with a handful of headline metrics
- Dashboards where one chart, picked by KPI cards and shown as a line or as bars, says more than a grid of small charts

### When not to use

- Large data sets or drill-downs – the chart shows up to 30 points per period
- A single number – use a KPI card instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { MetricsDashboard } from "@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard-clean";

export function Overview({ days, products, channels }) {
  return (
    <MetricsDashboard
      title="Sales"
      site="Northwind Store"
      data={days} // [{ date, revenue, orders, refunded }, …] oldest first
      products={products} // [{ name: "Linen overshirt", share: 0.22 }, …]
      channels={channels}
      currency="USD"
      defaultRange="30d"
      onExport={(range, metric) => console.log("export", range, metric)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` | `"Sales"` | Title in the bar on top |
| site | `string` | `"Northwind Store"` | Site or workspace shown under the title |
| defaultRange | `"7d" \| "30d" \| "90d"` | `"30d"` | Period to start on – shown as Week, Month and Quarter |
| defaultMetric | `"revenue" \| "orders" \| "aov" \| "refunds"` | `"revenue"` | Metric to start on |
| onExport | `(range, metric) => void` |  | Called when Export is pressed; the button confirms locally either way |
| data | `{ date: Date; revenue; orders; refunded }[]` | `sample data` | One entry per day, oldest first; 180 days give every range a previous period. Days missing a number count as 0; without a previous period the cards show no change |
| products | `{ name: string; share: number }[]` | `sample products` | Rows of Top products with their share of revenue (0–1); bars are relative to the largest share. An empty list shows a short note |
| channels | `{ name: string; share: number }[]` | `sample channels` | Rows of Channels, like products |
| currency | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO currency code for revenue, average order and the axis |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the period switch, Export, the KPI cards, the chart type, Compare and the chart
- ← / →: With the chart focused, moves the inspected point
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or last point
- ← / → / ↑ / ↓: On the KPI cards, the period or the chart type, picks the previous or next one
- Esc: Closes the chart's tooltip

### Accessibility

- Period and chart-type buttons use aria-pressed; the KPI cards are tabs with aria-selected
- The chart is labelled with the metric and range; the inspected point is announced through a status tooltip
- Changes are small tinted badges with an arrow that also say up or down in text, so they don't rely on color alone – and a falling refund rate counts as good

### Motion

- KPI values roll up from zero on first view and to their new amounts after that; list values count along – all with tabular numerals
- The chosen KPI card turns fully opaque while the others dim; the line draws in and glides to the new values, bars grow out of the zero line
- With prefers-reduced-motion values and views switch instantly

### Responsive

- Follows the block's own width with container queries: below 640px the KPI cards form a 2 × 2 grid and the two list cards stack
- On touch screens the buttons, segmented tracks, the Compare switch and the list rows grow to larger targets
- Below 460px the period switch fills the width and the chart is 168px tall
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

- The home of an agent product: everything your agents are doing, what happened since you last looked, and what's waiting on you – on one screen
- Teams that run several agents at once and lose track of who is doing what
- A morning check-in: the curve shows when things happened, the inbox what to answer first

- A single agent run – Run Inspector shows one run in depth
- Hundreds of agents – group them first; the middle shows every agent it's given

```tsx
import { MissionControl, type MissionAgent, type MissionEvent } from "@/components/ui/mission-control-clean";
```

# Model Router, clean style (Pro)

How a gateway splits its traffic across AI models – requests run as streaks of light from the gateway into each model's line, the line as wide as its share. The blended cost per 1K tokens on top and how it compares to what's live; pick Cost, Balanced or Quality and the split changes, the lines widen and narrow and the numbers roll. Every route below with share, p95 latency and price, a fallback to retry on another model, and Deploy

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/model-router
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/model-router-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/model-router-clean`

### When to use

- Showing how an AI gateway splits its traffic across models – and letting people pick a strategy for it
- Comparing what a cheaper or a stronger split would cost against the policy that's live, before deploying it
- Setting a fallback model that takes over when another one fails

### When not to use

- How much each model was used over a period – use Model Usage
- Picking one model for a chat – use Model Picker
- Requests routed to agents rather than models – use Agent Router

### Usage

```tsx
import { ModelRouter, type RouterModel, type RouterStrategy } from "@/components/ui/model-router-clean";

const models: RouterModel[] = [
  { id: "opus", name: "Claude Opus 5.5", provider: "Anthropic", logo: <ClaudeLogo />, p95: 2.16, cost: 0.0126 },
  { id: "gpt", name: "GPT-5.5", provider: "OpenAI", logo: <OpenAILogo />, p95: 1.34, cost: 0.0048 },
  { id: "flash", name: "Gemini 3 Flash", provider: "Google", logo: <GeminiLogo />, p95: 0.64, cost: 0.0007 },
];

const strategies: RouterStrategy[] = [
  { id: "cost", label: "Cost", shares: { opus: 6, gpt: 30, flash: 64 } },
  { id: "balanced", label: "Balanced", shares: { opus: 20, gpt: 50, flash: 30 } },
  { id: "quality", label: "Quality", shares: { opus: 60, gpt: 32, flash: 8 } },
];

export function Router() {
  return (
    <ModelRouter
      models={models}
      strategies={strategies}
      live={{ strategy: "balanced", fallback: { enabled: true, from: "opus", to: "gpt" } }}
      version={14}
      environment="chat-prod"
      onDeploy={(policy) => savePolicy(policy)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| models | `RouterModel[]` |  | The models the gateway routes to, top to bottom – each a line in the flow and a row in the table |
| RouterModel | `{ id, name, provider?, logo?, color?, p95, cost }` |  | p95 is the latency in seconds, cost the price per 1K tokens in dollars; provider shows on hover |
| strategies | `{ id, label, shares }[]` |  | The switch on top – shares are each model's part of the traffic by id, scaled to add up to 100% |
| live | `{ strategy, fallback: { enabled, from, to } }` |  | The policy that's live now – where it starts, and what the blended cost is compared to |
| version | `number` |  | The live policy's version – "Policy v14"; it goes up by one with every deploy |
| environment | `string` |  | Where it runs – "chat-prod", shown in the header and the footer |
| onDeploy | `(policy) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Deploys the policy – while a returned promise runs the button says Deploying |
| onChange | `(policy) => void` |  | Every edit to the strategy or the fallback |
| title | `string` |  | The heading and the section's accessible name |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

### Accessibility

- The strategy switch is a radio group with one tab stop – arrows move between Cost, Balanced and Quality
- The fallback is a switch with its state; each model picker opens a menu with Enter, Space or the arrows – arrows, Home and End move, Enter picks, Esc closes and puts focus back, Tab leaves it
- Revert moves focus to Deploy, so it never gets lost when the button goes away
- The routes are a real table with column and row headers
- The footer says Live, Unsaved changes or Deploying in words and is announced as it changes; Deploy is aria-disabled until something changed
- The flow is decoration and hidden from screen readers – the table carries the numbers
- A focus ring shows only for the keyboard

### Motion

- Streaks of light run along each line, gateway to model, as often as its share – they fade in, are full in the middle and fade out
- Switching the strategy eases every band and share bar to its new width, and the cost and shares roll to their new values
- Pointing at a line or a row brings that model forward everywhere and fades the rest
- Reduced motion stops the streaks and the rolls – the numbers simply change

### Responsive

- Fills its container's width – the lines stretch, the model names stay on the right
- Below 440px the strategy switch moves under the cost and the table keeps share and price
- Below 380px the fallback's pickers show just the model's logo – the name is in their label and their menu – so the rule stays on one line
- Long model names, strategy labels and the environment end in … with the full text on hover; long strategy lists wrap
- One model hides the fallback; no models at all reads No models to route to
- A fallback naming a model that isn't in the list falls back to the first ones, never the same model twice
- A strategy without shares splits evenly; shares that don't add up to 100 are scaled
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every model a stable id and use the same ids in each strategy's shares
- cost is per 1K tokens in dollars, p95 in seconds – the blended cost is the shares times the costs
- Keep three strategies or fewer and label them by what they favor – Cost, Balanced, Quality
- Persist the policy in onDeploy; pass the new live policy and version back in once it's saved

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: model-usage, agent-router, model-picker, cost-waterfall

# Model Usage, clean style (Pro)

How much each AI company's models were used – one stacked bar per company in its color with a segment per model, the most used darkest and the rest lighter shades; point at a bar for its models and their share. The period's total and change on top with tokens, cost and requests to switch between, and below what it all went into – search, analyze, code, test – across every model, or just the company you point at

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/model-usage
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/model-usage-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/model-usage-clean`

### When to use

- Showing how much each AI company's models were used in a period – tokens, cost or requests – and how that splits across their models
- A usage or billing page for a team that runs several providers side by side
- Showing what the usage went into – search, analyze, code, test – across every model, or for one company

### When not to use

- Usage over time, day by day – use KPI Chart or Breakdown Chart
- Plan limits and credits left – use Usage Meter
- Where one run's money went, step by step – use Cost Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { ModelUsage, type UsageCompany } from "@/components/ui/model-usage-clean";

const companies: UsageCompany[] = [
  {
    id: "anthropic",
    name: "Anthropic",
    logo: <ClaudeLogo />,
    models: [
      { id: "sonnet", name: "Claude Sonnet 5.5", usage: { tokens: 2_180_000, cost: 6.54, requests: 838 } },
      { id: "opus", name: "Claude Opus 5.5", usage: { tokens: 1_240_000, cost: 18.6, requests: 477 } },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: "openai",
    name: "OpenAI",
    logo: <OpenAILogo />,
    models: [{ id: "gpt", name: "GPT-5.5", usage: { tokens: 1_520_000, cost: 15.2, requests: 585 } }],
  },
];

export function Usage() {
  return <ModelUsage companies={companies} previous={{ tokens: 4_100_000, cost: 31.4, requests: 1620 }} />;
}
```

| metrics / defaultMetric | `UsageMetric[] / UsageMetric` |  | The measures to switch between, and the one shown first – tokens, cost, requests; one alone hides the switch |
| title | `string` |  | The period's name above the total – "This week" by default |
| previous / since | `{ tokens?, cost?, requests? } / string` |  | Last period's totals – adds "+38% since last week", green up, red down |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Two stops: the measure switch, then the chart
- ← / →: Walk the bars – each shows its models in the card and its company's tasks below
- Home / End: The first, the last bar
- Esc: Close the card

- The bars are buttons named with the company and its total; the card is a tooltip they point to
- The measure switch is a group of pressed buttons
- The task list is named after what it shows – all models, or the company pointed at
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only, in light and dark
- Color never carries meaning alone: every model and task is named with its value

### Motion

- The bars rise one after the other when the chart comes in
- Switching the measure resizes the bars and segments smoothly – they keep their order and shades
- Pointing at a bar fades the others and opens its card beside it
- Reduced motion turns it all off

- Fills its container's width; up to four or five companies read best

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every company and model a stable id
- Pass the same measures for every model – tokens, cost in dollars, requests
- Model order comes from the first measure and stays when switching
- Task kinds use the built-in names – search, analyze, code, test, plan, read, write, check – so they get their icon and color

- React 19

# Number Input, clean style (Free)

A field for one number – − and + that repeat while held, arrow keys and Page Up / Down, min, max and step, a unit like tokens or %, formatted for the locale

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/number-input
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/number-input-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/number-input-clean`

### When to use

- Counts and limits people tune in small steps: tokens per run, parallel agents, retries, seats, a budget, a temperature
- Settings forms where the value has bounds – it never lets a number past min or max get saved

### When not to use

- Numbers nobody counts up or down – phone numbers, card numbers, IDs, ZIP codes: use the Text Field
- Picking roughly from a wide range where the exact value matters less – a slider says that better
- A handful of fixed choices (1, 2, 4, 8) – use the Segmented Control or the Select

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { NumberInput } from "@/components/ui/number-input-clean";

export function RunLimits() {
  const [tokens, setTokens] = useState<number | null>(32000);

  return (
    <form className="grid gap-4">
      <NumberInput
        label="Max tokens per run"
        unit="tokens"
        value={tokens}
        onValueChange={setTokens}
        min={1000}
        max={200000}
        step={1000}
        hint="The answer stops here."
      />
      <NumberInput
        label="Budget per run"
        name="budget"
        prefix="$"
        defaultValue={25}
        min={0}
        max={100}
        step={5}
        formatOptions={{ minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }}
      />
    </form>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `number \| null` |  | The number; null is an empty field. Use it with onValueChange to control the field |
| defaultValue | `number \| null` | `null` | The starting number when the field keeps its own value |
| onValueChange | `(value: number \| null) => void` |  | Called after every step, and when typing is done (blur or Enter) – with the clamped number, or null when emptied |
| min | `number` |  | The lowest value: typing less is raised to it, − and Home stop there |
| max | `number` |  | The highest value: typing more is lowered to it, + and End stop there |
| step | `number` | `1` | What − / + and the arrow keys add or take away; steps land on multiples of it (counted from min) |
| largeStep | `number` | `step × 10` | What Page Up / Page Down add or take away |
| unit | `ReactNode` |  | Quiet text right after the value – "tokens", "%", "ms"; read out with the value |
| prefix | `ReactNode` |  | Quiet text or a 16px icon before the value – e.g. "$" |
| locale | `string` | `the browser's` | Shows and reads the number in this locale – 4,000 in en-US, 4.000 in de-DE; typing follows the same separators |
| formatOptions | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | How the value is shown once you leave the field, e.g. { maximumFractionDigits: 2 } or { style: "percent" } (then 0.25 shows 25%) |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown above the field; clicking it focuses the input |
| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – the error takes its place while there is one |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks the field invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message where the hint was |
| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 28 · 32 · 36px high; taller on touch screens |
| name | `string` |  | Sends the plain number (4000, not "4,000") with the form, through a hidden input |
| inputClassName | `string` |  | Extra class on the input itself |
| ...input props | `ComponentProps<"input">` |  | placeholder, disabled, readOnly, required, onBlur, onKeyDown, aria-label, ref and the rest go to the input |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: One step up or down
- Page Up / Page Down: A large step (10 steps by default)
- Home / End: Jumps to min or max, when they're set
- Enter: Takes what's typed – clamped and formatted – and submits the form as usual
- Esc: Drops what's typed and goes back to the last value
- Tab: Moves into the field – one stop per field; − and + are for the pointer, the arrow keys step

### Accessibility

- The input has role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and a readable aria-valuetext ("$25.00", "32,000 tokens")
- − and + are labelled buttons tied to the input with aria-controls; at a limit they stay focusable and say so with aria-disabled, so focus never drops
- The hint and the error are linked with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid and is announced politely
- Holding − or + keeps stepping, first after a pause, then faster; it stops at the limit
- Phones get a number pad – with a decimal key when the value has decimals, the full keyboard when it can go below zero
- Focus firms up the field's edge – no ring around the field; the buttons get a clear outline under keyboard focus

### Motion

- Each step rolls the new value in from the direction it moved – up for +, down for −
- The hint swaps for an error out of a short blur, without moving anything below
- With prefers-reduced-motion the value just changes

### Responsive

- Fills its container; the value hugs its text so the unit sits right after it, and − / + keep their place at the end
- Very long numbers fit to the field and are cut with an ellipsis before the buttons move
- Touch screens get taller fields, 32px buttons with a larger hit area and 16px text, so iOS doesn't zoom in
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Pagination, clean style (Free)

Pages of a long list – the range you see, previous and next, page numbers with … between them and rows per page, tabular numbers that keep the row still from 1 page to 10,000

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/pagination
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/pagination-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/pagination-clean`

### When to use

- Under a table or list that loads one page at a time: runs, logs, eval cases, invoices
- When people need to know how much there is – "1–25 of 1,284" – and jump to the first, last or a nearby page
- With pageSizes, when some want to see more rows at once

### When not to use

- A feed people read top to bottom – load more as they scroll instead
- Where a page sits in a hierarchy – use the Breadcrumb
- A few views of the same thing – use the Segmented Control
- A handful of rows – show them all

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@/components/ui/pagination-clean";

export function RunsFooter({ total }: { total: number }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageSize, setPageSize] = useState(25);

  return (
    <Pagination
      page={page}
      onPageChange={setPage}
      total={total}
      pageSize={pageSize}
      pageSizes={[25, 50, 100]}
      onPageSizeChange={setPageSize}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | `number` |  | Required. The page shown, from 1 – kept between 1 and the last page |
| onPageChange | `(page: number) => void` |  | Required. Called with the new page from the arrows, a number or a new size |
| total | `number` |  | All rows. Shows the range ("1–25 of 1,284", "0 of 0" when empty) and works out the pages |
| pageSize | `number` | `20` | Rows on a page |
| pageCount | `number` |  | The number of pages when you don't know the rows – the range becomes "Page 3 of 12" |
| pageSizes | `number[]` |  | Shows Rows per page with these sizes (the current one is added when it's missing) |
| onPageSizeChange | `(pageSize: number) => void` |  | A new size was picked. onPageChange follows with the page that holds the first row you saw |
| siblings | `number` | `1` | Page numbers on each side of the current one; with the first, the last and two … that makes 2 × siblings + 5 slots |
| compact | `boolean` | `false` | Only the range and the arrows – no page numbers |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | While rows load: everything stays where it is, nothing can be pressed |
| aria-label | `string` | `"Pagination"` | Names the navigation landmark – say which list, when a page has two |
| ...nav props | `ComponentProps<"nav">` |  | className, style, ref and the rest go to the <nav> |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through Rows per page, the arrows and the numbers
- Enter / Space: Goes to that page – the focus follows the page to where its number is now

### Accessibility

- A <nav> landmark around a list of real buttons: Previous page, Page 1 … Page 52, Next page
- The page you are on is marked aria-current="page"
- At the first or last page the arrow is aria-disabled, not disabled – it keeps the focus, so Tab doesn't jump to the top
- The range is a polite live region, so a screen reader hears "26–50 of 1,284" after each move; the … are hidden
- Rows per page is a native <select> with its label – the phone's own picker opens on touch
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click

### Motion

- Only soft color changes on hover – the numbers never move, so nothing animates

### Responsive

- Tabular numbers and a fixed count of slots, each as wide as the last page's number: the row keeps its width from page 1 to 10,000
- When the row is too narrow for the numbers, only the range and the arrows stay; the range and the pager wrap onto two lines before that
- Touch screens get 36px buttons and 15px text
- Right to left: the arrows turn round
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

An agent tries the same task several ways at once and the best one wins – every attempt races as a row with its model, approach and live bar, then gets a score; the best is marked and picked, and you can switch to another

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/parallel-attempts-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/parallel-attempts-clean`

### When to use

- An agent tries a task several ways at once – different models, prompts or approaches – and the best result wins
- Best-of-N runs, where you want to see them race, compare their scores and keep the say in which one is used
- Code fixes, drafts or plans that are cheap to try in parallel and easy to score

# Permission Request, clean style (Pro)

An agent asks for one specific right – who, why and exactly what will happen – and you allow it once, for an hour or always; then it folds into one line with the time left and Revoke

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/permission-request
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/permission-request-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/permission-request-clean`

### When to use

- An agent hits an action it isn't allowed to do yet and asks for that one right – push to main, send emails, spend money
- Granting access for a while instead of forever: just once, for an hour, or always
- Anywhere people should see exactly what will happen – the files, recipients or amounts – before they say yes

### When not to use

- Setting up front how much an agent may do in general – use Autonomy Dial
- Reviewing a finished result before it goes out – use Approval Card or Agent Inbox
- Connecting a tool for the first time (OAuth) – that's the provider's consent screen

### Usage

```tsx
import { PermissionRequest } from "@/components/ui/permission-request-clean";

export function PushRequest({ onAnswer }: { onAnswer: (allowed: boolean, until?: number) => void }) {
  return (
    <PermissionRequest
      agent={{ name: "Coder", model: "GPT-6 Sol" }}
      action="push to main"
      target="acme/web"
      risk="risky"
      reason="The fix for the flaky checkout test passed review and all checks."
      preview={[
        { id: "a", label: "src/checkout/cart.ts", meta: "+12 −4" },
        { id: "b", label: "Deploys to production after the merge" },
      ]}
      onDecisionChange={(d) => d && onAnswer(d.allow, d.until)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent | `{ name, model?, avatar? }` |  | Who asks – the avatar is a small mark, e.g. the model maker's logo; defaults to initials |
| action | `string` |  | What it wants to do, read after "wants to", e.g. "push to main" |
| target | `string` |  | Where, e.g. "acme/web" or "Stripe · live mode" – shown under the title with toolIcon |
| toolIcon | `ReactNode` |  | The tool's mark next to the target |
| risk | `"safe" \| "risky" \| "destructive"` | `"risky"` | Risky and destructive carry a tag; destructive also turns Allow red and leaves out Always |
| reason | `string` |  | The agent's own words on why it needs this |
| preview | `{ id, label, meta?, icon? }[]` |  | Exactly what will happen – files, recipients, amounts; meta is right-aligned, e.g. "+12 −4" |
| previewTitle | `string` | `"What will happen"` | Heading of the preview |
| previewLimit | `number` | `3` | Rows shown before "N more" |
| scopes | `("once" \| "timed" \| "always")[]` | `all three` | The choices of how long; one choice hides the switch |
| scope / defaultScope / onScopeChange | `PermissionScope` | `"once"` | Controlled or uncontrolled choice of how long |
| duration | `number` | `60` | Minutes a timed grant holds |
| decision / defaultDecision | `PermissionDecision \| null` |  | { allow, scope, at, until? } – null while it waits |
| onDecisionChange | `(decision \| null) => void` |  | Allow, Deny – and null for Revoke, Change or Ask again |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for the time left – without it the card ticks every second while a timed grant runs |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Allows, with the chosen scope – while the focus is in the card
- Esc: Denies
- ← / →: Picks how long

### Accessibility

- While it waits the card is a dialog labelled by its title ("Coder wants to push to main") and described by the reason
- How long is a radio group; the Allow button names the choice, e.g. "Allow for 1 hour"
- The decided line is a status, so screen readers announce "Allowed for 1 hour" or "Denied"

### Motion

- The preview rows rise in a beat after each other; the Allow label swaps softly when the scope changes
- On a decision the card folds to one line, the check or cross pops in, and a thin bar drains until a timed grant runs out
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 400px
- Below 340px the reason loses its indent, the buttons share the width and the keyboard hints go
- Touch screens get taller choices and buttons and no keyboard hints
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component only asks – store the decision and check it where the agent acts: allow, and for scope "timed" also Date.now() < until
- Destructive actions can never be allowed for always – the choice isn't offered, even if scopes lists it
- Revoke, Change and Ask again all call onDecisionChange(null): treat it as "not allowed, ask again"
- Keep the preview concrete (file names, addresses, amounts) – that is what makes people comfortable saying yes
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

# Plan vs Actual (Pro)

An agent's plan against what really happens – every step's bar grows over its dashed planned ghost, overruns turn amber, the steps after it slide right, and the expected finish moves away from the planned one

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/plan-vs-actual
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/plan-vs-actual.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/plan-vs-actual`

### When to use

- Showing whether an agent's run keeps to its plan – and if not, which step made it late
- Plans with steps that wait for each other, where one overrun pushes everything after it
- Giving people an honest expected finish time while the run is still going

### When not to use

- Where the time and money of each call go – use Trace Waterfall
- Reviewing or editing the plan before it runs – use Agent Plan
- Several agents working side by side – use Agent Lanes

### Usage

```tsx
import { PlanVsActual, type PlanStep } from "@/components/ui/plan-vs-actual-clean";

const steps: PlanStep[] = [
  { id: "brief", title: "Read the brief", plan: 20000, start: 0, end: 16000 },
  { id: "layout", title: "Build the layout", plan: 60000, deps: ["brief"], start: 17000 },
  { id: "stripe", title: "Wire up Stripe", plan: 45000, deps: ["layout"] },
];

export function Progress({ now }: { now: number }) {
  return <PlanVsActual steps={steps} now={now} task="Ship the pricing page" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `PlanStep[]` |  | { id, title, plan, deps?, start?, end?, icon? } – list a step after the steps it waits for |
| plan | `number` |  | Per step – how long it was planned to take, in ms; the planned start follows from deps |
| deps | `string[]` |  | Per step – ids of the steps that have to finish first |
| start / end | `number` |  | Per step – when it really started and finished, in ms from the start of the run; leave end out while it runs, both while it waits |
| now | `number` |  | Where the run is, in ms from its start – running bars grow to it, waiting steps can't start before it |
| task | `string` |  | What the run is for – next to the heading |
| formatTime | `(ms: number) => string` | `0:42` | Formats the axis, the bars' numbers and the finish lines |
| title | `string` | `"Plan vs actual"` | Heading of the bar on top |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the steps – the focused one shows what it waits for and what waits for it

### Accessibility

- The steps are a list; each one is focusable and reads how long it took against the plan, or when it's expected to start
- Late and early are said in words as well as color – “+25s” and “25s behind”
- The chart itself is hidden from screen readers – the rows carry everything it shows

### Motion

- Running bars grow with the run, with a sheen sweeping along and a glowing leading edge; past the plan the growing part turns amber
- Waiting steps glide to their new expected place when a step before them runs over or finishes early
- The expected finish line moves, the gap to the planned one tints, and the axis glides wider when the run needs more room
- Pointing at a step draws its links to the steps it waits for and the ones waiting for it
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing glides, sweeps or glows

- start, end and now are ms from the start of the run – subtract the run's start time from your event times

# Pricing Plans, clean style (Pro)

Pricing section with a monthly / yearly switch, three plan cards and collapsible details

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/pricing-plans
- Section: Blocks · Pricing
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/pricing-plans-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/pricing-plans-clean`

### When to use

- A pricing page or section with up to three plans and a monthly / yearly choice
- Plans that differ in a few limits plus a longer list of features

### When not to use

- One-time purchases – drop the billing switch or use a simpler card
- More than three or four plans – use a comparison table instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { PricingPlans } from "@/components/ui/pricing-plans-clean";

export function Pricing() {
  return <PricingPlans plans={plans} defaultBilling="yearly" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plans | `Plan[]` |  | Name, monthly and yearly price, limits, sync chip, features and an onSelect callback. One to three plans sit side by side, four two by two; a price that is not a number reads “Custom”; none shows a short empty note |
| title | `string` | `"Choose your plan"` | Section heading |
| subtitle | `string` |  | Line under the heading |
| defaultBilling | `"monthly" \| "yearly"` | `"yearly"` | Billing period shown first |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | Symbol in front of the prices, or a three-letter code like "EUR" to format them as that currency (cents only when a price has them) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the section |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the switch, the buttons and the detail toggles
- ← / →: Switch the billing period – the switch is one tab stop
- Enter / Space: Start a plan or show / hide details

### Accessibility

- The billing switch is a radio group
- Details toggles use aria-expanded; hidden details are inert
- Features that are not included are announced as such

### Motion

- The white chip slides to the chosen period and takes its width; prices roll digit by digit after a switch
- Details fold open and closed; reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Three columns on wide screens, one column below 860px
- Yearly shows the biggest saving any plan gets (e.g. −20%); it disappears when yearly isn't cheaper
- The plan with a badge gets the one dark button and an accent hairline; the others get white buttons
- Long plan names, badges, limit labels, sync chips and button labels stay on one line with an ellipsis and show in full on hover; feature labels wrap
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

### When to use

- Onboarding checklists that guide new users through their first steps
- Any short list of tasks where progress should feel rewarding

### When not to use

- Long step labels – each step stays on one line and cuts off with an ellipsis

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProgressTracker } from "@/components/ui/progress-tracker-clean";

const steps = [
  { id: "tools", label: "Connect your imported tools" },
  { id: "notify", label: "Turn on notifications" },
  { id: "project", label: "Create a project", done: true },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return <ProgressTracker title="Getting started" steps={steps} onChange={save} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `ProgressStep[]` |  | Each step has an id, a label, an optional done flag and icon |
| title | `string` | `"Getting started"` | Heading above the bar |
| autoPlay | `boolean` | `false` | Ticks the open steps one by one and starts over – stops when someone clicks or types |
| interval | `number` | `2200` | Pause between two automatic steps, in ms |

| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the steps
- Space / Enter: Tick or untick the focused step

### Accessibility

- Each step is a checkbox with aria-checked; the bar is a progressbar with the count as text
- Any click or key press stops the automatic play, so it never fights the user

### Motion

- The thin blue bar fills smoothly and a light band sweeps across it each time a step is done
- The hairline ring fills blue and pops, then the tick draws itself
- A thin line strikes through the label while it fades to gray
- On mount the card settles in and the rows fade up one after another
- Steps stay in place so nothing jumps; the counter rolls to the new number
- With prefers-reduced-motion every change is instant

### Responsive

- React 19

# Prompt Library, clean style (Pro)

Saved prompt templates with variables – type straight into the sentence, watch the finished prompt assemble below, and use it once every variable is filled

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/prompt-library
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/prompt-library-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/prompt-library-clean`

### When to use

- AI products where people reuse the same prompts with small changes – summaries, release notes, outreach, debugging
- Next to a chat composer, as the place to pick a saved prompt, fill in the blanks and send it
- Team prompt libraries where the template stays fixed and only a few words change per use

### When not to use

- Free writing – a plain composer is faster when nothing repeats
- Long templates with many variables – past about six fields a form with labels reads better than a sentence
- Choosing a command or action – use Command Menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { PromptLibrary } from "@/components/ui/prompt-library-clean";

export function Prompts() {
  return (
    <PromptLibrary
      templates={[
        {
          id: "meeting",
          title: "Summarize a meeting",
          category: "Notes",
          body: "Summarize the meeting below for {audience} in under {length}.",
          variables: { length: { default: "150 words" } },
        },
        {
          id: "error",
          title: "Explain an error",
          category: "Debug",
          body: "Explain this {language} error in plain words: {error}.",
        },
      ]}
      onUse={(prompt) => send(prompt)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| templates | `PromptTemplate[]` |  | { id, title, category?, tone?, body, variables? } – body holds the variables in curly braces, e.g. {audience}; variables maps a name to { description?, default? } |
| value | `string` |  | Id of the chosen template (controlled) |
| defaultValue | `string` |  | Id chosen at first when uncontrolled – the first template by default |
| onSelect | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when another template is chosen |
| onUse | `(prompt: string, template: PromptTemplate, values: Record<string, string>) => void` |  | Called with the finished prompt when Use is pressed – only possible once every variable is filled |
| onCopy | `(prompt: string) => void` |  | Called after the prompt was copied to the clipboard |
| title | `string` | `"Prompts"` | Heading above the list |
| useLabel | `string` | `"Use prompt"` | Label of the use button |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↓: From the search field into the list
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: Move through the list – the template opens as you go
- Esc: Clears the search
- Tab: Through the variable fields, then Copy and Use
- Enter: In a variable field: jumps to the next empty one, or uses the prompt once all are filled

### Accessibility

- A group named by the list's title; the templates are a listbox with options and aria-selected, only the chosen one is in the tab order
- Every variable is a real text field labelled with its name and description
- Use stays focusable while not ready (aria-disabled) and the last row says how many variables are missing
- A polite live region announces when all variables are filled, when the prompt was copied and when it was used
- The outgoing template that fades out during a switch is inert and hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The highlight slides along the list to the chosen template while the content crossfades – the old one fades out underneath
- The part you type into lights up in the field and in the preview, then fades back
- The token estimate in the last row rolls to its new value as you type
- Use pulses once when the last variable gets filled; Copy turns into a check for a moment
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 640px. Below 540px the list moves on top of the template; below 360px Copy keeps only its icon
- Fields grow with what you type and never get wider than the line
- Touch screens: taller list rows, fields and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Variables are written as {name} with letters, digits, - or _; the same name used twice is one field
- Values are kept per template inside the card, so switching back and forth keeps what was typed
- The token number is an estimate (about four characters per token) – pass the prompt to your tokenizer when it has to be exact
- Category colors follow the order the categories appear; set tone on a template to pick one

- React 19
