# Rate Limit Planner, clean style (Pro)

Plan when your agents run so they stay under the API's rate limit – the day's load as a line chart, one row per agent run to drag; Spread out lowers the peak, the overflow is hatched in red

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/rate-limit-planner
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/rate-limit-planner-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/rate-limit-planner-clean`

### When to use

- Scheduling agent runs, cron jobs or batch work against one API rate limit (tokens per minute)
- Showing why a run hit 429s – which runs overlap and when the day goes over
- An ops or settings page where people move their own jobs and see the peak change as they drag

### When not to use

- Live monitoring of every request – use a metrics chart; this plans a day
- Many separate limits at once (per model, per key) – one planner per limit
- More than about ten runs a day – the rows get long; group runs per agent first

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { RateLimitPlanner, type PlannedRun } from "@/components/ui/rate-limit-planner-clean";

const runs: PlannedRun[] = [
  { id: "triage", name: "Inbox triage", at: 8 * 60, peak: 46_000, rise: 45, halfLife: 70 },
  { id: "research", name: "Lead research", at: 11 * 60, peak: 82_000, rise: 60, halfLife: 90 },
  { id: "report", name: "Report writer", at: 15 * 60 + 30, peak: 74_000, rise: 55, halfLife: 100 },
];

export function Schedule() {
  const [plan, setPlan] = useState(runs);
  return (
    <RateLimitPlanner
      runs={plan}
      onRunsChange={setPlan}
      limit={120_000}
      checkpoint={{ at: 23 * 60, label: "Nightly batch" }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| runs | `PlannedRun[]` |  | The runs, controlled – each with id, name, start (minutes after midnight) and peak tokens per minute; pair with onRunsChange |
| defaultRuns | `PlannedRun[]` |  | Starting runs when uncontrolled |
| onRunsChange | `(runs: PlannedRun[]) => void` |  | Called on every drag, Spread out, edit, add and remove |
| limit | `number` |  | The API's limit in tokens per minute |
| buffer | `number` | `0.8` | Share of the limit to stay under – above it the badge says Close to limit |
| startHour | `number` | `6` | Hour the 24-hour window starts at |
| checkpoint | `{ at: number; label: string }` |  | A fixed time to check against, e.g. a nightly batch – what's still running then is read out |
| now | `number` |  | The time now, in minutes after midnight – runs that already started stay put, Spread out and Add run only use the time after it |
| actual | `number[]` |  | Measured tokens per minute from the window's start up to now – drawn solid, the plan ahead dashed, and compared in the footer |
| today | `"weekdays" \| "weekend"` | `"weekdays"` | Runs with days set to the other kind are left out |
| selected | `string` |  | Id of the run shown in its color in the chart – controlled; pair with onSelectedChange |
| onSelectedChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when a row or bar is picked |
| title | `string` | `"Rate limit"` | Heading of the card |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |
| PlannedRun.rise | `number` | `30` | Minutes until a run reaches its peak |
| PlannedRun.halfLife | `number` | `45` | Minutes until its load has halved again – the tail |
| PlannedRun.days | `"daily" \| "weekdays" \| "weekend"` | `"daily"` | Which days it runs on |
| PlannedRun.color | `string` |  | Any CSS color – by default each run takes the next color of the design system's palette |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through Spread out, each run's bar, its remove and edit buttons, Add run and the footer's Move to
- ← / →: On a bar: moves the run 15 minutes earlier or later
- Shift / ← / →: On a bar: moves it an hour (Page Up / Page Down too)
- Home / End: On a bar: the earliest start (now) or the latest that still fits the day
- Enter: On a bar or ⋯: opens the run's settings
- Delete: On a bar: removes the run – focus moves on to the next one
- Esc: Closes the settings and returns to ⋯; tabbing out closes them too

### Accessibility

- Every bar is a slider with the run's name, start and peak as its value text; runs that already started are marked as disabled
- The footer sentence is a polite live region and describes each bar – screen readers hear what a move did
- The settings window is a dialog; focus lands in the name field and returns to ⋯ when it closes
- The chart is decoration – everything in it is also in the badge, the rows and the footer

### Motion

- The lines ease to their new shape after every move; the peak's dot, the hatched overflow and the tooltip move with them
- Spread out, Move to and Add run glide the bars to their place; a drag follows the pointer directly
- New rows slide open and their bar grows in, removed rows fold away; the settings window pops in
- Reduced motion jumps to the end state and stops the running sheen

### Responsive

- Fills its container; below 560px the chart and bars take the full width and each run's name moves onto its own line above its bar
- On touch screens the picked row shows its remove and settings buttons – there's no hover to reveal them
- Broken numbers from an API (NaN, negative, a start outside the day) fall back to safe values instead of breaking the chart
- Touch works: drag a bar with a finger; the page still scrolls when you swipe elsewhere
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { RateLimitPlanner, type PlannedRun } from "@/components/ui/rate-limit-planner";

  { id: "triage", name: "Inbox triage", at: 8 * 60, peak: 46_000, rise: 45, halfLife: 70 },
  { id: "research", name: "Lead research", at: 11 * 60, peak: 82_000, rise: 60, halfLife: 90 },
  { id: "report", name: "Report writer", at: 15 * 60 + 30, peak: 74_000, rise: 55, halfLife: 100 },

export function Schedule() {
  const [plan, setPlan] = useState(runs);
  return (
    <RateLimitPlanner
      runs={plan}
      onRunsChange={setPlan}
      limit={120_000}
      checkpoint={{ at: 23 * 60, label: "Nightly batch" }}
    />
  );
}
```

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/rating
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/rating-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/rating-clean`

### When to use

- Thumbs up or down under an AI answer – variant="thumbs"
- Rating a run, an agent, a template or a support reply from 1 to 5 stars (or any max)
- Showing an average next to a name or in a list – readOnly, with halves ("4.5 out of 5")

### When not to use

- Thumbs together with copy, retry and share under a chat message – use Message Actions, which has them and a feedback row
- A scale with named steps (Low, Medium, High) – use the Segmented Control or the Toggle Group
- Turning something on or off – use the Switch or the Checkbox

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Rating } from "@/components/ui/rating-clean";

export function RateRun({ onRate }: { onRate: (stars: number | null) => void }) {
  const [stars, setStars] = useState<number | null>(null);

  return (
    <Rating
      aria-label="Rate this run"
      value={stars}
      onValueChange={(v) => {
        setStars(v);
        onRate(v);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | `"stars" \| "thumbs"` | `"stars"` | Stars from 1 to max, or thumbs up and down |
| value | `number \| null · "up" \| "down" \| null` |  | Stars: 1 to max, or null for none – read-only it may be a fraction, shown to the nearest half. Thumbs: "up", "down" or null |
| defaultValue | `same as value` | `null` | The starting value when value isn't controlled |
| onValueChange | `(value) => void` |  | Called with the new value, or null when it's cleared |
| max | `number` | `5` | Stars only – how many (1 to 50); more than fit wrap onto a new line |
| allowClear | `boolean` | `true` | Pressing the chosen one again, or Delete, clears it |
| readOnly | `boolean` | `false` | Only shows the value: no buttons, read out as one picture; stars show halves |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims it and turns the buttons off |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Stars 14, 18 or 24px; thumbs 24, 28 or 32px buttons – the hit areas grow on touch screens |
| getValueLabel | `(value: number, max: number) => string` | `"3 out of 5"` | Stars only – how a star and a read-only value are read out; translate it here |
| labels | `{ up?: string; down?: string }` | `"Good response", "Bad response"` | Thumbs only – the buttons' names and tooltips |
| name | `string` |  | Sends the value with a form (a hidden input; empty when nothing is chosen) |
| ...div props | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | aria-label, aria-labelledby, className, id, ref … go to the group. Without a name of your own it is "Rating" or "Rate this response" |

### Keyboard

- Tab: One tab stop: lands on the chosen star (or the first) or thumb
- → / ↑: One star more – in right-to-left pages ← is more
- ← / ↓: One star less (never below 1 – clear with Delete)
- Home / End: One star, or all of them
- Arrows: Thumbs: switches between up and down
- Space / Enter: Chooses the focused one; on the chosen one, clears it
- Delete: Clears it (Backspace too)

### Accessibility

- A radio group: each star is a radio named "3 out of 5" (getValueLabel), each thumb "Good response" or "Bad response" – the chosen one is announced as checked
- Read-only it is one role="img" named "4.5 out of 5" (or "No rating"), so a list of averages isn't a list of buttons
- The arrows move and choose at once, like native radios; one tab stop for the whole group
- Hovering previews only with a mouse – on touch a tap sets the value right away
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click

### Motion

- Choosing stars pops them one after the other up to the new value; a chosen thumb fills and tips with a little bounce
- The hovered star grows a little, a pressed one shrinks
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves – the stars fill at once

### Responsive

- Halves are drawn by clipping a filled star over an empty one, from the start side – mirrored in right-to-left pages
- Touch screens get a hit area of at least 32px per star and 36px per thumb
- Many stars wrap instead of running out of their row
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

```tsx
import { ReasoningSummary, type ReasonStep, type ReasonModel } from "@/components/ui/reasoning-summary-clean";

const steps: ReasonStep[] = [
  { id: "s1", kind: "search", label: "Searched the docs for rate limits", model: "opus", ms: 1800 },
  { id: "s2", kind: "analyze", label: "Compared the limits across three plans", model: "grok", ms: 2200 },
  { id: "s3", kind: "code", label: "Wrote a retry with backoff", model: "gpt", ms: 1600 },
  { id: "s4", kind: "test", label: "Ran it against the sandbox", model: "gpt", ms: 2600 },
];

const models: ReasonModel[] = [
  { id: "opus", name: "Claude Opus 5.5", logo: <ClaudeLogo />, effort: "medium", role: "Researching", provider: "Anthropic" },
  { id: "grok", name: "Grok 5", logo: <GrokLogo />, effort: "high", role: "Analyzing", provider: "xAI" },
  { id: "gpt", name: "GPT-5.5", logo: <OpenAILogo />, effort: "max", role: "Solving", provider: "OpenAI" },
];

export function Answer() {
  return <ReasoningSummary steps={steps} models={models} sources={sources} sourceCount={24} />;
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `ReasonStep[]` |  | Every step in order – one bar segment each, as wide as its share of the time |
| ReasonStep.kind / label | `string / string` |  | What kind of step it is – its color and icon – and what it did, shown in Steps |
| ReasonStep.ms / running | `number / boolean` |  | How long it took; leave ms out on a running step and it counts on its own |
| ReasonStep.model | `string` |  | The id of the model that did it – ties the step to its model for highlighting and details |
| models | `ReasonModel[]` |  | One row each: logo, name, an effort meter, role and time; a click opens its details below |
| ReasonModel.effort | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "max"` |  | How hard it thought – four small bars, lit in the color of the kind it spent most time on |
| ReasonModel.provider / tokens / cost / note | `string / { input?, output? } / number / string` |  | Its details: who makes it, what it read and wrote, what it cost in dollars, and why it was picked |
| sources / sourceCount | `ReasonSource[] / number` |  | The stacked logos and the Sources list (name, detail, href); sourceCount when there were more than you pass |
| running | `boolean` |  | Still reasoning – the header says "Reasoning", the mark twinkles, the bar leaves room to grow |
| estimate | `number` |  | How long it will likely take (ms) – the grey track at the end of the bar shows what's probably left |

| defaultOpen | `boolean` |  | Steps open from the start |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it |

- Tab: Four stops: the kinds, the models, Sources, Steps
- ← / → / ↑ / ↓: Walk the kinds (two columns) or the models – what belongs with the focused one lights up

# Repo Map, clean style (Pro)

A codebase as a treemap with coding agents working on it – every folder a group, every file a tile as large as its lines, in Context Map's tiles. Each agent is its pixel mark hopping from file to file; a file it edits fills with its color from the bottom up with a sheen running over it and keeps the color once it moves on, so the map fills as the work goes on. A file it only reads gets a dashed edge, two agents in one file blink orange. Point at a file for its path, lines and who changed what; click an agent to keep its files clear

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/repo-map
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/repo-map-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/repo-map-clean`

### When to use

- Coding agents working on one codebase – which files each one is in, what it changed and where they get in each other's way
- A run's footprint at a glance: the map fills with each agent's color as it works
- Spotting two agents editing the same file before their changes collide

### When not to use

- What fills one agent's context window – use Context Map
- A branch's commits one after another – use Commit Trail
- Changes as lines of code – use a diff view such as Diff Timeline

### Usage

```tsx
import { RepoMap, type RepoAgent, type RepoFile } from "@/components/ui/repo-map-clean";

const files: RepoFile[] = [
  { path: "src/lib/auth.ts", lines: 320, edits: [{ agent: "auth", added: 64, removed: 12 }] },
  { path: "src/lib/session.ts", lines: 240 },
  { path: "src/components/LoginForm.tsx", lines: 210 },
  { path: "tests/auth.test.ts", lines: 230 },
];

const agents: RepoAgent[] = [
  { id: "auth", name: "Auth agent", file: "src/lib/session.ts", action: "edit", task: "Adding token refresh" },
  { id: "tests", name: "Test agent", file: "tests/auth.test.ts", action: "read" },
];

export function Workspace() {
  return <RepoMap title="acme/web" branch="feat/token-refresh" files={files} agents={agents} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files | `RepoFile[]` |  | Every file – { path, lines, edits? }. The folder in its path groups it, its lines are its area; a path given twice shows once |
| edits | `{ agent, added?, removed? }[]` |  | Per file, oldest first – who changed it and how much. The last one's agent tints the file; the tile shows +added −removed |
| agents | `RepoAgent[]` |  | The agents – { id, name, color?, file?, action?, task? }. Each is its pixel mark in a color of the palette (blue when it works alone), sitting on the file it is at |
| action | `"edit" \| "read"` |  | Per agent – edit (default) fills the file with its color and runs a sheen over it; read gives it a dashed edge. Two agents editing one file make it blink orange |
| title / branch | `string` |  | The repo's name and its branch, in the bar |
| depth | `number` |  | How many folder levels group the files – 2 by default (src/components, src/lib …) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root – set the color variables on it, e.g. --ui-rpmc-height |

### Keyboard

- Tab: The agents in the bar, then one stop for the map
- ← / → / ↑ / ↓: Walk the files, folder by folder – each shows its card
- Home / End: First or last file
- Enter / Space: On an agent: keeps its files clear and fades the rest
- Esc: Hides the file's card, or clears the agent you look at

### Accessibility

- Every file reads its path, its lines, who is in it and who changed what – "src/lib/session.ts, 240 lines, conflict, Auth agent and UI agent editing"
- The agents in the bar are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) that say how many files each touched
- A polite live region says when an agent moves to another file
- Focus rings show for the keyboard only (:focus-visible), inside the tiles so the map never cuts them

### Motion

- An agent's mark hops from file to file on a soft ease and twinkles in a diagonal wave while it writes
- A file fills with the agent's color from the bottom up when it starts on it, and a sheen runs over it while it writes
- A conflict blinks orange until one of them moves on
- With prefers-reduced-motion the marks jump, the files tint at once and nothing blinks

### Responsive

- The map keeps its height and lays the files out again for any width – a file's name and its count show while there's room
- Narrow: a taller map, the count on its own line, the agents wrap
- Long paths and names end in … with the full text on hover and in the file's card
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give agents stable ids – their color and their mark come from it
- Keep the order of files stable – the treemap keeps neighbours next to each other, so the map doesn't jump
- Add an edit when an agent moves on from a file it wrote, and point file at where it is now

### Requirements

- React 19

# Review Center, clean style (Pro)

A focused workspace for what your agents want to do – the queue sorted by risk, one item at a time with the shaky spans marked, Approve, Edit, Reject and Skip on single keys, a stamp as each one leaves and the next one rising in

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/review-center
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/review-center-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/review-center-clean`

### When to use

- Human in the loop at volume: a person signs off what agents produced – code changes, migrations, plans, contract edits, refunds, payments – one item after another
- Code review for agents: a multi-file change as file rows with +/- counts and a unified diff with line numbers, the risky lines flagged with the agent's own note
- When the reviewer has to see why the agent wants something and where it is unsure, not only what it wants
- Review queues with a service level: oldest items and items close to their deadline need to stand out

### When not to use

- A board of background tasks with their status – use Agent Inbox
- A handful of yes/no questions answered in passing – use Decision Inbox
- One action that waits for a go, with a countdown – use Approval Card
- An agent asking for access to a tool or scope – use Permission Request
- An agent stuck on a decision that lays out its options and their consequences – use Decision Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { ReviewCenter, type ReviewItem } from "@/components/ui/review-center-clean";

const items: ReviewItem[] = [
  {
    id: "refund-4821",
    title: "Refund order #4821 for Maya Chen",
    agent: "Support agent", model: "Sonnet 5.5",
    type: "Refund", risk: "high", confidence: 0.62,
    createdAt: Date.now() - 26 * 60_000,
    reasoning: "Her blender arrived cracked – damaged items are covered within 30 days.",
    fields: [
      // A flagged span: marked in the proposal, its note shows on hover or with F
      { label: "Amount", value: [{ text: "$184.00", note: "Includes $20 express shipping.", source: "Refund policy §4" }] },
      { label: "Order", value: "#4821" },
    ],
    bodyLabel: "Reply to Maya",
    body: "Hi Maya, I'm so sorry your blender arrived cracked …",
  },
];

export function Reviews() {
  return (
    <ReviewCenter
      items={items}
      reviewed={24}
      onDecide={(item, result) => save(item.id, result)} // { decision, reason?, text?, fields? }
      onUndo={(item) => revert(item.id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `ReviewItem[]` |  | { id, title, agent, model?, icon?, type, risk, confidence, createdAt, reasoning?, fields?, body?, bodyLabel?, format?, sources? } – everything waiting; decided items hide themselves, new ids slide into the queue |
| risk | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` |  | Per item – sorts the queue (high first), feeds the High risk filter and shows as a small tag next to the agent (high and medium) |
| confidence | `number` |  | Per item, 0–1 – below lowConfidence the item counts as Unsure |
| fields / body | `ReviewText` |  | Per item – a string, or an array of strings and { text, note, source? } flags; flags are marked and explain themselves on hover, focus or F. Edit (E) works on these two |
| files | `ReviewFile[]` |  | Per item – a code change: { path, added?, removed?, diff?, start? } – a row per file, a unified diff with line numbers and a light syntax tint under the files that have one |
| steps | `ReviewStep[]` |  | Per item – a plan: { title, tool?, icon?, detail? } as numbered steps; a step with a flag gets an amber number |
| format | `"text" \| "code"` | `"text"` | Per item – "code" shows the body as a diff, like a file's |
| onDecide | `(item, result) => void` |  | Approved or rejected – result is { decision, reason?, text?, fields? }; text and fields only when the reviewer edited them |
| onUndo | `(item, result) => void` |  | The last decision was taken back – put the item back if you dropped it from items |
| onSkip | `(item) => void` |  | The reviewer moved on without deciding; the row is marked skipped |
| reviewed | `number` | `0` | How many were reviewed before (e.g. today) – the header counts on from here |
| total | `number` | `reviewed + waiting` | The total in the header |
| sla | `number` | `1800000` | How long an item may wait, in ms – waiting times turn amber at 75% and red past it |
| now | `number` |  | The clock (epoch ms) – defaults to the real one, ticking every 10s |
| lowConfidence | `number` | `0.7` | Below this an item is Unsure |
| reasons | `string[]` | `["Wrong info", "Tone", "Not allowed", "Other"]` | The quick reasons for a rejection, picked with 1–4 |
| order | `"risk" \| "oldest" \| "given"` | `"risk"` | High risk first then oldest, oldest first, or as passed |
| filter / defaultFilter | `"all" \| "high" \| "unsure"` | `"all"` | The queue's filter, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onFilterChange | `(filter) => void` |  | The filter changed |
| ref | `Ref<ReviewCenterHandle>` |  | approve, reject(reason?), edit, setDraft, save, cancel, skip, next, previous, undo, peek(index), select(id) |
| title | `string` | `"Review center"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- A: Approves the current item
- E: Edits the proposal in place – Cmd/Ctrl+Enter approves with the edits, Esc cancels
- R: Rejects – then 1–4 picks the reason, Esc cancels
- S: Skips to the next item without deciding
- J / K: Next and previous item (ArrowDown and ArrowUp work too)
- F: Shows the agent's note on the next flagged span
- Z: Undoes the last decision (Cmd/Ctrl+Z too)
- Esc: Closes the reason picker, the editor or a note

### Accessibility

- Shortcuts work while the focus is anywhere inside – a click on plain content keeps them working; buttons carry aria-keyshortcuts
- Every action is a real button; the reason picker is a labelled group
- Queue rows show only the title, the type and the waiting time; as buttons they are labelled with title, type, risk, confidence and waiting time; the current one has aria-current
- Flagged spans are focusable and point to their note with aria-describedby (role tooltip)
- Decisions, skips and undos are announced in a polite live region, with the new count
- When the row or field you were on leaves, the focus moves to the next item instead of getting lost

### Motion

- Calm and quick: a decided row shows a small check or cross where its time was, fades and closes up (about 300ms)
- The decided item fades up a few pixels while the next one follows a beat later from just below – the same soft ease as Trace Waterfall
- The pressed button flashes its decision's tint for a moment; the progress bar glides on
- Items that arrive open their row at their sorted spot with a soft highlight
- J and K slide the item up or down; the agent's note opens with a small scale and fade
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything changes at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: wide, the queue sits on the left and the item on the right, in a fixed-height workspace
- Under 640px the queue goes on top, three rows high, the item under it; its box glides to each item's height; buttons share the width
- Under 420px the agent line wraps between its parts instead of cutting them, button icons step aside and the flag counter hides – flags are tapped directly; diffs scroll sideways
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every waiting item – the component sorts, filters and hides what's decided; keep ids stable
- For code, pass files with a unified diff (git diff output works once split into its files); put a flag on the exact expression that worries the agent, not on a whole line
- Flag only the spans the agent is genuinely unsure about, each with a one-line note and, if you have it, its source
- createdAt is when the item started waiting, not when the agent run started
- If you remove decided items from items in onDecide, add them back in onUndo
- Colors are variables on .ui-rvcc, e.g. --ui-rvcc-flag-bg / --ui-rvcc-flag-edge for the flagged spans; --ui-rvcc-height sets the workspace height
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

# Root Cause Tree, clean style (Pro)

How an agent finds out why a run failed, as a fault tree – it checks one hypothesis after another, rules some out, confirms the cause, and the way up to the failure lights up

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/root-cause-tree
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/root-cause-tree-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/root-cause-tree-clean`

### When to use

- Showing how an agent debugs a failed run – every hypothesis it has, which it ruled out and which turned out to be the cause
- Postmortems for agent runs: the failure on top, the way down to what really broke, with the proof for each step
- Anywhere causes combine – an OR where one is enough, an AND where only several together break it

### When not to use

- Who started whom in a run – use Agent Tree
- Rewinding a run to an earlier point – use Agent Checkpoints
- A plain list of findings without causes – use Agent Findings

### Usage

```tsx
import { RootCauseTree, type Cause } from "@/components/ui/root-cause-tree-clean";

const failure: Cause & { detail?: string } = {
  id: "failure",
  title: "Checkout tests failing",
  detail: "4 of 12",
  children: [
    { id: "stripe", title: "Stripe API errors", status: "ruled-out", verdict: "Every call came back 200." },
    {
      id: "coupon",
      title: "Coupon not applied",
      gate: "and",
      status: "confirmed",
      children: [
        { id: "percent", title: "Discount sent as amount", status: "confirmed", evidence: { kind: "Diff", content: "- amount_off\n+ percent_off" } },
        { id: "recompute", title: "Total recomputed after", status: "checking" },
      ],
    },
  ],
};

export function Investigation() {
  return <RootCauseTree failure={failure} onAction={(cause, action) => agent.run(action, cause.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| failure | `Cause & { detail?: string }` |  | The failure on top – its children are the first hypotheses; detail is a short line next to its badge, e.g. "4 of 12" |
| children | `Cause[]` |  | Per cause: { id, title, icon?, files?, gate?, status?, verdict?, evidence?, at?, children? } – the hypotheses under it, as deep as you need |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Per cause: a small mark before the title, e.g. the logo of the tool or service it's about – it turns gray when ruled out |
| files | `string[]` |  | Per cause: the files it touches – the first shows as a chip on the card, the rest as "+2"; the evidence card lists them all with their full path |
| gate | `"or" \| "and"` | `"or"` | Per cause, for its children: or – one of them is enough; and – they only cause it together |
| status | `"open" \| "checking" \| "ruled-out" \| "confirmed"` | `"open"` | Per cause – a confirmed one without children is a root cause and lights the way up |
| verdict | `string` |  | Per cause: why it was ruled out or confirmed, in a sentence – shown with its evidence |
| evidence | `{ kind, source?, content }` |  | Per cause: the proof – kind is its label ("Log", "Diff", "Tool call"), content the lines, shown as code |
| onAction | `(cause, action: "fix" \| "retry") => void` |  | Fix it or Retry from here was pressed on a root cause – without it, the evidence is read only |
| formatTime | `(ms: number) => string` | `0:42` | Formats when a cause was checked (at) |
| title | `string` | `"Root cause"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Up to the parent, down to the first child – narrow, the previous and next row
- ← / →: Along the row, from one branch into the next – narrow, out to the parent and in to the first child
- Home / End: The failure on top, the last hypothesis
- Enter / Space: Shows that cause's evidence; again goes back
- Tab: From the tree on to the evidence – its code scrolls with the arrow keys – and Fix it / Retry from here
- Esc: Back to what the agent works on

### Accessibility

- The hypotheses are a tree with one tab stop; every card says its title, how it stands and, for a split, whether any or all of the ones below cause it
- The evidence under the tree is announced politely when it changes
- Status is never color alone: ruled out, confirmed and root cause are words, and ruled-out lines are dashed

### Motion

- The hypothesis being checked shimmers; one that's ruled out fades back flat with a dashed line, but stays
- The evidence card grows and shrinks with what's in it – short while there's nothing to show, easing to its new height
- When the root cause is confirmed, the way up to the failure draws itself in blue, from the cause up, one step after the other
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears

### Responsive

- Every card has a fixed height, so nothing moves when a hypothesis is checked, ruled out or confirmed; the failure's card fits its own title, the hypotheses all share one width – as wide as their longest title needs, growing into spare room – and a title too long for the room ends in “…”, shown whole in the evidence
- The tree lays itself out from its own width; when even the narrowest cards don't fit it becomes an indented list – two rows a card, the gates as chips on the cards
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Add every hypothesis as soon as the agent has it, as open – then move it through checking to ruled-out or confirmed
- Never remove a ruled-out hypothesis; it shows what was checked
- A confirmed cause with children is confirmed only when its gate is met: one child for or, all for and
- The blue of the way up is --ui-rctc-path; how far what you didn't pick fades is --ui-rctc-dim

### Requirements

- React 19

# Run Controls, clean style (Pro)

Every control a running agent needs, in one composer – stop it, resume from the word it stopped at, retry or dismiss, steer it mid-answer or queue what's next, with Chat or Act, permissions and how full the context is

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/run-controls
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/run-controls-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/run-controls-clean`

### When to use

- Chat and agent products where answers take a while and people want to stop, redirect or line up the next ask
- Any streamed answer that should survive a stop or a dropped connection and carry on from where it was

### When not to use

- A long conversation history – this shows the current turn; pair it with your own message list
- Steering a multi-step plan – Agent Steering shows the plan and where a note lands in it

### Usage

```tsx
import { RunControls } from "@/components/ui/run-controls-clean";

export function Assistant({ run, actions }) {
  return (
    <RunControls
      agent={{ id: "travel", name: "Trip planner" }}
      prompt={run.prompt}
      answer={run.answer}            // the text so far
      status={run.status}            // "idle" | "running" | "stopped" | "error" | "done"
      steers={run.steers}            // [{ at: 214, text: "Keep it to three days" }]
      queue={run.queue}              // [{ id: "q1", text: "Add a packing list" }]
      context={run.contextUsed}      // 0–1
      onSend={actions.send}
      onSteer={actions.steer}        // Enter while it runs
      onQueue={actions.queue}        // ⌥ Enter while it runs
      onUnqueue={actions.unqueue}
      onStop={actions.stop}          // Esc
      onResume={actions.resume}      // carry on from the same word
      onRetry={actions.retry}
      onDismiss={actions.dismiss}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent | `{ id: string; name: string }` | `{ id: "agent", name: "Agent" }` | The agent – its id gives it its own pixel mark |
| prompt | `string` |  | What was asked; without it the run area shows a quiet start |
| answer | `string` |  | The answer so far – it streams in as you update it |
| status | `"idle" \| "running" \| "stopped" \| "error" \| "done"` | `"idle"` | Running shows the caret and Stop; stopped and error show Resume, Retry and Dismiss; done shows Retry |
| steers | `{ at: number; text: string }[]` |  | Notes sent while it ran, drawn into the answer at the character they landed on |
| queue | `{ id: string; text: string }[]` |  | Messages waiting for the run to finish, above the composer |
| mode / defaultMode / onModeChange | `"chat" \| "act"` | `"act"` | Chat only answers; Act may change things – the permission menu only applies there |
| permission / defaultPermission / onPermissionChange | `"ask" \| "edits" \| "full"` | `"ask"` | What the agent may do without asking; Full access turns red |
| context | `number` |  | Share of the context window in use (0–1); orange from 80% |
| took | `number` |  | Seconds the run took, for “Done in 0:14” |
| onSend / onSteer / onQueue | `(text: string) => void` |  | Enter sends when idle; while running Enter steers and ⌥ Enter queues |
| onUnqueue | `(id: string) => void` |  | The × on a queued message |
| onStop / onResume / onRetry / onDismiss | `() => void` |  | The run's controls |
| placeholder | `string` |  | Text in the empty field |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send – or, while the agent works, steer it now
- ⌥ / Enter: While the agent works: queue the message for after
- Shift / Enter: New line
- Esc: Stop the run (closes the permission menu first)
- ← / →: Switch between Chat and Act
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: Move through the permission menu

### Accessibility

- Status changes (Writing, Stopped, Done, queued count) are announced in a polite live region – the streamed words are not, so screen readers aren't flooded
- The field explains its keys through aria-describedby, and changes its label while the agent runs
- Mode is a radio group, permissions a menu of radio items with the current one checked; the permission button keeps its name (Permissions: Ask first) when only its icon shows
- Words are counted with Intl.Segmenter, so “Stopped at 28 words” is right for Japanese or Thai too
- The conversation scrolls on its own and is focusable, so it can be scrolled by keyboard

### Motion

- A steering note drops into the answer where it lands; the caret pulses while the agent writes and its mark twinkles
- Queued messages and a new turn rise in; the buttons swap in place – Send, Stop, Queue and Steer
- Reduced motion turns all of it off

### Responsive

- The run keeps one height and scrolls, so the card never grows while it streams
- Up to four queued messages show; more scroll inside the tray, so the composer stops growing
- Long agent names end in an ellipsis with the full name on hover; long links and words wrap instead of widening the card
- On touch screens the Esc hint is hidden – Stop stays a button
- Right-to-left: the layout mirrors, the bubble, menu and indents included
- Below 420px the permission shows only its icon and the context only its ring
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

```tsx
import { RunningNow, type RunningTask } from "@/components/ui/running-now-clean";

const tasks: RunningTask[] = [

];
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

| onOpen | `(id) => void` |  | A click on a row, or Open on a task that needs you |

| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the trigger: opens the list and moves to the first task, or closes it
- ↓ / ↑: On the trigger: opens the list and moves to the first or the last task
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: Moves between the tasks – from a row or from its button
- Tab: From a task to its Pause, Resume or Open button, then on to the next task
- Esc: Closes the list and puts focus back on the trigger

### Accessibility

- The trigger says the whole summary – "Background tasks: 3 running, 2 need you" – and has aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls
- The list is a dialog named "Background tasks"; a click outside or tabbing out of it closes it
- Each row is a button that reads its title, state, step and steps – "Ingest pipeline – running. Embedding chunks. 2 of 4 steps"
- Every icon button names its task – "Pause Ingest pipeline", "Open Refund review – needs you"
- A polite live region says when a task starts waiting for you or finishes
- Focus never drops to the page: Pause and Resume keep it on the same button, and when a task finishes (or leaves the list) it moves to that row or the nearest one

- The ring fills like a pie as the steps go by, and changes color with it – orange, amber, teal, blue once done
- A new step crossfades in place: the old line slides up and out while the new one rises in; the counts in the trigger do the same
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything changes at once

- Every row is 52px in every state – a step that changes, a badge that comes or goes never moves another row
- The popover is 340px wide and never wider than the screen minus 32px, so it fits a 375px phone
- Touch screens get 36px buttons, a 36px trigger and 56px rows
- The list scrolls inside the popover after five and a half rows – the half row shows there is more – and stays clear of short screens
- On a phone narrower than 360px, or with four-digit counts below 420px, the trigger keeps only the numbers when both counts show; its label still reads the full summary

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every task a stable id – the crossfade and the live region track rows by it
- Keep step short and in the present – "Embedding chunks", not "The agent is currently embedding chunks"; for needs-you, write what it waits for
- done and total are steps; with total 0 the ring stays empty
- Paused tasks don't count as running in the trigger
- Colors are variables on .ui-rnc, e.g. --ui-rnc-teal or --ui-rnc-amber; the popover width is --ui-rnc-w

- React 19

# Scheduled Runs, clean style (Pro)

Agent tasks sorted into a week of sessions – each session has a usage limit, small tasks fill the gaps, big ones are split across sessions, and the stack flies in one card at a time

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/scheduled-runs
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/scheduled-runs-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/scheduled-runs-clean`

### When to use

- Agents that run against a usage limit per session – coding agents, API quotas, rate-limited tools – and a week of work to fit in
- Showing people where their queued tasks will run before they run, and which ones need more than one session
- A backlog that gets sorted into a calendar automatically, next to runs that were booked by hand

### When not to use

- Tasks handed from agent to agent – use Agent Handoff
- A queue that runs as soon as a worker is free, with no sessions – use Agent Queue
- What a single run costs in time and money – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { ScheduledRuns, type ScheduledTask } from "@/components/ui/scheduled-runs-clean";

const tasks: ScheduledTask[] = [
  { id: "metrics", title: "Weekly metrics report", usage: 40, at: { day: 1, session: 0 } },
  { id: "oauth", title: "Migrate auth to OAuth 2.1", agent: "Claude Code", usage: 140 },
  { id: "flaky", title: "Fix flaky checkout test", agent: "Claude Code", usage: 35 },
];

export function Week() {
  return <ScheduledRuns tasks={tasks} now={{ day: 1, session: 0 }} note="5-hour sessions" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `ScheduledTask[]` |  | { id, title, usage, agent?, detail?, logo?, at? } – booked tasks have at: { day, session }; the rest wait in the stack and are sorted in, in this order |
| usage | `number` |  | Per task – what it takes out of one session's limit, in percent; over the limit it's split across sessions |
| days | `(string \| { name, date? })[]` | `Mon–Wed` | Column heads – three days read best; more fit, the week then scrolls sideways on narrow screens |
| sessions | `string[]` | `["07:00", "12:00", "17:00"]` | Row heads – when each session starts |
| now | `{ day, session }` | `{ day: 0, session: 0 }` | The session running now – earlier ones are dimmed and take no new tasks; a red line marks where it starts |
| limit | `number` | `100` | What one session can take, in the unit of usage |
| minPiece | `number` | `15` | A split task never leaves a piece smaller than this in a session |
| agents | `{ name, logo? }[]` | `every task's agent` | The agents in the head as small overlapping logos – picking one fans them out, slides its name out and fades the other agents' tasks back |
| defaultMode | `"auto" \| "manual"` | `"auto"` | Auto sorts the stack in when switched to; Manual puts the sorted-in cards back on the stack – booked cards and cards placed by hand stay. Both switch mid-run |
| autoRun | `boolean \| number` | `false` | In Auto: sorts the stack in on its own – after 800ms, or after the number of ms |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Clears the week and sorts in again, over and over – for demos |
| title / note | `string` | `"This week"` | Heading, and a quiet note next to it – e.g. "5-hour sessions" |
| onScheduled | `(parts: ScheduledPart[]) => void` |  | Every piece in the week once the stack is sorted in – { task, day, session, usage, part, parts } |
| onPlace | `(task: ScheduledTask, parts: ScheduledPart[]) => void` |  | A task was dragged from the stack into a session – with the pieces it was split into |
| onMove | `(part: ScheduledPart, to: { day, session }) => void` |  | A card was dragged to another session – save it |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the cards – the stack first, then the sessions day by day
- Enter: Opens or closes the focused card's details
- Space: Picks the focused card up to move it – and drops it where it is aimed
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: While holding a card: the session a day earlier or later
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown: While holding a card: the session before or after on the same day
- Escape: Puts a held card back (with the mouse too); closes the details
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: On Auto / Manual: switches between them

### Accessibility

- Every card is a focusable button with a visible focus ring; its hint says what Enter and Space do – past cards say they can't move
- Moving by keyboard is announced in a polite live region: what was picked up, each session it's aimed at and whether it has room – or why not – and where it landed
- After a drop, focus moves to the card in its new session; Escape returns it to the card it came from
- The week is a grid with day and session heads; Auto / Manual is a radio group you switch with the arrows
- The button-like agent logos are toggle buttons named after their agent

### Motion

- Each card flies from the stack into its first session and shrinks into a chip on the way; the stack closes up behind it
- The other pieces of a split task drop into their sessions, the bars at the foot of the sessions fill
- A red line with a dot on its left sits between the sessions that are over and the one running
- A click on a card opens its details right under it – what it does, the agent, the session and its share; a click elsewhere closes them
- Dragging a card – from the stack or between sessions – lifts a copy under the pointer; sessions without room for it – full, out of places or already past – turn gray and striped, the one under it lights up
- With prefers-reduced-motion the cards appear in place without flying

### Responsive

- Every session keeps its height and takes two cards – sessions with two are full for dragging and for Auto
- A long stack scrolls inside its column – it never stretches the board
- Under 640px the stack moves on top and the week scrolls sideways
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every task a unique id – placing, moving and focus keep track of tasks by it
- A task without a usage (NaN) can't be scheduled and says so; a usage of 0 or less counts as 1%
- Booked tasks outside the days and sessions shown are left out
- usage is a share of one session's limit – e.g. estimated tokens divided by the session's token limit, times 100
- Auto never splits a task that fits one session – it waits for a session with room for all of it
- Dragged by hand, a task goes where it's dropped: whatever doesn't fit there runs on into the next sessions with room, after the last one into the earliest free one from now on; pieces are numbered by time and merge within a session
- Tasks that don't fit anywhere this week stay in the stack, marked "No room this week"
- Drag a task from the stack into a session to book it by hand – a big one is split from there on; Auto then sorts in only what's left
- A press that moves less than 4px is a click (details), anything more is a drag
- Holding a card in the stack pauses Auto until it's let go – a click lets Auto carry on
- Cards can be grabbed at any time – dragging one while Auto sorts in lets the card in the air land, then stops and switches to Manual; Auto picks up the rest again
- With loop, the demo waits while the pointer is over it and stops for good once someone clicks or drags
- Cards can be dragged to any session from now on with a free place (two cards at most) and at least minPiece of its limit left; past sessions can't be dragged from or to
- planWeek is exported – use it on the server to book the same plan the component shows
- Colors are variables on .ui-srn, e.g. --ui-srn-meter or --ui-srn-track

Agent tasks sorted into a week of sessions – each session has a usage limit, small tasks fill the gaps, big ones are split across sessions, and the stack flies in one card at a time

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/scheduled-runs
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install, classic style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/scheduled-runs.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Install, clean style: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/scheduled-runs-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key) – lands as `scheduled-runs-clean.tsx`, import from `@/components/ui/scheduled-runs-clean` – its docs: `scheduled-runs-clean.md`
- Import: `@/components/ui/scheduled-runs`

### When to use

- Agents that run against a usage limit per session – coding agents, API quotas, rate-limited tools – and a week of work to fit in
- Showing people where their queued tasks will run before they run, and which ones need more than one session
- A backlog that gets sorted into a calendar automatically, next to runs that were booked by hand

### When not to use

- Tasks handed from agent to agent – use Agent Handoff
- A queue that runs as soon as a worker is free, with no sessions – use Agent Queue
- What a single run costs in time and money – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { ScheduledRuns, type ScheduledTask } from "@/components/ui/scheduled-runs";

const tasks: ScheduledTask[] = [
  { id: "metrics", title: "Weekly metrics report", usage: 40, at: { day: 1, session: 0 } },
  { id: "oauth", title: "Migrate auth to OAuth 2.1", agent: "Claude Code", usage: 140 },
  { id: "flaky", title: "Fix flaky checkout test", agent: "Claude Code", usage: 35 },
];

export function Week() {
  return <ScheduledRuns tasks={tasks} now={{ day: 1, session: 0 }} note="5-hour sessions" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `ScheduledTask[]` |  | { id, title, usage, agent?, detail?, logo?, at? } – booked tasks have at: { day, session }; the rest wait in the stack and are sorted in, in this order |
| usage | `number` |  | Per task – what it takes out of one session's limit, in percent; over the limit it's split across sessions |
| days | `(string \| { name, date? })[]` | `Mon–Wed` | Column heads – three days read best; more fit, the week then scrolls sideways on narrow screens |
| sessions | `string[]` | `["07:00", "12:00", "17:00"]` | Row heads – when each session starts |
| now | `{ day, session }` | `{ day: 0, session: 0 }` | The session running now – earlier ones are dimmed and take no new tasks; a red line marks where it starts |
| limit | `number` | `100` | What one session can take, in the unit of usage |
| minPiece | `number` | `15` | A split task never leaves a piece smaller than this in a session |
| agents | `{ name, logo? }[]` | `every task's agent` | The agents in the head as small overlapping logos – picking one fans them out, slides its name out and fades the other agents' tasks back |
| defaultMode | `"auto" \| "manual"` | `"auto"` | Auto sorts the stack in when switched to; Manual puts the sorted-in cards back on the stack – booked cards and cards placed by hand stay. Both switch mid-run |
| autoRun | `boolean \| number` | `false` | In Auto: sorts the stack in on its own – after 800ms, or after the number of ms |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Clears the week and sorts in again, over and over – for demos |
| title / note | `string` | `"This week"` | Heading, and a quiet note next to it – e.g. "5-hour sessions" |
| onScheduled | `(parts: ScheduledPart[]) => void` |  | Every piece in the week once the stack is sorted in – { task, day, session, usage, part, parts } |
| onPlace | `(task: ScheduledTask, parts: ScheduledPart[]) => void` |  | A task was dragged from the stack into a session – with the pieces it was split into |
| onMove | `(part: ScheduledPart, to: { day, session }) => void` |  | A card was dragged to another session – save it |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the cards – the stack first, then the sessions day by day
- Enter: Opens or closes the focused card's details
- Space: Picks the focused card up to move it – and drops it where it is aimed
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: While holding a card: the session a day earlier or later
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown: While holding a card: the session before or after on the same day
- Escape: Puts a held card back (with the mouse too); closes the details
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: On Auto / Manual: switches between them

### Accessibility

- Every card is a focusable button with a visible focus ring; its hint says what Enter and Space do – past cards say they can't move
- Moving by keyboard is announced in a polite live region: what was picked up, each session it's aimed at and whether it has room – or why not – and where it landed
- After a drop, focus moves to the card in its new session; Escape returns it to the card it came from
- The week is a grid with day and session heads; Auto / Manual is a radio group you switch with the arrows
- The button-like agent logos are toggle buttons named after their agent

### Motion

- Each card flies from the stack into its first session and shrinks into a chip on the way; the stack closes up behind it
- The other pieces of a split task drop into their sessions, the bars at the foot of the sessions fill
- A red line with a dot on its left sits between the sessions that are over and the one running
- A click on a card opens its details right under it – what it does, the agent, the session and its share; a click elsewhere closes them
- Dragging a card – from the stack or between sessions – lifts a copy under the pointer; sessions without room for it – full, out of places or already past – turn gray and striped, the one under it lights up
- With prefers-reduced-motion the cards appear in place without flying

### Responsive

- Every session keeps its height and takes two cards – sessions with two are full for dragging and for Auto
- A long stack scrolls inside its column – it never stretches the board
- Under 640px the stack moves on top and the week scrolls sideways
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every task a unique id – placing, moving and focus keep track of tasks by it
- A task without a usage (NaN) can't be scheduled and says so; a usage of 0 or less counts as 1%
- Booked tasks outside the days and sessions shown are left out
- usage is a share of one session's limit – e.g. estimated tokens divided by the session's token limit, times 100
- Auto never splits a task that fits one session – it waits for a session with room for all of it
- Dragged by hand, a task goes where it's dropped: whatever doesn't fit there runs on into the next sessions with room, after the last one into the earliest free one from now on; pieces are numbered by time and merge within a session
- Tasks that don't fit anywhere this week stay in the stack, marked "No room this week"
- Drag a task from the stack into a session to book it by hand – a big one is split from there on; Auto then sorts in only what's left
- A press that moves less than 4px is a click (details), anything more is a drag
- Holding a card in the stack pauses Auto until it's let go – a click lets Auto carry on
- Cards can be grabbed at any time – dragging one while Auto sorts in lets the card in the air land, then stops and switches to Manual; Auto picks up the rest again
- With loop, the demo waits while the pointer is over it and stops for good once someone clicks or drags
- Cards can be dragged to any session from now on with a free place (two cards at most) and at least minPiece of its limit left; past sessions can't be dragged from or to
- planWeek is exported – use it on the server to book the same plan the component shows
- Colors are variables on .ui-sch, e.g. --ui-sch-meter or --ui-sch-track

### Requirements

- React 19

# Segmented Control, clean style (Free)

Switch between two to six options – a raised pill or underline that glides, stretches a little and can be dragged across, with icons, counts and badges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/segmented-control
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/segmented-control-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/segmented-control-clean`

### When to use

- Switching between two to six views of the same content – sections of a dashboard, list / board / calendar, monthly / yearly
- A choice that applies right away and where every option should stay visible

### When not to use

- More than six options or long labels – use a select or a menu
- Choices that are confirmed with a Save button inside a form – radio buttons read clearer there
- Turning one thing on or off – that's a switch

### Usage

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from "@/components/ui/segmented-control-clean";

export function DashboardTabs() {
  const [section, setSection] = useState("overview");
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      aria-label="Dashboard section"
      kind="tabs"
      value={section}
      onChange={setSection}
      options={[
        { value: "overview", label: "Overview", controls: "panel-overview" },
        { value: "analytics", label: "Analytics", controls: "panel-analytics" },
        { value: "reports", label: "Reports", controls: "panel-reports" },
        { value: "notifications", label: "Notifications", count: unread, controls: "panel-notifications" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options | `SegmentOption[]` |  | { value, label?, icon?, count?, badge?, disabled?, ariaLabel?, controls? } – two to six work best; give icon-only options an ariaLabel |
| value | `string` |  | Controlled value |
| defaultValue | `string` | `first enabled option` | Starting value when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the new value – on click, while dragging the indicator and on arrow keys |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 24, 28 or 32px tall (40px+ on touch screens); md is 13px text with 4px 10px padding |
| variant | `"buttons" \| "tray" \| "underline"` | `"buttons"` | Separate chips with a hairline whose light-gray fill slides to the active one, a compact light-gray track with a white raised pill, or text tabs on a hairline with a sliding line |
| fullWidth | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its container with equal segments, each as wide as the widest one needs |
| kind | `"radio" \| "tabs"` | `"radio"` | A radiogroup, or a tablist that switches panels (pair with controls on each option) |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the whole control |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Names the group – or use aria-labelledby |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focuses the active option (one tab stop for the whole control)
- ← / →: Moves to and selects the previous or next option, wrapping around; ↑ ↓ too as a radiogroup
- Home / End: Selects the first or last option
- ↵: Selects the focused option (Space works too)

### Accessibility

- A radiogroup with radios (aria-checked), or a tablist with tabs (aria-selected, aria-controls) with kind="tabs"
- Roving tabindex: only the active option is in the tab order; disabled options are skipped by the arrow keys
- Labels are read once; counts and badges are part of the name
- Visible focus ring on the focused option

### Motion

- The indicator slides to the picked option in about 200ms; the edge facing the target leads a touch – short and crisp, no bounce
- Labels keep one weight and only change color, so neighbours never shift; hover washes fade in and out in 90ms
- When a label or count changes, the option and the whole control morph to the new width and the indicator follows; a new count blurs in
- Pressing gives the indicator a little (scale 0.97); dragging it across the options selects as you go
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- If it doesn't fit, it scrolls sideways with soft edges on the sides that hide options and keeps the active one in view
- Touch screens: options are at least 40px tall; a tap picks on lift, so swiping to scroll never picks by accident
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Select, type SelectOption } from "@/components/ui/select-clean";

const models: SelectOption[] = [

export function ModelSetting() {
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options | `SelectOption[]` |  | { value, label, description?, icon?, disabled? } – an icon and a quiet second line are optional per option |
| value | `string \| null` |  | The chosen value – makes it controlled; null shows the placeholder |
| defaultValue | `string \| null` | `null` | Starting value when uncontrolled |

| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown above the field and used as the list's name |
| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – the error takes its place while there is one |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks the field invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message where the hint was |
| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 28 · 32 · 36px high, like the Text Field; taller on touch screens |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the field and ignores input |
| name | `string` |  | Sends the value with a form, through a hidden input |
| required | `boolean` |  | Sets aria-required – check it on submit like any other field |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper, e.g. a fixed width in a settings row |

# Settings / Privacy (Pro)

Privacy settings with a settings sidebar: switches for ad measurement, analytics and training on chats, this browser's cookies, product emails, active sessions to sign out, chats shared by link and a danger zone to export or delete every chat

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/settings-privacy
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/settings-privacy.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/settings-privacy`

### When to use

- The privacy page of a person's settings in an AI product
- Pages that list sessions or shared links someone may want to revoke

### When not to use

- Workspace-wide sign-in rules – use Settings / Security
- Which notifications go where – use Settings / Notifications

### Usage

```tsx
import { SettingsPrivacyScreen } from "@/components/ui/settings-privacy";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <SettingsPrivacyScreen
      privacy={settings}
      onSave={(privacy) => savePrivacy(privacy)}
      onExport={() => api.startExport()}
      onDeleteChats={() => api.deleteAllChats()}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| privacy | `PrivacyValues` |  | The switches, this browser's cookies, product emails, sessions (device, name, meta, current) and shared chats (title, scope, shared, views) – the sample person when left out |
| onSave | `(privacy: PrivacyValues) => void` |  | Called with all settings whenever something changes, signing out a session and stopping a share included |
| onExport | `() => void` |  | Called when an export of every chat and file is requested |
| onDeleteChats | `() => void` |  | Called once deleting every chat is confirmed |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` |  | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` |  | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While the settings load: the switches, the email subscription, sessions and shared chats as gray shapes in the shape of the real ones; counts are hidden |
| empty | `boolean` |  | Nothing shared yet: only this device signed in, and “No shared chats” (or “No public links”) with an Open chats button in the shared chats' place |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Switches use role="switch" with aria-checked; Manage cookies has aria-expanded and opens its choices right below
- The shared chats' filter is a tab list; stopping a share is a button named after the chat
- The current device can't be signed out from here – it carries a This device badge instead of a button
- Deleting every chat asks once more before it happens

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Below 600px controls move under their labels; sessions and shared chats keep their action beside them
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Settings / Profile (its sidebar), Settings / General and Settings / Security (their rows, switches and badges), Button and Segmented Control (installed with it)

Security settings with a settings sidebar: email domains to verify, sign-in rules with SSO and two-step verification, the identity provider details to copy, an IP allowlist and a danger zone that signs everyone out

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/settings-security.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/settings-security`

### When to use

- The security page of a workspace's settings
- Admin pages with domains, single sign-on and network rules

### When not to use

- A single member's password or devices – put those under Settings / Profile
- The workspace's name and address – use Settings / General

### Usage

```tsx
import { SettingsSecurityScreen } from "@/components/ui/settings-security";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <SettingsSecurityScreen
      security={settings}
      onSave={(security) => saveSecurity(security)}
      onVerifyDomain={(domain) => api.checkTxtRecord(domain)}
      onSignOutAll={() => api.revokeSessions()}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| security | `SecurityValues` |  | Domains, join by domain, SSO, metadata URL, two-step verification, session length and IP ranges – the sample workspace when left out |
| onSave | `(security: SecurityValues) => void` |  | Called with all settings whenever something changes – switches and lists at once, the metadata URL on blur |
| onVerifyDomain | `(domain: string) => Promise<boolean>` |  | Checks the domain's TXT record; resolve true once it is found. The demo waits a moment and says yes |
| onSignOutAll | `() => void` |  | Called once signing everyone out is confirmed |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` |  | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` |  | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` |  | While the settings load: the domains, switches, session length, identity provider and IP ranges as gray shapes in the shape of the real ones |
| empty | `boolean` |  | Nothing set up yet: “No domains yet” with Add domain and “No IP ranges” with Add range in the lists' place; SSO and joining stay off |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Switches use role="switch" with aria-checked; a switch that needs a verified domain is disabled and says why
- Adding a domain or range is a small form: Enter adds, Escape cancels; wrong input answers with a toast
- Copy buttons turn into a check for a moment; read-only fields select their text on focus
- Remove buttons show on hover and on keyboard focus, always on touch screens

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Below 600px each control moves under its label; switches and the domain rows stay on one line
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Settings / Profile (its sidebar), Settings / General (its rows) and Button (installed with it)

# Setup Guide, clean style (Pro)

Onboarding panel with a progress bar and collapsible task groups that strike through when done

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/setup-guide
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/setup-guide-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/setup-guide-clean`

### When to use

- Onboarding with several areas, each made of a few steps that build on each other
- A floating guide in a dashboard corner that people can fold away and come back to

### When not to use

- A single short list of steps – the Progress Tracker is lighter
- Steps that can be done in any order – here each task unlocks the next

### Usage

```tsx
import { SetupGuide } from "@/components/ui/setup-guide-clean";

const groups = [
  {
    id: "workspace",
    title: "Set up your workspace",
    tasks: [
      { id: "name", label: "Choose a workspace name" },
      { id: "invite", label: "Invite your teammates" },
    ],
  },
  { id: "verify", title: "Verify your account", tasks: [{ id: "email", label: "Confirm your email", done: true }] },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return <SetupGuide groups={groups} onChange={save} onClose={hideGuide} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups | `SetupGroup[]` |  | Groups with an id, a title and tasks; each task has an id, a label and an optional done flag |
| title | `string` | `"Setup guide"` | Heading above the bar |
| onEdit | `() => void` |  | Shows an Edit link in the header |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button in the header |
| onChange | `(done: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the ids of all finished tasks |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the panel |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between groups, tasks and header buttons
- Enter / Space: Open or close a group, tick or untick a task

### Accessibility

- Group headers are buttons with aria-expanded, the closed panels are inert
- Tasks that are not unlocked yet are disabled; finished ones are pressed toggle buttons
- The bar is a progressbar with its percentage as value

### Motion

- Groups unfold smoothly; a finished group is struck through, folds away and opens the next one
- Reduced motion turns the transitions off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker, profile-menu

# Spinner, clean style (Free)

A small turning arc for work that runs right now – a faint ring in the text color, any size, inside a button or a status row, announced only when it has a label

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/spinner
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/spinner-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/spinner-clean`

### When to use

- Something that works right now and ends on its own: a run, a check, a connect, a save
- In place of a button's icon while its action runs – the button keeps its width
- As the status icon of a row that is still running, next to rows that show a check

### When not to use

- A whole area waiting for its data – use the Skeleton, so the page keeps its shape
- An agent thinking or writing – use the Thinking Loader or the agent's own pixel mark
- Work with a known length – show its progress, like the Progress Tracker

### Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/ui/spinner-clean";

export function ConnectButton({ busy, onConnect }: { busy: boolean; onConnect: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button type="button" aria-disabled={busy || undefined} onClick={() => !busy && onConnect()}>
      {busy ? <Spinner /> : <PlugIcon />}
      {busy ? "Connecting" : "Connect GitHub"}
    </button>
  );
}

// On its own, without words next to it: give it a label
<Spinner size={12} label="Checking domain" />
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | `number` | `14` | Width and height in px |
| label | `string` |  | Announced as a status (role="status" with aria-label). Leave it out when text next to it already says what happens – then it is hidden from screen readers |
| className | `string` |  | Extra classes – color it with color, it draws in currentColor |
| ...svg props | `ComponentProps<"svg">` |  | style, ref, data-* – everything goes to the <svg> |

### Accessibility

- With label: role="status" and aria-label, so screen readers say what is loading
- Without label: aria-hidden – the text next to it ("Running", "Connecting") carries the meaning, nothing is read twice
- Drawn in currentColor, so it always has the contrast of the text around it

### Motion

- One turn every 800ms, linear – the arc on a ring at 18% of the color
- With prefers-reduced-motion it keeps turning, slowly (2.4s): it is the only sign that something still runs
- Speed as a variable: --ui-spnc-speed on .ui-spnc

### Responsive

- A fixed size in px, so it never pushes text around; sits on the text's middle with vertical-align
- Dark mode needs nothing: it takes the text color

### Requirements

- React 19

# Stat Card, clean style (Pro)

One number with its label, how it changed – green or red, lower can be better – and room for a chart below or beside it; numbers roll, the card can be a link

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/stat-card
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/stat-card-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/stat-card-clean`

### When to use

- The KPI row on top of a dashboard – spend, tokens, latency, error rate
- One number with how it changed against the period before, and a small chart under or beside it
- Cards that open a detail view – pass href or onClick and the whole card becomes the target

### When not to use

- A chart that needs axes and a full tooltip – put a Trend Chart in a card of its own
- Many numbers in one table – a Data Table reads better than a wall of cards

### Usage

```tsx
import { StatCard } from "@/components/ui/stat-card-clean";
import { TrendChart } from "@/components/ui/trend-chart-clean";

export function Spend() {
  return (
    <StatCard
      label="Spend"
      value={2741}
      format={(n) => `$${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`}
      change={16.5}
      changeLabel="vs last week"
      chart={
        <TrendChart
          variant="sparkline"
          labels={["Mar 3", "Mar 4", "Mar 5", "Mar 6"]}
          series={[{ label: "Spend", values: [412, 455, 398, 470] }]}
        />
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | What the number is |
| value | `number \| string` |  | A number rolls when it changes and is shown through format; a string is shown as it is |
| format | `(n: number) => string` | `1,284 / 2.5B` | Formats a number value |
| change | `number` |  | Change in percent against the period before – a small badge with an arrow |
| changeFormat | `(n: number) => string` | `"12.4%"` | Formats the change; gets the absolute value |
| changeLabel | `string` |  | Quiet text after the change, e.g. "vs last week" |
| lowerIsBetter | `boolean` | `false` | A rise is bad news – red – and a fall good news – green |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | A 16px icon before the label |
| chart | `ReactNode` |  | Any chart – a Trend Chart sparkline fits it exactly |
| layout | `"stacked" \| "inline"` | `"stacked"` | The chart below the number or to its right |
| footer | `ReactNode` |  | The card's last row |
| loading | `boolean` | `false` | Placeholders instead of number, change and chart – the card keeps its size |
| href | `string` |  | Makes the whole card a link |
| onClick | `() => void` |  | Makes the whole card a button |
| hitProps | `HTMLAttributes` |  | Extra attributes for the link or button – e.g. role="tab", aria-selected and tabIndex when the cards pick what a chart shows |
| action | `ReactNode` |  | A small control in the top right corner – a menu or filter; stays clickable on a link card |
| selected | `boolean` |  | One card of a set is picked: false fades the card's content |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |
| style | `CSSProperties` |  | Inline styles on the card, e.g. CSS variables |
| --ui-statc-skel-h | `CSS variable` | `40px` | Height of the chart placeholder while loading – match it to a taller chart |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focus the card when it is a link or a button, then the chart inside it
- Enter: Open the card's link or press its button

### Accessibility

- Screen readers hear the final value and the change in words ("up 16.5% vs last week"), never a number on its way
- A link or button card names its label, value and change; the chart inside stays reachable on its own
- While loading the card is marked busy

### Motion

- A number rolls up from zero on first view and to its new value when it changes
- Placeholders carry a slow sheen while loading; reduced motion turns both off

### Responsive

- Fills its grid cell; the value wraps rather than being cut, the label and comparison end in an ellipsis
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
