# Stepper Form, clean style (Pro)

A multi-step flow for onboarding and setup – steps that fill and check off, sliding steps, a card that morphs to each step, inline validation and a success state

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/stepper-form
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/stepper-form-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/stepper-form-clean`

### When to use

- Onboarding, checkout or setup wizards where one long form would feel like too much at once
- Flows whose later steps depend on earlier answers, ending in a review before anything is created

### When not to use

- Two or three fields – a single form is faster
- Settings people jump around in freely – use tabs or sections instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { StepperForm, StepperField, StepperInput, StepperTags, StepperChoices, StepperReview, type Step } from "@/components/ui/stepper-form-clean";

type Values = { name: string; slug: string; invites: string[]; plan: string };

const steps: Step<Values>[] = [
  {
    id: "workspace",
    title: "Workspace",
    heading: "Name your workspace",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <>
        <StepperField name="name" label="Workspace name">
          <StepperInput value={values.name} onChange={(e) => setValues({ name: e.target.value, slug: slugify(e.target.value) })} />
        </StepperField>
        <StepperField name="slug" label="Workspace URL">
          <StepperInput prefix="acme.app/" value={values.slug} onChange={(e) => setValues({ slug: e.target.value })} />
        </StepperField>
      </>
    ),
    validate: (v) => ({ name: v.name.trim() ? undefined : "Give your workspace a name" }),
  },
  {
    id: "team",
    title: "Team",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <StepperField name="invites" label="Email addresses" optional>
        <StepperTags value={values.invites} onChange={(invites) => setValues({ invites })} />
      </StepperField>
    ),
  },
  {
    id: "plan",
    title: "Plan",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <StepperChoices label="Plan" value={values.plan} options={plans} onChange={(plan) => setValues({ plan })} />
    ),
  },
  {
    id: "review",
    title: "Review",
    render: ({ values, goTo }) => (
      <StepperReview
        onEdit={goTo}
        rows={[
          { label: "Workspace", value: values.name, step: "workspace" },
          { label: "Plan", value: values.plan, step: "plan" },
        ]}
      />
    ),
  },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return (
    <StepperForm<Values>
      steps={steps}
      initialValues={{ name: "", slug: "", invites: [], plan: "pro" }}
      submitLabel="Create workspace"
      onComplete={(values) => api.createWorkspace(values)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `Step<V>[]` |  | { id, title, heading?, description?, render(ctx), validate?(values) } – render gets values, setValues, errors, goTo and next; validate returns messages by field name |
| initialValues | `V` |  | Values shared by all steps, so Back and Edit keep what was entered |
| onComplete | `(values: V) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Runs on the last step; a promise shows the submitting label until it settles, a thrown error is shown next to the button |
| initialStep | `number` | `0` | Index of the first step shown |
| step | `number` |  | Controlled step index; pair with onStepChange |
| onStepChange | `(step: number) => void` |  | Called whenever the step changes |
| submitLabel | `string` | `"Finish"` | Label of the button on the last step |
| submittingLabel | `string` | `"Creating…"` | Label while onComplete runs |
| success | `(values: V, reset: () => void) => ReactNode` |  | Replaces the steps once done – StepperSuccess gives the popping green check, a heading and a line |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| StepperField | `{ name, label, hint?, optional?, children }` |  | Label, control and inline message for the field name in validate; the control shakes when Continue finds a problem |

### When to use

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { TagInput } from "@/components/ui/tag-input-clean";

const EMAIL = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$/;

export function InviteField() {

  return (
    <TagInput

      value={emails}
      onChange={setEmails}
      placeholder="name@company.com"
      avatar
      splitOnSpace
      max={10}
      normalize={(t) => t.trim().toLowerCase()}
      validate={(t) => (EMAIL.test(t) ? true : `“${t}” doesn't look like an email address.`)}
      name="emails"

  );

```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string[]` |  | The chips – makes it controlled |

| onChange | `(tags: string[]) => void` |  | Called when a chip is added or removed |

| normalize | `(tag: string) => string` | `trim` | Cleans a value first, e.g. lowercases an email |

| avatar | `boolean` | `false` | A small circle with the first letter on every chip, for people |

| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – a message takes its place while there is one |

| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Add…"` | Shown while there are no chips; "Add more…" after the first |

# Text Area, clean style (Free)

The multi-line twin of the Text Field – grows with the text, a character count, a button for more room and ⌘ Enter to send

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/text-area
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/text-area-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/text-area-clean`

### When to use

- Anything longer than a line in a form: descriptions, notes, bios, feedback, instructions or context for an assistant
- Settings and creation dialogs next to Text Fields – same label, hint, error and focus, so a form reads as one

### When not to use

- A single line – names, emails, URLs – use the Text Field
- Writing to an assistant or a person with send, attachments or a model picker – use the Chat Composer

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { TextArea } from "@/components/ui/text-area-clean";

export function CompanyContext({ onSave }: { onSave: (text: string) => void }) {
  const [text, setText] = useState("");

  return (
    <TextArea
      label="Company context"
      hint="Added to every chat in this workspace."
      value={text}
      onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)}
      maxLength={2000}
      counter
      minRows={3}
      maxRows={8}
      expandable
      onSubmitShortcut={onSave}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown above the field; clicking it focuses the textarea |
| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – the error takes its place while there is one |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks the field invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message where the hint was |
| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| counter | `boolean` | `false` | Shows "120/2,000" under the field, red once a prefilled value is over the limit; needs maxLength |
| minRows | `number` | `3` | Height when empty, in lines |
| maxRows | `number` | `10` | It grows with the text up to this many lines, then scrolls inside |
| expandable | `boolean` | `false` | A small button in the top corner that gives the field more room – and back |
| expandedRows | `number` | `16` | Lines while expanded |
| expanded | `boolean` |  | Controls the expanded state from outside; pair with onExpandedChange |
| onExpandedChange | `(expanded: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the button gives more or less room |
| onSubmitShortcut | `(value: string) => void` |  | ⌘/Ctrl+Enter – save or send without reaching for the mouse; Enter alone still makes a new line |
| inputClassName | `string` |  | Extra class on the textarea itself, e.g. a monospace font for prompts |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper |
| ...textarea props | `ComponentProps<"textarea">` |  | Everything else – value, defaultValue, onChange, name, placeholder, required, disabled, readOnly, maxLength, ref – goes to the textarea |

### Keyboard

- Enter: A new line
- ⌘ / Enter: Calls onSubmitShortcut (Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux)
- Tab: Moves on to the More room button, then out of the field

### Accessibility

- A real <textarea> with a <label> tied to it – works with forms, autofill and screen readers
- The hint, the error and the count are linked with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid and is announced politely
- The More room button reports its state with aria-pressed and points at the field with aria-controls; the shortcut is listed in aria-keyshortcuts
- Without a label, a text placeholder becomes the field's accessible name – better still, pass aria-label

### Motion

- No focus ring: the hairline edge firms up on hover and a little more on focus
- The field grows line by line as you type, without animation – it never lags behind the caret
- More room glides the height open and closed; the corner icon swaps out of a short blur
- An error nudges the field once and its message slides in where the hint was – nothing below moves
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; it measures again when its width changes, because the text wraps differently
- On touch screens it uses 16px text, so iOS doesn't zoom in on focus, and the corner button grows to 32px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Thinking Loader, clean style (Free)

A small working pill for AI replies – an eight-ray spinner and a shimmering label that rolls through phases and settles on a check

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/thinking-loader
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/thinking-loader-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/thinking-loader-clean`

### When to use

- The wait between sending a prompt and the first streamed token – one line that says what the model is doing
- Agent and pipeline steps with real labels: searching, reading, running a tool, writing
- Inline in a chat bubble or next to a button where a full panel would be too much

### When not to use

- When people should see the sources and every step – use Thinking State
- Page or data loading with no phases – a skeleton or a plain spinner reads calmer
- Waits under half a second – the loader would only flash

### Usage

```tsx
import { ThinkingLoader } from "@/components/ui/thinking-loader-clean";

export function AssistantPending({ streaming }: { streaming: boolean }) {
  return (
    <ThinkingLoader
      phases={["Thinking", "Searching the web", "Reading sources", "Writing response"]}
      interval={2200}
      done={streaming}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| phases | `string[]` | `["Thinking", "Searching the web", "Reading sources", "Writing response"]` | Labels to walk through, one after another |
| interval | `number` | `2200` | Time per phase in ms when the phase isn't controlled |
| phase | `number` |  | Controlled index into phases – the timer stops and the loader shows this phase |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Start over after the last phase instead of holding it |
| done | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the spinner into a check and the label into doneLabel; setting it back to false starts over |
| doneLabel | `string \| ((seconds: number) => string)` | `(s) => `Thought for ${s}s`` | Label once done – a function gets the seconds since the loader started |
| size | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | 26 or 32px tall – 12 or 13px label |
| variant | `"pill" \| "plain"` | `"pill"` | A white chip with hairline shadows, or just the spinner and the label |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- role="status" with aria-live="polite": screen readers hear each new phase and the done label once
- The spinner, the check and the label rolling out are aria-hidden; the shimmer copy has empty alt text, so labels are read once

### Motion

- Eight thin accent-blue rays fade one after another, so the spinner turns without rotating
- A darker band sweeps through the gray label while it works
- On a new phase the old label rolls up and blurs out, the new one rolls in, and the chip glides to its new width
- Done: the spinner shrinks away while the check grows in and draws itself; the label stops shimmering
- With prefers-reduced-motion the labels switch instantly and the spinner and shimmer stand still

### Responsive

- Sizes to its label; long phases stay on one line, so keep them short (two to four words)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Map phases to real events (tool calls, retrieval, first token) with the phase prop when you have them; the timer is a fallback
- Set done when the first token arrives and swap the loader for the streamed message shortly after

### Requirements

- React 19

# Time Picker, clean style (Free)

A time of day you type or pick – a list every few minutes with a gliding highlight, 12 or 24 hours by locale, min and max, and typing that understands 930, 9:30 pm or 21.30

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/time-picker
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/time-picker-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/time-picker-clean`

### When to use

- A time of day in a form: when an agent runs, when the daily digest is sent, quiet hours, a reminder
- Next to a Date Picker for a date and a time, or on its own in a settings row – same height, edge, label, hint and error as the Text Field

### When not to use

- A day – use the Date Picker; a period of days – use the Date Range Picker
- A duration ("for 45 minutes") or a rhythm ("every 2 hours") – a number field or a Select reads better
- Three or four fixed slots people choose between – use the Segmented Control or a Select

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { TimePicker } from "@/components/ui/time-picker-clean";

export function RunAt() {
  const [time, setTime] = useState<string | null>("09:30");
  return (
    <TimePicker
      label="Run at"
      value={time}
      onChange={setTime}
      step={15}
      hint="Every weekday, in your time zone."
      name="runAt"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string \| null` |  | The chosen time as "HH:mm" (24 h, like a native time input) – makes it controlled; null shows the placeholder |
| defaultValue | `string \| null` | `null` | Starting time when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value: string \| null) => void` |  | Called with "HH:mm" when a time is picked or typed, or null when the field is cleared |
| step | `number` | `15` | Minutes between the times in the list, counted from min – typing can still set any minute |
| min | `string` |  | The earliest time, "HH:mm" – the list starts here, earlier typed times are put back |
| max | `string` |  | The latest time, "HH:mm" – ignored when it lies before min |
| hourCycle | `12 \| 24` |  | 9:30 PM or 21:30 – by default the locale's |
| locale | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for how times are written – the browser's by default; its own AM / PM words can be typed too |
| placeholder | `string` |  | Shown in gray while nothing is chosen – by default 9:00 in the right format, as an example |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Shown above the field and used as the list's name |
| hint | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the field – the error takes its place while there is one |
| error | `ReactNode` |  | Marks the field invalid (red edge, aria-invalid) and shows the message where the hint was |
| optional | `boolean` | `false` | Adds "Optional" next to the label |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 28 · 32 · 36px high, like the Text Field; taller on touch screens |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the field and ignores input |
| name | `string` |  | Sends "HH:mm" with a form, through a hidden input |
| required | `boolean` |  | Sets aria-required – check it on submit like any other field |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper, e.g. a fixed width in a settings row |
| ref | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  | The text input – focus it after a validation error |

### Keyboard

- ↓ / ↑: Open the list at the chosen time (or the next one from now); inside it, move between times
- PageDown / PageUp: In the open list: an hour later or earlier
- 0–9 / A–Z: Type a time – "9", "930", "9:30 pm", "21.30"; the list jumps to it as you type
- Enter: Pick the highlighted time, or keep what was typed
- Esc: Close the list; pressed again, undo what was typed
- Tab: Keep what was typed and move on

### Accessibility

- The editable combobox pattern: a text input with role="combobox" and aria-autocomplete="list" that controls a listbox; the focus stays in the input while aria-activedescendant follows the highlight
- Typed text that isn't a time, or lies outside min / max, is put back to the last good time when the field is left – nothing half-typed is ever sent
- The label names both the field and the list; hint and error are linked with aria-describedby, an error sets aria-invalid
- No focus ring on the text field – its edge firms up instead; the list button is reached by pointer only, the keys open the list from the input

### Motion

- The list fades in out of a small lift from the field's edge – downward, or upward when it opens above – centred on the chosen time
- One soft highlight glides between the rows as the pointer, the keys or the typing move; the check on the chosen time draws itself
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container – about 120px is enough; the list is as wide as the field
- The list opens where there is room and stays inside the window; it lives in the top layer, so a card's overflow never cuts it
- Touch screens get 40px rows and 16px text (no zoom on iOS); dark mode built in via .dark or data-theme="dark" on an ancestor

### Requirements

- React 19

# Toaster, clean style (Pro)

Calm toasts from anywhere – a stack that fans out on hover, promise toasts that morph from spinner to check, swipe to dismiss

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/toaster
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/toaster-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/toaster-clean`

### When to use

- Short confirmations after an action – saved, copied, sent, moved to trash (with Undo)
- Background work people started and want to hear back from – uploads, syncs, exports (toast.promise)
- Errors that don't block the page, e.g. a sync that failed and can be retried later

### When not to use

- Errors in a form – show them next to the field
- Anything people must read or decide on – use a dialog or an inline banner
- Long-running progress with details – a progress panel or tracker fits better

### Usage

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from "@/components/ui/toaster-clean";

// Once, near the root of the app
export function App() {
  return (
    <>
      <Routes />
      <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
    </>
  );
}

// Anywhere – no hook or context needed
function save() {
  toast.success("Draft saved", { description: "Q3 Board Report · all changes kept" });
}

function remove(file: File) {
  trash(file.id);
  toast("File moved to trash", {
    description: file.name,
    action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => restore(file.id) },
  });
}

function upload(file: File) {
  toast.promise(api.upload(file), {
    loading: { title: "Uploading report…", description: file.name },
    success: (res) => ({ title: "Report uploaded", description: `Shared with ${res.people} people` }),
    error: (err) => ({ title: "Upload failed", description: String(err) }),
  });
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| position | `"top-left" \| "top-center" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right"` | `"bottom-right"` | Corner or edge the stack sits in; new toasts come in from that edge |
| inline | `boolean` | `false` | Positions the stack inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the viewport |
| id | `string` |  | Only shows toasts sent with { toaster: id } – for a second, separate stack |
| duration | `number` | `4000` | Default time on screen in ms; each toast can override it, Infinity keeps it open |
| visibleToasts | `number` | `3` | Toasts visible at once; older ones wait (with a paused timer) until there's room |
| expand | `boolean` | `false` | Always shows the stack fanned out instead of on hover and focus |
| offset | `number` | `24 (20 inline)` | Distance from the edges in px; phones always use 12px gutters |
| gap | `number` | `10` | Space between toasts when fanned out, in px |
| hotkey | `string \| null` | `"F8"` | Key (KeyboardEvent.key or .code) that moves focus to the newest toast |
| hairline | `boolean` | `true` | A 1px line along the bottom that runs down with the timer and stops when it pauses |
| closeButton | `boolean` | `true` | Small close button on hover and focus – always visible on touch screens |
| label | `string` | `"Notifications"` | Name of the region for screen readers (the hotkey is added) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the region |
| toast(title, options?) | `(ReactNode, ToastOptions) => ToastId` |  | Shows a plain toast; also toast.success, toast.error, toast.info and toast.loading. Returns the id |
| toast.promise(promise, messages, options?) | `<T>(Promise<T> \| () => Promise<T>, { loading, success, error }) => Promise<T>` |  | A loading toast that turns into success or error; each message is a title, { title, description } or a function of the result |
| toast.dismiss(id?) | `(ToastId?) => void` |  | Closes one toast, or all of them without an id |
| ToastOptions | `{ id?, description?, action?: { label, onClick }, duration?, icon?, toaster?, onDismiss? }` |  | Pass an existing id to update that toast in place (the timer restarts, the text crossfades). action.onClick closes the toast unless it calls event.preventDefault() |

### Keyboard

- F8: Moves focus to the newest toast and fans the stack out
- Tab: Goes from toast to toast, through their action and close buttons
- Esc: Closes the focused toast (or the newest) and moves focus to the next one; focus returns where it was after the last

### Accessibility

- The stack is a labelled region ("Notifications (F8)"); every toast is focusable
- New and updated toasts are read out in a polite status region – errors in an alert region, so they come first
- The timer pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is in the stack and while the tab is hidden, so nothing vanishes mid-read
- Swiping is never the only way out: there's Esc and a named close button
- Icons are decorative; color is limited to the status icons (green, red, blue for info), the text says what happened

### Motion

- New toasts lift in from the edge; the ones behind move back, shrink a little and peek out
- Hover or focus fans the stack out into a list – every toast is measured, so positions and heights glide
- Promise toasts: the spinning arc closes into a ring while a check or cross draws in; the text crossfades and the card resizes
- Closed toasts fade and sink a few pixels while the rest of the stack moves up; swiped toasts fly out in the swipe direction, short swipes rubber-band back
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly – only the spinner keeps turning

### Responsive

- 356px wide on larger screens; under 600px it spans the width with 12px gutters (and respects the home indicator)
- Touch: tap the stack to fan it out, swipe sideways or down to dismiss; close and action buttons get bigger hit areas
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Render <Toaster /> once; call toast() from event handlers or effects, not during render
- Use toast.promise for async work instead of separate loading and success toasts
- Keep titles to a few words and put details in description

### Requirements

- React 19

- F8: Moves focus to the newest toast and fans the stack out
- Tab: Goes from toast to toast, through their action and close buttons
- Esc: Closes the focused toast (or the newest) and moves focus to the next one; focus returns where it was after the last

- The stack is a labelled region ("Notifications (F8)"); every toast is focusable
- New and updated toasts are read out in a polite status region – errors in an alert region, so they come first
- The timer pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is in the stack and while the tab is hidden, so nothing vanishes mid-read
- Swiping is never the only way out: there's Esc and a named close button
- Icons are decorative; color is limited to the success and error icons, the text says what happened

### Motion

- New toasts lift in from the edge; the ones behind move back, shrink a little and peek out
- Hover or focus fans the stack out into a list – every toast is measured, so positions and heights glide
- Promise toasts: the spinning arc closes into a ring while a check or cross draws in; the text crossfades and the card resizes
- Closed toasts fade and sink a few pixels while the rest of the stack moves up; swiped toasts fly out in the swipe direction, short swipes rubber-band back
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly – only the spinner keeps turning

### Responsive

- 356px wide on larger screens; under 600px it spans the width with 12px gutters (and respects the home indicator)
- Touch: tap the stack to fan it out, swipe sideways or down to dismiss; close and action buttons get bigger hit areas
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Render <Toaster /> once; call toast() from event handlers or effects, not during render
- Use toast.promise for async work instead of separate loading and success toasts
- Keep titles to a few words and put details in description

### Requirements

- React 19

# Toggle Group, clean style (Free)

A row of toggle buttons – several on at once or one that can be cleared, labels or icons, a tray or separate chips, one tab stop with arrow keys

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/toggle-group
- Section: Components · Buttons
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/toggle-group-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/toggle-group-clean`

### When to use

- Filters where several can be on at once: Running, Needs you, Failed – type="multiple"
- A formatting or view toolbar: bold, italic, code; visible columns; layers on a map
- One optional choice that can also be none, like Group by Agent, Model or Day – type="single", pressing it again clears it

### When not to use

- Exactly one of a few views must always be picked (List / Board) – use the Segmented Control
- A single on or off setting – use the Switch, or an Icon Button with pressed for one tool
- Many options or long labels – use the Filter Menu or the Select
- Choices saved later with a form – use Checkboxes

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { ToggleGroup } from "@/components/ui/toggle-group-clean";

export function RunFilters() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState(["running", "needs-you"]);

  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      aria-label="Show runs"
      value={status}
      onChange={setStatus}
      items={[
        { value: "running", label: "Running" },
        { value: "needs-you", label: "Needs you" },
        { value: "done", label: "Done" },
        { value: "failed", label: "Failed" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `ToggleGroupItem[]` |  | { value, label?, icon?, ariaLabel?, disabled? } – give icon-only items an ariaLabel, it's also their tooltip |
| type | `"multiple" \| "single"` | `"multiple"` | multiple: any number can be on, the value is a list · single: at most one, pressing it again turns it off |
| value | `string[] \| string \| null` |  | Controlled value – a list with type="multiple", one value or null with type="single" |
| defaultValue | `string[] \| string \| null` |  | Starting value when uncontrolled – nothing on by default |
| onChange | `(value: string[]) => void \| (value: string \| null) => void` |  | Called with the new value; a list keeps the items' order, null when the single item was turned off |
| variant | `"buttons" \| "tray"` | `"buttons"` | Separate quiet chips with a hairline – the pressed ones filled light gray – that wrap onto a new line, or a compact light-gray track with pressed items raised in white |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 24, 28 or 32px tall (36px+ on touch screens); md is 13px text with 4px 10px padding |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Disables every item |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Names the group – or use aria-labelledby |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focuses the group once – the item last used, or the first one that's on
- ← / →: Moves between the items, wrapping around (↑ ↓ too); turned around in right-to-left pages
- Home / End: Moves to the first or last item
- Space / Enter: Turns the focused item on or off

### Accessibility

- A role="group" of real buttons with aria-pressed – screen readers say pressed or not pressed for each
- Arrow keys only move the focus; nothing changes until Space or Enter, so moving through a filter row is safe
- One tab stop for the whole group (roving tabindex); disabled items are skipped
- Icon-only items need ariaLabel – it names them and shows as the tooltip
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never after a click

### Motion

- A pressed item's fill grows in from its middle and fades; it dips slightly while held down
- With prefers-reduced-motion it changes instantly and doesn't dip

### Responsive

- buttons wrap onto a new line when they don't fit; the tray scrolls sideways instead
- Long labels end in … rather than pushing past the container
- Touch screens get items at least 36px tall
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Tool Access Map, clean style (Pro)

An agent in the middle with every tool it can reach around it – which ones it used, which failed and which it calls right now; open a tool for its calls and replay one on its own

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/tool-access-map
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tool-access-map-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/tool-access-map-clean`

### When to use

- Seeing at a glance which tools of the run an agent can reach, which it actually used – and which one it calls right now
- Debugging a tool call: read its input and output, then replay it on its own, with the same input or a changed one
- Runs with several agents, each with its own set of tools – switch between them with the tabs on top

### When not to use

- Who started whom – use Agent Tree
- Agents calling each other and their tools as one network – use Agent Graph
- A single call with its arguments and result in a chat – use Tool Call Card

### Usage

```tsx
import { ToolAccessMap, type MapAgent } from "@/components/ui/tool-access-map-clean";

const agents: MapAgent[] = [
  {
    id: "coder",
    name: "Coder",
    model: "GPT-6 Sol",
    status: "running",
    task: "Build the pricing page",
    tools: [
      { id: "github", name: "GitHub", calls: [{ id: "c1", status: "done", input: { branch: "pricing-page" }, output: { ref: "refs/heads/pricing-page" }, duration: 450 }] },
      { id: "terminal", name: "Terminal", calls: [{ id: "c2", status: "running", input: { cmd: "npm test" } }] },
      // A tool it can use but hasn't yet
      { id: "stripe", name: "Stripe" },
    ],
  },
];

// Every tool of the run – the ones an agent can't reach are grayed out on its map, with a dashed line
const tools = [
  { id: "github", name: "GitHub" },
  { id: "terminal", name: "Terminal" },
  { id: "stripe", name: "Stripe" },
  { id: "slack", name: "Slack" },
];

export function Tools() {
  return <ToolAccessMap agents={agents} tools={tools} onReplay={(call, input, tool) => agent.call(tool.id, input)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `MapAgent[]` |  | { id, name, model?, avatar?, status, task?, tools } – pass them again whenever a call starts or comes back |
| tools | `AccessTool[]` | `the tools of all agents together` | Every tool of the run, { id, name, icon?, description? }, in the order they're laid out – the first half on the left |
| agent.tools | `AgentTool[]` |  | Per agent: { id, calls? } for every tool it has access to – name and icon come from tools; one without calls shows as not used yet, one that isn't listed as no access |
| calls | `ToolCall[]` |  | Per tool, oldest first: { id, status, input, output?, error?, at?, duration?, replay? } – a running call turns its line blue |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per agent – shown as a badge on its card; waiting reads "Needs you" |
| agent | `string` |  | Controlled id of the agent on the map |
| defaultAgent | `string` | `the first agent` | The agent on the map at first, uncontrolled |
| onAgentChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | A tab was picked |
| onReplay | `(call, input, tool, agent) => void` |  | Replay was pressed – input is the call's own, or the one it was changed to (parsed from JSON when the original was an object) |
| formatTime | `(ms: number) => string` | `0:42` | Formats when a call was made |
| title | `string` | `"Tool access"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: Moves between the agent tabs
- Tab: Moves through the tools; Enter opens the calls of one
- ↑ / ↓: Moves through the calls of a tool and shows each – the list is one tab stop
- Esc: Back from the calls to the map – focus returns to the tool
- ⌘ / Enter: Runs the changed input

### Accessibility

- The agents are tabs; the map is their tab panel and says whose tools it shows
- Every tool it can reach is a button that says its name, how it stands and how many calls it got; one without access says so and can't be opened
- Opening a tool moves focus into its calls; going back returns it to the tool, and the map underneath is inert meanwhile
- Status is never color alone: running and failed are badges with words, unused tools say "Not used yet", the others "No access"
- The counts in the bar on top are announced politely when they change; each keeps its width, and the blue running tag sits to their left so nothing shifts

### Motion

- Every tool the agent can use has a blue line, the rest a gray dashed one; while a tool is being called, a deeper blue shimmer keeps running down its line, from the agent to the tool
- Switching agents keeps the tools and their gray lines in place: the blue runs in again over the lines from the agent, the card's content moves in from below, and tools gray out or come back softly
- The calls view slides in over the map as a white card, and the map grows to fit it
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears and the shimmer stays off

### Responsive

- Every tool card has a fixed size, so nothing moves when a call starts, finishes or fails
- The map lays itself out from its own width; below 540px the tools sit in a grid under the agent and the lines give way
- In the calls view, narrow puts the list above the call
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every tool of the run in tools, and per agent only the ones it may use – the rest gray out with a dashed line
- Keep calls oldest first and add new ones at the end; mark a replayed call with replay: true
- Up to ten tools fit the map comfortably; more still work but make it tall
- Line colors are solid, so lines that run together keep their color: --ui-tamc-used for access, --ui-tamc-off without, --ui-tamc-glint for the shimmer; how far a tool without access fades is --ui-tamc-dim

### Requirements

- React 19

# Tool Call Card, clean style (Free)

An agent's tool call in one line – live timer, status and summary, folds open to highlighted arguments and result with copy, retry on errors and a group that sums them up

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/tool-call-card
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tool-call-card-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/tool-call-card-clean`

### When to use

- Tool and function calls in an agent chat or run log – what was called, with what, and what came back
- Agents that call several tools per turn – wrap them in ToolCallGroup so the answer isn't buried under cards
- Developer-facing views where people need to copy the exact arguments or result to debug

### When not to use

- Plain reasoning with no tool calls – use Thinking State or Thinking Loader
- End users who never care about JSON – show a one-line status instead and keep the details in a log
- Huge payloads (megabytes of JSON) – trim or paginate them first; the card renders the whole string

### Usage

```tsx
import { ToolCallCard, ToolCallGroup } from "@/components/ui/tool-call-card-clean";

export function ToolCalls({ calls }: { calls: ToolCall[] }) {
  return (
    <ToolCallGroup>
```

# Tooltip, clean style (Free)

A small dark label for one control – shows on hover after a short wait and at once under keyboard focus, neighbours follow instantly, an optional shortcut inside, flips to stay on screen

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/tooltip
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tooltip-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/tooltip-clean`

### When to use

- The name of an icon-only control, with its shortcut: search ⌘K, filter, pin, share
- The full text of a label that is cut off with an ellipsis – a run name, a file name, a long branch
- One short extra line about a control that already has a visible or accessible name

### When not to use

- Anything you can click, select or copy inside it – use the Popover, which takes the focus and stays open
- A list of actions – use the Dropdown Menu
- Information someone needs to finish a task, or the only label of a control: touch screens never show tooltips – put it on the page, or in the control's aria-label
- A status after an action (Copied, Saved) that should be read out – use the Toaster

### Usage

```tsx
import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons";
import { Tooltip } from "@/components/ui/tooltip-clean";
import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/icon-button-clean";

export function SearchTool({ onSearch }: { onSearch: () => void }) {
  return (
    // One child element: the Tooltip clones it and adds its handlers, ref and aria-describedby
    <Tooltip content="Search runs" shortcut="⌘K" side="bottom">
      {/* title="" leaves out the Icon Button's own browser tooltip */}
      <IconButton variant="secondary" icon={Search01Icon} label="Search runs" title="" onClick={onSearch} />
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| content | `ReactNode` |  | The label – a few words, wraps at 240px. Text only: never a link or button inside. Empty or null renders the child alone |
| shortcut | `string` |  | A keyboard shortcut after the label in a quieter tone, e.g. "⌘K" or "⇧⌘S" |
| children | `ReactElement` |  | Exactly one element that takes a ref and focus – a button, a link, an Icon Button. Its own handlers and ref keep working; they run first, and preventDefault in one stops the tooltip's |
| side | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"top"` | Where it shows; flips to the other side when that has more room, and goes above or under when there is no room beside it |
| align | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | Which edges line up; above and under, start is the left (the right in RTL). Pushed inside the window when it would stick out |
| offset | `number` | `6` | Gap to the trigger in px |
| delay | `number` | `500` | How long the pointer rests on the trigger before it shows, in ms. Keyboard focus, and a neighbour within 300ms of the last one, show it at once |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Never shows it – e.g. when the label is not cut off |
| open | `boolean` |  | Controls it from outside, with onOpenChange; leave it out and it opens on its own |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever it wants to open or close |
| className | `string` |  | A class for the label |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focusing the trigger by keyboard shows it at once; moving on hides it
- Esc: Hides it, before anything around it (a dialog, a panel) reacts; it stays hidden until the focus or pointer leaves
- Enter / Space: Clicking the trigger hides it

### Accessibility

- role="tooltip"; while it shows, the trigger points to it with aria-describedby (added to any it already has) – a description, never the name
- The name stays on the trigger: an icon-only button needs its own aria-label (the Icon Button's label). When the tooltip only repeats that name, screen readers just get the shortcut from it, so nothing is read twice
- Opens under keyboard focus, never after a click; Escape hides it without moving the focus (WCAG 1.4.13)
- The pointer can move from the trigger onto the label without it closing, so it can be read under a screen magnifier
- Touch has no hover, so a tap never opens it – never put information only in a tooltip
- Only one shows at a time on the page

### Motion

- Fades in and drifts 2px from the trigger's side; it disappears at once
- Once one is open, moving to a neighbour (within 300ms) shows the next one instantly and without the fade
- With prefers-reduced-motion it appears without the drift

### Responsive

- It lives in the top layer (popover), so a card's overflow or z-index never cuts it; it follows its trigger on scroll and resize
- Always on screen: it flips sides and is pushed inside the window; long text wraps at 240px (never wider than the window)
- A label in another script reads in its own direction (dir="auto")
- Dark mode built in: a light label on dark pages – switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Trace Waterfall, clean style (Pro)

Where the time and money of an agent run go – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a bar on a live timeline, with tokens and cost per step, the slowest call marked and branches that fold into their parent

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/trace-waterfall
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/trace-waterfall-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/trace-waterfall-clean`

### When to use

- Debugging an agent run: how long each step took, where the time and the money went, which call is slow
- A run view next to a chat or a log – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a bar on one timeline
- Live runs, where you want to watch spans start, grow and finish while the agent works

### When not to use

- Who started whom, at a glance – use Agent Tree
- Several agents side by side over the last half hour – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's plan as a checklist – use Agent Plan

### Usage

```tsx
import { TraceWaterfall, type TraceSpan } from "@/components/ui/trace-waterfall-clean";

const run: TraceSpan = {
  id: "run", name: "Orchestrator", kind: "agent", status: "running", start: 0,
  input: "Launch the new pricing page",
  children: [
    { id: "plan", name: "Plan the launch", kind: "llm", model: "Opus 5.5", detail: "Opus 5.5", status: "done",
      start: 900, end: 7800, tokensIn: 3240, tokensOut: 880, cost: 0.115 },
    { id: "search", name: "web_search", kind: "tool", detail: "Linear pricing", status: "running", start: 8100 },
  ],
};

export function Run({ startedAt }: { startedAt: number }) {
  // Times are ms from the start of the run; with startedAt the component keeps its own clock while it runs
  return <TraceWaterfall root={run} startedAt={startedAt} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| root | `TraceSpan` |  | { id, name, kind, status, start, end?, detail?, icon?, model?, tokensIn?, tokensOut?, cost?, input?, output?, error?, children? } – the whole run as a tree, rebuilt as it goes on |
| kind | `"agent" \| "subagent" \| "llm" \| "tool"` |  | Per span – picks the bar's tint: agents slate, LLM calls violet, tool calls teal; failed spans are red |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per span – a running span has no end yet and grows into "now" |
| start / end | `number` |  | Per span, in ms from the start of the run; leave end out while it runs |
| detail | `string` |  | Per span – a few muted words after the name, e.g. the model or the query |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Per span – a small mark, e.g. the model maker's or the tool's logo; defaults to a swatch in the kind's color |
| cost / tokensIn / tokensOut | `number` |  | Per span, its own – agents add up their children, so don't pre-sum |
| input / output / error | `string` |  | Per span – short previews shown in the details window |
| now | `number` |  | The clock in ms from the start of the run – e.g. a faster one for a demo or a replay |
| startedAt | `number` |  | When the run started (epoch ms) – without now, the component ticks its own clock from here while a span runs |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of folded spans, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: string[]) => void` |  | A span was folded or opened |
| openId / defaultOpenId | `string \| null` | `null` | The span whose details are open, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null, span?: TraceSpan) => void` |  | Details opened (with the span) or closed |
| markSlowest | `boolean` | `true` | Marks the slowest finished LLM or tool call with a small "Slowest" tag |
| minRange | `number` | `10000` | The shortest time the axis shows, in ms – it grows in round steps as the run gets longer |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.042"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Trace"` | Heading of the bar; next to it the root's input (or name) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the waterfall (one row is in the tab order) and on to the details window
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Moves between the rows; Home and End jump to the first and the last
- ArrowRight: Opens a folded span, or moves to its first child
- ArrowLeft: Folds an open span, or moves to its parent
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the details of the focused span
- Esc: Closes the details

### Accessibility

- The rows are a tree: every span is a treeitem with its level, labelled with name, kind, status, duration and cost; aria-expanded on spans with children
- Roving focus – only one row is in the tab order, so the waterfall is a single stop
- The details window is a dialog labelled with the span's name, with a close button; Esc closes it and returns focus to the row
- The run's state in the bar (Live, Done, Failed) is announced politely when it changes
- Ticks, grid lines and the "now" line are decoration and hidden from assistive tech

### Motion

- New spans slide in as rows and their bars grow from their start point
- A running span grows live, with a sheen and a soft glow at its leading edge; a "now" line moves across
- When the run outgrows the axis, the range glides to the next round value – ticks fade in and out where they are, bars rescale with it, nothing jumps
- Folding closes the children's rows smoothly and shows their calls as small marks on the parent bar; the chevron turns
- Rows that leave – a new run, removed data – close up a beat after each other, bottom first

# Tree View, clean style (Free)

A nested list of folders and files or any hierarchy – branches that open with a chevron and grow in height, indent guides, one selected row, icons and quiet meta, arrow keys and type-ahead as in the WAI-ARIA tree

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/tree-view
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tree-view-clean.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/tree-view-clean`

### When to use

- Folders and files: an agent's workspace, a repository, a knowledge base, the outputs of a run
- Any hierarchy you browse and pick one item from: projects and their chats, a docs outline, nested categories
- A side panel next to a viewer – the selected row decides what the viewer shows (onSelect)

### When not to use

- Who started whom in an agent run, with status and cost per agent – use the Agent Tree
- Rows with many columns, sorting or several selected at once – use the Data Table
- Where you are in a hierarchy, shown in a header – use the Breadcrumb
- A flat list of choices – use the Select, the Dropdown Menu or the Command Menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { TreeView, type TreeNode } from "@/components/ui/tree-view-clean";

const files: TreeNode[] = [
  {
    id: "prompts",
    label: "prompts",
    icon: <FolderIcon />,
    openIcon: <FolderOpenIcon />,
    children: [
      { id: "prompts/system", label: "system.md", icon: <FileIcon /> },
      { id: "prompts/tools", label: "tools.md", icon: <FileIcon /> },
    ],
  },
  { id: "agent", label: "agent.yaml", icon: <CodeIcon />, meta: "2 KB" },
];

export function Workspace({ onOpen }: { onOpen: (id: string) => void }) {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <TreeView
      aria-label="Workspace"
      items={files}
      defaultExpanded={["prompts"]}
      selected={selected}
      onSelect={(id, node) => {
        setSelected(id);
        if (!node.children) onOpen(id);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `TreeNode[]` |  | { id, label, icon?, openIcon?, meta?, disabled?, children? } – ids must be unique in the whole tree; any children list (even an empty one) makes a branch |
| expanded | `string[]` |  | Controlled: the ids of the open branches |
| defaultExpanded | `string[]` | `[]` | Uncontrolled: the branches open at the start |
| onExpandedChange | `(expanded: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the new list of open ids when a branch opens or closes |
| selected | `string \| null` |  | Controlled: the id of the selected row |
| defaultSelected | `string \| null` | `null` | Uncontrolled: the row selected at the start |
| onSelect | `(id: string, node: TreeNode) => void` |  | A row was picked – a click, Enter or Space; folders too (a click on a folder also opens or closes it, its chevron only opens or closes) |
| guides | `boolean` | `true` | Thin vertical lines under each open branch; the one around the selected row is darker |
| emptyText | `string` | `"Empty"` | Shown inside an open branch without children |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Names the tree – or use aria-labelledby |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root <ul>; give a parent a height and overflow: auto to scroll a long tree |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focuses the tree once – the row last used, else the selected one, else the first
- ↓ / ↑: Next or previous row you can see; disabled rows are skipped
- →: Opens a closed branch; on an open one, goes to its first child (← in right-to-left pages)
- ←: Closes an open branch; otherwise goes to the parent (→ in right-to-left pages)
- Home / End: First or last row you can see
- Enter: Selects the row – on a branch it also opens or closes it, like a click
- Space: Selects the row, nothing else
- *: Opens every branch next to the focused row
- a–z: Jumps to the next row whose name starts with what you type; the same letter again steps on

### Accessibility

- The WAI-ARIA tree pattern: role="tree", each row a treeitem with aria-level, aria-posinset, aria-setsize and aria-expanded on branches, children in a role="group"
- One selected row with aria-selected; disabled rows have aria-disabled and are skipped by the arrow keys
- One tab stop for the whole tree (roving tabindex) – the arrow keys move inside it
- Each row is named by its label only; meta is its description, so a screen reader says "report.md, 12 KB" without the children
- Closed branches are hidden from screen readers and the keyboard; if a branch closes around the focused row, the focus moves up to it
- The ring shows only under keyboard focus (:focus-visible), inside the row, never around the open branch below

### Motion

- A branch grows and shrinks in height (220ms), its chevron turns with it
- With prefers-reduced-motion branches open and close at once

### Responsive

- One line per row: long names end in … with the full name on hover; meta takes at most 45% of the row
- Deep levels indent 16px each, but never past 45% of the width – names stay readable in a narrow panel
- Touch screens get rows at least 36px tall
- Right-to-left: the indent, guides and chevron flip, and ← / → swap
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Trend Chart, clean style (Pro)

The chart on its own for any card or layout – line, area, bars or a sparkline from the same data, with a tooltip, this period against the last, and charts that follow the same day together

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/trend-chart
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/trend-chart-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/trend-chart-clean`

### When to use

- Any chart inside your own card, KPI tile, table row or dashboard layout – it brings no card of its own
- Values over time: a line, an area, bars per day, or a small sparkline next to a number
- This period against the last – mark a series as previous and it is drawn dashed or faint
- A row of charts that should read the same day together – share `index` between them

### When not to use

- More than about six series – the chart and the tooltip get hard to read
- Long time ranges with hundreds of points – use a chart library with zoom and sampling
- Parts of a whole – use Breakdown Chart or Model Usage

### Usage

```tsx
import { TrendChart } from "@/components/ui/trend-chart-clean";

export function Spend() {
  return (
    <TrendChart
      variant="area"
      label="Spend per day"
      labels={["Mar 3", "Mar 4", "Mar 5", "Mar 6"]}
      format={(n) => `$${Math.round(n)}`}
      series={[
        { label: "This week", values: [412, 455, 398, 470] },
        { label: "Last week", values: [356, 380, 371, 390], previous: true },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| labels | `string[]` |  | One label per point; first, middle and last are shown on the axis |
| tooltipLabels | `string[]` |  | Longer labels for the tooltip header, falls back to labels |
| series | `TrendSeries[]` |  | { label, values, color?, previous? } – values line up with labels, null leaves a gap; previous draws it dashed (line) or faint (bar) |
| variant | `"line" \| "area" \| "bar" \| "sparkline"` | `"line"` | How the same data is drawn – a sparkline has no axes and a small tag instead of the tooltip |
| format | `(n: number) => string` | `compact, e.g. 1.2k` | Formats tooltip values – and the axis, unless axisFormat is set |
| axisFormat | `(n: number) => string` |  | Shorter numbers for the axis, e.g. "$1.6T" while the tooltip shows the full amount |
| height | `number` | `152 (sparkline 40)` | Height of the plot in px |
| axis | `boolean \| "x"` | `true (sparkline false)` | Value labels on the left and dates below, only the dates ("x"), or none – without axes a small tag replaces the tooltip |
| tooltip | `boolean` | `true` | The popover or tag with the values – off when the card shows the value itself; the point stays marked |
| zero | `boolean` | `true` | Start the value axis at zero; false zooms in around the values for averages and rates (bars always start at zero) |
| index | `number \| null` |  | The highlighted point, controlled – share it between charts so they move together |
| onIndexChange | `(index: number \| null) => void` |  | Called when the pointer or the keys move to another point, or leave |
| defaultIndex | `number` |  | Point that stays highlighted while nobody hovers |
| label | `string` | `"Chart"` | Name for screen readers |
| emptyText | `string` | `"No data yet"` | Quiet text in the plot when there are no values, or only zeros |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the chart |

```tsx
import { VoiceOrb } from "@/components/ui/voice-orb";
```

- Listening: dots jump outward with the level and take on the accent color; a soft glow follows the loudness
- Thinking: the sphere collapses into a tilted, fast spinning ring with a light running around it

# Workflow Builder (Pro)

Nodes on a canvas joined by curves – drag them in from a palette, set each one up, then run the workflow and watch every step light up

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/workflow-builder
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/workflow-builder.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/workflow-builder`

### When to use

- Automations people build themselves – triggers, AI steps, requests, conditions and actions joined into a flow
- Any graph people arrange by hand and then test, step by step

### When not to use

- A fixed sequence nobody rearranges – use a form or a step list
- Hundreds of nodes – use a list of rules with search

### Usage

```tsx
import { WorkflowBuilderScreen } from "@/components/ui/workflow-builder";

export default function Page() {
  return <WorkflowBuilderScreen workspace="Northwind" project="Customer onboarding" onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Northwind"` | Organisation in the path and the sidebar's workspace |
| project | `string` | `"Customer onboarding"` | Project in the path |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| loading | `boolean` | `false` | A saved workflow is being opened: gray cards where the nodes sit and neutral curves, Run off – the palette, path bar and toolbar stay real |
| empty | `boolean` | `false` | A new workflow: an empty canvas with one centered “Add a trigger” and an Add trigger button; the palette, path bar and toolbar stay real and the run panel shows its own empty states |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| nodes | `{ id; type; title; sub?; x; y; config? }[]` |  | The nodes – `type` is one of the palette's types, x and y in canvas pixels; `config` holds what the settings panel edits (a trigger without `source` shows as not configured) |
| edges | `{ id; from; port: "out" \| "yes" \| "no"; to }[]` |  | The curves between them – `port` is the output they leave from; a branch has Yes and No |
| branch | `string` | `"Main"` | Branch in the path – Main shows as Production |
| comments | `{ id; x; y; text; author? }[]` |  | Comments already on the canvas (posted, shown as pins) |
| stepResults | `Record<nodeId, { ms?; credits?; error? }>` |  | What each node returns in a test run – an error fails that step and stops the run |
| labels | `{ publish?: string }` |  | Labels, e.g. for a translation |
| palette | `{ id; label; items: { type; label; kind; icon; sub; description }[] }[]` |  | The palette's groups – kind is trigger, agent, tool, logic or action |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Path bar → Publish → palette (one stop) → canvas (one stop) → comment pins → toolbar → run panel → settings when open
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: Palette: move between the node types. Canvas: ↓ follows a node's first outgoing edge, ↑ goes back along an incoming one, Home / End jump to the first / last node of the flow
- ← / →: Canvas: the nearest node in the same row (else the previous / next in the flow)
- Alt ← / Alt → / Alt ↑ / Alt ↓: Nudge the focused node by 10px (Alt Shift: 50px)
- Enter: Open the focused node's settings (focus moves into them), or add the focused palette item under the selected node
- A: On a node: open the node picker at its first free output
- E: On a node: focus its first connection – then ← → cycle through that node's connections, ↑ / ↓ go to the node it leaves / enters, Delete removes it, Esc goes back
- Delete: Remove the focused node (⌘Z brings it back) or the focused / selected connection
- Enter / ⇧ Enter: In a comment: post it, or start a new line; on a pin, Enter opens it and the arrow keys move it (Shift: 50px)
- Space: Hold and drag to pan, whatever is under the pointer
- V / C: Select and comment tools – with Comment, a click on the canvas places a comment
- + / - / ⇧1: Zoom in, zoom out, fit to view
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: On the run panel's top edge: resize it (Shift: bigger steps), Home / End for the smallest / largest
- Esc: In this order: a dragged connection, the node picker, an open comment (back to its pin), the settings (back to the node), the palette sheet, the run panel, the comment tool, the selection

### Accessibility

- The canvas is one Tab stop (a roving tabindex): the selected node – or the first in the flow – takes Tab, the arrows move along the edges, so 40 nodes are never 40 stops
- Nodes are labelled buttons that say their kind and state (set up, running, done in a time, failed); the selected one is pressed. Connections are focusable too, named 'Connection from … to …'
- Connections can also be made and removed without the pointer: a node's settings list where each output goes, with Connect to… and a remove button for each
- Menus (path bar, Connect to…, selects) open with Enter, Space or ↓, move with the arrows and Home / End, close with Esc (focus back on their button) or Tab; the node picker closes when the focus leaves it
- Every control shows the accent focus ring for the keyboard only (:focus-visible) – never on a click; a focused connection thickens with an accent halo instead of a box
- On phones the palette and settings sheets keep the focus inside until they close
- A test run is announced politely, once per finished step and at the end (including a failure and its message) – not on every frame of the animation
- A comment's pin is a button that names its author and text; an open, posted comment has × to close and Delete and Resolve buttons, and its head folds it
- Every toolbar button has a label and a tooltip with its shortcut; the run panel's tabs are one tab stop with arrows; its top edge is a separator with its current height
- Long names end in '…' with the full text in a tooltip; file names keep their extension; names in right-to-left scripts read in their own direction; durations roll up (1.42s, 2m 05s, 1h 02m) and figures use thousands separators
- The tints of triggers come with words – Not configured, Active, Paused, Failed

### Motion

- The dot grid pans and zooms with the canvas – its spacing follows the zoom, the dots keep their size
- Opening the run panel keeps the zoom and place – it covers the bottom of the canvas; while the run plays the view glides (never zooms) to keep the running node in sight
- A connection being dragged follows the pointer as a dashed accent curve; inputs that can take it ring in accent and the one it snaps to fills
- A palette item being dragged is the node card itself under the pointer, at the canvas's zoom
- The palette and the settings slide and fade in; the run panel slides up from the bottom and the canvas makes room
- While a test run plays, a gradient runs along each edge in the sender's colour, the next node's input glows as it arrives, a trace runs once round the running card, then its status chip turns into a check with the time
- Steps appear one by one in the run panel
- With prefers-reduced-motion there is no gradient along the edges or trace – the running node gets a steady ring in its kind's colour, curves light without drawing and nothing slides

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- The flow runs from top to bottom and opens at 100% (never below 90% on a desktop canvas); Fit to view never zooms past 100%
- Pan by dragging the background, with Space + drag or two fingers; zoom with the toolbar, ⌘/Ctrl + wheel or a pinch. A plain wheel pans right away when the canvas fills a page that doesn't scroll; in a longer page, once you've clicked into it
- Below 640px the palette becomes a sheet behind Add node, the settings a sheet from the bottom, the path bar moves past the sidebar button and the run panel keeps the figures that matter; touch targets grow to 36px and fields use 16px text
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell (installed with it)

# World Map Continental (Pro)

World map with one highlighted continent and a pastel band along its coastline, switchable between all six

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/world-map
- Section: Illustrations · Maps
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/world-map.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/world-map`

### When to use

- Showing that you serve, operate in or focus on one continent
- Market, coverage or expansion sections on a landing page, where a calm map says more than a list of countries

### When not to use

- Data maps with values per country – this is a decorative illustration, not a chart
- Showing individual countries – each continent is one merged shape without borders, simplified from Natural Earth 1:110m

### Usage

```tsx
import { WorldMap } from "@/components/ui/world-map";

export function MarketSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <WorldMap />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| continent | `"north-america" \| "south-america" \| "europe" \| "africa" \| "asia" \| "oceania"` |  | Highlighted continent (controlled). Pair it with onContinentChange to keep the menu working |
| defaultContinent | `Continent` | `"europe"` | Continent highlighted first when continent is not set |
| onContinentChange | `(continent: Continent) => void` |  | Called when the viewer picks a continent in the menu |
| showSwitcher | `boolean` | `true` | Show the continent menu in the top-left corner |
| label | `string \| ((continent: Continent) => string)` | `"World map with Europe highlighted" …` | Accessible description of the map; by default it follows the current continent |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the menu button: open the continent list. In the list: pick the highlighted continent
- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: On the menu button: open the list. In the list: move through the continents
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last continent
- Escape: Close the list and return focus to the menu button
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- The map is one image whose label names the highlighted continent; the shapes inside are hidden from screen readers
- The menu button reports the current continent and its expanded state; the list is a listbox with options, the selected one marked with aria-selected

### Motion

- A soft pastel band travels along the coastline of the continent's main landmass in a continuous 14-second loop: a blurred glow that only spreads outwards, with three sharp layers on top – the same band as in the DACH Region map
- Switching continents fades the old highlight back into the gray world while the new one settles in from slightly smaller with its shadow; the band starts anew
- The menu morphs open out of its button, and the hover fill glides between rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion the band stays still, continents swap instantly and the menu opens without the morph

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the solid gray world and the lighter highlighted continent read on light and dark surfaces alike
- Keeps a 540 : 242 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The menu scales down with the illustration (to about 60 %); on small sizes the open list may extend below the map
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

# Writing Assistant, clean style (Pro)

AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/writing-assistant
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/writing-assistant-clean.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/writing-assistant-clean`

### When to use

- A small AI helper inside an editor, CRM or sidebar – rewrite, shorten, translate or draft
- Landing pages that should show an assistant you can actually try, including voice input

### When not to use

- Long conversations with files, tools and model settings – use the Chat Composer or the AI Chat / Start screen
- When you can't send voice to the browser's speech service – set speech="simulate" or hide the mic

### Usage

```tsx
import { WritingAssistant } from "@/components/ui/writing-assistant-clean";

export function Helper() {
  return (
    <WritingAssistant
      name="Quill"
      tagline="Your writing companion."
      respond={async (message) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/write", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ message }) });
        return (await res.json()).text;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | `"Quill"` | Assistant name on top |
| tagline | `string` | `"Your writing companion."` | Line under the name |
| greeting | `string` | `"What should we write?"` | Line on the welcome screen |
| suggestions | `string[]` |  | Chips that send themselves as a message |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask anything…"` | Placeholder of the prompt field |
| respond | `(message) => string \| Promise<string>` |  | Your answer for a message; a sample writer is used by default |
| speech | `"auto" \| "simulate"` | `"auto"` | auto uses the browser's speech recognition when available, simulate always plays a sample take |
| dictation | `string` |  | Sentence used for simulated dictation |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Sends what's in the prompt field
- Shift / Enter: Starts a new line – the field grows up to four lines, then scrolls
- Tab: Moves through the suggestions, the field, the mic, Send and New chat

### Accessibility

- The mic is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that says what it does next
- New messages are announced politely; the Writing… line carries a label
- Everything works with the keyboard; dictation is optional

### Motion

- A faint glow in the classic pink-violet-blue drifts behind the welcome line and quiets down once you chat; the welcome view hands over to the chat with a short rise
- While listening, the mic turns into a light blue tile with three calm bars and a soft ring breathing outwards; words appear live in the field
- When you stop speaking, the finished sentence moves into the chat as your message; a shimmering Writing… line holds the place, then the reply streams in word by word
- With prefers-reduced-motion the glow and the shimmer stand still and replies appear at once

### Responsive

- One white card that fills its container up to 380px wide; the prompt, mic and send lie right at the bottom of the card
- Dictation uses the Web Speech API (Chrome, Edge, Safari) with the page language; elsewhere a short simulated take plays
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
