# Theming: the project's brand on affectUI

affectUI items read a small set of shared design tokens before their own
defaults. Set the tokens once in the project's global CSS and every item that
reads them follows, in light and dark. A token that isn't set keeps the
affectUI default, so you can start with one (usually `--aui-primary`).

## The tokens

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--aui-font` | Font family of every component |
| `--aui-font-mono` | Code, keys, IDs and numbers set in mono |
| `--aui-radius` | Controls: fields, buttons, selects – small and large sizes follow it |
| `--aui-radius-sm` | Small parts: chips, tags, keys, menu rows |
| `--aui-radius-lg` | Cards, panels, menus and dialogs |
| `--aui-ink` | Text, labels and titles |
| `--aui-muted` | Hints, icons and second lines |
| `--aui-placeholder` | Placeholders and the faintest text |
| `--aui-surface` | Fields and cards |
| `--aui-subtle` | Gray layers behind cards, hover washes, chip fills |
| `--aui-overlay` | Menus, popovers and dialogs |
| `--aui-border` | Hairline edges at rest |
| `--aui-border-strong` | Edges on hover and focus, unchecked boxes |
| `--aui-primary` | Primary buttons, checked boxes and switches, the send button |
| `--aui-on-primary` | Text and icons on the primary fill |
| `--aui-focus` | Keyboard focus ring – keep it at 3:1 contrast or more |
| `--aui-danger` | Errors, failed runs, destructive actions |
| `--aui-danger-soft` | Background of error badges and notices (rolling out) |
| `--aui-warning` | Needs attention, waiting for you, limits close |
| `--aui-warning-soft` | Background of warning badges and notices (rolling out) |
| `--aui-success` | Done, connected, copied |
| `--aui-success-soft` | Background of success badges and notices (rolling out) |
| `--aui-info` | Running, live, informational |
| `--aui-info-soft` | Background of info badges and notices (rolling out) |
| `--aui-blue` | Palette: info, running – for dots, bars, charts and icons |
| `--aui-green` | Palette: success, done |
| `--aui-amber` | Palette: waiting, queued |
| `--aui-orange` | Palette: warning, needs you |
| `--aui-red` | Palette: danger, failed |
| `--aui-pink` | Palette: category color |
| `--aui-purple` | Palette: category color |
| `--aui-teal` | Palette: category color |
| `--aui-cyan` | Palette: category color |
| `--aui-shadow-card` | Edge and lift of cards and fields |
| `--aui-shadow-popover` | Menus, popovers and dialogs above the page |
| `--aui-ease` | Easing of enter, glide and morph animations |

**Which items read them:** every component, block and screen, in both styles
(classic and clean), light and dark. Each reads a token only where its meaning
fits – a card's shadow, a menu's background, a primary button – and keeps its
own value everywhere else: company logos, illustrations and mock app screens,
lift shadows, inverted tooltips and other special shades stay as they are. The
`-soft` status backgrounds are still rolling out: items tint them from the
palette color today (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--aui-red) 10%, transparent)`).
Check the item's reference file or its source: a component reads the tokens
when its CSS contains `var(--aui-`. Items installed before the tokens existed need a
reinstall to pick them up.

## Two ways in

- **The theme file** (best for a project without a design system yet):
  `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/affectui-theme.json` writes
  `styles/affectui-theme.css` – every token commented out with the clean and
  classic defaults and a dark block. Import it once in the global CSS
  (`@import "../styles/affectui-theme.css";`) and uncomment only what you set.
  Ask before installing, like any affectUI item.
- **A block in the global CSS** (best when the project already has shadcn/ui
  or its own variables): the steps and blocks below.

Tokens marked *rolling out* are defined but not yet read by many items; set them
anyway when the brand needs them – items pick them up as they move over.

## Steps

1. **Find the global CSS** the app already loads: `app/globals.css`,
   `src/index.css`, `src/app.css` or the file `components.json` names under
   `tailwind.css`. Write into that file; never create a second global stylesheet.
2. **Find where the brand lives**, in this order:
   - shadcn/ui variables (`--primary`, `--foreground`, `--border`, `--radius` …)
     in that CSS file → map to them (below), so the palette stays in one place
   - other CSS variables or a Tailwind theme with brand colors → map to those
   - a color, font or radius the user named → write the values directly
   - nothing → ask for the brand color once; set only `--aui-primary` and
     `--aui-focus` from it
3. **Write one `:root` block, and a dark block** under the selector the app uses
   for dark mode (`.dark` for shadcn and `next-themes`, `[data-theme="dark"]`
   otherwise). **Every color token you set on `:root` needs a dark value too** –
   a token on `:root` replaces the items' built-in dark colors, so a dark
   `--aui-ink` set only there leaves dark text on dark fields. The exception:
   tokens that point at variables which switch on their own (shadcn's), and
   `--aui-font` / `--aui-radius`. Put both right after the project's own variables, with a one-line
   comment `/* affectUI design tokens */`. Only set tokens you have a value for.
4. **Check contrast:** `--aui-ink` on `--aui-surface` at least 4.5:1,
   `--aui-focus` against the page at least 3:1. A brand color too light for a
   focus ring: use a darker shade of it.
5. **Report** the block you wrote, which installed items read the tokens, and
   which ones need a reinstall.

## shadcn/ui with Tailwind v4 (OKLCH or hex values)

The variables hold whole colors, so they pass straight through:

```css
/* affectUI design tokens */
:root {
  --aui-font: var(--font-sans);
  --aui-radius: var(--radius);
  --aui-ink: var(--foreground);
  --aui-muted: var(--muted-foreground);
  --aui-placeholder: var(--muted-foreground);
  --aui-surface: var(--background);
  --aui-subtle: var(--muted);
  --aui-overlay: var(--popover);
  --aui-border: var(--border);
  --aui-border-strong: var(--input);
  --aui-primary: var(--primary);
  --aui-on-primary: var(--primary-foreground);
  --aui-focus: var(--ring);
  --aui-danger: var(--destructive);
}
```

shadcn sets its dark values on `.dark`, and these references follow them – no
dark block needed. Drop `--aui-font` when the project has no `--font-sans`.

## shadcn/ui with Tailwind v3 (bare HSL numbers like `222 47% 11%`)

Wrap every color in `hsl()`:

```css
/* affectUI design tokens */
:root {
  --aui-radius: var(--radius);
  --aui-ink: hsl(var(--foreground));
  --aui-muted: hsl(var(--muted-foreground));
  --aui-placeholder: hsl(var(--muted-foreground));
  --aui-surface: hsl(var(--background));
  --aui-subtle: hsl(var(--muted));
  --aui-overlay: hsl(var(--popover));
  --aui-border: hsl(var(--border));
  --aui-border-strong: hsl(var(--input));
  --aui-primary: hsl(var(--primary));
  --aui-on-primary: hsl(var(--primary-foreground));
  --aui-focus: hsl(var(--ring));
  --aui-danger: hsl(var(--destructive));
}
```

Tell the formats apart by reading `--primary`: a value with `oklch(`, `#` or
`rgb(` is v4 style; three bare numbers are v3 style.

## No design system: values from the user

```css
/* affectUI design tokens */
:root {
  --aui-primary: #4f46e5;
  --aui-focus: rgba(79, 70, 229, 0.6);
  --aui-radius: 10px;
}

.dark {
  --aui-primary: #a5b4fc;
  --aui-on-primary: #1e1b4b;
}
```

## Don't

- Don't edit the installed component files to change colors.
- Don't override an item's own `--ui-<prefix>-…` variables for brand colors –
  that is for one-off tweaks of a single item; the brand goes into the tokens.
- Don't wrap items in Tailwind color classes; they don't reach inside.
- Don't set tokens the project has no value for – the defaults are tuned.

---
name: eased
description: Design rules and component patterns for building interfaces with Eased (eased.dev), the motion-first React component library for shadcn. Use when building or changing any UI in a project that has components/eased/ or the Eased tokens, when installing Eased components, or when the user asks for layout, spacing, corner radii, shadows, colour, type, focus states or animation to look and feel polished.
---

# Eased

Eased components ship with their motion, spacing and corners already tuned. This skill holds the rules they were built with, so the screens you compose around them meet the same standard. Each rule has a number you can check.

Read this before you write UI code. For a specific component, read its docs first (the `get_component` MCP tool, or `https://eased.dev/components/<slug>.md`).

## Using Eased components

### Install

Components install with the shadcn CLI. The source lands in your project, so you own it.

```bash
npx shadcn add https://eased.dev/r/button.json https://eased.dev/r/tooltip.json
```

- Requirements: React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 and a `components.json`. If there's no `components.json`, run `npx shadcn init` first.
- Files land in `components/eased/<name>/<name>.tsx`. Import from there: `import { Button } from "@/components/eased/button/button"`.
- Every component brings `eased-tokens` (merged into your global CSS) and `eased-motion` (`components/eased/lib/`) with it. There's no CSS file to import.
- Install `<name>-demo` too when you want a realistic usage example to copy patterns from.
- Install with the CLI; don't copy source by hand. The CLI brings the shared stylesheet and helpers.
- Pro components install from the `@eased-pro` registry with a Pro token: see https://eased.dev/docs/installation#pro-components.
- With the Eased MCP server (`https://eased.dev/api/mcp`), use `search_components`, then `get_component`, then `get_install_command`.

### Tokens

Style with semantic tokens only. Never use a raw colour, a literal radius or an arbitrary pixel value in component code.

| Role | Classes |
|---|---|
| Canvas, surface, well, raised | `bg-bg`, `bg-surface`, `bg-surface-sunken`, `bg-surface-raised` |
| Hover and pressed fills | `bg-surface-hover`, `bg-surface-active` |
| Borders: divider, interactive, input | `border-line-subtle`, `border-line`, `border-line-strong` |
| Text: primary, secondary, muted, disabled | `text-text`, `text-text-secondary`, `text-text-muted`, `text-text-disabled` |
| Brand fill and its text | `bg-brand` + `text-text-on-brand` (`bg-brand-hover`, `bg-brand-active`) |
| Brand tint, text, line | `bg-brand-subtle`, `text-brand-text`, `border-brand-line` |
| States | `bg-{success,warning,danger,info}`, `bg-*-subtle`, `text-*-text`, `text-text-on-*` |
| Radius | `rounded-control-2xs` 4 · `rounded-control-xs` 6 · `rounded-control-sm` 8 · `rounded-control` 10 · `rounded-panel` 16 · `rounded-surface` 24 · `rounded-pill` |
| Shadows | `shadow-resting`, `shadow-raised`, `shadow-floating`, `shadow-overlay`, `shadow-thumb`, `inset-shadow-well`, `inset-shadow-highlight` |
| Control heights | `h-control-xs` 24 · `h-control-sm` 32 · `h-control-md` 36 · `h-control-lg` 40 · `h-control-xl` 48 (also `size-control-*`) |
| UI type (line height and tracking included) | `text-ui-2xs` 11 · `text-ui-xs` 12 · `text-ui-sm` 13 · `text-ui` 14 · `text-ui-md` 16 · `text-ui-lg` 18 |
| Easing | `ease-enter`, `ease-standard`, `ease-exit`, `ease-spring-snappy`, `ease-spring-smooth`, `ease-spring-bouncy` |

Utilities and variants:

- `radius-nested`: a concentric inner radius, read from `--radius-outer` and `--pad` on the parent.
- `focus-ring`: Eased's keyboard focus ring.
- `hit-area`: grows a small target's tap area to 44×44px without changing how it looks.
- `image-ring`: a 1px alpha ring for photos, avatars and logos.
- `fade-x`: scroll-edge fades.
- `squircle`: superellipse corners, for radii of 16px or more.
- `hover-fine:` and `group-hover-fine:`: hover styles on mouse and trackpad only.
- `reduced:`: styles under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Raw variables are prefixed `--eased-`. Light follows `:root`, and dark follows `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` on an ancestor. Re-brand by restating `--eased-brand-1` to `--eased-brand-12`.

Motion presets live in `components/eased/lib/motion.ts`:

- `snappy`, `smooth` and `bouncy` springs
- `ease`, `duration`, `stagger` and `blur`
- `enter`, `fade`, `exit` and `reducedFade` transitions
- the `useSafeReducedMotion()` hook

Press classes live in `components/eased/lib/press.ts`: `press`, `pressIcon` and `pressWide`.

### Composition patterns

- **One implementation per role.** Use the installed Eased Button, Avatar, Spinner, Kbd or Segmented. Don't build a second one beside it.
- **Button variants:**
  - `primary`: the one filled action in a region.
  - `secondary`: the default.
  - `ghost`: toolbars and quiet actions.
  - `danger`: outlined.
  - `danger-solid`: only in the final confirm step.
  - Sizes: `sm`, `md` and `lg`, plus `icon-sm`, `icon` and `icon-lg` for icon-only buttons.
- **Concentric nesting.** Wrap nested layers in `Frame` and `FrameInner` from `concentric-frame`, or set `--radius-outer` and `--pad` on the parent and give the child `radius-nested`.
- **Nesting levels:**
  - Page frames: `rounded-surface`, with `p-5` or `p-6`, and `border border-line-subtle`.
  - Cards inside a frame: `rounded-panel` with `p-4`.
  - Controls inside a card: `rounded-control` or `rounded-control-sm`.
- **Repeating rows.** For people, files and settings, put a grid on the parent: `grid grid-cols-[auto_minmax(0,1fr)_auto]`, or `rowGrid` and `rowGridRow` from `components/eased/lib/layout.ts` (the `eased-layout` item). Trailing controls then share a column.
- **Don't wrap Eased components in extra animation.** Their motion is tuned already, and a second transition fights it.
- **Popover and menu triggers** press by colour and never scale. Eased Button does this when `aria-haspopup` is set.
- **Destructive actions** use Undo Pill (a 5-second undo) or a confirm step. They never act immediately.
- **Missing a component?** Build it from Base UI primitives and Eased tokens, following these rules. Keep it outside `components/eased/`, so updates don't overwrite it.

## Alignment and grouping

1. **One edge, one x.** Everything stacked in a column shares one leading edge, including labels, values, buttons, icons and footers. Draw a vertical line down each column's left edge and down the content's right edge. Nothing may cross either line.
2. **Align variable-width text by its leading edge.** Give role or status labels ("Owner", "Can edit") a fixed-width column or a grid track, or make them same-width controls such as Select or Badge. Ragged right-aligned text is allowed only for numbers, with `tabular-nums`.
3. **Use a grid where rows repeat.** Use shared tracks or `subgrid`, never a per-row `justify-between`.
4. **Optical icon alignment.** When an icon leads a label, the icon's visible edge sits on the content line. Pull a ghost button left by its own padding (`-ml-2` on `px-2`).
5. **Footers share the body's inset.** A footer's first item and last button sit on the same left and right lines as the body content.
6. **Same thing, same place.** A control repeated in every row keeps one width and position. Hover-revealed actions use `invisible`, not `hidden`, so nothing jumps.
7. **Vertical anchors.** Avatars, icons and checkboxes centre on the first line of text, unless every row has the same line count. When text sizes differ side by side, use `items-baseline`.
8. **Balance the panel.** Left and right insets are equal. Top and bottom insets are equal, or the top is slightly larger. The first and last list items add no space beyond the padding.

## Spacing

1. **Use the 4px scale only.** No arbitrary pixel values.
2. **Keep a 1:2 ratio.** The gap between groups is at least twice the gap inside a group:
   - label to field: 4–8px (`gap-1.5` or `gap-2`)
   - field to field: 16–24px (`gap-4`)
   - section to section: 32–48px (`gap-8`)
   - Never use equal gaps between unrelated items.
3. **Gap, padding and edge.** Inside a group, the item gap `a` is at most the group's padding `p`. Unboxed groups sit at least `2a` and at least `p` apart. Boxed groups may sit `a` apart.
4. **Control heights.** Elements in one row share one height. Use a page's primary action at `h-control-lg` with `text-ui`, and buttons in cards and dense UI at `h-control-sm` with `text-ui-sm`.
5. **Horizontal padding.** A control's side padding is 0.4–0.5 × its height, so a 36px control gets 14–16px. Icon-only controls are square.
6. **Icon size follows text.** 12px text takes a 14px icon. 13–14px text takes 16px. 16px text takes 18–20px. Icons are `shrink-0` and sit in an `inline-flex items-center` row.
7. **Icon-to-label gap** is 6–8px (`gap-1.5` or `gap-2`). Use one stroke width per surface: 1.5px beside 400–500 weight text, 2px beside 600.
8. **Hit areas.** The minimum tap area is 44×44px (`hit-area`). The minimum visual target is 24×24px.
9. **One density per block.** Dense blocks use 13–14px text, 36px rows and 12–16px padding. Comfortable blocks use 16px text, 44–48px rows and 24–32px padding. Never mix the two in one block.

## Corners

1. **Concentric radii.** Inner radius = outer radius − padding − border width, never below 0: `max(0px, calc(var(--radius-outer) - var(--pad) - 1px))`. Use `radius-nested`.
2. **Below 2px, change approach.** If the computed inner radius is under 2px, raise the outer radius, or clip the child (`overflow: clip`) instead of rounding it.
3. **Radius by role:**
   - 36–40px controls: `rounded-control`.
   - 28–32px controls: `rounded-control-sm`.
   - Chips of 24px or less: `rounded-control-xs` or `rounded-pill`.
   - Cards, popovers, menus and toasts: `rounded-panel`.
   - Dialogs, sheets and full-bleed media: `rounded-surface`.
4. **Pills.** Use `rounded-pill` for chips, switches and avatars. Never pill a card.
5. **Thumbs.** Thumb height = track height − 2 × track padding. Thumb radius = track radius − track padding.
6. **Floating objects aren't nested.** When the inset on every side is at least 1.25 × the parent's radius, the child keeps its own role radius and gets `shadow-floating`.
7. **Nested images** inherit their radius with `border-radius: inherit`, never a second literal.

## Depth and colour

1. **Resting cards** get `border-line-subtle` and either no shadow or `shadow-resting`. Never pair a strong border with a strong shadow.
2. **Floating layers** (popovers, menus, tooltips, dialogs) get `shadow-floating` or `shadow-overlay`, plus `border-line` and `bg-surface-raised`.
3. **No nested shadows.** A shadowed element never contains another shadowed element. Show at most three surface levels: `bg`, `surface` and `surface-raised`.
4. **Hover is one step.** Hover fills use `bg-surface-hover` and pressed fills use `bg-surface-active`. Hover changes colour or shadow by one step. It never changes size, weight or position.
5. **One brand fill per region.** `bg-brand` marks the primary action, at most once per region.
   - Brand as text or an icon uses `text-brand-text`.
   - Tints (`bg-brand-subtle`) mark state, never decoration.
6. **Status badges** use `bg-*-subtle` with `text-*-text`. Solid state fills appear only on buttons and progress bars.
7. **Text roles:**
   - Headings and labels: `text-text`.
   - Descriptions: `text-text-secondary`.
   - Metadata and placeholders: `text-text-muted`.
   - Disabled: `text-text-disabled`.
8. **Contrast.** Body text meets WCAG 4.5:1 in both themes.
9. **Dark mode** is a token swap. If a component needs more than two `dark:` classes, fix the token instead.

## Type

1. **Default UI size** is `text-ui` (14px). Dense tables may use `text-ui-sm` (13px). Nothing interactive goes below 12px.
2. **Weights.** Body text is 400. Labels, titles and buttons are 500. Use 600 only for headings of 24px or more. Never change weight on hover, focus or selection.
3. **`tabular-nums`** on every number that changes or aligns.
4. **Wrapping.** Headings get `text-balance` and paragraphs get `text-pretty`.
5. **Truncation.**
   - Flex text children get `min-w-0`.
   - Single lines use `truncate`.
   - Multiple lines use `line-clamp-*`.
6. **Hierarchy.** Use at most two text sizes in a card and three in a block.
7. **Punctuation.** Use `…`, not `...`. Loading labels end with `…`.

## States

1. **Focus.** Use `:focus-visible` only, with one ring: 2px, with a 2px gap (`focus-ring`). Text inputs show focus with a soft glow and a firmer border instead. Menu items show focus with a highlight fill. Never `outline-none` without one of these.
2. **Press:**
   - Text buttons scale to 0.97 (`press`).
   - Icon buttons of 48px or less scale to 0.96 (`pressIcon`).
   - Bars and cards wider than 220px scale to 0.985 (`pressWide`).
   - The press goes down in 100ms and releases on the snappy spring.
3. **Hover** applies only under `hover-fine:`. Touch gets an `:active` colour.
4. **Disabled.**
   - Filled buttons use `opacity-50`.
   - Outlined buttons keep their shape and use `text-text-disabled`.
   - Always `cursor-not-allowed`, and explain why inline.
5. **Loading.** Keep the width, overlay a spinner on a transparent label and set `aria-busy="true"`.
6. **Forms.** Errors show inline beside the field. On submit, the first invalid field gets focus.
7. **Every state.** Render empty, short, average and very long content, in both themes, at 360px and 1440px.

## Motion

### Springs per role

Use only these three springs:

| Spring | Motion | CSS | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snappy` | `{ type: "spring", stiffness: 520, damping: 38 }` | `ease-spring-snappy`, 350ms | Presses, toggles, thumbs, indicators, text swaps, rolling digits |
| `smooth` | `{ type: "spring", visualDuration: 0.4, bounce: 0 }` | `ease-spring-smooth`, 450ms | Height, layout, FLIP, panels; no overshoot |
| `bouncy` | `{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 26 }` | `ease-spring-bouncy`, 600ms | Shape morphs and playful reveals only; never on exits |

### Durations

| Interaction | Duration |
|---|---|
| Press | 100ms |
| Hover and colour | 150ms |
| Tooltip and popover | 150–200ms |
| Dialog | 300ms |
| Sheet | 500ms |

Interaction feedback never takes longer than 200ms.

### Enter and exit

1. **Enter.**
   - Move 4–8px toward the trigger, scale from 0.96–0.97 and fade in.
   - Use `ease-enter` (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) or a spring.
   - Never scale from 0.
2. **Exit.**
   - Travel half the distance and scale to 0.98.
   - Use `ease-exit` (`cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)`).
   - An exit lasts at most 0.75 × its enter and never overshoots.
3. **Origin.** Set `transform-origin` to the trigger, so a popover grows out of what opened it.
4. **Interruptible.** Open and close with CSS transitions plus `@starting-style`, or Motion's `animate`, so reversing mid-flight is smooth. Use `@keyframes` only for entrances that play once on mount.
5. **Text and icon swaps.** The outgoing item moves up 3px and blurs 4px. The incoming item rises from 4px below. Tween the blur separately from the spring.
6. **Stagger.** 16ms per character, 35ms per list item, 40ms per word and 80ms per line, totalling 400ms at most. Entrances play once per mount.

### What moves and what doesn't

1. **Animate only** `transform`, `opacity`, `clip-path`, `filter` (blur up to 8px) and colours.
   - Never animate `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding` or `box-shadow` per frame.
   - Never use `transition: all`.
2. **Don't animate** keyboard-driven, high-frequency actions: opening a command menu or context menu, adding or removing list items, typing.
3. **Indicators glide.** Tab underlines, segmented thumbs and selections move with shared layout. The items under them never scale or change weight.
4. **`will-change`** only during a gesture, reset afterwards. Never put it in a stylesheet.

### Reduced motion

1. Every animated component has a reduced branch: opacity only, at 100ms (`reducedFade`), or no animation.
2. In CSS, use the `reduced:` variant. In JS, read the setting after hydration with `useSafeReducedMotion()`, never during the first render.
3. Loops pause off-screen and under reduced motion. Anything that autoplays for more than 5 seconds gets a pause control.

## Before you finish

- [ ] Every column passes the one-edge check, and footers share the body's inset.
- [ ] Gaps between groups are at least twice the gaps inside them.
- [ ] Nested corners are concentric, and there are no literal radii or raw colours.
- [ ] Every focusable element shows one visible focus treatment.
- [ ] Every animation uses a named spring or duration and has a reduced branch.
- [ ] It works at 360px with no sideways scroll, in light and dark.

author: Briyan Hingrajiya

files.content:
"use client"

/* Animated context menu for `@ui-sdk/react/menu`: a menu opened by a right-click, a long press or
   Shift+F10 on a `MenuContextTrigger`. It is the animated menu primitive (same sheet, same gliding
   highlight, same row cascade, same drawn checks), so everything from `@/components/primitives/menu`
   passes through, and the parts are also exported under ContextMenu* names.

   The one difference is the unfold. A context menu has no trigger to grow out of: UI SDK anchors it
   to the press point and puts that point in `--transform-origin`. So the sheet starts smaller (0.6),
   does not slide toward a trigger, and grows straight out of the pointer. */

import {
  Menu,
  MenuCheckboxItem,
  MenuContent as MenuContentPart,
  MenuContextTrigger,
  MenuGroup,
  MenuGroupLabel,
  MenuItem,
  MenuItemIcon,
  MenuItemIndicator,
  MenuRadioGroup,
  MenuRadioItem,
  MenuSeparator,
  MenuShortcut,
  MenuSub,
  MenuSubContent,
  MenuSubTrigger,
} from "@/components/primitives/menu"
import * as React from "react"

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

/* UI SDK accepts a class name or a function of state; keep both working. */
function withClass<S>(base: string, className: string | ((state: S) => string | undefined) | undefined) {
  return typeof className === "function" ? (state: S) => cn(base, className(state)) : cn(base, className)
}

export * from "@/components/primitives/menu"

/* Unfold from the point: no travel, a deeper scale and blur, the same spring in and quick fade out. */
const contextMenuMotion = cn(
  "data-starting-style:[translate:0_0] data-starting-style:scale-[0.6] data-starting-style:blur-[8px]",
  "data-ending-style:scale-[0.94]",
  /* Reduced motion: appear in place, no scale or blur. */
  "motion-reduce:data-starting-style:scale-100 motion-reduce:data-starting-style:blur-none motion-reduce:data-ending-style:scale-100",
)

function ContextMenuContent<Payload = unknown>({
  className,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof MenuContentPart<Payload>>) {
  return <MenuContentPart<Payload> className={withClass(contextMenuMotion, className)} {...props} />
}

export {
  Menu as ContextMenu,
  MenuCheckboxItem as ContextMenuCheckboxItem,
  ContextMenuContent,
  MenuGroup as ContextMenuGroup,
  MenuGroupLabel as ContextMenuGroupLabel,
  MenuItem as ContextMenuItem,
  MenuItemIcon as ContextMenuItemIcon,
  MenuItemIndicator as ContextMenuItemIndicator,
  contextMenuMotion,
  MenuRadioGroup as ContextMenuRadioGroup,
  MenuRadioItem as ContextMenuRadioItem,
  MenuSeparator as ContextMenuSeparator,
  MenuShortcut as ContextMenuShortcut,
  MenuSub as ContextMenuSub,
  MenuSubContent as ContextMenuSubContent,
  MenuSubTrigger as ContextMenuSubTrigger,
  MenuContextTrigger as ContextMenuTrigger,
}

"use client"

/* Keyframery's four motion styles: calm, springy (the default), snappy and playful.

   The motion style is a UI SDK preference, so it lives with the animated drop-in for
   `@ui-sdk/react/preferences`. This file passes everything through from there, so
   `motionStyle`, `MotionStyle` and `createMotionStyle` are the same objects whichever of the two
   you import them from. */

export * from "@/components/primitives/preferences"

/* Theming: set on a part or its ancestor; unset variables preserve the original theme.

   --badge-ink: Variant label (default: --primary-foreground / --secondary-foreground / --foreground / --destructive; success green mix 82% (dark green)).
   --badge-border: Outline hairline (default: --input).
   --badge-height: Badge height (default: 1.25rem).
   --badge-gap: Icon and label gap (default: 0.375rem).
   --badge-radius: Corners (default: calc(infinity * 1px)).
   --badge-padding: Horizontal padding (default: 0.5rem).
   --badge-font: Label size (default: 11px).
 */

/* Styled badge: the animated primitive plus the Keyframery look. Same variants as shadcn/ui's badge,
   plus `success`. */

import * as React from "react"

import { Badge as BadgePrimitive } from "@/components/primitives/badge"
import { Speed, type SpeedProps } from "@/lib/keyframery"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

const variants = {
  default: "bg-[var(--badge-face,var(--primary))] text-[color:var(--badge-ink,var(--primary-foreground))] shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgb(255_255_255/0.14),0_1px_2px_rgb(0_0_0/0.18)]",
  secondary:
    "bg-[var(--badge-face,var(--secondary))] text-[color:var(--badge-ink,var(--secondary-foreground))] shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_rgb(0_0_0/0.04)] dark:shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_rgb(255_255_255/0.05)]",
  outline: "bg-[var(--badge-face,transparent)] text-[color:var(--badge-ink,var(--foreground))] shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_var(--badge-border,var(--input))]",
  destructive: "bg-[var(--badge-face,color-mix(in_oklab,var(--destructive)_12%,transparent))] text-[color:var(--badge-ink,var(--destructive))] dark:bg-[var(--badge-face,color-mix(in_oklab,var(--destructive)_18%,transparent))]",
  success:
    "bg-[var(--badge-face,color-mix(in_oklch,oklch(0.62_0.16_150)_14%,transparent))] text-[color:var(--badge-ink,color-mix(in_oklch,oklch(0.62_0.16_150)_82%,var(--foreground)))] dark:text-[color:var(--badge-ink,oklch(0.62_0.16_150))] dark:bg-[var(--badge-face,color-mix(in_oklch,oklch(0.62_0.16_150)_18%,transparent))]",
} as const

type BadgeProps = React.ComponentProps<typeof BadgePrimitive>

function Badge({
  speed,
  className,
  variant = "default",
  ...props
}: BadgeProps & { variant?: keyof typeof variants } & SpeedProps) {
  const look = cn(
    "inline-flex h-[var(--badge-height,1.25rem)] w-fit shrink-0 items-center justify-center gap-[var(--badge-gap,0.375rem)] rounded-[var(--badge-radius,calc(infinity*1px))] px-[var(--badge-padding,0.5rem)] text-[length:var(--badge-font,11px)] leading-none font-medium whitespace-nowrap tabular-nums",
    "transition-[background-color,color,box-shadow] duration-[calc(200ms*var(--kf-speed,1))] ease-house motion-reduce:transition-none!",
    "[&>svg]:size-3 [&>svg]:shrink-0 [&_[data-slot=roll]]:leading-[15px] has-data-[slot=roll]:min-w-5 has-data-[slot=roll]:px-1.5",
    variants[variant],
  )
  return (
    <Speed speed={speed}>
      <BadgePrimitive
        data-variant={variant}
        className={typeof className === "function" ? (state) => cn(look, className(state)) : cn(look, className)}
        {...props}
      />
    </Speed>
  )
}

export { Badge }

/**
 * Keyframery · motion-style
 * MIT License · Copyright (c) 2026 Briyan Hingrajiya
 * https://keyframery.com/docs/components/motion-style
 * https://github.com/keyframery/keyframery
 */
"use client"

export * from "@/components/primitives/motion-style"

/* Theming (inherited; each default preserves the original light/dark appearance):
   --motion-style-track: Switcher well (default: --muted)
   --motion-style-key: Selected key (default: --background, --accent in dark)
   --motion-style-ink: Unselected text (default: --muted-foreground)
   --motion-style-selected-ink: Selected text (default: --foreground)
   --motion-style-height: Option height (default: 2rem)
   --motion-style-radius: Well corners (default: 12px)
   --motion-style-key-radius: Key corners (default: 9px)
   --motion-style-gap: Option gap (default: 0.125rem)
*/


/* The motion style switcher: a segmented control whose key stretches between the four styles.
   It applies the choice to <html> itself, so dropping it anywhere is enough.

   It is built in `@/components/ui/preferences`, on the preference switcher there, and passed
   through here under its own name. */

import * as React from "react"

import { MotionStyleSwitcher as MotionStyleSwitcherPart } from "@/components/ui/preferences"

export {
  createMotionStyle,
  MotionStyle,
  motionStyle,
  type MotionStylePreference,
  motionStyles,
  type MotionStyleValue,
} from "@/components/ui/preferences"

/* Theme aliases follow the shared switcher, including its dark key surface. */
function MotionStyleSwitcher({ style, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof MotionStyleSwitcherPart>) {
  const theme = {
    "--preferences-track": "var(--motion-style-track,var(--muted))",
    "--preferences-key": "var(--motion-style-key,var(--kf-preferences-key))",
    "--preferences-ink": "var(--motion-style-ink,var(--muted-foreground))",
    "--preferences-selected-ink": "var(--motion-style-selected-ink,var(--foreground))",
    "--preferences-height": "var(--motion-style-height,2rem)",
    "--preferences-radius": "var(--motion-style-radius,12px)",
    "--preferences-key-radius": "var(--motion-style-key-radius,9px)",
    "--preferences-gap": "var(--motion-style-gap,0.125rem)",
  } as React.CSSProperties
  return <MotionStyleSwitcherPart {...props} style={typeof style === "function" ? (state) => ({ ...theme, ...style(state) }) : { ...theme, ...style }} />
}

export { MotionStyleSwitcher }

---
name: asciicn
description: Build ASCII art, ANSI art and text-mode visuals with the asciicn engine (lib/ascii, a WebGL2 glyph shader and Canvas2D grids) in a React or shadcn/ui app. Use when the user wants ASCII, ANSI, Braille, CP437, PETSCII, katakana, halftone glyphs, a terminal or CRT look, an ASCII background, hero, painted landscape or city scene, halftone dots, 3D object, terminal window, meter, card, loader, text effect, or image/video/webcam to ASCII, or a .txt/.ans/.svg/.png/.webm export, or when code imports lib/ascii or components/asciicn.
---

# asciicn

asciicn is an ASCII engine. It draws pictures with real glyphs: a tone from 0 (empty) to 1 (full) becomes a character from a charset, coloured by a colour mode, on a grid of cells that snap to whole device pixels. You build the effect the user asked for on top of it. The asciicn components and backgrounds are examples of what the engine draws, not a menu. Install one only when it is exactly what the user asked for. Otherwise write your own, and borrow technique from the closest example's source.

The engine has two renderers that share one set of look props:

- **`AsciiShader`** (`@/lib/ascii/shader`, registry item `ascii-shader`): WebGL2. You write a GLSL `field` that returns a tone per sample; the GPU picks glyphs from a glyph atlas. For anything that moves or varies per cell: backgrounds, city skylines, glows, noise, fog, water.
- **`AsciiGrid`** (`@/lib/ascii`, registry item `ascii-core`): Canvas2D. You write a `draw` function that fills a frame of glyphs on the CPU, directly or through `mapTones`. For things you compute in JavaScript: 3D meshes, simulations, terminal panes, sampled images and video, text layouts.

## 1. Set up the engine

Find the engine: `lib/ascii/index.ts`, under the `lib` alias in `components.json` (imports below use `@/lib/ascii`; use the project's alias). If it is missing, install it:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-core.json {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-shader.json {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-export.json
```

That also installs `ascii-tokens`: the CSS variables `--ascii-ink`, `--ascii-paper`, `--ascii-cell`, `--ascii-font`, `--ascii-glow` and `--ascii-color-<name>`, written into the project's global CSS and mapped to the shadcn `--primary` and `--background`. The engine needs React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4.

If `lib/ascii` exists but lacks something this skill names (TypeScript says a prop such as `colorField` or `charset` doesn't exist on `AsciiShader`, or `lib/ascii/grid.tsx` is missing), replace the engine. This keeps the project's `lib/utils.ts` (`yes n` answers no to every overwrite question):

```bash
rm -rf lib/ascii && yes n | npx shadcn@latest add {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-core.json {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-shader.json {{REGISTRY_URL}}/ascii-export.json
```

Don't use `--overwrite`: it also replaces `lib/utils.ts`. If the project edited files inside `lib/ascii`, tell the user before replacing them.

Done when `lib/ascii/index.ts`, `lib/ascii/grid.tsx` and `lib/ascii/shader.tsx` exist and the global CSS defines `--ascii-ink`.

## 2. Pick the technique

| The user wants                                                                              | Use                                                                   | Read                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| A background or hero that is a picture: a landscape, a city, a place at a time of day       | `AsciiShader`, `field` + `colorField`, `dots`, `square`, `truecolor`  | [scenes.md](references/scenes.md)                     |
| A surface whose tone varies per cell or moves: gradients, noise, fog, water, nebulae, glows | `AsciiShader` with a GLSL `field`                                     | [fields.md](references/fields.md)                     |
| Many hues at once: a rainbow, a sunset, a hue per shape                                     | `AsciiShader` with a `field` and a `colorField`, `truecolor` mode     | [fields.md](references/fields.md#colour)              |
| Something you compute in JavaScript: a 3D mesh, particles, a simulation, a game of life     | `AsciiGrid` + `createToneField` + `mapTones`                          | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#asciigrid)   |
| A waveform, a line of values, a meter or a progress bar                                     | `AsciiGrid` writing glyphs (`eighthsBar`, Braille, `BOX`) or DOM text | [recipes.md](references/recipes.md#a-braille-trace)   |
| A terminal pane, boxed panel, status line or log                                            | `AsciiGrid` with `frame.write` and `BOX`, or a `<pre>`                | [recipes.md](references/recipes.md#a-terminal-pane)   |
| A photo, logo, video or webcam as ASCII                                                     | `sampleToField` into `mapTones` on an `AsciiGrid`                     | [recipes.md](references/recipes.md#an-image-as-ascii) |
| Static ASCII art that must render on the server or in an email                              | `AsciiPre` (a `<pre>` of a frame), or plain text in a `<pre>`         | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#static-art)  |
| A file: `.txt`, `.ans`, `.svg`, `.png`, `.webm`                                             | `ascii-export`                                                        | [export.md](references/export.md)                     |

Then choose a charset and a colour mode for the picture with [charsets.md](references/charsets.md). The charset is the biggest single decision: Braille for fine lines and wireframes, blocks or quadrants for solid shapes, `standard` or `dense` for photos, katakana for signage, `edge` for outlines, `dots` for halftone pictures. `dots` has five dot sizes (` ·∙•⦁●`); the two smallest are specks, so dark areas can stay quiet. Pair it with the `square` look prop: cells as wide as tall, so the dots lie on an even lattice instead of rows. Braille and quadrants stretch on square cells, so keep `square` for round-glyph ramps.

The examples in [examples.md](references/examples.md) (written when the skill is installed; if it's missing, read {{SITE_URL}}/.well-known/agent-skills/asciicn/references/examples.md) are references. If the user asked for exactly one of them, install it. If not, write your own: read the closest example's source for its field or draw function, then build what the user described. Never swap the request for an example that is merely nearby, and never guess at an example's props; read its docs page or source.

Done when every visual in the request has a renderer, a charset and a colour mode.

## 3. Build it

If the effect is for a landing page, or a section of one, read [landing-pages.md](references/landing-pages.md) before anything else. If it is a background scene (a place, a landscape, a city), follow [scenes.md](references/scenes.md) step by step and start from its starter scene; it covers framing for phones, the calm centre behind a headline and how to check the result. A good effect on a generic page still looks generated: the page has to be about the product, and the effect has to come from it.

1. Read the reference for your technique, and [recipes.md](references/recipes.md) for complete components to adapt.
2. Write the component in its own file with `"use client"` (both renderers are client components; `AsciiPre` renders on the server).
3. Give it typed props for what the user would tweak (charset, colour, speed, intensity, value), with defaults that already look good. Pass the engine's look props through (`charset`, `chars`, `colorMode`, `phosphor`, `ramp`, `fx`, `cell`, `speed`, `animate`) and accept a `handle` so the frame can be exported.
4. Place it with [placement.md](references/placement.md): a renderer fills a positioned parent (`absolute inset-0`), and content sits in a sibling above it.
5. Colour it with [theme.md](references/theme.md): token names (`"ink"`, `"blue"`, `--chart-1`) so it follows light and dark.

Done when the component renders the requested look with no `[ascii-shader]` or WebGL errors in the console.

## 4. Check it in a browser

Open the page and look at it. Screenshot it at desktop and phone widths (1440x900 and 390x844; a background scene also behind a sample headline and buttons), in light and dark mode, and once with reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`). Zoom into a screenshot: you must see individual glyphs. Hold it to [quality.md](references/quality.md).

Done when every check in quality.md passes. A screenshot of a flat block, an empty box or blurry glyphs means the field returns the wrong range, the parent has no size, or the cell isn't snapped: fix it and look again.

## Rules for every effect

- Draw glyphs, never pixels. Every visual is characters from a charset (or DOM text). No dots on a canvas, no CSS gradients standing in for glyphs.
- A field returns a continuous tone in [0, 1]: 0 empty, 1 the densest glyph. Write smooth math (`smoothstep`, `exp`, `mix`) and let the engine pick glyphs.
- `uv` runs 0 to 1 with y up. `res.x / res.y` is the box's true aspect ratio, so multiply x by it before measuring distances. Braille samples 2x4 per cell and quadrants 2x2, so never assume one sample per glyph: use `1.0 / res.y` for one sample row.
- Paint with theme colours (`"ink"`, palette names, `--css-variables`). Phosphors, ramps and literal colours are for when the user asks for a terminal look or specific colours.
- Text sits on clear ground. Fade the tone toward 0 behind headings, or give the text its own panel. Text contrast stays at 4.5:1 or better.
- Motion is slow. Choose `stillTime` so the reduced-motion frame looks finished. Decorative canvases are `aria-hidden`; data visuals have a text equivalent.

# Choosing a charset and a colour mode

The charset decides what the picture is made of; the colour mode decides how it is lit. Choose both for the subject, not by habit.

## Charsets

| Id          | Samples per cell | Glyphs                                 | Use it for                                                                   | Avoid it for                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `standard`  | 1x1              | ` .:-=+*#%@`                           | Photos, portraits, classic ASCII art, anything people should read as "ASCII" | Fine lines (too coarse)                      |
| `dense`     | 1x1              | 70 glyphs, `.` to `$`                  | Smooth gradients, faces, fog and clouds                                      | Small cells under 10px (glyphs turn to mush) |
| `blocks`    | 1x1              | ` ░▒▓█`                                | Bold fills, bars, ANSI art, light-mode backgrounds                           | Detail                                       |
| `quadrants` | 2x2              | ` ▘▝▀▖▌▞▛▗▚▐▜▄▙▟█`                     | Solid shapes at twice the resolution: logos, pixel art, maps, terrain        | Soft gradients                               |
| `braille`   | 2x4              | `⠁` to `⣿`                             | Waveforms, wireframes, contour lines, orbits, night skies, fine 3D           | Large filled areas (looks grey)              |
| `cp437`     | 1x1              | `·•○◘♠♣♥♦▲▼☺☻░▒▓█`                     | DOS, BBS and retro-PC moods                                                  | Corporate UI                                 |
| `petscii`   | 1x1              | `╱╲─│╭╮●◆▄▌█`                          | Commodore 64 moods, playful retro                                            | Photos                                       |
| `katakana`  | 1x1              | `ｱｳｴｵｶｷｼﾂｿﾝ` and digits                | Signage, glyph streams                                                       | Anything that should read as calm            |
| `dots`      | 1x1              | ` ·∙•⦁●`, five sizes                   | Halftone print, painted scenes and backgrounds (with `square`), soft glows   | Text-like art                                |
| `edge`      | 1x1              | `- / \| \` on edges, `standard` inside | Line drawings, outlines of a photo or a 3D shape, blueprints                 | Flat fields with no edges                    |

`dots` draws five round dots from geometry, not the font, in radii of 0.07, 0.13, 0.24, 0.33 and 0.42 of the cell. The first two are specks: use tones up to about 0.25 for quiet sky and shadow that reads as air, and save the large dots for light. Set `square` with it, so cells are as wide as tall and the dots lie on an even lattice; on default cells (about twice as tall as wide) the rows sit twice as far apart as the columns and the picture reads as stripes. `square` is for ramps of round glyphs; Braille and quadrants stretch on it. [scenes.md](scenes.md) builds whole pictures this way.

Custom ramps: `chars=" .oO@"` (empty to dense, at least two glyphs) wins over `charset`. Use a custom ramp for a brand ("` -=≡`" for a minimal look, `" 01"` for binary). Order glyphs by how much ink they show in the font, or the tones will jump.

Rules of thumb:

- Braille and quadrants only show detail when the field has detail at sample scale. A soft glow in Braille looks like grey static; use `dots` or `standard` for soft things.
- On a light background, sparse charsets (`standard`, `dots`, `braille`) look faint. Prefer `blocks`, a larger `cell`, or `invert` for dark-on-light art.
- `edge` needs contrast in the field. It is best on images and on fields with clear shapes.
- Mixing charsets on one page is fine when each part has its own role: Braille for a waveform, blocks for a progress bar, standard for a hero image.

## Colour modes

| Mode        | How a glyph is coloured                                                        | Use it for                                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mono`      | Every glyph in `--ascii-ink`, or a `phosphor`                                  | Most UI, terminals, anything that should follow the theme |
| `palette`   | The tone picks a colour from `palette` (paper, then inks from faint to strong) | Theme-coloured backgrounds with depth, one hue per line   |
| `duotone`   | The tone picks a colour on a `ramp`, dark to bright                            | Moody backgrounds, heat, night skies                      |
| `truecolor` | The source colour per glyph: a `colorField`, an image, a video                 | Photos, video, sunsets, neon, anything with real colour   |
| `ansi16`    | The source colour snapped to 16 terminal colours (`ansi="vga"` or `"xterm"`)   | ANSI art, terminal screenshots, `.ans` export             |

Phosphors for `mono`: `p1` green `#33ff66`, `p3` amber `#ffb000`, `ibm` white `#f4f4f5`, `blueprint` cyan `#38bdf8`. They are fixed colours, so give them a dark paper in light mode (wrap the section in `className="dark"` or set `paper`).

Duotone ramps: `mainframe`, `sodium`, `heliograph`, `infrared`, `outrun`, `orchid`, `glacier`, `ember`, `toxic`, `vapor`. Read `RAMPS` in `lib/ascii/palettes.ts` for the stops, or pass your own: `ramp={["#0b1020", "#3b82f6", "#e0f2fe"]}`.

## Grading

`grade={{ brightness, contrast, gamma, saturation }}` adjusts tones before the glyph is chosen. Raise `contrast` (1.2 to 1.6) when a field or image uses only a few glyphs. Lower `gamma` (0.7 to 0.9) to open up shadows in a photo. `invert` swaps dense and empty, for dark ink on a light page.

`dither="bayer4"` (or `"bayer8"`, `"blue-noise"`) blends neighbouring glyph levels in a fixed pattern. It smooths gradients in short ramps such as `blocks` and `dots`.

## Picking for common requests

| Request                               | Charset               | Colour mode                             |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| A terminal or CRT panel               | `standard` + text     | `mono` with `p1` or `p3`, `fx={CRT_FX}` |
| A photo turned to ASCII               | `standard` or `dense` | `truecolor`, or `mono` for print        |
| A waveform or a line of values        | `braille`             | `mono` or `palette` per line            |
| A density grid or level bars          | `blocks`              | `palette`                               |
| A logo in ASCII                       | `quadrants`           | `mono`                                  |
| A night sky, orbit or wireframe globe | `braille`             | `mono` or `duotone`                     |
| Fire, a nebula, a sunset              | `dense` or `blocks`   | `truecolor` with a `colorField`         |
| A blueprint or technical drawing      | `edge`                | `mono` with `blueprint`                 |
| Newsprint or a halftone portrait      | `dots`                | `mono`, `invert` on light pages         |
| A painted landscape or city scene     | `dots` with `square`  | `truecolor` with a `colorField`         |
| Retro game or BBS screen              | `cp437` or `petscii`  | `ansi16`                                |

# Engine API The engine installs as plain source. When this file and the code disagree, the code wins: read `lib/ascii/index.ts` and the file named in each section. - `@/lib/ascii` (item `ascii-core`): CPU side. Charsets, palettes, frames, cell metrics, `AsciiGrid`, `mapTones`, theme and motion hooks. No WebGL. - `@/lib/ascii/shader` (item `ascii-shader`): `AsciiShader`, the WebGL2 glyph renderer. - `@/lib/ascii/export` (item `ascii-export`): files. See [export.md](export.md). ## Look props Both renderers, and every component and background, take the same look props (`AsciiLook` in `lib/ascii/look.ts`): | Prop | Type | What it does | | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `charset` | `CharsetName` | Which glyphs draw the tones. See [charsets.md](charsets.md) | | `chars` | `string` | A custom ramp from empty to dense, such as `" .oO@"`. Wins over `charset` | | `colorMode` | `"mono" \| "truecolor" \| "ansi16" \| "duotone" \| "palette"` | How glyphs are coloured | | `phosphor` | `"p1" \| "p3" \| "ibm" \| "blueprint"` | `mono`: a CRT screen colour instead of `--ascii-ink` | | `ramp` | `RampName \| string[]` | `duotone`: a named ramp or `#rrggbb` stops, dark to bright | | `ansi` | `"vga" \| "xterm"` | `ansi16`: which 16-colour table. Default `"vga"` | | `grade` | `{ brightness, contrast, gamma, saturation }` | Tone grading before the glyph is chosen | | `invert` | `boolean` | Dense glyphs for dark tones. Use for dark-on-light art | | `threshold` | `number` | Braille and quadrants: the tone that lights a dot. Default 0.5 | | `edgeThreshold` | `number` | `edge`: Sobel strength that draws `- / \| \`. Default 0.22 | | `dither` | `"none" \| "bayer2" \| "bayer4" \| "bayer8" \| "blue-noise"` | Ordered dithering between glyph levels, for smooth gradients with few glyphs | | `background` | `"paper" \| "transparent"` | `"transparent"` draws glyphs only, so the page shows between them | | `square` | `boolean` | Cells as wide as tall (`cell` sets both sides), so `dots` lies on an even lattice. Braille and quadrants stretch on it. Default `false` | | `fx` | `PostFx` | CRT effects, each 0 to 1: `scanlines`, `bloom`, `curvature`, `glitch`, `flicker`, `vignette`. `CRT_FX` is a full preset, `NO_FX` turns them off | Shared runtime props: `cell` (glyph cell height in CSS px, default `--ascii-cell`), `speed` (time multiplier, default 1), `animate` (`false` holds a still frame), `fps` (cap), `stillTime` (seconds drawn when motion is off or reduced), `fallback` (shown until the first frame) and `handle` (a ref filled with an `AsciiHandle` for export). ## AsciiShader `lib/ascii/shader.tsx`. A client component that fills its positioned parent. ```tsx "use client"; import { AsciiShader } from "@/lib/ascii/shader"; const FIELD = /* glsl */ ` float field(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t) { vec2 p = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(res.x / res.y, 1.0); return smoothstep(0.45, 0.0, length(p)) * (0.75 + 0.25 * sin(t)); }`; export const Glow = () => ( ); ``` | Prop | What it does | | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `field` | GLSL: `float field(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t)` returning a tone in [0, 1]. See [fields.md](fields.md) | | `colorField` | GLSL: `vec3 colorField(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t)` (or `vec4`) returning RGB 0..1 for `truecolor` and `ansi16` | | `uniforms` | `{ name: number \| [x, y] \| [x, y, z] \| [x, y, z, w] }`, declared for you. Names must not start with `u_` | | `palette` | Paper then inks, as token names or CSS colours. Used by `colorMode="palette"` | | `ink`, `paper` | Mono overrides | | `interaction` | `"none" \| "repel" \| "ripple" \| "trail"`: what the pointer does to the field | | `audio` | Audio bands from `useAudioBands` (`lib/ascii/audio.ts`), read as `u_audio`, or `null` | | `seed` | A number read as `u_seed`, for seeded variations. Default 0 | | look props | All of the table above | Default `colorMode` is `truecolor` when `colorField` is set, otherwise `palette` (paper to ink). Keep the `field` string a module-level constant and pass changing values through `uniforms`; a new string recompiles the shader. `data-state` on the root reports `running`, `paused` (offscreen or hidden tab), `static` (reduced motion or `animate={false}`) or `fallback` (no WebGL2, or a compile error, which is logged with the line). ## AsciiGrid `lib/ascii/grid.tsx`. A Canvas2D grid of glyphs drawn by a function you write, at device resolution, theme-aware, paused offscreen, one still frame under reduced motion. ```tsx "use client"; import { AsciiGrid } from "@/lib/ascii"; import type { AsciiGridDrawContext } from "@/lib/ascii"; const draw = ({ frame, columns, rows, time }: AsciiGridDrawContext) => { const message = "SYSTEM READY"; const x = Math.floor((columns - message.length) / 2); frame.write(x, Math.floor(rows / 2), message); frame.put( x + message.length + 1, Math.floor(rows / 2), time % 1 < 0.5 ? "█" : " " ); }; export const Ready = () => ( ); ``` `draw(ctx)` runs every frame while animating, once for a still frame, and again on resize. `ctx` holds: - `frame`: a `MutableFrame`, cleared to spaces before each draw. `put(x, y, glyph, rgba?)`, `write(x, y, text, rgba?)`, `fillRect(x, y, w, h, glyph, rgba?)`, `get(x, y)`. Out-of-bounds writes are ignored, so you never need to clip. Row 0 is the top. - `columns`, `rows`: the grid size for the current box and cell. - `time` (seconds, scaled by `speed`), `delta` (seconds since the last draw, 0 when still). - `pointer`: `{ x, y, inside, down }` in cell units, when `interactive` is set. - `metrics`: the measured `CellMetrics`. Props: `draw`, `cell`, `ink`, `paper` (default `"transparent"`), `colored` (per-glyph colour; set it when you pass `rgba` or use a colour mode), `speed`, `animate`, `fps` (default 30), `stillTime`, `interactive`, `fallback`, `handle`. ### Tones to glyphs on the CPU For anything with a tone per point (3D shading, a heightmap, a simulation), fill a `ToneField` and let `mapTones` choose glyphs. It handles every charset, sub-cell sampling and colour mode the same way the GPU does. ```ts import { createToneField, fillToneField, mapTones, resolveCharset, } from "@/lib/ascii"; // Inside draw: const charset = resolveCharset("braille"); const field = createToneField(columns, rows, charset); // columns*2 by rows*4 samples for Braille fillToneField(field, (u, v) => /* u, v in [0, 1], v = 0 at the TOP */ Math.max( 0, 1 - Math.hypot(u - 0.5, v - 0.5) * 2 ) ); mapTones(field, columns, rows, { charset, colorMode: "mono" }, frame); ``` `fillToneField`'s callback may return a tone or `[tone, r, g, b]` (0..255) when the field was created with `{ color: true }`. `mapTones(field, columns, rows, options, into?)` writes into `into` (pass `ctx.frame`) and takes `charset`, `chars`, `grade`, `invert`, `threshold`, `edgeThreshold`, `dither`, `colorMode`, `ramp`, `ansi` and `palette` (paper to ink, as `[r, g, b]` bytes). Reuse the field across frames: create it once per size (keep it in a ref and recreate when `columns` or `rows` change), and refill it each frame. ## Charset helpers `lib/ascii/charsets.ts`: - `CHARSETS`, `CHARSET_NAMES`, `resolveCharset(charset, chars?)` returns `{ id, label, kind, glyphs, grid }`. `kind` is `"ramp"`, `"braille"`, `"quadrants"` or `"edge"`; `grid` is the samples per cell (`[2, 4]` for Braille). - `rampChar(charset, tone)`: the glyph for a tone on a ramp charset. - `brailleChar(mask)` with `BRAILLE_DOT_BITS[row][col]` (row 0..3, col 0..1): build a Braille glyph dot by dot, for traces, waveforms and plots. - `quadrantChar(mask)`, `QUADRANT_GLYPHS`; `edgeChar(gx, gy)` (y down) picks `-`, `/`, `|` or `\`. - `EIGHTHS_UP` (` ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█`) and `EIGHTHS_RIGHT` (` ▏▎▍▌▋▊▉█`): bars with eighth-cell precision. `eighthsBar(value, width)` returns a horizontal bar string for `value` in [0, 1]. - `SHADES` (` ░▒▓█`), `BOX` (`ascii`, `light`, `heavy`, `double`, `rounded`, each with `tl tr bl br h v x`), `SPINNERS`. ## Colour helpers `lib/ascii/palettes.ts` and `lib/ascii/color.ts`: - `PHOSPHORS`, `RAMPS`, `ANSI16.vga`, `ANSI16.xterm`, `sampleRamp(stops, t)`, `hexToRgb`, `rgbToHex`, `nearestIndex(rgb, palette)` (OKLab distance), `luma`, `gradeTone`, `gradeRgb`. - `cssColor(name)`: `"green"` to `var(--ascii-color-green, …)`, `"--chart-1"` to `var(--chart-1)`. - `useAsciiColors(ref, names?)`: resolves token names (default paper and ink) to concrete RGBA on the client and re-renders when the theme changes. Returns `null` until mounted. `resolveColor(css)`, `subscribeToTheme(callback)` for non-React code. - `seriesColor(color, i)`, `SERIES_COLORS`: `color` if set, otherwise the i-th named colour in a fixed order, for telling several lines apart. ## Cell metrics `lib/ascii/measure.ts`: `measureCell({ cell, font, dpr })` returns `{ width, height, deviceWidth, deviceHeight, dpr, fontSize, font }`. The cell height is `cell`; the width is the font's advance; both snap to whole device pixels so glyphs stay sharp. `gridSize(metrics, width, height)` gives `{ columns, rows }`. `readCell(el)` and `readFont(el)` read `--ascii-cell` and `--ascii-font`. `DEFAULT_CELL` is 12. ## Motion hooks `lib/ascii/motion.ts`: `useFrameLoop((time, delta) => …, { target, enabled, fps, stillTime })` drives your own loop with the same rules as the renderers (pause offscreen and in hidden tabs, one frame under reduced motion). `usePrefersReducedMotion()`, `useInView(ref)`, `useDocumentVisible()`. ## Static art `AsciiPre` (`lib/ascii/pre.tsx`) renders an `AsciiFrame` as a `

For a CPU renderer that needs the CRT look, `CrtOverlay` (`lib/ascii/crt.tsx`) approximates `fx` in CSS over a canvas or DOM text.
