# Writing a field

A field is the GLSL function you write for `AsciiShader`. It returns a tone for one sample point; the engine grades it, picks the glyph from the charset, colours it and draws it from a glyph atlas.

```glsl
float field(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t) {
  // uv:  the sample centre, 0 to 1 on both axes, (0, 0) bottom left, y up
  // res: the sample grid, measured in sample rows (see below)
  // t:   seconds of motion, already multiplied by `speed`
  return uv.y; // 0 = empty cell, 1 = the densest glyph
}
```

The return value is clamped to [0, 1]. With a ramp charset (`standard`, `dense`, `blocks`, `cp437`…), the tone picks a glyph by ink coverage: 0.1 is a `.`, 0.9 is a `#` or `@`. With `braille` and `quadrants`, each dot or quadrant lights where its own sample is above `threshold`. With `edge`, the engine runs a Sobel filter over your tones and draws `- / | \` along edges.

## The `res` contract

The field is sampled on a grid finer than the glyph grid when the charset packs several dots into one glyph:

| Charset       | Samples per cell |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| Ramps, `edge` | 1 x 1            |
| `quadrants`   | 2 x 2            |
| `braille`     | 2 x 4            |

`res.y` is the number of sample rows. `res.x` is `res.y * boxWidth / boxHeight`, so `res.x / res.y` is always the box's true aspect ratio, even though a glyph cell is about half as wide as it is tall. Two consequences:

- Measure distances in square units: `vec2 p = vec2(uv.x * res.x / res.y, uv.y);`. Circles stay round in every charset.
- `1.0 / res.y` is one sample row. Use it for line widths and finite differences. Don't use `1.0 / res.x` as "one cell", and don't assume one sample per glyph: a line one sample wide is a quarter of a Braille cell.

Write the field once and it works in every charset. Test it in `standard` and in `braille`: if it only looks right in one, it assumes a sample size.

## The rules of the language

Fields are GLSL ES 1.00 (the field pass runs on WebGL2, but in the 1.00 dialect).

- Every literal used as a float needs a decimal point: `2.0`, not `2`. `int` and `float` never mix without a cast: `float(i)`.
- Loops need constant bounds: `for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)`. Break early with `if (float(i) >= count) break;` when the count is a uniform.
- No arrays in uniforms. Pass up to four numbers per uniform (`vec4`) and use several uniforms.
- Write helpers above `field` in the same string, prefixed with your component's name (`topoHeight`, `waveCrest`) so they never collide.
- Reserved: uniforms starting with `u_`, helpers starting with `ascii_`, and the names `field`, `colorField`, `main`, `hash21`, `snoise`, `fbm`, `spectrum`, `paletteColor`, `oklch`, `toSrgb`, `aces`.
- GLSL ES 1.00 keeps words it never uses, and none compile as names: `input`, `output`, `half`, `fixed`, `long`, `short`, `double`, `unsigned`, `public`, `static`, `extern`, `external`, `class`, `union`, `enum`, `typedef`, `template`, `goto`, `inline`, `noinline`, `volatile`, `cast`, `sizeof`, `this`, `packed`, `default`, `switch`, `interface`, `namespace`, `using`, `asm`, `flat`, `superp`, and types such as `hvec2`, `dvec3`, `fvec4` or `sampler3D`. Names starting with `gl_` or `webgl_`, or containing `__`, are reserved too. Built-in names (`dot`, `step`, `mix`, `length`, `distance`, `noise`) can't be variables either. Prefixed names avoid all of them.
- A broken field logs a compile error with the line, and the component shows its fallback. Read the console, fix the GLSL, reload.

## Built-in helpers

| Helper                                  | Returns                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `float hash21(vec2 p)`                  | A stable pseudo-random value in [0, 1). `hash21(floor(p))` gives one value per grid square. |
| `float snoise(vec2 p)`                  | 2D simplex noise in [-1, 1], feature size about 1 unit of `p`.                              |
| `float fbm(vec2 p)`                     | Four octaves of simplex noise, in [0, 1], mean 0.5.                                         |
| `vec3 spectrum(float h)`                | A saturated rainbow, red at 0 and 1. Wraps.                                                 |
| `vec4 paletteColor(float x)`            | The palette's ink colours (every entry after paper) as a ramp from 0 to 1.                  |
| `vec3 oklch(float L, float C, float h)` | An OKLCH colour, `h` in radians, as linear RGB. Pass it through `toSrgb` before returning.  |
| `vec3 toSrgb(vec3 linear)`              | Linear RGB to sRGB, clamped.                                                                |
| `vec3 aces(vec3 x)`                     | ACES filmic tone map, for bright, saturated colour that shouldn't clip.                     |

## Built-in uniforms

| Uniform             | Type  | Value                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `u_time`            | float | Same as `t`                                                                                  |
| `u_resolution`      | vec2  | Same as `res`                                                                                |
| `u_pointer`         | vec3  | Pointer `xy` in `uv` space, `z` = presence from 0 to 1, smoothed. 0 when the pointer is away |
| `u_pointerVelocity` | vec2  | Pointer velocity in `uv` per second                                                          |
| `u_click`           | vec3  | Last press position `xy`, `z` = seconds since it                                             |
| `u_audio`           | vec4  | Bass, mid, treble, level, each 0 to 1, from the `audio` prop (`useAudioBands`)               |
| `u_seed`            | float | The `seed` prop (default 0). Offset noise by it so two copies of a component can differ      |

Read `u_pointer` for parallax or steering: `vec2 look = (u_pointer.xy - 0.5) * u_pointer.z;`. For push, ripple and trail effects you don't need to write anything: set `interaction="repel"`, `"ripple"` or `"trail"` and the engine applies them to your tones.

## Your own uniforms

Pass anything the user should control as a uniform, never by rebuilding the string:

```tsx
<AsciiShader
  field={FIELD}
  uniforms={{ topoScale: scale, topoLines: lines, topoFocus: [0.7, 0.4] }}
/>
```

`topoScale` becomes `uniform float topoScale;`, `topoFocus` becomes `uniform vec2 topoFocus;`. They are declared for you; declaring them yourself is a compile error.

## Coordinates

```glsl
float aspect = res.x / res.y;
vec2 p = vec2(uv.x * aspect, uv.y);         // x 0..aspect, y 0..1, square units
vec2 c = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(aspect, 1.0);    // centred: (0, 0) in the middle, y -0.5..0.5
```

A point given from the top left, as CSS does (`[x, y]` with y down), converts with `vec2(x * aspect, 1.0 - y)`. Rotate with `mat2(cos(a), -sin(a), sin(a), cos(a)) * c`. To keep a pattern the same size in cells whatever the box size, scale by `res.y`: `p * res.y / 40.0` is one unit per 40 sample rows.

## Building blocks

Each returns a tone in [0, 1]. Combine with `max` (union), `min` (intersection), `*` (mask), `mix` (blend).

### Gradients and light

```glsl
float linear = uv.y;
float radial = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.6, length(c));
float glow = exp(-dot(c, c) * 8.0);                 // larger number = tighter
float edgeFade = smoothstep(0.0, 0.35, uv.y);       // clear the bottom edge
```

Glyph ramps are coarse (10 levels in `standard`), so wide soft gradients band. Set `dither="bayer4"` to blend neighbouring glyph levels, or use `dense` (70 levels).

### Noise

```glsl
float clouds = fbm(p * 3.0 + vec2(t * 0.04, 0.0));
float ridges = 1.0 - abs(snoise(p * 2.5));
float warped = fbm(p * 2.0 + 0.6 * vec2(fbm(p * 1.5 + t * 0.03), fbm(p * 1.5 - t * 0.02)));
```

### Lines

Thin lines read best in `braille` (eight dots per glyph). Measure the distance to the line in sample rows, then turn it into a tone that is 1 on the line and 0 a sample or two away:

```glsl
float px = 1.0 / res.y;                                  // one sample row
float ring = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5 * px, abs(length(c) - 0.3));
float wave = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5 * px, abs(p.y - 0.5 - 0.1 * sin(p.x * 6.0 + t)));
```

Contour lines of a height function `h(p)`, about `width` samples wide:

```glsl
float topoLine(float h, float hx, float hy, float count, float width) {
  float v = h * count;
  float offset = abs(fract(v + 0.5) - 0.5);
  float perSample = max(length(vec2(hx - h, hy - h)) * count, 1e-4);
  float d = offset / perSample;
  return (1.0 - smoothstep(width * 0.5 - 0.5, width * 0.5 + 0.5, d)) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.06, 0.1, offset));
}
// float h = topoHeight(p);
// float hx = topoHeight(p + vec2(1.0 / res.y, 0.0));
// float hy = topoHeight(p + vec2(0.0, 1.0 / res.y));
// return topoLine(h, hx, hy, 12.0, 1.5);
```

Use a smooth height for contour lines (one or two low-frequency `snoise` layers); raw high-frequency `fbm` breaks lines into dots.

### Shapes and shading

A flat 1.0 inside a shape draws a solid block of `@`. Shade it so the glyphs vary:

```glsl
float disc = 1.0 - smoothstep(r - 0.01, r + 0.01, length(c));
float lit = disc * mix(0.3, 1.0, smoothstep(-0.3, 0.3, c.y + c.x * 0.4));   // lit from the top right
float rim = disc * smoothstep(r * 0.6, r, length(c));                       // denser at the edge
```

For a sphere or a 3D look, compute a normal and a light (`max(dot(n, light), 0.0)`) and return the lambert term. Glyph ramps read shading very well; that is what ASCII art is good at.

### Columns

Per-column motion uses the glyph grid, not the sample grid. Step in whole cells: `floor(uv.x * columns)`, where `columns` is `res.x` divided by the charset's samples per cell across (1 for ramps). Pass `columns` as a uniform when the charset can change, or keep per-column effects on a ramp charset such as `katakana`.

## Motion

- Drift by adding `t * speed` to coordinates: speeds of 0.01 to 0.08 units per second read as calm.
- Pulse with `1.0 + 0.05 * sin(t * 0.4)`.
- Avoid `hash21` of anything with `t` in it: every glyph changes every frame and the effect flickers. For glyphs that change on purpose (falling glyphs, glitches), quantise time first: `hash21(vec2(column, floor(t * 8.0)))`.
- `stillTime` sets the frame shown under reduced motion. Pick one where the composition looks finished.

## Colour

`colorField` is an optional second function. It returns the colour of the glyph in a cell; `field` still decides which glyph. Setting it makes `truecolor` the default colour mode, and `ansi16` snaps its output to 16 terminal colours.

```tsx
const FIELD = /* glsl */ `
float field(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t) {
  vec2 c = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(res.x / res.y, 1.0);
  return exp(-pow(abs(length(c) - 0.3), 2.0) * 900.0);
}`;

const COLOR_FIELD = /* glsl */ `
vec3 colorField(vec2 uv, vec2 res, float t) {
  vec2 c = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(res.x / res.y, 1.0);
  return toSrgb(oklch(0.75, 0.15, atan(c.y, c.x) + t * 0.3));
}`;

<AsciiShader
  field={FIELD}
  colorField={COLOR_FIELD}
  charset="braille"
  className="absolute inset-0"
/>;
```

- Same arguments and uniforms as `field`. Return `vec3` RGB or `vec4` RGBA in [0, 1].
- `field` and `colorField` compile into one shader. Shared geometry goes in a helper; the engine keeps one copy of a helper that appears word for word in both strings.
- `oklch` gives even, controllable hues; `spectrum` is fully saturated and goes thin on white (yellow and cyan vanish). Mix in theme ink for light mode: `mix(spectrum(h), paletteColor(0.0).rgb, 0.25)`.
- Without `colorField`, `palette` mode maps tone to the palette and `duotone` to the ramp.
- To paint a whole picture (a landscape or a city), paint the colour first and read the tone back from it, in one cached function both fields call. [scenes.md](scenes.md) shows how.

| Colour                            | GLSL body                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hue across the box                | `return toSrgb(oklch(0.72, 0.14, uv.x * 6.2832));`                                            |
| Hue around a centre               | `return spectrum(atan(c.y, c.x) / 6.2832);`                                                   |
| Theme colours along x             | `return paletteColor(uv.x).rgb;` with `palette={["--ascii-paper", "--chart-1", "--chart-2"]}` |
| Fire: dark red to white by height | `return aces(vec3(3.0, 1.2, 0.4) * tone);` with the tone from a shared helper                 |
| Fade out instead of thinning      | `return vec4(spectrum(uv.x), smoothstep(0.0, 0.3, uv.y));`                                    |

## Tuning the look

- Too busy behind text: multiply the tone (`* 0.6`) or clear it under the text with `smoothstep` on `uv`.
- Glyphs too uniform: widen the tone range. A field that sits between 0.4 and 0.6 draws one or two glyphs; stretch it with `smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, x)` or `grade={{ contrast: 1.4 }}`.
- Too dark in light mode: sparse charsets read faint on white. Try `blocks`, a bigger `cell`, or `invert`.
- Want a bolder look: `cell={16}` to `cell={20}`. Fine texture: 10 to 12.

# Designing a landing page around an ASCII effect

A working ASCII effect on a generic page still reads as generated. The effect has to be the page's identity, drawn from what the product is, and the page around it has to be specific, quiet and true. Do this before you write a field.

## 1. Know the product

The page is for the product in this repo, not for asciicn. asciicn is the tool you build with: don't name it on the page, and don't make the page about ASCII art.

Read the README, `package.json`, the existing pages and any copy in the repo. Write yourself a short brief:

- What the product is and who it is for, in one sentence, in the product's own words.
- The one thing a visitor should do (install, sign up, download, book).
- The facts you can use: features, platforms, prices, numbers. Only facts that are in the repo or the user's message.

If there is no product to read about, ask the user what the page is for. If nobody can answer, pick something plausible, keep it modest, and say what you picked.

## 2. Find the effect in the subject

The hero effect should be something only this product would show. Take it from the product's own world and render it in glyphs, as a field, a CPU grid, an image or a Braille trace:

| The product is about             | An ASCII effect drawn from it                                               |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Maps, outdoors, travel           | Braille contour lines of real-looking terrain, a route over them            |
| Audio, music, voice              | A waveform or spectrum, lines stacked like a spectrogram                    |
| Money, trading, analytics        | A price line or volume ridges, a dense band where activity is               |
| Infrastructure, uptime, networks | Packets along paths, a grid of hosts, a pulse at the incident               |
| Weather, climate, energy         | Isobars, a radar sweep, heat rising off a surface                           |
| Sleep, health, calm              | A slow breathing ring, a tide line, a night sky                             |
| Food, drink, physical goods      | The product photo itself as ASCII (`sampleToField`), steam rising in glyphs |
| Space, science, research         | A night sky, orbits, a particle trace, a slow nebula                        |
| A developer tool or API          | The product's real output in a terminal pane: its CLI, its logs, its data   |

A soft glow or drifting noise fits almost any product, which is why it says nothing about this one. Use one only as a supporting layer.

## 3. Compose the page

Spend the boldness in one place: the hero effect. Keep everything else quiet and disciplined.

**Pick the hero that fits**, not the split layout by default:

- **Full-bleed field.** The effect fills the hero and the headline sits on cleared ground (see [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline)).
- **The product shot.** A real product photo or screenshot converted to ASCII, large, with the headline beside or above it. It can resolve into the photo on hover.
- **One big number or object.** A rotating ASCII object or a Braille ring behind a real figure the product has, with the label in HTML.
- **A live demo.** A terminal pane that runs the product's real command, or an effect that responds to one control, so the page shows what the product does.

**Build the rest from the content.** A section exists because the product has something to say there, not because landing pages have one.

- Show, don't list. One wide section that shows a feature working beats three cards that name three features.
- Vary the rhythm: a wide section, then a narrow one; text left, then right. Avoid rows of identical cards.
- Use at most two or three ASCII effects on the page, each tied to content: the hero, a trace of real data, an ASCII product photo, one section break.
- One accent colour at most. The glyph ink carries the page's colour; buttons and text stay in the theme. A phosphor colour is an accent too.
- Typography carries the personality. One family is fine. Set a clear scale with weight and size, sentence case throughout.
- Keep vertical rhythm even (about `py-24` to `py-32` between sections on desktop, `py-16` on a phone) and line lengths under 80 characters.

## 4. Write true, plain copy

- The headline says what the product does for whom, in plain words. No wordplay that needs the subhead to explain it.
- The subhead adds two specifics: how it works, what you get.
- Buttons say what happens: "Download for Mac", "Start a free trial", "Read the docs".
- Use only facts from step 1. No invented stats, testimonials, customer logos, ratings or prices. If a section needs a number the product doesn't have, drop the section.

## 5. Don't ship the tells

These make a page read as generated, whatever the effect looks like:

- An all-caps, letter-spaced label above every heading, or monospace micro-labels used as decoration. ASCII invites terminal styling; use it where the product is a terminal, not as costume on every heading.
- Numbered markers (01, 02, 03) on things that aren't a sequence.
- One word in the headline set apart in italic, grey or colour; a serif display line followed by a grey second line.
- A row of three identical feature cards; a stats strip with invented numbers.
- Captions or pills laid over a visual ("Field study 01", "Signal / in motion"); a round arrow button on a card that goes nowhere.
- A fake product UI built from divs; fake testimonials; placeholder logos.
- A glowing orb or gradient in a rounded card as the whole hero.
- Em dashes, "elevate", "seamless", "unleash", "next-gen", an arrow on every link, decorative coloured dots.

## 6. Look at it as a visitor

Screenshot the whole page at 1440px and 390px, in light and dark mode. Go through every item in section 5 against the screenshots and the code, one by one, and fix each one you find; search the code for `—` and `uppercase`. Then answer honestly:

- In five seconds, can you tell what the product is and what to do next?
- Is the ASCII effect the first thing you notice, and does it belong to this product?
- Would this page be mistaken for any other product's page? If yes, the hero or the copy is generic: go back to step 2.
- Remove one element that isn't earning its place.

Then run every check in [quality.md](quality.md).

# Putting an ASCII effect on a page ## Layering `AsciiShader` and `AsciiGrid` fill their nearest positioned ancestor. Content goes in a sibling, above: ```tsx
…
``` - `isolate` on the section keeps `-z-10` inside it, so the effect never slips behind the page background. - The section needs height from its content or a `min-h-*`. A renderer takes the size it is given; zero height draws nothing. - Round corners and borders go on the section with `overflow-hidden`, so the canvas is clipped to them. - Renderers ignore the pointer unless `interactive` or `interaction` is set, so links and buttons above stay clickable. An interactive background still sits under content: give the content `pointer-events-none` on empty areas only if the effect should react there. ## Landing pages Read [landing-pages.md](landing-pages.md) first. These are the placements. - **Hero:** a full-bleed effect behind the headline. Clear the area under the text (tone near 0) and let the effect peak toward the edges or a corner. Fade it out at the bottom with `smoothstep` on `uv.y` so the next section starts clean. - **Clearing space for text:** measure the text block and pass its box to the field as a uniform. [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline) has the component. An ellipse in `uv` is too big on desktop and too small on a phone. - **Section break:** a band 6 to 12 rows tall: a glyph gradient, a row of box-drawing characters, or a slow wave in Braille. - **Feature card:** a small `AsciiGrid` or shader behind the top half of a card, under the icon and title. - **Terminal pane:** a `rounded-lg border bg-black` box with an `AsciiGrid` or a `
`, wrapped in `className="dark"` so the tokens take their dark values.
- **Behind a big number or headline:** a glow or a rotating object centred behind the text. Real text stays HTML on top; never draw the headline into the field.

## Meters, traces and status

- **Traces and meters:** draw them in an `AsciiGrid` (Braille lines, `EIGHTHS_UP` bars, `blocks` for density) or as DOM text in a `
`. Keep the value and the label as HTML text beside or over the glyphs.
- **Accessible names:** a trace canvas gets `role="img"` and an `aria-label` with the data in words, or a visually hidden table. A meter gets `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`.
- **Many on one page:** at most 8 `AsciiShader` instances hold a WebGL context at once; others show their fallback until one scrolls away. Use `AsciiGrid` (Canvas2D) or DOM text for grids of small pieces.
- **Colour meaning:** status colours from the palette (`"green"`, `"orange"`, `"red"`) map to good, warning and critical. Pair colour with a glyph or label so it never carries meaning alone (`█` up, `▒` degraded, `·` no data).

## Sizing cells

`--ascii-cell` sets the glyph height for the whole page (12px by default). Override it on a wrapper for one section, or pass `cell` to one component. 10 to 12px reads as texture, 14 to 18px as deliberate ASCII art, 20px and up as large letters. Cells always snap to whole device pixels; don't scale a renderer with CSS `transform: scale()`, which blurs the glyphs.

## Next.js and server components

- Files that use `AsciiShader`, `AsciiGrid`, `useAsciiColors`, `useFrameLoop` or a canvas start with `"use client"`. A server page imports and renders them like any component.
- `AsciiPre`, `frameToText`, `mapTones` and the charset helpers run on the server too.
- Webcam and file input stay in the browser: read them with `useMediaElement` in a client component and never upload them.

# Quality checks

Run every check before calling an effect done. Each is something you can see or measure.

## Glyphs

- Individual glyphs read at 100% zoom. Zoom into a screenshot: you see characters, not a blur, not pixel dots, not a flat block.
- Glyphs are crisp at device pixel ratio 1, 2 and 3, and after browser zoom. A blurry result means the canvas is scaled by CSS or the cell isn't whole device pixels; let the renderer size itself.
- The effect uses more than two or three glyphs. A field stuck between two tones draws a flat pattern; widen its range or raise `grade.contrast`.
- Shapes are round where they should be (aspect corrected with `res.x / res.y`) and look right in both `standard` and `braille`.
- The box has the intended size at 1440px and 390px wide, with no horizontal scroll at 390px.
- Light and dark mode both look intentional. Toggle the `.dark` class to check; the media query alone doesn't change a shadcn theme.

## Text and contrast

- Text over glyphs has 4.5:1 contrast against the densest glyphs behind it, or sits on cleared ground or its own panel.
- Real text stays real: headings, labels and values are HTML, selectable and read by screen readers. Never draw copy into a canvas.

## Motion and accessibility

- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the renderer root has `data-state="static"` and shows a finished frame (`stillTime`). Emulate it: `agent-browser set media dark reduced-motion`, Playwright `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" })`, or DevTools Rendering.
- Offscreen and in a hidden tab, the root reports `data-state="paused"`.
- Decorative canvases are `aria-hidden` (the renderers set it by default). Data visuals have an accessible name with the value.
- Nothing flashes more than three times a second. Glyphs that change every frame at random (`hash21` with raw `t`) flicker; quantise time.
- Controls you add (charset pickers, export buttons) are keyboard reachable with a visible focus ring.

## Performance

- At most 8 `AsciiShader`s are live at a time. Use `AsciiGrid` or DOM text for many small pieces.
- The `field` string is a module-level constant; changing values go through `uniforms`.
- Keep fields cheap: `fbm` is four noise calls, and Braille samples eight points per glyph. A field calling `fbm` a dozen times can drop frames on a phone at small cell sizes.
- `AsciiGrid` draw functions allocate nothing per frame: create tone fields and arrays once per size and reuse them.
- Images and video are sampled at grid size, never at full camera resolution.

## Console

- No compile errors, `uniform … skipped` warnings, or WebGL context-lost messages.
- No hydration warnings: client-only values (theme colours, sizes, `Math.random`) are read in effects or hooks, not during render.

## Checking state in a browser

```js
[...document.querySelectorAll("[data-state]")].map((el) => el.dataset.state);
// "running" on screen, "static" under reduced motion, "paused" offscreen, "fallback" when nothing drew
```

# Theme and colour

## The tokens

`ascii-tokens` writes these into the project's global CSS, in `:root` and `.dark`:

| Variable               | Default                    | What it controls                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ascii-ink`          | `var(--primary)`           | Glyph colour in `mono`, and the top of the default palette        |
| `--ascii-paper`        | `var(--background)`        | The surface behind the glyphs                                     |
| `--ascii-cell`         | `12px`                     | Glyph cell HEIGHT in CSS px. The width follows the font's advance |
| `--ascii-font`         | the project mono font      | The font glyphs are drawn in                                      |
| `--ascii-glow`         | about 0.35 light, 0.9 dark | Bloom strength, 0 to 1                                            |
| `--ascii-color-<name>` | tuned per theme            | `blue`, `purple`, `green`, `pink`, `orange`, `red`, `grey`        |

Tailwind gets matching utilities from `@theme inline`: `text-ascii-ink`, `bg-ascii-paper`, `text-ascii-blue` and so on.

## Naming colours in props

Every colour prop takes an `AsciiColor`:

- A palette name: `"ink"`, `"blue"`, `"purple"`, `"green"`, `"pink"`, `"orange"`, `"red"`, `"grey"`. These win over the CSS keywords they share.
- A CSS variable name: `"--chart-1"`, `"--ascii-paper"`.
- Any CSS colour: `"var(--accent)"`, `"oklch(0.7 0.15 272)"`, `"#fff"`.

Prefer names and variables. They follow light and dark mode and a site palette switch on the next frame without a reload; literal colours don't.

## Palettes

`palette` is paper first, then inks from faint to strong:

```tsx
<AsciiShader
  field={FIELD}
  colorMode="palette"
  palette={["--ascii-paper", "--chart-5", "--chart-1"]}
/>
```

Two entries (paper, ink) cover most effects. Three to five give depth: the faint ink colours sparse glyphs, the strong ink colours dense ones. For several lines or labels, give each its own colour with `seriesColor(undefined, i)` or the palette names.

## Light and dark

Dark mode comes from the `.dark` class on `<html>`. The renderers watch that class and the `--ascii-*` variables and redraw when they change. To check dark mode in a browser, toggle the class (`document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark")`); the media query alone doesn't change shadcn themes.

- Glyphs are thin. Keep 4.5:1 between ink and paper, like body text.
- Bloom (`fx.bloom`, scaled by `--ascii-glow`) reads in dark mode and washes out in light mode. Components should read `--ascii-glow` rather than a fixed bloom.
- A section that must always be dark (a terminal, a phosphor screen) wraps itself in `className="dark"` so the tokens take their dark values there.

## Overriding for one section

```tsx
<section style={{ "--ascii-ink": "var(--chart-2)", "--ascii-cell": "16px" } as React.CSSProperties}>
```

Everything inside draws in the new colour and cell size. Type the style as `React.CSSProperties & Record<"--ascii-ink" | "--ascii-cell", string>` if the project forbids casts.

files.content:
---
name: arc
description: Builds and reviews React interfaces with the Arc UI library (uiarc.dev) so they match Arc's design bar, choosing the right Arc component or block, installing it with the shadcn CLI, and applying Arc's rules for tokens, type, copy, layout, motion, accessibility, and responsive behavior. Use when the user mentions Arc or uiarc, when the project contains components/arc/foundation.css (or the older registry/foundation.css) or imports from @/components/arc (or the older @/registry/components and @/registry/blocks), or when asked to build or polish UI such as a settings page, pricing section, dashboard, landing page, sign-in, form, table, chart, dialog, or command palette.
---

# Arc

Arc is a React component and block library (CSS modules, semantic CSS variables, Motion). Free items install with the shadcn CLI; Pro items are licensed. The quality bar is a calm, neutral interface where type, spacing, and one considered interaction carry the character.

## Workflow

Copy this checklist and tick it off:

```
Arc task:
- [ ] 1. Find: pick an existing Arc block or component for each region (components.md)
- [ ] 2. Install: one shadcn command for every id, foundation.css imported once
- [ ] 3. Wire: documented props only, real data, callbacks return promises
- [ ] 4. Compose: page container, spacing rhythm, states (composition.md)
- [ ] 5. Style and copy: tokens, sentence case, no eyebrows (design.md, copy.md)
- [ ] 6. Review: run checklist.md, fix, run it again until every line passes
```

**Find.** With the Arc MCP server (`https://uiarc.dev/api/mcp`): `search_components` with the user's intent, then `get_component` on the top two or three and compare `whenToUse` and `whenNotToUse`. The first connection opens a browser sign-in to an Arc account (free is enough); if a tool call fails with an auth error, ask the user to reconnect the server rather than guessing. Results mark Pro items `pro, unlocked` when the signed-in account has Pro; otherwise pass `tier: "free"`. Without MCP: read `https://uiarc.dev/llms.txt`, then `https://uiarc.dev/components/<id>/markdown`. Never rebuild an Arc item from scratch, and never reconstruct or imitate Pro source.

**Install.**

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @uiarc/button @uiarc/input @uiarc/switch
```

This needs `{ "registries": { "@uiarc": "https://uiarc.dev/r/{name}.json" } }` in `components.json`; without it use full URLs (`https://uiarc.dev/r/button.json`). Once per project: `import "@/components/arc/foundation.css";` in the root layout (Arc installs into an `arc/` folder under the `components` alias from `components.json`, for example `src/components/arc/`, and its files import each other with relative paths, so no `tsconfig.json` change is needed), and load Geist and Inter as `--font-geist` and `--font-inter`. Pro members install `@uiarc-pro/<id>` with a Pro token (`https://uiarc.dev/docs/ai#pro-access`).

**Wire.** Copy the import line from the item's usage example (a few use a default export, such as `segmented-control`). Selection components take `value` and `onValueChange`; pickers and editors (`date-picker`, `calendar`, `time-picker`) take `value` and `onChange`. When a callback is typed `void | Promise<…>`, return the promise: the item shows its own pending, success, and error states.

## Core principles

1. **Use Arc before writing UI.** Compose components; do not restyle their internals.
2. **One purpose per surface.** One `h1`, one primary action, one memorable detail. Remove ornamental copy and decoration.
3. **Neutral surfaces, meaningful color.** Semantic tokens only. The accent marks active, selected, and emphasized data. Status colors mean status.
4. **Hierarchy from size, spacing, and contrast.** Regular 400 and medium 500 weights only.
5. **Motion explains a change.** Shared tokens, transform and opacity, one continuous movement, reduced motion respected.
6. **Every state designed.** Empty, loading, success, error, disabled, long content, 390px, dark mode.

## Never do

- Eyebrow labels, overlines, or kicker text above headings. All caps or `text-transform: uppercase`.
- Em dashes in copy. Use a period, comma, colon, or parentheses.
- Hand-made focus rings, outlines, or halos, or any ring on pointer focus. Keyboard focus already gets Arc's subtle `:focus-visible` ring from `foundation.css`; tune it with `--focus-outline` tokens.
- Raw hex, Tailwind color classes, or arbitrary font sizes on Arc surfaces.
- Decorative gradients, glows, or colored shadows inside components. Icons inside rounded tiles.
- Nested cards, double page gutters, or a second page container inside a block.
- A toast as the only confirmation of a foreground action.
- Browser-only values (`window`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, `localStorage`) in the first render.

## Quick decisions

| The user wants | Use | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 to 5 views of the same data | `segmented-control` | `tabs` (tabs swap whole panels) |
| Peer panels of one object | `tabs` | Separate routes for each panel |
| On or off that applies now | `switch` | `checkbox` (checkbox is for forms that submit) |
| One of a few visible options | `radio-group`, or `radio-cards` with descriptions | `select` for fewer than 5 options |
| Long option list | `select`, `combobox` to search | `radio-group` |
| A decision that must interrupt | `dialog` | `drawer` |
| A long form or record detail beside the page | `drawer` | `dialog` |
| A task on phones | `bottom-sheet` | `dialog` for mobile-first tasks |
| Destructive action | `confirm-morph`, `hold-to-confirm` for irreversible | A modal for every delete |
| Records to compare | `sortable-data-table` | Hand-built tables |
| KPI row | `metric-card` | Hand-built cards |
| Result of a save | The button or row confirms in place | `toast` (background work only) |

The full catalog by job, with free and Pro ids, is in components.md.

## Reference files

Read only the file the task needs. Each is one level from here.

| File | Read it when |
| --- | --- |
| [components.md](components.md) | Choosing an item: every live id by job, overlays, inputs, data, marketing blocks |
| [composition.md](composition.md) | Laying out a page: containers, dashboards, marketing sections, states, React correctness |
| [design.md](design.md) | Tokens for color, type, surfaces, radii, spacing, icons, metallic and brand treatments |
| [copy.md](copy.md) | Writing any visible text: headings, buttons, errors, empty states, claims |
| [motion.md](motion.md) | Adding or reviewing animation |
| [accessibility.md](accessibility.md) | Semantics, keyboard, names, announcements |
| [responsive.md](responsive.md) | Widths, touch targets, overflow, tables on phones |
| [checklist.md](checklist.md) | Before you finish. Always |
| [example-settings.md](example-settings.md) | Worked example: account settings page |
| [example-pricing.md](example-pricing.md) | Worked example: pricing section with plans, comparison, and FAQ |
| [example-dashboard.md](example-dashboard.md) | Worked example: analytics overview with KPIs, chart, and table |
| [INSTRUCTIONS.md](INSTRUCTIONS.md) | Short always-on rules for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or Cursor rules |
